A benchmark with no timetable is not a transition plan but a permanent probation system, and the cost is economic and generational: investment that might come to Sarajevo goes instead to Zagreb or Belgrade, and young Bosnians leave for Vienna or Munich rather than build careers at home.
Tellingly, even Europeans who helped build the system now recognize this. In a recent Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung essay, former High Representatives Carl Bildt and Wolfgang Petritsch argued the OHR should be abolished without delay – proof that the case for ending supervision is no longer dismissed as a peculiarly American view. But their proposed route, tying closure closely to EU accession, has a problem of its own.
Whether Bosnia’s problems are better resolved inside the EU than left to accumulate outside it is for Brussels and its member states to determine – that is not Washington’s fight. But relying on accession – a moving target, and not Bosnia’s to move – makes for an unstable peg on which to hang the OHR’s closure. A better answer is to give the exit its own timetable, set ahead of that hard-to-predict point.
The answer is neither to walk away tomorrow nor to preserve the OHR indefinitely, but to use the machinery one final time to make itself obsolete: reconvene the PIC at ministerial level, narrow its purpose to a single task, and invest one individual of sufficient standing – palatable to both Washington and the Europeans – to negotiate the shape of a post-OHR Bosnia and direct the Bonn Powers toward that terminal purpose. That High Representative could then set a realistic timetable against the existing 5+2 benchmarks, publicize progress as each is met, and wind the office down accordingly, without prejudice to EU accession but not held up by it either.
There is a useful principle elsewhere in the Western Balkans. The Berlin Process, a decade-old initiative backed by Berlin and Brussels, has focused on regional economic integration rather than indefinite political oversight. Washington need not embrace the European project behind it to recognize the underlying logic: countries become more stable partners when they trade, invest and build institutions as sovereign actors, not when economic engagement entrenches the very powerbrokers whom reform should be displacing.
This is the basis of a genuine US-European bargain – Washington presses for less intrusive supervision and more commercial opening, Europe insists the transition leave behind functioning institutions rather than a vacuum, and the levers each side controls are aligned behind one timetable. The pay-off, if it holds, is striking: the day may usefully come when nationalist rhetoric in Bosnia is relegated to football chants and graffiti – the ordinary background noise of an imperfect European democracy, rather than an existential threat requiring a foreign administrator’s powers of censure. That day should arrive by design, through the PIC’s one final ministerial act – convening to invest a high representative with that terminal mandate – and a Bosnian settlement finally trusted, and required, to stand on its own.
Bosnia has spent 30 years suspended between international supervision and sovereign responsibility. The objective now should not be another 30 years managing that suspension but ending it – deliberately and credibly – in a way that serves Bosnia’s sovereignty and American and European interests alike. Bosnia could then do what it has long been ready to do: build, rather than merely endure, its own future.
The views expressed in this opinion article are the author’s and not necessarily those of Kyiv Post.
Christopher Geidt is a British parliamentarian, an independent member of the House of Lords. He was the chief adviser to Queen Elizabeth II for a decade. A former soldier and diplomat, from 1992 he worked in Bosnia and much of former Yugoslavia for nearly ten years. Lord Geidt was: Political Adviser and Special Assistant to Carl Bildt at the International Conference for Former Yugoslavia, the Office of the High Representative and the Office of the UN’s Special Envoy for the Balkans; Senior Adviser to High Representative Carlos Westendorp; and Senior Adviser to Sir Arthur Watts, the Special Negotiator for Succession Issues for former Yugoslavia. He is the Co-Founder and Director of WB30, a foundation in The Hague advocating for the simultaneous admission of all six West Balkan entities to the European Union by 2030.

title: Okpebolo To Sign Convicted Kidnappers’ Death Warrants If They Don’t Appeal In 30 Days
body: Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State has said he will sign the death warrants of four people convicted of kidnapping at the Vegetable Market along Airport Road, Benin City, if they fail to appeal their sentences within 30 days. ﻿ The governor stated this at a fellowship programme at God’s People Worldwide Prayer Ministry in Benin City, the state capital, where he gave an account of his administration’s efforts to curb kidnapping, cultism and violent crimes. Governor Okpebholo said insecurity was one of the biggest challenges he met on assumption of office and that he had discussed the security situation and the state of roads in Edo with President Bola Tinubu. He said he responded to the Vegetable Market kidnapping incident by informing the President about the attack and assuring him the state would handle it. The governor said he prayed for the arrest of the perpetrators within 24 hours before instructing the Commissioner of Police. “I told him I wanted these guys arrested because I already have an approval from God, and they were caught within that time,” Okpebholo was quoted as saying on Friday. He said that the suspects had been sentenced to death by an Edo State Special Criminal Court on September 29, 2026, for the abduction of a woman at the market. “They are already sentenced to death, and I pray they don’t appeal the judgment. Even when they appeal the judgment, they are only delaying time. If within 30 days, they don’t appeal, I will execute,” the governor said. Okpebholo added that before commencing his administration’s crackdown on kidnapping and cultism, he met with prominent traditional rulers across the state to warn them against interceding for anyone involved in such crimes. He also recounted what he described as spiritual battles associated with the campaign, saying strange incidents occurred after his government demolished a building linked to a cult group. “A black bird died in my office when I demolished their building. A vulture also died in my bed while contesting for governorship,” he said. In his remarks at the event, Founder of God’s People Worldwide Prayer Ministry, Apostle Ehijele Umuahia, urged members of the congregation to participate actively in the 2027 general elections and vote for the governor and his preferred candidates. Citing Proverbs 29:2, Umuahia said prayers for leaders should go hand-in-hand with civic responsibility, calling on Christians to come out in large numbers to vote. He described Okpebholo as a humble man with a long-standing commitment to God, saying he has known him for over 15 years from the days of the late Chief Tony Anenih. “Whenever Chief Tony Anenih came to visit me, he was one of those who accompanied him,” Umuahia said. “That was how we came to know each other.” Special Trial Justice Aigbona Momodu of the Edo State Special Criminal Court sentenced the four men — Marvellous Isaac, Wisdom Michael, Rufus Emete Michael and Gift Raphael — to death on multiple counts for their involvement in the kidnapping of the woman on June 14, 2026. They were tried on an 11-count charge bordering on kidnapping, conspiracy, armed robbery, cultism, and unlawful possession of firearms. “My hands are tied under the law. I wish I have the law permit me to exercise my discretion. I would have, but my hands are tied. I will just impose the sentence as prescribed by the law,” Justice Momodu, while delivering the judgment. The judge sentenced Isaac to seven years’ imprisonment on count one, death by hanging or lethal injection on counts two to nine, 10 years’ imprisonment on count 10, and life imprisonment on count 11. Michael was sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment on count one and death by hanging or lethal injection on counts two to nine. Emete Michael received seven years’ imprisonment on count one and death sentences on counts two, three, four, six and seven. Raphael was sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment on count one and death on counts two, four, six and eight. Justice Momodu also ordered the confiscation of a JoJef pump-action firearm and four cartridges tendered as exhibits in the case, directing that the exhibits be handed over to the Edo State Police Armourer at the State CID for destruction within 30 days. The Edo State Special Criminal Court was inaugurated on July 1, 2026, to handle kidnapping and cultism-related cases and expedite the prosecution of violent crimes in the state. The post Okpebolo To Sign Convicted Kidnappers’ Death Warrants If They Don’t Appeal In 30 Days appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Police rescue kidnap victim in Oyo
body: The Police Command in Oyo State has neutralised a suspected kidnapper and rescued a 15-year-old kidnapped victim during a coordinated security operation along the Awe–Iwo Road area in the state. The Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade disclosed this in a statement on Sunday in Ibadan. Ayanlade said that the successful operation reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to combating kidnapping and other violent crimes through intelligence-led policing. The PPRO said that the operation followed credible intelligence received by the Command on Thursday at about 5:00 p.m that suspected kidnappers were demanding ransom for the release of a kidnapped victim. According to him, the kidnapped victim was abducted from the Onidundun area of Akinyele Local Government Area on Oct.18. “Upon receipt of the intelligence, the Oyo State Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Olugbenga, directed operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Section (AKS), working in close collaboration with Oyo Zone Vigilante Group of Nigeria, to move against the suspects and secure the victim’s release. “Consequently, the operatives mobilised to the Pipeline, Ajagba axis along the Awe–Iwo Road, where they advanced on the suspects’ location. “At about 9:30 p.m the operation resulted in a gun duel after the suspected kidnappers opened fire upon sighting the advancing security team,” he said. Ayanlade said that the successful operation led to the rescue of the kidnapped victim, identified as Sumaila Muhammadu, a 15-year-old male. He said that a yet-to-be-identified suspected kidnapper was neutralised while other members of the gang fled in different directions with gunshot injuries. Ayanlade said that the neutralised suspect was taken to the Hospital, where he was confirmed dead by a medical doctor and his corpse subsequently deposited at the morgue. According to him, police operatives recovered one Android mobile phone and a cutlass during the operation and efforts currently ongoing to apprehend the fleeing suspects. He urged residents of the community to be calm and promptly report anyone with suspicious gunshot wounds to the Police. Ayanlade further urged medical practitioners, hospital administrators, and other healthcare workers to promptly notify the Police of anyone seeking treatment for gunshot injuries. The post Police rescue kidnap victim in Oyo appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Nigerian student dies after asthma attack while celebrating birthday with friends in London
body: A 26-year-old Nigerian international student, Obanyeli Jesse Chima, has died after suffering an asthma attack while preparing to celebrate his birthday with friends in London. Chima had recently completed his master’s degree in Public Health and was awaiting graduation when the incident occurred. According to MyLondon, the incident happened on Saturday, September 19, when Chima met his friend, Eva, and her partner to celebrate their birthdays, which fell on consecutive days. While waiting in a lounge, Chima reportedly told Eva that he needed to step outside for some air because he was experiencing an asthma attack. He began struggling to breathe and used three inhalers he had with him, but they failed to provide relief. Eva called an ambulance, but Chima collapsed while she was speaking to the emergency operator. Eva told MyLondon: “Our friend started CPR after being guided by the ambulance operators. Multiple ambulances came, and they spent around two hours working on him to stabilise his heart. They finally got him to the hospital and told us he’s on life support. They said he might only have memory loss, but he will be fine. “Two days later, they said he’s not getting better. There was no improvement. They eventually did a brain test on him and confirmed that he was brain-dead. On September 25, we lost him. It’s horrible because we were just laughing, and four days later, we had to see his lifeless body.” She said the gathering had been planned as an opportunity for the friends to celebrate their birthdays together, as all three had birthdays in September. “The weekend he suffered was the only weekend we all had free – all our birthdays are in September. He, my partner, and I all have our birthdays one day after another. That weekend was our chance to hang out, but instead we ended up at the hospital.” Chima had recently completed his master’s degree in Public Health and was looking forward to his graduation. “His family had saved money for his graduation, and now that money needs to be used to bury their child. It’s horrible”, Eva continued. Chima and Eva became friends after leaving Nigeria to study in London. He had also worked at Chelsea Football Club, the team he supported. Eva described him as a ‘beloved and cherished friend who was the life of the party’. Despite being described as physically fit, his sudden death shocked his friends, who had not anticipated such an outcome. Chima leaves behind three siblings in Nigeria, where his family is making arrangements to bring his body home for burial. To support the grieving family, Eva and her friends have launched a fundraising campaign to cover the cost of transporting his body to Nigeria, alongside mortuary fees and other related expenses. Explaining the reason for the fundraiser, Eva said: “We’re trying our best to see what we can raise. His family were planning for graduation. As international students, it’s tough already. We want to help take the burden off his family. Nobody has money saved up to bury a child. “His dad made enquiries about burying him in the UK but most of his family is in Nigeria. The family want to see his body before they lay him to rest, so returning him to Nigeria makes more sense; he should be closer to home.” Eva hopes to raise between £7,000 and £9,000 to cover the costs of repatriating Chima’s body to Nigeria. Vanguard News The post Nigerian student dies after asthma attack while celebrating birthday with friends in London appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: We’ll not backdate resignations after our letter to INEC – NNPP
body: The New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) says it will not give in to blackmail of backdating the resignation of members elected on its platform , who failed to complete the process before its letter to INEC on the issue. The party also warned those approaching some members of its leadership to desist as falsifying the records is tantamount to criminality. This is contained in a statement signed by its Founder and Chairman Board of Trustees, Dr Boniface Aniebonam on Sunday. The NNPP insisted that those approaching it now to backdate their incomplete resignation will not be accommodated for obvious reasons. The party was reacting to controversy within its ranks that some of its elected members affected by the letter to INEC have approached the leadership to backdate their resignation. Recall that the NNPP in a letter to INEC on Monday, Oct. 19, stated that Gov. Abba Yusuf of Kano State, 18 members of the House of Representatives , 28 members of the State House of Assembly from Kano, and 2 Senators elected on its platform in 2023, did not complete the constitutional requirements for resignation from the party. The letter, which was jointly signed by the NNPP National Chairman, Dr Agbo Major and General Secretary , Mr Oginni Olaposi stated that the members, who are now in other political parties and contesting for the 2027 general elections have not complied with the constitutional requirements governing resignation from the NNPP. “We write to formally inform the commission of the purported resignation and subsequent political activities of certain elected public office holders, who obtained their respective mandates on the platform of our great party but have failed to comply with prescribed procedures for lawful termination of their membership.” The NNPP leadership assured its members that it will not give in to pressure to reconsider those who left without due process or give in to pressure regarding the matter. “We told those of them who approached us to go back and begin their resignation processes from their wards then ensure that it is properly documented in accordance with the NNPP constitution. “The Constitution of the NNPP (2023, as amended) contains provisions governing the resignation of members, while the Electoral Act, 2026 (as amended), regulates relevant aspects of political party membership, nomination and participation in elections. ” These provisions are not intended to be observed selectively or disregarded at the convenience of individual members, particularly persons who attained elective public office through the sponsorship, structures and electoral platform of the party.” It pointed out that the letter to INEC would be updated to include some members elected on its platform in Katsina and Jigawa, who also did not complete their resignation processes. “We are not scheming for any member to return but the right process must be followed to the letters. We believe in the rights of people to chose where they wish to belong but it must be properly documented as required by law. “In the event of a post election lawsuit by their opponents requiring NNPP to come with records of their resignation, we will do so. As a party, the NNPP is firm on issues regarding its constitution and image and will not renage on that. “We do not know the windows open to them now to complete their resignation but we will attend to those who wish to complete the process. “The electoral guidelines, party constitution and the constitution of Nigeria are specific on the processes and procedures of resignation from a political party. “We are all witnesses to the fact that elected officers of political parties have been in the abuse of processes and procedures to be followed when resigning from political parties.” According to the party, what seems to be the norm is that some of the candidates claim that due to internal crisis in their previous political parties, they tendered resignation letter at their ward levels. “Unfortunately most of them do not ensure that such resignation letters were documented and recorded at the national secretariat of the party and material evidence obtained. “The national secretary has the mandate to keep the register of all members of each political party nationwide. “Any member, who claims to have resigned from a political party and did not ensure that such records are documented and recorded at the national secretariat of the party and material evidence obtained, is deemed not to have resigned. “It is even funny to note that some elected members of the national assembly openly resigned their membership of a political party during plenaries.Some don’t even bother to notify the parties on whose platform they were elected. “This abuse of people’s mandate for selfish interest must be put to a stop. The consequences of their ungratefulness is that they never realised that they belong to two political parties, which is against the electoral laws and the Constitution of Nigeria, and should therefore, suffer the consequences. “The only members exempted from the resignation saga are those who were expelled from the NNPP. “NNPP secured victory at the Abia State High Court Uzuakoli, Federal Capital Territory High Court Abuja and Appeal Court in Owerri, to earn full recognition of INEC to restore the original logo and filled candidates for the 2027 general elections. “Betrayers, who cannot provide INEC with a valid record of resignation are deemed members of NNPP, and cannot be candidates of any other political party for the purposes of contesting the 2027 general elections,” it added. The post We’ll not backdate resignations after our letter to INEC – NNPP appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ukrainian Attacks Kill 4 in Belgorod and Lipetsk, Hit Perm Industrial Plant
body:
Overnight Ukrainian drone attacks killed four people in southwestern Russia’s Belgorod region, one in the Lipetsk region and damaged an industrial site in the Perm region of the Ural Mountains, officials said Sunday.
In the city of Belgorod near the Russian border with Ukraine, an attack killed three people and injured 13, said Belgorod regional governor Alexander Shuvayev.
The overnight attack on Belgorod damaged 30 apartment buildings, 35 cars, four houses, three administrative buildings, eight commercial premises and three social facilities, Shuvayev said.
In a separate incident on Sunday morning, one person was killed and another injured when a Ukrainian drone struck a car in the village of Voznesenovka near the town of Shebekino, local authorities said.
A drone attack on Russia's Perm region damaged an industrial facility, injuring five of its workers, regional governor Dmitry Makhonin said on Sunday.
Emergency services were at the scene and the injured people received the necessary medical help, he said on the state-backed MAX messaging app without providing further detail on the nature of the damage.
Meanwhile, Russia’s Defense Ministry said that its drones had struck a cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk during an overnight attack.
The ministry said the vessel was being used to supply the Ukrainian army.
Russian forces also hit a logistics center, a distribution center and a logistics terminal in the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv. The ministry said the facilities had been used for storage and distribution of dual-use cargo for the Ukrainian military.
Reuters could not independently verify the Defense Ministry's information.
Later on Sunday, southwestern Russia's Lipetsk region Governor Igor Artamonov said a Ukrainian missile strike on an industrial zone in the city of Yelets killed a security guard and injured a paramedic.
Artamonov said the security guard worked at one of the industrial facilities located on the site. The paramedic at the medical center was taken to hospital, where she was receiving the necessary treatment, the governor said.
The governor did not identify the facility that was hit in the strike.
Reuters could not independently verify the report. There was no immediate comment from Ukraine.

title: Tomato prices remain high as pepper gets cheaper in Lagos
body: The drop in pepper prices has brought some relief to traders and buyers in Lagos markets, but the high cost of tomatoes continues to weigh on traders’ sales and consumers’ purchasing power. Traders and consumers who spoke with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in separate interview in Lagos described how changing prices had affected sales, household spending and the quantities of produce they could afford. They cited seasonal availability and transportation costs among the factors influencing the market. Malam Mohammed, a tomato seller at Costain Bus Stop, said he sourced his produce from Mile 12 Market, where prices varied according to variety, size and place of origin. He said a paint of tomatoes, which sold for N6,000 in August and September, now cost N7,000, while a basket had risen from between N35,000 and N40,000 to between N45,000 and N65,000. Mohammed explained that the high cost of tomatoes made it difficult for traders to maximise profits, adding that some customers complained about the sizes and quantities they received for the prices paid. “This business is not a straight business,” he said. He said the complaints had caused him to lose some customers, prompting him to reduce the quantity of tomatoes he purchased at a time to avoid losses from spoilage. Mohammed also said a large bag of pepper currently sold for between N30,000 and N40,000, although he could not recall its exact price in August and September because of fluctuations. Mrs Rukayat Sherif, another trader at Costain Bus Stop, said she bought tomatoes and pepper from Mile 12 Market because she trusted the source. She said a basket of Ghana tomatoes currently sold for between N40,000 and N45,000, compared with N50,000 and above in August and September. Sherif added that a paint of tomatoes now cost N7,000, against between N4,000 and N5,000 in September. She said a small bag of pepper, which sold for between N30,000 and N35,000 in August and September, now cost between N20,000 and N25,000. Sherif noted that five pieces of tomatoes sold for N500, while pepper was also available for N500 in small rubber plates containing a generous quantity. She attributed the price changes partly to seasonal availability and transportation costs, explaining that some tomatoes damaged during transportation the previous week had been sold at reduced prices to prevent further deterioration. She expressed hope that tomato prices would fall to more affordable levels, adding that lower prices would improve sales and reduce customers’ complaints. Mrs Regina Owho, a tomato seller at Suru Market, Suru-Alaba, said large baskets of tomatoes currently sold for about N50,000, while smaller baskets cost between N35,000 and N45,000. Owho recalled that a basket sold for about N40,000 in August and September, although prices fluctuated during that period. She said the frequent changes made it difficult for traders to predict their purchasing costs, adding that the basket she bought on the day of the interview cost N40,000. Mrs Mary Chigozie, a resident of Vaughan Street, Costain, said she spent between N2,000 and N5,000 daily on tomatoes and pepper but had reduced the quantities used in cooking because of the high cost of tomatoes. She said small quantities of tomatoes that previously sold for N200 or N300 now cost N500 or N1,000. Chigozie explained that she sometimes combined pepper with tomato paste or prepared red-oil stew when fresh tomatoes became too expensive. She expressed concern that prices could rise further during the December festive period and urged the government to support and protect farmers. On pepper, Mrs Rukayat Rasheeb, a trader at Olaogun Street, Abule-Nla Junction, Costain, said a bag currently sold for between N45,000 and N60,000, the same price range recorded in August and September. She, however, observed that pepper was now more plentiful than during the earlier period. Rasheeb explained that prices generally declined when pepper was in season and increased when it became scarce. She expressed optimism that prices could fall further, while noting that transportation and loading expenses added to traders’ costs. Mr Okoro Ebubechi, who also sells pepper at Olaogun Street, Abule-Nla Junction, said he currently bought a small basket for N20,000, compared with between N30,000 and N40,000 in September. He attributed the reduction to increased availability during the current season, adding that transportation expenses influenced the prices charged by traders. Ebubechi said customers were buying larger quantities because pepper had become more affordable. He added that he sold pepper in different quantities, including portions worth N500, to accommodate buyers with varying budgets. He expected prices to rise again in December if pepper became less available. Mrs Odunayo Igwe, a pepper trader at Ilogbo Mosque, Apapa Road, said a bag currently sold for N30,000, the same price recorded in September. She explained that although the price had remained unchanged, pepper was now more plentiful than in September, when supplies were lower. Igwe also identified transportation costs as a factor affecting selling prices and expressed hope that prices would decline further. Mrs Patience Niju, a pepper seller at Suru Market, Suru-Alaba, said she currently bought a small bag for N25,000 and a larger bag for N40,000. She added that a small bag of shombo cost N20,000, while a larger one sold for N30,000. Niju said the prices were unchanged from August and September, but the bags contained more pepper in October. She welcomed the increased quantity, saying it encouraged customers to buy more and helped her sales move faster. Mrs Teni David, a civil servant residing in Iyana Ipaja, said N200 to N500 could now buy more pepper than in August and September, when the same quantity cost between N1,000 and N1,500. She said the increased availability had enabled her to buy larger quantities for household consumption. David attributed the seasonal glut partly to limited preservation facilities, explaining that large quantities of pepper entered the market as the produce ripened, prompting traders to sell quickly before it lost its freshness. She called on the government to establish more processing centres where farmers and traders could preserve and package pepper during periods of abundance. According to her, such facilities would help reduce waste and maintain supplies during the off-season. David warned that prices could rise again when the current season ended. Ms Mary Udonwa, another pepper consumer, said the produce had become more affordable, allowing households to buy larger quantities. She said she currently spent between N500 and N1,500 on pepper, depending on her needs. Udonwa explained that high prices in August and September had forced her to reduce the amount used in cooking, sometimes relying on small quantities or ground pepper when fresh pepper became expensive. She attributed the current reduction to increased market supply and suggested that some sellers might be lowering prices to avoid losses from spoilage. Udonwa also expected pepper prices to rise during the Christmas and New Year festivities. The post Tomato prices remain high as pepper gets cheaper in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: NDLEA recovers tons of illicit drug consignments in nine states
body: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has recovered tons of illicit drugs in Kano, Lagos, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta states. The Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Mr Femi Babafemi, said this in a statement on Sunday in Abuja. Giving a breakdown, Babafemi said a suspect was arrested in Warri, Delta with a huge cache of pharmaceutical opioids. These included 29,350 capsules of tramadol, 6,620 tablets of tramadol 200mg, 4,116 bottles of codeine syrup, 11,340 tablets of Rohypnol and 3,500 tablets of diazepam. “Others are 300 ampoules of pentazocine injection, 200 ampoules of diazepam injection, and quantities of tramadol 225mg, Molly and Cocodamol. “He was transferred along with a white Hummer bus from the Nigeria Police Force, Delta State,” he said. In a separate arrest at Enhere Junction, Warri, a 46-year-old physically challenged woman was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Oct. 19 with 6.0kg of skunk. Meanwhile, a 41-year-old suspect was also arrested on Oct. 19 in Adamasingba, Ibadan, Oyo State, following his initial escape from arrest when NDLEA officers seized 197.8kg of cannabis sativa from his house on Sept. 16. Babafemi said a raid in Gerawa area of Kano on Oct. 22 led to the arrest of a suspect and seizure of 159 blocks of cannabis sativa weighing 97.2kg. Also, NDLEA officers at the Lankaviri checkpoint, Yorro Local Government Area, Taraba, on Oct. 23, arrested another suspect with 95 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 60.175kg. “The same day, the Nigeria Police Force handed over a suspect arrested at Dakka village, Bali LGA, with 112 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 81.49kg,” he said. Similarly, in Niger State, another suspect was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Oct. 19 on Sabo-Kainji road, Borgu LGA, with 64,000 pills of opioids, including tramadol and diazepam. Babafemi said NDLEA officers also arrested another suspect on Oct. 21 at Nasaru Town, Ningi LGA, Bauchi State, where they seized 379kg of cannabis sativa packed in seven jumbo sacks. “Acting on intelligence, NDLEA officers on Oct. 20 raided a farm at Board-Ala, Akure South, Ondo, and recovered 56 bags of abandoned cannabis sativa weighing 583kg. “Two cannabis farms in Ugbada Forest, Uzebba, Owan West LGA, Edo, with an estimated yield of 2,023.14kg, were destroyed on Oct. 18 by NDLEA operatives. “They also burnt 450kg of processed cannabis at the site and took 97kg as exhibit,” he said. In a related operation at Ewe community, Owan West, another suspect was arrested with 35kg of the same psychoactive substance. With the same vigour, commands and formations of the agency across the country continued their War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitisation activities to schools, worship centres, workplaces and communities, among others, in the past week. These include WADA enlightenment lectures to students and staff of Oje Grammar School, Ibadan, Oyo State; Government Day Secondary School, Kwamba, Niger State, Baptist Primary School, Olorunda, Ogun. Others are Government Secondary School, Yalea, Kano State; Community Secondary School, Igogoro, Enugu State; Urban Girls Secondary School, Onitsha, Anambra; and Kelebe Community Grammar School, Osogbo, Osun, among others. Babafemi quoted the NDLEA Chairman, retired Brig.-Gen. Buba Marwa, as commending the officers and men of Kano, Lagos, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta commands for their vigilance. This, he said, included their diligence, professionalism and intelligence-driven approach to the various successful operations. Marwa urged them and their colleagues across the country to sustain the tempo of the war against drug trafficking and substance abuse. title: The city does not smell of roses, By Temitope Sodipo
body:
Lagos does not need to experience its own Great Stink before taking decisive action. The warning signs are visible and painfully olfactory. This challenge presents an opportunity to rethink how a fast-growing metropolis can manage its resources and infrastructure more effectively. A cleaner Lagos will require investment, planning, innovation and sustained public cooperation. Above all, it calls for a shared commitment to protecting the environment, preserving public health, and creating a city in which people can live and work with dignity.
What is that stench? Oh, it is the waste collection and disposal truck leaving a trail of small debris and foul smell in its wake. Incidentally, each part of Lagos seems to have its own distinctive smell, but the common denominator is that none exactly smells of roses.
Like many rapidly growing cities, Lagos faces the arduous task of keeping its environment clean while accommodating an expanding population, increasing consumption and rising volumes of waste. With an estimated 13,000 to 15,000 metric tonnes of waste generated daily, the demands on its collection and disposal systems are enormous. From waste accumulating at collection points through an aging and insufficient fleet of compactor trucks to landfill capacity, blocked drainage channels, flooding and inadequate sewage systems, these challenges highlight the significant infrastructure deficit and the intricate relationship between urban growth, infrastructure development, and environmental sustainability.
Lessons from the Great Stink of 1858, a fascinating episode in London’s history? That summer, unusually hot weather intensified the stench from the River Thames, which had become the receptacle for much of the city’s untreated sewage. London’s population had grown rapidly, placing increasing demands on sanitation infrastructure that had struggled to keep pace. The resulting stench was so unbearable that parliamentary proceedings were disrupted. The crisis prompted legislation to fund a comprehensive sewerage system, which transformed London’s sanitation infrastructure and helped protect public health. What had begun as an intolerable environmental nuisance became a catalyst for an ambitious programme of urban renewal.
Yet, more than a century-and-a-half later, London continues to grapple with sewage pollution and other environmental pressures on the Thames. Similarly, the cleanup of the Seine ahead of the 2024 Paris Olympics required substantial investment in wastewater and sanitation infrastructure, as part of a broader €1.4 billion programme, underscoring the scale of investment and planning that environmental renewal can demand. These examples demonstrate that environmental management is never truly complete, even for cities with established infrastructure. The infrastructure for maintaining and renewing urban systems must continue to evolve as population grows, consumption patterns change, and environmental demands become more complex.
…a clean environment is a shared responsibility. Public authorities and waste management operators have important roles to play in providing reliable services, while residents and businesses can contribute through responsible disposal, waste segregation, and avoidance of the use of drainage channels as dump sites. Public education and consistent enforcement can reinforce these efforts.
What, then, can Lagos learn from these experiences?
First, waste management should be understood as an essential component of urban planning and development. Efficient collection and disposal involve more than deploying trucks. They require suitable transfer and disposal facilities, effective drainage, appropriate sewage systems, reliable funding, regular maintenance, and coordination across the relevant agencies.
Second, a clean environment is a shared responsibility. Public authorities and waste management operators have important roles to play in providing reliable services, while residents and businesses can contribute through responsible disposal, waste segregation, and avoidance of the use of drainage channels as dump sites. Public education and consistent enforcement can reinforce these efforts. Ultimately, the objective is to build a city where waste is managed safely and efficiently, rather than merely moved from one location to another. A refuse truck that leaves a trail of dirt behind may have removed waste from one street only to share it across geographies. Effective waste management requires more than collection, a process that still has room for improvement. The quality of transportation and final disposal matters just as much.
Apparently, urbanisation has expanded the cattle egret’s dietary preferences. After all, bird sef must chop! But there is a difference between adaptation and progress. The cattle egret may have found an alternative food source, but its resourcefulness should not become an excuse for ours to falter. Birds can adapt to our waste; our cities should not have to.
Few metaphors for the evolution of waste management as a developmental challenge are as apt as the cattle egret — Lagos Waste Management Authority’s unofficial mascot. Once commonly seen trailing cattle in search of food (ticks borne by the herds), these adaptable birds now seem equally comfortable accompanying refuse trucks and foraging around heaps of garbage. Apparently, urbanisation has expanded the cattle egret’s dietary preferences. After all, bird sef must chop! But there is a difference between adaptation and progress. The cattle egret may have found an alternative food source, but its resourcefulness should not become an excuse for ours to falter. Birds can adapt to our waste; our cities should not have to.
Lagos does not need to experience its own Great Stink before taking decisive action. The warning signs are visible and painfully olfactory. This challenge presents an opportunity to rethink how a fast-growing metropolis can manage its resources and infrastructure more effectively. A cleaner Lagos will require investment, planning, innovation and sustained public cooperation. Above all, it calls for a shared commitment to protecting the environment, preserving public health, and creating a city in which people can live and work with dignity. And perhaps, one day, when a waste collection truck passes, the only thing left in its wake will be the sound of its engine, not the stench.
Temitope Sodipo is a lawyer in the financial services sector. An avid gardener, birdwatcher, and arts enthusiast. She writes from Lagos.

title: IGP Disu proposes 200% gratuity, pension for retired officers
body: The Inspector-General of Police (I-G), Mr Olatunji Disu, has proposed a 200 per cent gratuity and pension for retired police officers as part of the ongoing reforms in the Nigeria Police Force. Disu told newsmen on Sunday in Abuja that the proposal was before a Presidential Committee, set up to examine police concerns and recommend sustainable solutions. He said the proposal was to intensify efforts to secure improved retirement benefits for personnel of the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) and address the longstanding pension challenges. The I-G also said that the committee was made up of representatives of the Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation. According to him, other representative in the committee are the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, the Budget Office of the Federation and the National Pension Commission (PenCom). “Under the proposed arrangement, eligible officers can retire on pension benefits linked to their last salaries, alongside the enhanced gratuity.” Disu said the package was also, expected to address recurring protests by serving officers, seeking to exit the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), a contentious issue within the force. “The initiative is aimed at resolving the outstanding pension liabilities, provide more adequate retirement benefits and create a more efficient pension administration system. “It also seeks to cover officers who retired before the new framework takes effect, with provisions to review their benefits in line with the revised terms, rather than limiting reform to future retirees,” he said. I-G said the intervention of President Bola Tinubu in the police pension crisis had raised expectations among retired officers, who had long complained about inadequate benefits, delayed payments and administrative bottlenecks. According to him, for many pensioners, timely access to benefits is essential for meeting household expenses and medical bills amid rising living costs. He said the Federal Government had cleared the backlog of pension payments that previously left some retirees waiting for up to two years and introduced pension increment. Disu revealed that some of the beneficiaries currently receive almost double of their previous payments. “Our engagement with the presidency, PenCom and other relevant institutions is seen as important to sustain the NPF reform momentum. “The committee is expected to recommend measures on outstanding liabilities, funding arrangements and benefit administration. “It is also, to provide a framework to resolve pension challenges and improve coordination among the institutions responsible for policy, funding and administration,” he said. He added that the proposal remained subject to the committee’s deliberations, relevant government approvals, funding arrangements and implementation guidelines. He said the 200 per cent gratuity should not be regarded as approved or existing entitlement, adding that the final outcome would determine whether it would be adopted. title: Missiles Strike Energiya Defense Battery Plant in Yelets
body:
Cruise missiles struck the “Energiya” defense-industrial enterprise in the city of Yelets in Russia’s Lipetsk region on Sunday, Oct. 25, targeting one of Russia’s foremost manufacturers of specialized power sources for guided missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles, Radio Liberty and open-source intelligence monitors reported.
Lipetsk Region Governor Igor Artamonov confirmed an attack on the municipal industrial zone on Sunday, stating that municipal emergency services and defense specialists deployed to the impact zone, while refraining from identifying the enterprise in his initial dispatches.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
According to independent Russian monitoring outlet Astra and military open-source intelligence channels, incoming cruise missiles struck the production complex of the Energiya research and production enterprise.
Local monitoring channels and defense analysts suggested that the precision interdiction was executed using air-launched cruise missiles, potentially British-supplied Storm Shadow systems.
The facility functions as Russia’s largest scientific and industrial developer in the specialized field of autonomous chemical power sources, high-capacity accumulator batteries, and electrochemical energy units.
The Yelets plant occupies a critical, specialized niche within the Russia’s military-industrial complex, manufacturing electrochemical power components across military, aerospace, and civil aviation sectors.
The enterprise develops and serially manufactures autonomous power supplies, specialized primary battery arrays, and compact lithium cells integrated directly into Russian strike drones, loitering munitions, and electronic control systems.
Energiya’s power units are essential components installed within surface-to-air missile systems, airborne avionics suites, naval combat vessels, and specialized guidance complexes for ballistic and cruise platforms.
Due to its strategic integration into the Kremlin’s defense-industrial supply chain, the Energiya enterprise is subjected to comprehensive international sanctions imposed by the US , the EU , the UK , Canada , Switzerland , Japan , Australia , and Ukraine.
The facility has previously been targeted in long-range interdiction strikes. In May 2025, an aerial strike ignited a major blaze across one of the primary production workshops, followed by a separate strike reported in January 2026.
The missile strike on Energiya in Lipetsk region coincides with an expanding Ukrainian precision campaign systematically targeting critical suppliers of specialized components, chemical precursors, and metallurgy across Russia’s rear defense sector.
Overnight into Sunday, long-range Ukrainian strike drones hit the “Avisma” chemical-metallurgical complex in Berezniki in the Perm region – located 1,500 kilometers (932 miles) away in the Ural Mountains – damaging a core facility of the world’s largest titanium producer vital for Russian combat aircraft, jet turbines, and missile fuselages.
Concurrently on Saturday, Ukrainian precision munitions struck the Tolyattikauchuk petrochemical facility in Samara region and the Omsky Kauchuk chemical enterprise in Siberia, both of which manufacture synthetic rubbers and chemical binders essential for solid rocket propellant used in Iskander-M ballistic missiles and intercontinental systems.
Those operations followed confirmed precision Storm Shadow missile strikes on the Proton defense microelectronics complex in Oryol , which destroyed key production facilities supplying optoelectronics and power semiconductors for missile and air defense platforms.

title: Russian LNG accounts for 20% of European market — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 25. /TASS/. Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) still accounts for a significant segment of the European market of around 20%, Russian President Vladimir Putin told Vesti reporter Pavel Zarubin.
Russia has never refused to supply energy resources to Europe, he noted.
"It is they who have opted out, and who continue to make plans to phase out what they still receive from Russia. And, incidentally, that is quite a significant amount! Our LNG accounts for 20% of the European market. That is a substantial market share," Putin stressed.

title: Russian MFA to respond to accusations of Moscow being behind unrest in Europe — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 25. /TASS/. Russia will not ignore the accusations coming from Europe that it is inciting unrest there, and the Foreign Ministry will definitely respond accordingly, Russian President Vladimir Putin told Vesti reporter Pavel Zarubin.
"When we are accused, here we certainly must respond in some way. I believe the Foreign Ministry will respond to this appropriately and with due care," he said.
"The most important thing is that, without analyzing the causes of the events taking place and without making adjustments to their own economic, foreign, and domestic policies, they will not eliminate these causes," Putin said, speaking about European elites who are prone to "blaming someone abroad.".

The mods at r/opensource posted new submission rules that, among other things, banned projects that use AI. The post made Saturday evening opens by saying, “If your project uses AI, is made by AI, or is intended for AI, it’s not welcome on r/opensource. AI, as it exists today, is incongruent to this Open Source community.”
The new rules have set off a firestorm in the comments, and even spurred the creation of a rival sub r/trueopensource . Moderator Wolvereness has waded into the comments to explain that there’s nuance and room for selective enforcement, such as “software that incidentally has accessibility features that use AI,” including automatic captioning. But that hasn’t slowed complaints from the community who feel the new rules are too broad, misguided, or vague. Many have pointed out that the Linux kernel now contains some AI-generated code, and so projects using it could be banned under the new rules.
While the AI ban is getting most of the attention, mods are placing other restrictions on posts as well. Projects submitted must be at least one year old, actively maintained, and have multiple contributors. That would bar solo developers with new projects from looking for help. The mods even say “we can no longer field requests asking for maintainers or people to contribute.”
The mods also effectively banned any non-English-speaking members of the community. “If you don’t speak English, you need to find a different community,” the post reads. “We cannot distinguish between AI-written and AI-translated. Since you don’t speak English, you can’t even verify yourself if it translated correctly.”

title: Netanyahu trial defense presses Mandelblit over Eshel wiretap he ordered halted
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's defense pressed former attorney-general Avichai Mandelblit on Sunday over whether investigators exceeded his authorization, as Judge Moshe Bar-Am questioned how police were supposed to distinguish between steps they could have taken independently and those requiring further approval.The sixth day of Mandelblit's testimony at the Jerusalem District Court focused on a wiretap of Netanyahu confidant Natan Eshel that Mandelblit ordered stopped, and on the early inquiries that developed into the criminal cases against the prime minister.Defense lawyer Amit Hadad argued that investigators gathered evidence through unauthorized actions and then used it to secure permission to investigate further. Mandelblit maintained that he had approved examining defined subjects, while acknowledging that the Eshel wiretap should have been brought to him beforehand.Under Basic Law: The Government, opening a criminal investigation into a sitting prime minister requires the attorney-general's consent. Hadad's questioning has sought to establish exactly what Mandelblit approved, when he approved it, and whether investigators stayed within those limits.Mandelblit, who authorized the investigations and later approved the indictment, was called as a defense witness. Netanyahu's trial began in May 2020 and concerns three cases involving alleged gifts and dealings with media owners. He denies wrongdoing in all three.Mandelblit angry about Eshel wiretapOn Sunday, Mandelblit said he had been angered to discover that police were tapping Eshel, a close Netanyahu associate involved in his personal and political affairs. Investigators had obtained a court warrant, but Mandelblit said they had not sought his approval.“When I discovered it had been done, I ordered it stopped immediately,” he said.Hadad argued that Netanyahu was the operation's real target, pointing to references in the warrant to Eshel's contact with the principal suspect, described as “a senior elected official.”Prosecutor Keren Tzviran disputed that interpretation. She said the warrant concerned suspicions against Eshel himself, and that references to Netanyahu did not make every suspected offense listed in it an allegation against the prime minister.Mandelblit said he had not been specifically told that numerous conversations between Eshel and Netanyahu had been intercepted. He said his concern was the sensitivity of listening so closely to someone so involved in the prime minister's affairs.Investigations into alleged gifts may have gone beyond A-G ordersThe questioning then returned to the development of Case 1000, which concerns expensive gifts Netanyahu allegedly received from businessmen Arnon Milchan and James Packer, and actions he allegedly took to benefit Milchan. Netanyahu faces fraud and breach-of-trust charges in that case.Hadad challenged whether permission to examine accommodation associated with Packer at the Royal Beach Hotel extended to questioning Milchan's assistant, Hadas Klein, and driver Yonatan Hasson about gifts to Netanyahu and his wife.Mandelblit said he had not known the details of that questioning. He maintained, however, that he had not stopped the broader examination of suspicions that Netanyahu received substantial benefits from business people.Bar-Am pressed him on how investigators were meant to understand those boundaries, asking whether the permission amounted to blanket approval to examine Netanyahu's affairs.Mandelblit rejected that characterization. The subject itself set the limits, he said, and investigators were expected to return to him as significant suspicions developed. They did not need approval for every individual action.Bar-Am questioned whether investigators needed more concrete instructions to prevent them from mistakenly doing something they were not permitted to do. Mandelblit said regular meetings were intended to provide that oversight.He also distinguished the early information about cigars and champagne from the evidence that later persuaded him to authorize a full investigation. What changed his assessment, he said, was information suggesting a regular supply of gifts and the use of code names, which he viewed as indicating concealment.Mandelblit said the wording police proposed for Netanyahu's first questioning had angered him because he believed it pushed Case 1000 toward bribery, while he viewed the suspicions as closer to breach-of-trust issues.The distinction is critical to the charges ultimately filed. Netanyahu faces fraud and breach-of-trust allegations in both Case 1000 and Case 2000, which concerns discussions with Yediot Aharonot publisher Arnon Mozes about favorable coverage in exchange for steps against rival newspaper Israel Hayom.The bribery charge is in Case 4000, alongside fraud and breach of trust. Prosecutors allege that Netanyahu advanced regulatory measures benefiting telecommunications company Bezeq in exchange for intervention in the Walla news website's coverage.

title: Who is Lorne Doerkson, B.C.’s next premier?
body:
British Columbians got their best look so far at Lorne Doerkson on Saturday night, their premier-designate , and self-described “guy from Williams Lake.”
The interim B.C. Conservative leader delivered a rollicking victory speech as he revelled in a sweeping majority win, secured in a snap provincial election called by outgoing Premier David Eby in a disastrous political miscalculation.
Doerkson had emerged from obscurity to unify a fractured Opposition that was a political basket case just six weeks ago. The party had seen waves of defections under former leader Kerry-Lynne Findlay.
The former bronco rider said he knew all about coming back from indignity.
“I have watched a lot of people get thrown at a rodeo and I’ll say I’ve been thrown a few times myself,” Doerkson said.
“But what I’ve learned, what I have learned from that (is) you pick up yourself, dust yourself off and you get back on.”
Doerkson, who has worked as a newspaper publisher and auto dealer, was once little known outside Williams Lake and his home riding of Cariboo-Chilcotin, which he has represented since 2020.
But that all changed on Sept. 20, when he was hurriedly installed as interim leader of the Conservatives — having returned from a trip to Africa — after the resignation of Findlay, whose divisive leadership had been tearing the party asunder.
Two days later, Doerkson was campaigning to become premier after Eby’s early election call.
“I didn’t expect this, I certainly didn’t seek this and I certainly did not plan two years ago to somehow put all of these stars into alignment,” Doerkson said in a campaign interview.
“I mean, the fact is, (in) politics every day is an exciting day and the next one you have no idea what is about to happen.”
His first task was returning Conservative defectors to the fold, including seven who said just days earlier that they were joining the upstart CentreBC party.
He was sometimes being a scarce presence on the campaign trail. But Doerkson and the Conservatives consistently led Eby and the NDP in opinion polls, as the premier faced intense criticism over an early election call that he seemed to struggle justifying.
Before his elevation, Doerkson had stayed mostly out of the culture-war fray, his time in the legislature spent mostly hyper-focused on his riding and region, beset by wildfires and hospital emergency room closures.
Doerkson’s time as publisher of the local newspaper had put him squarely at the heart of the community. As a former rodeo rider, he framed positions on health care from his perspective as a former visitor to emergency rooms.
Scott Tucker, who owns the local Home Hardware in Williams Lake, has been Doerkson’s financial agent since he entered politics, and said in a recent interview that he had known the man for about 15 years or more.
They’re both Rotarians and would encounter each other at community events, where Doerkson was more often than not the master of ceremonies.
Tucker said Doerkson is “not one to go it alone,” describing him as someone who seeks out guidance and input from others, drawing on his experience in business, and volunteering and dealing with different points of view.
Doerkson was certainly gracious in victory.
He thanked Eby for his public service, saying “it asks a lot of a person and a lot of their family.”
“He has given to this province for years, of both of those things. So thank you very much, David Eby,” said Doerkson, who also thanked Green Leader Emily Lowan for “all that she’s done to inspire thousands of young British Columbians.”
His acknowledgment of his political rivals drew warm applause.
But the night belonged to the guy from Williams Lake.

title: Dubai awards Dh3 billion in contracts to expand stormwater drainage network
body: Dubai Municipality has awarded four contracts worth Dh3 billion to expand the emirate’s stormwater drainage network, as part of a wider project aimed at increasing rainwater drainage capacity by 700 per cent by 2033. The project falls under the third phase of the Dh30 billion Tasreef programme and will involve constructing and extending 100km of main drainage lines, with diameters of up to three metres. The work will cover 100 square kilometres across key residential, commercial, industrial and tourism areas, including Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa, Al Manara, Al Quoz, Al Barsha, Al Wasl, Zabeel, Al Bada’a, Al Satwa and Al Marmoom. The project forms part of Dubai’s long-term efforts to improve infrastructure resilience and prepare for future climate challenges while accommodating the emirate’s urban expansion. “Dubai did not simply stop to assess the damage or look for solutions. It took a swift and bold decision to begin a drainage programme designed to serve the city for the next 100 years,” Marwan bin Ghalita, director general of Dubai Municipality, said earlier this month. Dubai Municipality awards contracts for four new projects under Phase 3 of the ‘Tasreef’ Programme to develop Dubai’s stormwater drainage network. With a total value of AED3 billion, the projects will involve the construction and extension of approximately 100 kilometres of main… pic.twitter.com/fjuUCstjOe — Dubai Media Office (@DXBMediaOffice) October 25, 2026 The Tasreef scheme was launched in 2024 after the country experienced widespread flooding caused by unprecedented rainfall in April that year. In June 2025, the municipality completed a Dh277m sewerage and rainwater drainage network in Nad Al Sheba, while in April this year, the drainage network in Al Quoz Creative Zone was completed. The wider Tasreef programme approved aims to increase Dubai’s rainwater drainage capacity sevenfold and enable the system to handle more than 20 million cubic metres of water daily once completed. The project is scheduled for completion in 2033 and is designed to meet the emirate’s drainage needs for the next 100 years. Rather than focusing solely on repairing damage, authorities opted for a long term infrastructure upgrade to improve the emirate’s preparedness for extreme weather events. Earlier in the week, the municipality announced it hadprepared 10 temporary water collection lakes in "strategic locations to accommodate rainwater runoff in the event of heavy rainfall and reduce pressure on the main drainage networks".

title: Nigerian businesses need more than bank loans to thrive – Finance Minister
body:
The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, says Nigerian businesses need more than conventional loans to grow, calling for patient capital, experienced investors and stronger institutional support to help promising enterprises expand.
Mr Oyedele said access to credit alone would not resolve the structural challenges facing entrepreneurs, many of whom struggle to secure the financing, skills and networks required to scale their businesses.
He spoke on Saturday in Abuja at the fourth edition of the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA) Prize for Innovation, where seven startups received awards worth a combined $277,000.
Speaking through his Special Adviser on Finance and Investment, Marie Ukpere, the minister said small and medium-sized enterprises are vital to livelihoods and employment but often lack the resources to grow beyond their current size.
“We also recognise that high-potential businesses often require more than conventional credit. They need patient capital, experienced investment partners, and networks that can help them enter new markets and achieve scale,” he said.
Mr Oyedele said Nigeria’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy would depend partly on its ability to help small businesses become medium-sized enterprises and, eventually, larger companies capable of competing in international markets.
The minister highlighted several government-backed institutions and programmes aimed at improving access to finance and supporting business development.
He cited the Development Bank of Nigeria and the National Credit Guarantee Company as part of efforts to ease financing constraints. The credit guarantee company is designed to reduce lending risks for financial institutions and encourage more lending to small businesses and manufacturers.
He also referred to the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation, which is intended to expand access to consumer credit and support household purchasing power, as well as the $618 million Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises programme, which provides financing and business support to young entrepreneurs.
Mr Oyedele said the NSIA was also anchoring venture capital funds to attract institutional investment into Nigerian businesses.
He added that the authority was developing an impact innovation fund with the Japan International Cooperation Agency, with British International Investment expressing interest in participating.
The proposed fund is expected to support commercially viable businesses addressing economic and development challenges.
“The real measure of your success will not be the prize you receive today. It will be the businesses you go on to build afterwards,” the minister told the finalists.
Earlier, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the NSIA, Aminu Umar-Sadiq, said the 12 finalists were selected from more than 6,000 applications after five stages of screening and business development activities.
He said the competition formed part of the authority’s strategy to support entrepreneurs alongside its investments in infrastructure and other sectors.
This year’s competition focused on healthcare, manufacturing and food systems, which Mr Umar-Sadiq identified as sectors with the potential to create jobs, build skills and improve productivity.
He said all 12 finalists would participate in a six-week learning programme at Lagos Business School, while strategic partners would offer further opportunities for financing and business development.
According to him, the NSIA works with companies receiving its investment to strengthen corporate governance, improve management and expand demand for their products.
“When the equity injection goes into these companies, we work very closely with the management teams to enhance their value proposition, strengthen their governance and broaden the demand for their products,” he said.
Mr Umar-Sadiq cited previous winners, including Money Africa and Sycamore, as examples of businesses whose progress should be assessed over time.
He said the impact of startup investments should be measured over about five years rather than judged by immediate results.
Also speaking, the National Coordinator of the Presidential Unlocking Healthcare Value Chain Initiative, Abdu Mukhtar, described healthcare as a significant investment opportunity.
He estimated Nigeria’s addressable healthcare market at $20 billion and said the sector already has about 250,000 small and medium-sized enterprises, citing figures from the International Finance Corporation.
“We estimate that across the healthcare value chain, the addressable market is about $20bn. There are already about 250,000 SMEs in healthcare, according to the IFC,” he said.
Mr Mukhtar identified pharmaceutical manufacturing, medical devices, clinical research, telemedicine and healthcare logistics as areas where entrepreneurs could develop businesses.
Affiong Williams, founder and chief executive officer of ReelFruit and lead judge of the competition, said her company had raised more than $7 million over 14 years.
She attributed its ability to attract investment to preparation, credibility, and resilience, urging entrepreneurs to understand customer needs, build strong networks, and stay focused despite economic uncertainty.
Dave DeLucia, founder and director of Cascador, said preparing businesses to attract investment was as important as providing capital.
“Capital readiness is just as important or more than the capital itself,” he said, adding that entrepreneurs outside Lagos often needed greater institutional support.
At the competition, Come Again Foods emerged as the overall winner, receiving a combined prize of $105,000.
Protein Kapital came second with $70,000, while InstantRad placed third, receiving $50,000.
Other award recipients were Eight Medical, Uwana Energy, Tryctor and Smartei Agri Tech.
The NSIA said the $277,000 award package comprised $220,000 from the authority, $45,000 from Cascador and $12,000 from Wema Bank.
Beyond the cash awards, the finalists are expected to benefit from business development support and opportunities to connect with potential investors.
The competition is part of the NSIA’s efforts to support innovative businesses and help them develop into sustainable enterprises in Nigeria.

title: Europe Should Be Included in Ukraine Peace Discussions, Kremlin Aide Says
body:
Europe should be included in discussions on a peace settlement in Ukraine because its position could be crucial, Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said on Sunday.
The U.S. has been unable to put pressure on Kyiv to agree to a peace deal, Ushakov said in an interview with state television correspondent Pavel Zarubin.
“Before, it seemed after Anchorage, that the U.S. administration might be able to dictate something and force Kyiv to comply. But so far, this hasn't really worked out,” Ushakov said, referring to a 2025 meeting in Alaska between U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
“That's because it's not enough to talk only to Kyiv; we need to talk to the whole of Europe, which fully supports Kyiv.”
After initially leaving it to Trump to try to broker an end to Russia's war in Ukraine, the EU has made cautious approaches to Russia. The leaders of Britain, Germany and France have said they supported a proposal for talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Putin to try to secure a ceasefire, and that Europe would play a role.
Russia, meanwhile, has said it would be open to dialogue but not ultimatums.
On Sunday, Ushakov said that Russia was ready to resume three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the U.S. after Russia's National Unity Day on Nov. 4, echoing Kremlin comments this week on Putin's willingness to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine as soon as next month.
Zelensky said on Friday that peace negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the U.S. had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, adding that he hoped a meeting of their leaders would follow.
Ushakov also commented on a potential meeting between Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, saying that preparations had already started. The proposed meeting is set to be held on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China over Nov. 18-19.
A separate meeting between Putin and Trump in Shenzhen had not been agreed upon, Ushakov said.

title: Yemeni forces intercept Houthi weapons being smuggled from coast
body: Yemeni security forces have arrested 13 alleged members of a Houthi cell and seized a lorry carrying weapons, ammunition and explosives smuggled by sea into Shabwa province, the governor’s office said on Sunday. Shabwa Governor Awad Al Wazir, who also heads the provincial security committee, said the operation followed surveillance and intelligence-gathering efforts as fighting rages between the Yemeni government and the Iran -backed Houthis. Preliminary investigations found the weapons had been transported by boat and handed over to the cell’s members along the southern Yemeni coast. The shipment was due to be moved for the benefit of the Iran-aligned Houthis, according to a report submitted to the governor. The seized cargo included sniper rifles, ammunition, improvised explosive devices described by the authorities as highly destructive and various types of projectiles. Investigations are continuing to establish the circumstances of the smuggling operation, identify its wider network and determine who else was involved, the report said. The seizure came days after a Houthi ballistic missile attack against members of the Rapid Intervention Forces in Shabwa that, according to the governor’s office, killed 77 people and wounded 195. The Houthis acknowledged the attack, describing it as a concentration of “Saudi enemy” forces managed by Saudi officers. The Iran-backed group claimed Saudi personnel were among dozens of people killed or wounded. Saudi authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Al Wazir called on security and military units to increase readiness, strengthen surveillance and inspections along land and maritime routes, and improve co-ordination and intelligence-sharing to prevent further smuggling and infiltration attempts. The Houthis have recently attacked government-held sites, including Aden airport and the presidential palace in the interim capital. A missile and drone attack on the palace killed five security personnel. Yemeni government forces launched a campaign this month to recapture Houthi-held areas, making advances near the strategic Bab Al Mandeb strait, while the rebels continue to besiege Taiz , a major stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in the southern highlands. Shabwa, an energy-rich province on Yemen’s southern coast, is home to the Balhaf liquefied natural gas site, the country’s largest industrial investment. Yemen’s civil war began in 2014 when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa. A Saudi-led military intervention followed in 2015 at the government’s request. A UN-brokered truce in 2022 maintained a fragile calm until fighting intensified again this year. The conflict has become another front in the wider US-Israeli war against Iran, with the Houthis escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia , the world’s largest crude oil exporter. Yemen is already experiencing one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, and renewed fighting threatens to further worsen conditions for civilians.

title: Pope’s envoy becomes first foreign representative to gain access to Ukrainian POWs held by Russia since 2022
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said a foreign representative was allowed to physically visit Ukrainian prisoners of war held by Russia for the first time since Russia’s full-scale invasion began in 2022. The visit by Cardinal Matteo Zuppi, Pope Leo XIV’s special envoy, marks a potential step toward greater access to Ukrainian captives, whom Russia has largely kept inaccessible to international humanitarian organizations. Cardinal Zuppi visits Ukrainian POWs Lubinets said he had been informed that Zuppi was allowed to meet Ukrainian servicemembers held in Russian captivity. The prisoners also confirmed that representatives of Russia’s human rights ombudsman had begun visiting them. Lubinets said he regularly meets with Russia’s human rights commissioner, Yana Lantratova. At their latest meeting, the two discussed further steps toward returning Ukrainian citizens held by Russia. “Every exchange is negotiations,” Lubinets said, adding that each one offers a chance to make progress on returning both prisoners of war and civilians. During his three-day Moscow visit in September, Zuppi also met with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov, Russia’s human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova, and children’s rights commissioner Maria Lvova-Belova , according to Vatican News. The discussions covered missing persons, family reunification, and the return of Ukrainian children, with Zuppi calling for faster checks to help families reunite. Lubinets said he hoped the new access would continue and pledged to keep working toward the return of all Ukrainian citizens held in Russian places of detention. Russia blocks access to Ukrainian captives Russia has kept the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) from accessing Ukrainian prisoners of war since 2024. The ICRC is mandated under the Geneva Conventions to visit prisoners of war and monitor their treatment. Around 1,500 Ukrainians held by Russia have never had their status as prisoners confirmed by the ICRC and face prosecution, according to Ukraine. Without confirmation of their captivity, their families may lack official acknowledgment of their whereabouts and status. Explore further Russia has kept the Red Cross away from Ukrainian POWs since 2024. Now about 1,500 captives it never confirmed as prisoners face prosecution On 23 October, Ukraine returned 270 people from Russian captivity, including 261 military personnel and nine civilians. The released captives included five survivors of Russia’s July 2022 attack on the Olenivka prison barracks, as well as Ukrainian defenders held since 2018. title: Trump’s Big Lie About Ukraine
body:
Donald Trump has just claimed that the United States had done “a lot” for Ukraine, but that Ukraine has done “nothing” for the United States.
This is unjust in the highest degree. And not just untrue in the normal sense – it is a big lie designed to bring about horror and chaos.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
At the moment, the United States has agreed to purchase Russian diesel, which breaks its own laws as well as international sanctions agreements, and in effect places America on the Russian side of the war. It is also denying Ukraine access to Starlink services (which have been paid for), thereby making it much harder for Ukraine to defend its people against Russian attacks.
The United States provides almost no military aid to Ukraine, and it has been the policy of the Trump administration to deny such aid.
Europeans purchase American arms and deliver them to Ukraine, but even these contractual agreements are not being met by the American side. The most important weapons in question are Patriot interceptors , which Ukrainians need to defend themselves from Russian ballistic missiles.
In other words, the Trump administration has acted to make Ukrainians more vulnerable to Russian attacks. In case there was any doubt about the general drift of this: The president of the United States has now repeatedly called for the president of Ukraine to leave office. And so the question is not how much the United States is doing for Ukraine. The question is why the United States is working to help the Russian aggressor right now.
But that might not even be the greatest injustice in Trump’s statement that “You know what, we’ve given a lot to Ukraine. They’ve given nothing to us.” Ukrainians have fought the largest war since 1945 for almost five years now. The war is longer than the First World War and longer than the American engagement in the Second World War. They suffer military and civilian casualties every day.
Proportional to population, they have suffered losses on a scale Americans have never experienced, with the exception of the Civil War. They live through the equivalent of a 9/11 in Russian terror attacks every few weeks.
And yet Ukrainians are defending themselves, and very effectively. In so doing they are also giving a great deal to us. Because they have been doing so for so long and so well , it is – sadly – all too easy to take for granted Ukrainian contributions to American and world security. So I will just enumerate a few of them here.
Ukraine is defending the basic principle of international law, which is that states are sovereign and that one state should not seize territory from another by way of aggression.
Ukraine is fulfilling the entire NATO mission, which is to defend Europe from Russian aggression. It is doing the job that NATO assigns to its thirty-two members, which include the United States and Canada. Ukraine is doing this job itself.
Ukraine is making a world war less likely. Russia has already brought to life the most worrying security concern on the scale of Europe, which is a Russian invasion of a European country.
