title: Murderer Netanyahu will lose Israel’s election!: TGB
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – The chairman of Youth Union of Türkiye (TGB) in a statement in Israeli envoy’s residence in Ankara, three days before the elections slated for October 27 in Israel, said, “We already know the result: Netanyahu will lose."
The Youth Union of Türkiye (TGB) held a press statement in front of the Israeli Ambassador’s Residence in Ankara, three days before the general elections scheduled for 27 October in Israel. TGB Chairman Mirza Çelik declared: “We already know the election result: Netanyahu will lose and stand trial.”
The Youth Union of Türkiye (TGB) gathered in front of the Israeli Ambassador’s Residence in Ankara on Saturday, 24 October, three days before Israel’s general elections scheduled for 27 October. At the demonstration, where the flags of Yemen, Iran and Palestine flew alongside Turkish flags, young people declared that they placed no faith in “the ballot box of genocidal perpetrators”.
In his statement, TGB Chairman Mirza Çelik described Israel as “the greatest enemy of the oppressed, the cruellest of oppressors and a murderer of children”. Emphasizing that they did not need to wait for the elections to take place to know the result, Çelik said: “We are not waiting for the elections to be held to know the result. Because we have absolutely no faith whatsoever in the democracy of murderers and perpetrators of genocide.”
Explaining how they already knew the outcome through examples from history, Çelik continued his speech with the words of Yunus Emre: “Those who prosper through oppression will meet a disastrous end.”
Çelik listed the fates of figures he described as oppressors throughout history:
Çelik then declared: “Oppressor Netanyahu, you too have prospered through oppression. You too are destined to meet the same tragic end as all the other oppressors.”
Çelik stated that just as the Pharaoh drowned in the Red Sea, Israel was now meeting its end in the Red Sea. He said that Yemen was drowning Israel in the Red Sea, Iran was doing the same in the Strait of Hormuz, and Palestine had turned Gaza into “a hell for Zionist Israel”.
“In the history of the world, oppressors have been no more than a handful, but no one has enough breath to count the brave who have made the world unbearable for them,” Çelik said. Addressing Israel with the words, “Oppressor Netanyahu, let us show you the brave men who have brought about your downfall,” he commemorated those who had fought against Israel:
Çelik declared: “These great heroes have defeated Israel. Set up whatever ballot boxes you wish, hold whatever votes you wish. O Israel, you have lost. Your big brother, your patron, your leader, the United States, has also lost.”
Stating that Israel had spent years attempting to drive Palestinians from their lands, Çelik addressed Israel in the following words: “Despite all your immorality, all the shameless attacks you have carried out, and your blindness to the point of murdering children, you have lost. The Palestinians have won. From this point onwards, it is impossible for Israel to survive through Zionist policies.”
Çelik stated that attitudes towards Israel had changed throughout the region, declaring: “There is not a single nation left in this region that will tolerate genocidal, oppressive Israel.”
Directly addressing Israel in his speech, Çelik said: “We call out from here: Israel, know your limits! The more you attempt to cross your borders and extend beyond them, the more you will drown.” Stating that Zionism and Netanyahu had also “destroyed” Israel itself, Çelik continued: “Now Netanyahu, just like Zionism, will be consigned to the dustbin of history. An Israel that covets Palestine cannot survive.”
Çelik then recited the poem We Shall Not Leave by Palestinian resistance poet Tawfiq Zayyad. The poem expresses the determination of Palestinians to remain on their land, protect the shade of their olive and fig trees, squeeze stones if they are thirsty and sustain themselves on mud if they are hungry, but never abandon their homeland. Following the poem, Çelik declared: “The Palestinians have not abandoned their land, and they never will. But you will get out, and you will stand trial.”
During the demonstration, a peace symbol was placed inside the emblem on the Israeli flag, emphasising that Israel could only find a place in the region in this way.
Following Çelik’s declaration that “you will stand trial”, one of the most striking moments of the demonstration took place. A long sheet of paper listing the crimes attributed to Israel was unfurled towards the ground. The “criminal record”, extending downwards in front of the residence, created a striking visual scene.
Announcing, “We are opening oppressor Netanyahu’s criminal record: For which crimes will Netanyahu stand trial?”, Çelik read out the accusations one by one. Each accusation was accompanied by the declaration “you will stand trial”:
Declaring, “You will stand trial, Netanyahu,” Çelik added: “Yes, oppressor Netanyahu, the end of the road is now in sight for you.”
After reading out Israel’s criminal record, Çelik turned to the upcoming Israeli elections. Declaring, “Yes, oppressor Netanyahu, the end of the road is now in sight for you. Let us see what will come out of the ballot box you have set up to save yourselves,” Çelik opened a ballot box symbolising the Israeli elections. Instead of votes, he took out objects representing criminal prosecution and imprisonment: handcuffs, a prison uniform and a diary.
Çelik displayed these items one by one to members of the press and the cameras. The handcuffs and prison uniform conveyed the message that “Netanyahu’s place is not on an election platform, but in a courtroom and a prison.” The diary symbolised the days of imprisonment awaiting Netanyahu.
Çelik announced the election result with the following words: “There is only one outcome for you in these elections, Netanyahu: defeat and standing trial.”
At the end of the demonstration, balloons bearing images of Netanyahu’s face marked with an “X” were released into the air towards the Israeli Ambassador’s Residence. The balloons rising into the sky marked the final scene of the demonstration.
Deputy Chairman of the Youth Union of Türkiye (TGB)

title: Elon Musk says Ukraine ‘violated Starlink terms’ as full speed service returns
body: Elon Musk has said that the Ukraine military “violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people” and that “loophole” was subsequently closed last week. On October 24, 2026, the SpaceX owner turned to social media where he stated that Starlink was a civilian commercial service which should never be used for “offensive drone strikes to kill people”. “Starshield, a different system, is controlled by the US government,” Musk wrote. “What they decide to do is up to them.” Musk’s social media post came on the same day that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that Starlink and Starshield operations had been “restored to the speeds we had before the restrictions”. “The speeds are now where they need to be,” the president said. “The restoration began overnight, and by this morning, speeds were already sufficient.” Earlier in October 2026, Ukraine began reporting unexpected speed restrictions that disrupted drone operations and its ability to intercept attacks by Russia. Various differing reports blamed the White House while others claimed Elon Musk and Starlink were responsible for restrictions. Comments by senior US administration figures over the last two weeks seemed to offer little clarity on the situation. In Musk’s latest post explaining the “loophole” he said that Starlink remains “critical to the defense of Ukraine, as it is the only system that cannot be jammed or blown up, at least for now”. “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact,” Musk wrote. He added: “SpaceX has done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth BY FAR.” While there has been no official response from Ukraine to Musk’s statement on X, presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov, wrote on Telegram that the comments were unclear. “It is very strange that Elon Musk does not know about the restrictions on Starlink operation in Ukraine,” Beskrestnov said. “1. Starting from the winter of 2026, all StarLink terminals over the territory of Ukraine (including occupied territories) have a speed limit of 70-90 km/h. 2. StarLink does not operate over the territory of Russia. Thus, we PHYSICALLY CANNOT USE COMMERCIAL STARLINK for deep strikes and middle strikes.” RELATED Riyadh Air moves operations away from Saudi capital to Al Qassim Airport The post Elon Musk says Ukraine ‘violated Starlink terms’ as full speed service returns appeared first on AeroTime .

title: London 'Palestine House' places life-size statue of Marwan Barghouti on roof next to Palestine flag
body: A life-size bronze statue of Marwan Barghouti, a senior Fatah official serving five life sentences in Israel for his involvement in the murder of five people in terrorist attacks, has been placed atop a building on High Holborn in the Camden borough of central London, alongside a giant Palestinian flag hanging from the building.Camden Council is investigating whether the statue was installed legally and whether planning permission was required.The investigation followed a complaint filed on Thursday by the pro-Israel British legal organization UK Lawyers for Israel (UKLFI). The following day, the council's planning enforcement department confirmed that an investigation into the property was underway and that the complaint had been referred to the relevant officer. At this stage, no determination has been made that the statue was installed unlawfully.The statue depicts Barghouti with his handcuffed hands raised above his head, his fingers forming a V for victory, resembling the well-known photograph taken after his arrest. It stands on the roof of Palestine House, a Palestinian cultural and community center founded by Osama Qashoo, a Palestinian filmmaker and activist living in the UK.Qashoo was among the founders of the Free Gaza Movement in 2007 and one of the organizers of the Gaza flotilla. He was aboard the Mavi Marmara when Israeli naval commandos took control of the vessel in May 2010. His name also appears in a document published by the Meir Amit Intelligence and Terrorism Information Center following the incident. Palestine House hosts cultural events, film screenings, and exhibitions.Activists campaign for Barghouti's release from prisonBarghouti, 66, was convicted in Israel in 2004 of five murders and sentenced to five life terms plus an additional 40 years in prison. Despite his lengthy imprisonment, he continues to hold considerable political standing in Palestinian society, and his supporters have been conducting an international campaign for his release.This is not the statue's first appearance in London. In June, activists campaigning for Barghouti's release attempted to erect it in Parliament Square, but police prevented the installation and the statue was removed. It subsequently found a home on the building's rooftop.This is also not the first time Palestine House has faced scrutiny from planning authorities. Previous complaints have concerned Palestinian flags displayed near the building, a giant advertisement for a beverage called Gaza Cola, and an illuminated sign bearing the slogan "Stop the Genocide." The council ordered some of the signs removed and refused to grant retrospective approval for other illuminated signage.UKLFI seeks to remove statue due to property being in conservation areaUKLFI is challenging the installation of the Barghouti statue on planning and legal grounds, arguing that neither the statue nor its base appears in the building plans approved in July 2025. The organization emphasizes that the property is located in a conservation area and that approval for the rooftop extension was based partly on assurances that it would not be particularly prominent when viewed from street level. It is now demanding an investigation into whether the statue alters the building's appearance in a way that requires separate planning permission.The legal organization has also sharply criticized the council's handling of the matter on public and moral grounds."Camden Council's failure to enforce the law in relation to this building is a disgrace," a UKLFI spokesperson said.According to the spokesperson, the authorities' conduct encourages violations of the law and undermines public confidence, particularly when controversial messages and the glorification of an individual convicted of terrorism are involved.

title: Ukrainian drones reportedly strike major shopping mall in Russia’s Belgorod overnight
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the MegaGRINN shopping and entertainment complex in the Russian city of Belgorod during a mass drone attack overnight on 25 October, when the mall was closed and no visitors were inside, according to the Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+. Russian authorities reported that a civilian was killed and 10 people were injured in the broader mass drone attack on Belgorod. One of the injured was an ambulance worker, according to the regional operational headquarters. The majority of the drones reportedly targeted one area in the city center, according to ASTRA. Belgorod’s largest shopping complex targeted Exilenova+ identified the reported target as MegaGRINN, Belgorod’s largest shopping and entertainment complex covering about 163,000 square meters. The facility houses more than 200 stores, a supermarket, restaurants, a cinema, and entertainment areas. Belgorod is a Russian city about 34 kilometers (21 miles) from Ukraine’s northeastern border and roughly 70 kilometers (43 miles) from Kharkiv. The city and surrounding oblast have repeatedly come under Ukrainian drone attacks during Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine. Belgorod Oblast borders Ukraine’s Sumy, Kharkiv, and Luhansk oblasts. Russian forces have used the region to launch missile and drone attacks on Ukraine and to stage ground offensives across the border. Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian retail infrastructure The reported strike comes amid an intensified Russian campaign against Ukrainian retail and logistics infrastructure. These attacks have included strikes on shopping centers during business hours, including a 21 August Russian drone attack on the crowded Soniachna Halereia mall in Kryvyi Rih, where 16 people were killed and more than 120 injured. The reported strike on MegaGRINN took place overnight, when the complex was reportedly closed and empty of visitors. Russian authorities reported casualties from the wider attack on Belgorod, but have not linked them to the mall. title: Alkinoos Ioannidis Sings Six Unreleased Manos Hadjidakis Songs
body: Six unreleased Hadjidakis songs reach listeners for the first time on Paides epi Kolono , a work Manos Hadjidakis wrote in 1977–1978 but never finished. Giorgos Hadjidakis edited the new album, which came out on Friday 23 October, the composer’s birthday. It holds 13 songs in total. Alkinoos Ioannidis sings the six unreleased Hadjidakis songs in the composer’s original orchestrations, recorded for the first time. The Athens Chamber Choir sings with him. Record label Panik Oxygen issued the unreleased Hadjidakis songs on digital platforms and on vinyl. More details on the composer’s archive appear on the composer’s official website . Hadjidakis wrote both music and lyrics for Ena Fantasma ti Nychta (A Ghost in the Night). It opens with the lines “It is a demon and it runs through the wilderness” . Why the stage cantata stalled “It is a stage cantata, which was due to be staged as an audiovisual event in Kolonos,” Ioannidis said. However, the mayor of the time “in the end avoided it, perhaps because he considered it particularly daring” , he said. As a result, the composer left the work, almost finished, in a drawer, where the unreleased Hadjidakis songs stayed until now. Besides Hadjidakis, lyricists Nikos Gatsos, Agathi Dimitrouka, Manos Eleftheriou and Michalis Bourboulis wrote the words. In the score, the composer calls the piece “a study in the mangas style of the ’30s” . His note of 4 and 5 March 1978 adds that “Oi Paides epi Kolono compose Greek images of love, squalor and despair” . Before this album, Hadjidakis had recorded Megalos Erotikos (1972) and Paraloga (1976). Later came Epochi tis Melissanthis (1980). A tribute to popular culture Ioannidis described the songs as “a tribute by Hadjidakis to our popular culture” . In his view, the composer “passes it through his own filter, transforming it into something new” , and does not seek popular hits. He also recalled the lecture on rebetiko that Hadjidakis gave at the Theatro Technis on 31 January 1949. Until then the Left had banned the genre while the bourgeoisie hunted it, Ioannidis said. At that time the gendarmerie barred Markos Vamvakaris from leaving Piraeus, so Hadjidakis secured a special permit to bring him to the theatre. When the lecture ended, Vamvakaris took his bouzouki, went on stage and said “Hello, lads” . Across the 13 songs, references run from Oedipus to Vassilis Tsitsanis. Its lyrics capture the ordinary people of the Kolonos neighbourhood. Other unreleased Hadjidakis songs include Paides, oi en ti Asfalto , Epeidi Imastan Polloi and Oloi oi Angeloi t’Ouranou . The choral Metavasi and Sto Stavro, sto Soma Ekeino join them. Earlier recordings such as Vrechei sto Sideradiko and Ta Vradia tis Sarakostis close the album. Panik Oxygen expects to follow the unreleased Hadjidakis songs with another unreleased work, Koinos Vios , towards the end of the year. title: Preparations Underway for Putin-Trump-Xi Trilateral Summit, Ushakov Says
body:
Preparations have commenced for a trilateral summit bringing together Russian President Vladimir Putin , US President Donald Trump , and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov announced on Sunday, Oct. 25.
Speaking to Russian state television network Vesti and reported by news outlet Astra, Ushakov confirmed that Moscow, Beijing, and Washington have agreed in principle to convene the three-way leader-level meeting.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Right now, I can already state definitely that Moscow , Beijing, and Washington are in principle ready to hold it, and preparations for it have already begun,” Ushakov said.
The senior Kremlin aide indicated that the trilateral summit is being planned to take place on the sidelines of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ summit scheduled for Nov. 18–19 in Shenzhen, China.
Addressing parallel diplomatic tracks, Ushakov characterized a prospective three-way meeting involving delegations from the Russia, the US and Ukraine in November as exploratory in nature, describing it as having a “range-finding character.”
Ushakov also addressed the possibility of Vladimir Putin attending the Group of 20 (G20) summit in Miami, Florida, scheduled for December, confirming that the Kremlin has received a formal invitation to the gathering from Washington.
However, the aide stated that Putin’s prospective travel to the US remains contingent upon the operational progress and concrete diplomatic outcomes achieved during the November APEC meetings in Shenzhen.
“For now, we are discussing the November summit in Shenzhen, but we have received an invitation,” Ushakov stated regarding the Miami G20 invitation .
Asked directly whether the decision regarding Putin’s travel to Florida depends significantly on the success of the trilateral summit in China, Ushakov answered affirmatively.
“Of course. But as I say: first comes November, and then comes December,” Ushakov emphasized, underscoring that diplomatic sequencing will dictate Moscow’s scheduling determinations.
The prospect of direct leader-level engagements involving Trump, Putin, and Xi unfolds amid acute sensitivity across European capitals regarding great-power diplomacy brokered without the direct participation of affected European partners and Ukraine.
Former Ukrainian Prime Minister Arseniy Yatsenyuk cautioned on Saturday that three-way arrangements between Washington, Moscow, and Beijing risk partitioning European security architectures, comparing prospective summitry without Ukraine to the 1938 Munich Agreement and the 1945 Yalta Conference.
President Volodymyr Zelensky has consistently stressed that no diplomatic architecture affecting Ukraine’s sovereignty or borders can be concluded over Kyiv’s head .
The Kremlin’s confirmation of the Miami invitation also intersects with institutional pushback from EU officials and international legal bodies.
EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs Kaja Kallas and the European Commission have repeatedly criticized White House overtures toward the Russian head of state, citing state-sponsored hybrid sabotage operations across Europe and an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague charging Putin with war crimes connected to the unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children .
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Firefighters contain blaze after refrigerated truck catches fire on Route 2 near Hadera
body: A refrigerated truck caught fire on Route 2 near Hillel Yaffe Medical Center in Hadera on Sunday, with firefighters preventing the flames from spreading to nearby vegetation, Israel Fire and Rescue Services' Coastal District said.A report of a burning truck on the shoulder of the Coastal Highway was received by the district's emergency dispatch center at 10:39 a.m.Firefighters put out truck that caught ablaze on Route 2Firefighters from the Hadera station arrived at the scene and found the refrigerated truck completely engulfed in flames, with the fire having spread to a nearby fence.Firefighters worked to extinguish the burning truck while simultaneously preventing the flames from spreading to surrounding vegetation.The crews successfully contained the fire and continued working to extinguish the truck blaze, according to the latest update from Israel Fire and Rescue Services.

title: Serres Father Bites Into Glass in His Toddler’s Koulouri
body: A 35-year-old man in Serres suffered a koulouri glass injury when a 2.1-centimetre shard hidden in the sesame bread ring cut his tongue and palate, his lawyer said. The incident happened on Wednesday 21 October. His three-year-old child had already eaten about half of the koulouri before the father finished it. Bleeding from the mouth, he went to the city’s general hospital for first aid. He did not swallow the shard, which measures 2.1 by 0.6 centimetres. How the koulouri glass injury happened Lawyer Dimitris Golemis said his client bought the koulouri from a bakery in the city of Serres. It belongs to a chain that runs other bakeries too, he said. “Things could have turned out even worse, as my client bought the koulouri for his child, who is three years old,” Golemis said. The toddler ate about half and left the rest, so the father picked it up. He suddenly felt the glass in his mouth and, luckily, did not swallow it, the lawyer said. “Imagine if the child had eaten it,” he added. Family turns to the authorities The family has the receipt for the purchase, Golemis said. They have also sent an extrajudicial notice to the bakery company about the koulouri glass injury, but so far they have had no reply. Golemis said the family will also take the case to every competent authority, including the national food safety regulator , EFET. “Food safety is a very serious public health issue,” Golemis said. EFET handles consumer complaints about food across the country. In June, after a complaint about a suspected foodborne illness, Attica authorities stopped tonnes of unsuitable meat from reaching the market. Koulouri, a sesame-crusted bread ring, is a popular street food and a staple breakfast snack across Greece. Since the koulouri glass injury, the family’s priority has been protecting other consumers, the lawyer said. They will also pursue the matter administratively, civilly and criminally, he said. title: Stop Translating Every Word: How to Read Ukrainian Like You Mean It
body:
You open a Ukrainian news article. Three words in, you hit one you don’t know. You stop, look it up, and start again. Two lines later, it happens again. Ten minutes on, you have technically read every word, and you have no idea what the story was about.
Anyone learning Ukrainian knows this feeling. On Nov. 1, Language Lab , a Kyiv-based Ukrainian language school, is hosting a free online webinar built around a simple idea: the problem usually isn’t vocabulary or grammar. It’s the way most learners read, slowly and word by word, chasing the meaning of each term instead of the meaning of the text.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“This happens because you focus on words instead of meaning,” the workshop’s materials put it. The session sets out to change that, with a toolkit of reading strategies that most people already use without thinking in their native language.
The workshop leans on the British reading scholar Christine Nuttall, who argued in 1996 that the best way to learn a language is to live among its speakers, and the next best is to “read extensively in it.”
For the many foreigners in Ukraine who hear Ukrainian daily but still struggle with a news feed, that matters. According to the workshop, regular readers build vocabulary faster, use grammar more accurately, and feel more confident. The gains don’t stay on the page: reading also feeds speaking, listening and writing.
The catch is that reading only helps if you can keep doing it. Word-by-word decoding exhausts the brain fast, and most learners give up long before the benefits arrive.
The session, which is suitable for all Ukrainian learners, introduces different reading strategies and types of reading, from a quick skim to slow, careful study. It then shows how to apply them to very different sources: short ads and social media posts, news articles, and even fiction.
The core argument is that reading is not one skill but several. In English, you switch modes without thinking: you glance at headlines, hunt for a time in an email, settle into a novel. In Ukrainian, many learners use only the slowest mode for everything, and that is what wears them out.
The webinar also looks at how much work context can do. Knowing who is writing, to whom and why often lets a reader follow a text, or guess an unfamiliar word, without stopping to translate. Language Lab promises practical tips and real-life teaching hacks to make reading in Ukrainian simpler and more enjoyable.
The takeaway is that reading is about meaning, not every word. “You don’t need to read perfectly,” the workshop materials say. “You need to read smart.”
The organizers stress that this is a workshop, not a lecture. Participants are encouraged to jump in with questions, and the session closes with 15 minutes of Q&A. It is pitched at learners who want to speed up their path to fluency in Ukrainian.
The details: Language Lab’s reading webinar runs online on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 5 p.m. Kyiv time. Registration is here . Language Lab offers Ukrainian lessons, cultural immersion events and a learners’ community, with a free trial lesson available at lngglab.com.

title: How to apply: EFCC opens portal for 2026 job recruitment
body: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has opened its recruitment portal for 2026, inviting eligible Nigerians to apply for positions across various cadres, including detective officers and skilled professionals. The recruitment exercise offers opportunities for candidates with qualifications ranging from secondary school certificates to university degrees, diplomas and professional experience. According to the recruitment information, applicants are required to submit their applications online through the commission’s official recruitment portal. Interested candidates are advised to review the eligibility criteria for their preferred positions and ensure they meet the requirements before applying. EFCC recruitment 2026: Available positions The recruitment exercise covers four major categories, each with specific educational qualifications and age limits. 1. Detective Superintendent — Assistant Superintendent of EFCC II, GL 08 Applicants seeking this position must possess a bachelor’s degree or Higher National Diploma (HND) from a recognised institution. Candidates must also provide a valid National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge or exemption certificate. Age requirement: 18 to 30 years. 2. Detective Inspector — Inspector of EFCC II, GL 06 Candidates applying for this position must possess a National Diploma (ND) or National Certificate in Education (NCE) from a recognised institution. Age requirement: 18 to 27 years. 3. Detective Assistant — Detective Assistant II, GL 04 Applicants must have at least five credit passes in WAEC, NECO, GCE or NABTEB, including English Language and Mathematics. The required credits must be obtained in no more than two sittings. Age requirement: 18 to 25 years. 4. Professionals and skilled workers The category is open to qualified professionals and experienced workers in several fields. Eligible disciplines include: Medicine Pharmacy Law Nursing Medical Laboratory Science Engineering and technology-related disciplines The commission is also seeking experienced personnel in the following areas: Human Resources Management Financial Analysis Media and Publicity Policy Analysis Legal Services Research Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Library Services Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Driving Administrative and Clerical Services Estate Surveying and Valuation Applicants must have graduated from recognised institutions and possess an NYSC discharge or exemption certificate. Membership of a relevant professional association will be an added advantage. Age requirement: 18 to 40 years. General requirements for EFCC recruitment 2026 Applicants must meet the commission’s general eligibility conditions to be considered for recruitment. The requirements include: Applicants must be Nigerian citizens. Candidates must possess basic computer skills. All academic and professional qualifications must be declared during the application process. Applicants must be medically fit and provide evidence of fitness from a government-approved hospital. Candidates must not have tattoos on any part of their bodies. Applicants must have no criminal record. Additional requirements apply to cadets. Candidates in this category must be single, while male applicants must be at least 1.67 metres tall and female applicants must have a minimum height of 1.64 metres. For professionals and skilled workers, a valid national driver’s licence will be an added advantage. Applicants must also demonstrate good character and integrity. How to apply for EFCC recruitment 2026 Interested and qualified Nigerians are required to complete their applications online through the official EFCC recruitment portal. Follow these steps: Visit the official recruitment portal at https://recruitment.efcc.gov.ng . Review the available positions and select the category that matches your qualifications. Read the eligibility requirements carefully to confirm that you meet the criteria. Complete the online application form with accurate personal, educational and professional information. Declare all required academic and professional qualifications and provide the requested supporting information. Review your application to ensure that the details supplied are correct before submitting it. Keep a copy of the completed application form, as shortlisted candidates may be required to present printed copies during screening. Applicants are advised to use only the official recruitment portal and follow any additional instructions published by the commission. EFCC recruitment 2026: Deadline and application fee The recruitment information states that applications are expected to be submitted within one week of the commencement of the exercise. However, applicants should confirm the official opening and closing dates on the EFCC recruitment portal before submitting their applications, as a specific deadline was not provided in the supplied information. The application process is stated to be free of charge . Applicants are warned against individuals or organisations demanding money in exchange for recruitment assistance. The commission advises prospective candidates to rely on information published through its official recruitment portal and avoid unauthorised agents claiming to facilitate employment. Application portal: https://recruitment.efcc.gov.ng Vanguard News The post How to apply: EFCC opens portal for 2026 job recruitment appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Lamb Souvlaki: Juicy Greek Skewers With a Lemon and Oregano Marinade
body: Lamb souvlaki, the Greek grill favourite, needs just eight ingredients and a few hours in a lemon and oregano marinade. Lamb souvlaki served on warm pita bread. Photo: Allrecipes What is lamb souvlaki? Souvlaki means small pieces of meat grilled on a skewer. According to Wikipedia , the word comes from the Medieval Greek soúvla, which means skewer. In Athens and the south, many people call the skewer kalamaki instead. Cooking meat on skewers is an ancient idea. Archaeologists have found stone and ceramic supports for skewers from Bronze Age Santorini and Mycenaean sites. Homer also describes meat roasted on spits in the Iliad. However, modern souvlaki only became a popular fast food in the 1960s. Today, Greek street food ranks among the world’s best , and food guide TasteAtlas also has a dedicated entry for the dish. In Greece and Cyprus, pork is the usual meat, as with the slow-turned kontosouvli . Lamb souvlaki, by contrast, has a richer flavour that suits a weekend barbecue. Ingredients for the lamb skewers This recipe comes from Kim’s Cooking Now, a contributor on Allrecipes. It serves four and holds 4.9 out of 5 from seven ratings. Each serve has about 346 calories and 19 g of protein, according to Allrecipes. For the lamb souvlaki, you need: 1/3 US cup (about 80 ml) olive oil 1 1/2 US tablespoons freshly squeezed lemon juice 1 1/2 US tablespoons red wine vinegar 1 1/2 US tablespoons chopped fresh oregano 2 garlic cloves, minced 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper 1 1/2 pounds (about 680 g) boneless leg of lamb, trimmed of fat and cut into 2.5 cm cubes Australian cooks should note that a US tablespoon holds 15 ml, while an Australian one holds 20 ml. So, use about 22 ml each of lemon juice and vinegar. For lamb souvlaki, a boneless leg works well because it stays tender on the grill. Shoulder is another option, although it carries more fat. Also, trimming the fat helps stop flare-ups over hot coals. Cut the cubes to the same size, so all the lamb skewers cook evenly. How to make lamb souvlaki Allrecipes lists 15 minutes of preparation and 10 minutes of cooking. The marinade, however, needs at least three hours, so the total time is about 3 hours and 25 minutes. First, whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, oregano, garlic, salt and pepper in a medium bowl. Next, add the cubed lamb and stir until every piece is coated. Cover the bowl and chill the lamb for three hours, or overnight. Then heat a barbecue to medium-high and lightly oil the grill. Thread the lamb onto skewers and keep any leftover marinade for basting. Grill the lamb skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning them often and brushing on the marinade. Finally, serve the lamb souvlaki hot, straight off the skewer. If you use wooden skewers, soak them in water first so they don’t burn. In addition, stop basting a few minutes before the end, since the marinade has touched raw meat. Tips from home cooks Six home cooks have reviewed this lamb souvlaki on Allrecipes. In the most helpful review, Ms Tall Lady says the marinade kept the lamb from tasting gamy. She served the skewers with a Greek salad, pita, tzatziki and roast potatoes. Another reviewer, LovesCooking, followed the directions exactly and found the lamb soft and tender. Her verdict: “Definitely a keeper for future game days, an awesome crowd pleaser.” Lizzy70 added vegetables to her lamb skewers and plans to marinate the meat overnight next time. Finally, msmith7646 made it as written and served it with rice pilaf and green beans. What to serve with souvlaki Kim’s Cooking Now suggests tzatziki and pita bread, or garlic roast potatoes and a Greek salad. A homemade tzatziki takes only minutes while the lamb chills. For a fuller table, add a classic horiatiki salad and a bowl of Greek lemon rice . Then squeeze extra lemon over the lamb souvlaki just before serving. Fried potatoes, as many Greek tavernas offer, are another popular side. The full method, with step-by-step photos, is in the original recipe on Allrecipes . Leftover skewers also make a quick lunch the next day, wrapped in warm pita with tomato and onion. title: Ukraine strikes Russian titanium plant, facility producing missile, drone components, monitoring channels claim
body:
Editor's note: This story was updated to include details of a reported Ukrainian attack on Lipetsk Oblast.
Ukrainian forces struck Avisma, one of the world's largest titanium sponge producers in Russia's Perm Krai, and the Energiya plant in Lipetsk Oblast, which manufactures components for missile systems and drones, on Oct. 25, Ukrainian and Russian monitoring channels reported.
Perm Krai Governor Dmitry Makhonin said at around 11 a.m. local time that 11 drones had been downed during a Ukrainian attack on the region.
Makhonin added that an "industrial facility" in the northern part of the region had sustained "minor" damage but continued to operate as normal. The governor did not specify which facility had been damaged.
According to Makhonin, five employees of the facility were also injured in the Ukrainian attack.
Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ said the strike targeted Avisma in the town of Berezniki, located about 170 kilometers (105 miles) from the regional center of Perm. The plant is part of Russian metallurgical corporation VSMPO-AVISMA.
Located more than 1,400 kilometers (870 miles) from the Ukrainian-Russian border, Avisma has been under U.S. sanctions since 2023. The plant manufactures products used in military aircraft, nuclear submarines, armored vehicles, and missile systems.
Later in the day, Ukrainian forces also attacked the Energiya plant in the city of Yelets, in Russia's Lipetsk Oblast, more than 200 kilometers (120 miles) from the Ukrainian border, the Russian independent media outlet Astra reported, citing open-source intelligence (OSINT) data.
Lipetsk Oblast Governor Igor Artamonov said an "industrial zone" had been targeted, injuring one person. The governor did not identify the facility that came under attack.
Energiya is Russia's largest research and production enterprise specializing in electrochemical power sources. Its products are used across various sectors, including the defense industry, civil aviation, maritime transport and energy. The plant manufactures batteries for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), power sources for air defense missile systems, and batteries for aircraft and naval vessels.
The enterprise is under sanctions imposed by the U.S., the European Union, the U.K., Canada, Switzerland, Japan, Australia and Ukraine.
The plant was previously attacked in May and July 2025, as well as in January 2026 .
Ukraine had not commented on the reported strikes in Lipetsk Oblast and Perm Krai at the time of publication.
Ukraine regularly strikes military targets deep within Russia and occupied territories in an effort to diminish Moscow's ability to continue waging its war.
Ukraine's General Staff said Ukrainian forces also struck Russian military radar stations in Belgorod Oblast overnight on Oct. 25, as well as a Russian command post in occupied Zaporizhzhia Oblast and a command-and-observation post in occupied Kherson Oblast.
Other targets included concentrations of Russian troops in the occupied parts of Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts, the General Staff added.
Earlier, Ukrainian monitoring channels reported a fire at the Omsky Kauchuk petrochemical plant in the Russian city of Omsk following a Ukrainian attack.
The overnight attack on Belgorod also damaged a local shopping and entertainment center, monitoring channel Exilenova+ reported.
Belgorod Mayor Valentin Demidov said one person was killed and 10 others were injured in the attack. Residential buildings and cars were also damaged, he added.

title: Airbus and BAE reportedly set for talks over role in GCAP fighter program
body:
Airbus and BAE Systems executives are reportedly set to meet next week to discuss a potential role for the European aerospace group in the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), a development that could help define whether Germany joins the next-generation fighter project led by the United Kingdom, Italy and Japan.
Four people familiar with the plans told the Financial Times that the companies will discuss possible cooperation in future combat air systems. The talks are expected to include the fighter itself as well as collaborative combat aircraft and the combat cloud that will connect aircraft, sensors and other assets.
The meeting moves the debate over Germany's possible participation from government discussions toward the industrial arrangements required to make it possible.
Germany has been evaluating its options after the breakdown of the Future Combat Air System (FCAS) partnership with France, whose centerpiece was a next-generation fighter intended to replace the Eurofighter Typhoon and Dassault Rafale from around 2040.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
The United Kingdom has already signaled that it is open to German participation in GCAP . London and Berlin have also discussed requirements and potential workshare, but bringing Germany into the program would require an agreement with Italy and Japan and changes to an industrial structure that is already taking shape.
Germany could significantly expand the economic and industrial base behind GCAP. Its participation would add another major defense budget, a potential Luftwaffe requirement and companies including Airbus and MTU Aero Engines to a program already supported by three large economies.
It could also distribute development costs across a larger production base. Next-generation combat aircraft programs involve not only a new fighter but also engines, sensors, weapons, autonomous aircraft and the digital infrastructure connecting them.
That potential benefit comes with a difficult negotiation. BAE Systems, Leonardo and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries have already established Edgewing as the industrial organization responsible for developing the GCAP fighter, with workshare and intellectual property arrangements negotiated among the three founding countries.
Airbus is unlikely to accept a peripheral position in such a program. Mike Schoellhorn, chief executive of Airbus Defence and Space, has previously said the company would need a meaningful role rather than joining simply to manufacture individual structures such as a wing or tail surface.
Any expansion would also have to preserve GCAP's schedule. The three partner countries are targeting entry into service in 2035, five years before the timeframe previously associated with the FCAS fighter.
Germany could theoretically pursue a new program led by Airbus, potentially with Spain and other partners, but that would require establishing another next-generation combat aircraft project almost from the beginning.
Another possibility discussed in recent months involves cooperation with Sweden. Airbus and Saab have explored potential collaboration, while Stockholm is conducting studies and technology demonstrations to determine what should eventually succeed the Gripen.
Sweden, however, has not yet decided to develop a new crewed fighter. Its current Future Fighter System studies are intended to preserve different options beyond 2040 and include autonomous subsonic and supersonic demonstrators.
That puts a possible Airbus-Saab program at a much earlier stage than GCAP, which already has a multinational organization, an industrial structure and a defined target for service entry.
For Germany, joining GCAP would therefore mean negotiating its place inside an existing program rather than creating another one. For the current partners, accepting Germany could reduce the financial burden and expand the potential market, but would also require accommodating a participant with enough industrial and economic weight to demand substantial influence.
There is a historical parallel to the situation Germany now faces. During the 1980s, France participated in European efforts to develop a common fighter but disagreements over requirements, industrial leadership and design authority eventually led Paris to pursue the Rafale independently .
Germany remained with the United Kingdom, Italy and Spain in the program that produced the Eurofighter Typhoon.
More than three decades later, Germany chose France as its principal partner for a successor combat aircraft. FCAS was launched in 2017, with Dassault Aviation responsible for the New Generation Fighter and Airbus representing much of the German and Spanish industrial participation.
The partnership subsequently became dominated by disputes over workshare, intellectual property and authority over the fighter's design. Dassault consistently argued that its experience as a combat aircraft prime contractor required it to retain control over key engineering decisions and protect technologies developed independently by the company.
Those disagreements ultimately proved incompatible with the industrial structure sought by Germany and Airbus.
A German move toward GCAP would therefore reunite much of the industrial partnership behind the Eurofighter . BAE Systems, Airbus and Leonardo already work together on the Typhoon, although GCAP would add Japan's Mitsubishi Heavy Industries to a considerably different multinational structure.
The meeting between Airbus and BAE Systems next week will not determine German participation by itself. It could, however, establish whether there is enough industrial space inside GCAP for Airbus to join a program whose principal roles have already been divided among its British, Italian and Japanese founders.

title: Messolonghi Lagoons: Birds, Salt and History for Families
body: The Messolonghi lagoons, the largest in Greece, turn a weekend in Messolonghi into a family trip of birdwatching, cycling and history. Pack cameras, binoculars and bikes, because that is the basic kit for a family visit to the capital of Aetolia-Acarnania . Italians named the town mezzo-laghi since it sits between lagoons. It ranks among the most beautiful weekend escapes close to Athens, in any season. Why the Messolonghi lagoons suit families The Messolonghi lagoons surround a town that is safe for children and full of activities. Since the streets are completely flat, bikes have become the main way to get around. Strabo called these waters Kynia limni, while Homer described them as Perikallea. Locals prefer the name Messolonghi–Aitoliko lagoons, among the most important wetlands in Europe. Over time, the deltas of the Evinos and Acheloos rivers shaped them. Today they form a national park of 61,600 hectares, including 19,000 hectares of pure wetland. The Ramsar Convention has protected the Messolonghi lagoons since 1971, and they also belong to the Natura 2000 network. At least 280 bird species shelter here, as well as 23 reptile species and nesting loggerhead turtles. A walk through the Holy City Past the stone gate, Greek flags fly everywhere in a town many call the Holy City. No other place is so closely tied to the Revolution of 1821. Tell the children about the heroic Exodus of April 1826. Under siege by the forces of Ibrahim and Kiutahi, the people broke out, but thousands died or fell captive. Later, that sacrifice inspired the poet Dionysios Solomos . Today the Garden of Heroes, open from 9 am to 5 pm, tells the story. Governor Ioannis Kapodistrias ordered its creation in 1830, although it took its present form in 1930. Inside the Garden of Heroes, children will find 50 monuments and a mound for the unnamed heroes of the Exodus. Busts honour Markos Botsaris, Alexandros Mavrokordatos, Solomos and Lord Byron , who died here in 1824. Cannons on the wall will thrill young visitors, though only a small section survives, rebuilt under King Otto in 1838. Tourlida, stilt huts and salt Begin exploring the Messolonghi lagoons at Tourlida, an islet linked to town by a 5-kilometre road and cycle path. Its wooden jetties hold gaites, the traditional keel-less boats. Fishermen’s wooden huts on pointed stilts, called pelades, also stand in the water and make wonderful photos. Between the islets, reed traps hold small fish until they grow. Tourlida has small beaches as well, and locals take mud baths because the clay has a reputation for healing. At the end of the road lies the Black Salt Pan, where salt rises in dark hills. If you come in the morning, visit the Salt Museum, the only one in Greece. Its 1946 building once housed salt-pan workers, while a collection of 1,500 salt cellars crowns the visit. For generations, the Messolonghi lagoons have ranked among the biggest natural fish-producing areas in Greece. Grey mullet roe gives the famous avgotaracho , a Protected Designation of Origin product. In Aitoliko, a workshop shows children how makers salt it with afrina and coat it in natural wax. Later, try it in a fish taverna with eel and lagoon prawns. Boats, kayaks and birdwatching Next, see the Messolonghi lagoons up close by boat. The non-profit Messolonghi by locals runs eco-tours in a traditional boat with a guide. Along the way, the islets of Tourlida, Komma, Marmarou, Plostaina, Prokopanistos and Schoinias dot the water. Fishermen around them will describe their traditional fishing methods . In addition, the group offers tours for photography and stargazing. Families can also hire a canoe or kayak, since the town even hosts a national championship in the sport. For more adventure, the Messolonghi aero club flies two-seater planes with experienced pilots. Each flight lasts 30 to 40 minutes. Patient children can photograph birds from the reed beds, embankments or observation hides. Of the 280 species in the Messolonghi lagoons, 60 enjoy protection. More than 40,000 ducks and waterbirds gather here, including Dalmatian pelicans, storks and flamingos. Cormorants and raptors such as eagles also hunt here, so follow the rules: no shouting, no clapping and stay hidden. Museums, salt mountains and Aitoliko Messolonghi is the birthplace of poet Kostis Palamas and of five Greek prime ministers. Visit his house and the 1850 home of the Trikoupis family, which produced Spyridon and Charilaos Trikoupis. Kids enjoy the Xenokrateio Archaeological Museum, which uses multimedia to display 1,200 finds. Similarly, the Museum of History and Art shows paintings of the siege, while two rooms honour Byron. On the old road to Aitoliko, salt mountains up to 15 metres high glitter like snow. In particular, the salt pans of the Messolonghi lagoons produce more salt than anywhere else in Greece. Aitoliko, often called little Venice , sits on an islet in the water. During the mid-19th century, it was a trading centre with its own fleet. Two multi-arched stone bridges from the late 19th century link it to the mainland. See the Vaso Katraki Engraving Centre and Museum, then the folklore museum and Limanaki Park. Finally, end your trip around the Messolonghi lagoons with sunset on the southern side of Aitoliko. title: Moscow to host 2030 World Weightlifting Championships
body:
GENEVA, October 25. /TASS/. The 2030 World Weightlifting Championships will be held in Moscow, the press service of the International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced.
"All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the Championships in your respective countries will be a huge success. <…> This demonstrates our sport is growing worldwide and the staging of our competitions is highly desirable for many nations around the planet," the IWF General Secretary Jose Quinones was quoted as saying.
Russia has been granted the right to host a major international competition in an Olympic sport for the first time since 2022.

title: Putin surprised anti-Americanism was EU leaders’ first reaction to unrest
body:
MOSCOW, October 25. /TASS/. Blaming Russia for allegedly inciting mass unrest in Europe did not emerge immediately as European leaders initially placed the blame on the incumbent US administration, Russian President Vladimir Putin noted with surprise when speaking with Vesti reporter Pavel Zarubin.
"What surprised me was that the initial reaction was not anti-Russian at all, it was anti-American if you happened to notice. Claims immediately began to circulate that the events unfolding in Europe resulted from the present American administration’s actions, its support for right-wing parties and movements," Putin said.
"That I found strange and unexpected. I didn’t expect European leaders to launch such attacks against their primary ally, their protector, in the military sense of the term, across the ocean," he added.

title: Russian drone attack in Kyiv region injures woman
body:

title: Over 50,000 killed in Europe over summer due to worst heat wave on record
body: Over 50,000 people were killed this past summer in Europe due to a brutal heat wave, marking it as the deadliest the continent has ever faced, CNN reported on Friday.The report cited a new analysis published in two peer-reviewed papers in the journal Nature Health that attributed over half of the deaths to climate change driven by fossil fuel pollution.According to the journal, temperatures reached levels 2.9 degrees Celsius above the 1991-2020 average, with some areas seeing periodic temperatures over 12 degrees Celsius above the average.The findings come as world leaders are set to attend annual United Nations climate talks in Turkey, according to CNN, with a UN report earlier last week warning that the planet has missed its chance to limit the effect of global warming to an increase of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.The Nature Health report concluded that the 2026 summer season was "likely to have been the most dangerously hot summer that Europe has experienced to date," with southern and western Europe being worst affected.UK, other generally cooler European regions experienced record heat, CNN reports CNN noted that the United Kingdom and other European regions known for cooler climates also suffered from thousands of heat-related deaths.Nature Health evaluated 854 European cities in 30 countries, comparing recorded temperatures with those estimated after removing climate change from the equation. Scientists then used the relationship between high temperatures and daily deaths to model the likely number of heat-related deaths between June and August through peer-reviewed research.According to the report, over 800 people between the ages of 20 and 44 were killed by the heat wave, though the highest rates were among those 85 and older.An estimated total of 50,391 people died over the summer, with the analysis noting the death toll as being substantially higher than the 2022 and 2003 summer heat waves in Europe, as well as the highest in 26 years.The journal also found that fossil fuel pollution-driven climate change accounts for about two-thirds of modern heat-related deaths, compared with around 40% earlier this century."I think we can be quite confident in stating that the summer of 2026 is likely to have been the worst on record for heat-related mortality across much of Europe," Clair Barnes, an author on the reports and an extreme weather and climate change researcher at Imperial College London, told CNN. "We're well off-track to limit the worst consequences of climate change, and governments need to realize that without faster action and coordination, things will only get worse.""Until we kick the fossil fuel habit, we will continue to see increasingly hot and dangerous summers," she added. "These numbers are a stark reminder that our hotter, more extreme summers are having an increasingly severe impact on public health. Behind these statistics are real people whose lives were lost and real families who grieve for them."Extreme heat a 'silent killer,' Warwick University associate professor saysWarwick University health and environment associate professor Raquel Nunes told CNN the findings are "growing evidence of how deadly extreme heat can be, despite being described as a 'silent killer' due to its impacts not always being immediately visible."Nunes, who CNN noted was not involved in the research, added that the high death toll amongst those under 65, numbering in the thousands, was particularly alarming.European Mortality Monitoring Network (EuroMOMO) chief physician Lasse Vestergaard acknowledged that the Nature Health findings largely matched the network's, but advised CNN that the results must be treated with caution "as they involve several uncertainties and assumptions."

title: Turkey Moves to Legislate ‘Blue Homeland’ Maritime Doctrine
body: Turkey is preparing legislation to formalise its controversial ‘Blue Homeland’ maritime doctrine, with potential implications for Greece, Cyprus and disputes over maritime rights in the Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean. According to Turkish broadcaster Habertürk, the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) is finalising a bill designed to protect what Ankara describes as Turkey’s sovereign rights and national interests at sea. The legislation is expected to be drafted in November and submitted to the Turkish parliament before the end of 2026. Bill targets maritime boundaries and disputed islets Reports indicate the proposed framework would establish rules governing Turkey’s maritime jurisdiction, including its territorial waters and exclusive economic zone (EEZ). The legislation is expected to define Turkey’s territorial waters as extending six nautical miles in the Aegean Sea and 12 nautical miles in the Black Sea and Mediterranean. It would also reportedly require Ankara’s direct authorisation for economic, scientific and environmental activities within Turkey’s EEZ, including activities involving the seabed and subsoil. Another provision is expected to address the legal status of islets commonly described in Turkey as “grey zones”, invoking international maritime law. Such provisions could intensify existing tensions between Greece and Turkey over maritime boundaries, sovereignty and the interpretation of international law. Great Sea Interconnector adds to tensions Ankara had initially planned to introduce the legislation in the autumn but subsequently postponed the move. According to reports cited by Kathimerini, Turkey opted to monitor developments surrounding the Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnection project, the Great Sea Interconnector (GSI), before proceeding. The project has become a focal point in the wider dispute over maritime activities and jurisdiction in the Eastern Mediterranean. The proposed legislation would formalise Ankara’s approach to maritime claims at a time when Greece and Turkey remain at odds over the limits of their respective rights in the Aegean. The bill’s final wording and its eventual passage through parliament will determine how Turkey seeks to translate the ‘Blue Homeland’ doctrine into domestic law. title: IDF pushing for Hebron attack to be classified as clash between soldiers, terrorists, not terror
body: The IDF is making an effort to characterize Friday's incident in Hebron as an encounter between combat troops and two terrorists, rather than a terrorist attack, in an attempt to avoid professional criticism over the advance preparations of the Judea Regional Brigade, operating under the 98th Division.At the same time, however, the military says the troops' response prevented a larger attack. The IDF and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) are still investigating the incident to determine what terrorist network assisted the attackers. At the time of writing, the assessment is that the attack was carried out by a Hamas cell that received assistance from the organization's headquarters in Turkey.This was not the work of a lone attacker, but rather an organized terrorist network that received assistance from additional operatives in obtaining a handgun, an M4 rifle, ammunition, and training. The terrorists studied the terrain, conducted reconnaissance, and developed operational plans that enabled them to hold off IDF forces for more than 20 minutes. During that time, the military was unable to deploy an attack drone or an aerial surveillance system to eliminate them.Nevertheless, the IDF has noted that the bravery of the soldiers must be acknowledged. The regional defense officer, who found himself caught up in the incident, and the deputy battalion commander actively engaged the terrorists and killed them.There is no doubt that this terrorist network operated under the noses of IDF and Shin Bet intelligence officials, despite a general warning that Hamas intended to carry out attacks in the area ahead of the elections scheduled for this coming Tuesday.Shin Bet, IDF arrest suspects for possible knowledge, support of terror attackOver the past 24 hours, IDF and Shin Bet forces have arrested several Palestinians suspected of assisting the terrorists, or at least knowing that they were preparing to carry out an attack.The suspects were transferred to the Shin Bet for questioning, and further arrests are expected.IDF Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth emphasized that the military acted as a protective barrier, shielding the civilian population from terrorism, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz spoke of offensive operations.At a time when tensions in the West Bank are escalating, and the IDF has deployed an additional divisional headquarters, the 98th Division, to improve command and control capabilities in violent hotspots and areas facing an immediate terrorist threat, the question must be asked: What has the IDF actually done so far?IDF demolishes illegal structures in HebronThe IDF demolished illegal structures in the Hebron area earlier in the morning, demolitions that had already been planned and were unrelated to the terrorist attack. Troops searched 200 buildings in Hebron without finding weapons, ammunition, or terrorist infrastructure. According to the defense minister, approximately 2,000 residents were evacuated.It is clear that these residents will return to their homes shortly and that the evacuation was intended to protect them from potential clashes while IDF forces searched the area.A new and effective approach is needed to address terrorist hotspots in a city such as Hebron, which presents different challenges from the refugee camps in Jenin, Tulkarm, and Nablus. Such an approach is necessary not only to prevent copycat attacks and attacks inspired by this incident, but also to dismantle organized terrorist networks.The terrorists came from a very large clan in Hebron, one of whose members was released as part of the Gilad Schalit prisoner exchange deal. The threat of further terrorist attacks continues to loom.

title: Three Hebron residents arrested for online incitement to terrorism, support for Hamas
body: Three Hebron residents were arrested overnight on Sunday on suspicion of expressing support on social media for the terrorist attack in the West Bank on Friday, in which St.-Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem were killed, as well as for Hamas.According to police, the suspects posted photographs of the terrorists alongside messages of praise and songs glorifying them. One of the suspects referred to the attack as "Operation Hebron." Their online activity was monitored by the IDF's Central Command, and security forces raided their homes overnight.The investigation centers on posts the three suspects published after the attack. According to police, one suspect shared photographs of the terrorists and wrote: "The right is mine and the land is mine. You have no place on our land. This morning, they are alive with their Lord, receiving their sustenance."A song playing in the background included the lyrics, as quoted in the police statement: "In paradise, they will not accept a life of humiliation. Indeed, they are the finest of men."In addition to that post and another suspect's description of the attack as "Operation Hebron," investigators identified content calling for armed conflict against Israel.Suspect shares posts calling for armed combat against 'occupying Zionists'According to police, the third suspect shared statements by religious figures and others calling for Arab and Islamic armies to mobilize for war and armed combat against the "occupying Zionists."The suspect added his own message: "O mighty Allah, victory is near, O Lord of the oppressed."A song playing in the background included the lyrics: "Fight them, Allah will punish them by your hands and humiliate them, grant you victory over them, and heal the hearts of the believing people."Police said the posts were among numerous publications containing incitement and expressions of support for and identification with the enemy, including Hamas.Following the discovery of the posts, officers from the Special Patrol Unit (YASAM) and detectives from Israel Police's Judea and Samaria District raided the suspects' homes in Hebron overnight.During searches of the properties, officers seized the suspects' mobile phones and computers as evidence for the investigation. The three suspects, including individuals aged 17 and 50, were taken to the Hebron police station in the Judea region, where they remain under investigation on suspicion of incitement and support for terrorism.IDF, police conduct Hebron operation following terror attackThe arrests were carried out as part of an operation by Judea and Samaria District police officers and IDF troops from the Judea Brigade in Hebron following Friday's terrorist attack.As part of the operation, security agencies are working together to monitor social media and identify individuals who incite against Israel, support terrorism and its perpetrators, or glorify terrorists.Police said they would continue taking action against incitement and support for terrorism in public spaces and on social media, particularly expressions of support for attacks against security forces.Meanwhile, the investigation into the terrorist attack itself is being conducted by the counterterrorism unit of the Judea and Samaria District's Central Investigations Unit. Investigators are also examining the possible involvement of individuals who helped carry out the attack.

title: Russia Targets Epicentr Stores Across 4 Cities in Under 24 Hours
body:
Russian forces targeted shopping centers belonging to the Epicentr retail network across Kharkiv , Zaporizhzhia , Vinnytsia, and Poltava in under 24 hours, company officials and regional authorities reported on Sunday, Oct. 25.
Head of Epicentr’s Public Relations Department Yuliia Chudnovets announced on Facebook that the commercial chain had been subjected to a coordinated sequence of aerial strikes across central, southern, and eastern Ukraine.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Vinnytsia, Poltava. Again in less than 24 hours,” Chudnovets stated, characterizing the concerted bombardment as a campaign aimed at the total destruction of the retail network’s infrastructure.
The corporate statement follows Sunday morning strikes in Poltava, where a strike drone hit an Epicentr hypermarket building , igniting an immediate fire, causing structural damage, and injuring a 52-year-old woman, according to Poltava Regional Military Administration Head Vitalii Diakivnych.
The targeting of the Poltava hypermarket forms part of a synchronized assault against commercial retail hubs across multiple regional centers.
In Kharkiv’s Osnovianskyi district, Russian munitions engaged commercial facilities in a double-tap attack. Initial reports indicate that Russian forces launched a missile at the commercial center , followed by a secondary strike within a minute of the first impact. The strikes wounded a 39-year-old man and ignited an extensive structural fire across the commercial premises.
Concurrently over the weekend, strikes hit commercial trade facilities in Zaporizhzhia, damaging retail sites and adjacent vehicles, while infrastructure and residential quarters were engaged during a drone barrage across Vinnytsia region .
The coordinated wave against Epicentr centers coincided with broader strikes on commercial and municipal logistics, including the overnight destruction of an emergency fire-tanker truck in Kharkiv during secondary strikes on first responders and an attack on a warehouse in Lozova that killed a 45-year-old commercial employee.
Ukrainian municipal authorities and retail operators have repeatedly emphasized that systematic standoff strikes directed against large-scale construction hypermarkets, civilian shopping hubs, and logistics warehouses serve no military objective.
Epicentr hypermarkets function as primary commercial centers for building supplies, consumer goods, and municipal repair materials utilized by local populations and utility services to restore homes and infrastructure following aerial bombardments.

title: Putin says accustomed to Russia being blamed for all mortal sins including unrest in EU
body:
MOSCOW, October 25. /TASS/. Blaming Russia for all mortal sins as is happening now, amidst the mass unrest in European countries, has become a standard practice for the West, Russian President Vladimir Putin told Vesti reporter Pavel Zarubin.
"There is nothing unexpected here: as is well known, Russia has always been accused of every mortal sin," he said.

title: Peskov Says Kremlin Open to EU Envoy if Focused on Genuine Peace
body:
The Kremlin would support the appointment of a EU diplomatic envoy to participate in negotiations, provided that the designated representative demonstrates a genuine commitment to facilitating a peaceful settlement, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated on Sunday, Oct. 25.
Speaking to Russian state news agency TASS, Peskov asserted that Moscow remains open to European diplomatic engagement, but accused Brussels of failing to adopt a constructive approach toward resolving the conflict in Ukraine.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“If the European Union puts forward a negotiator who genuinely wants to contribute to a peaceful settlement, we would support it,” Peskov said.
The Kremlin spokesperson criticized European leaders for procedural delays in establishing a diplomatic track with Moscow, claiming that the EU has long expressed an interest in appointing an interlocutor but lacks the institutional resolve to finalize a mandate.
Peskov alleged that the bloc “has wanted to do this for a very long time, but either cannot or does not dare to” designate a representative.
Peskov’s comments arrive as European capitals actively debate appointing a high-level envoy to secure direct European representation in prospective settlement talks, amid concerns that bilateral engagements between Washington and Moscow could sideline European and Ukrainian security interests.
According to diplomatic sources cited by The Telegraph, five European leaders are under consideration to represent the continent in discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin .
The candidates include Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Czech President Petr Pavel, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre.
European diplomats have reportedly initiated exploratory contacts with prospective candidates to evaluate their willingness to assume the role.
“There first needs to be a consensus that we need to negotiate with the Russians,” a source familiar with internal deliberations told the British newspaper. “Secondly, there needs to be a consensus on what that position is.”
The diplomatic initiative follows apprehension across European capitals regarding the Trump administration’s unilateral diplomacy with Moscow, which has included backchannel discussions on post-war economic ties alongside the bilateral commercial diesel agreement and executive sanctions waivers under the Lindsey O. Graham Act.
Reaching internal consensus across European institutions has proven complex. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul previously faced resistance over a proposal to lead European diplomatic efforts , while European Council President António Costa declined to undertake the envoy role during a recent meeting of European Union heads of state.
Diplomatic sources suggested that appointing a collective delegation of European leaders could prove more viable than selecting a single envoy, mitigating inter-state friction and reducing the likelihood of individual national vetoes.
The concept of a European negotiating representative has circulated for several months. In June, Meloni endorsed Stubb as a viable candidate to conduct dialogue between Kyiv and Moscow.
Stubb has maintained an active role in European coordination, participating alongside President Volodymyr Zelensky and US special presidential envoy Steve Witkoff in consultations in Oslo on Oct. 20.
Stubb has also maintained regular communication with US President Donald Trump , while asserting that asymmetric military pressure – including Ukrainian long-range strikes against Russian territory – remains essential to forcing Moscow into substantive negotiations.
The Kremlin’s conditional opening toward a European negotiator coincides with diplomatic preparations for prospective trilateral talks between delegations from the US, Ukraine, and Russia.
Following an Oct. 21 meeting in St. Petersburg between Putin and Witkoff , the Kremlin confirmed that Moscow is prepared in principle to resume trilateral consultations in early November, with Abu Dhabi and Switzerland identified by diplomatic sources as prospective venues.
Zelensky has affirmed Kyiv’s readiness to engage in trilateral consultations provided that an enforceable ceasefire and binding security guarantees serve as baseline conditions, while warning that economic accommodations granted to Moscow without verified de-escalation merely prolong the conflict.
