title: NG troops deliver baby food to Oleshky
body:
According to Ukrinform, Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi announced this on Facebook .
“Despite the Russian occupation and the difficult conditions faced by the residents of the Kherson region, our units continue to support the people,” the interior minister noted.
According to him, the day before, National Guard troops used drones to deliver 15 packages weighing a total of over 600 kilograms to families with children. Specifically, the packages contained breakfast cereals, milk, educational games, and toys.
“Among the children currently in the besieged town of Oleshky are some who were born during the full-scale war and have never known life without terror. We are supporting these families and delivering essential supplies to them,” the minister added.
Vyhivskyi also expressed his gratitude to everyone who assembled these packages, operated drones, and provided cover, as well as to those who, at the risk of their lives, are helping Ukrainians in the temporarily occupied territory.
As reported by Ukrinform, Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian Parliament’s Commissioner for Human Rights, held an online meeting with Russian Human Rights Ombudswoman Yana Lantratova, during which they discussed the previously agreed-upon details of the humanitarian mission in Oles hky.

title: Russian Strike Hits Epicentr Mall in Poltava, Woman Injured
body:
A Russian aerial strike struck the Epicentr shopping center in the central city of Poltava on Sunday, Oct. 25, igniting a fire across the commercial building and injuring a 52-year-old woman, regional authorities reported.
Head of the Poltava Regional Military Administration Vitalii Diakivnych announced on Telegram that incoming fire struck the large retail center, triggering an immediate blaze and causing structural damage.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“A fire broke out. Information regarding the extent of the damage is being clarified. Liquidation of the consequences of the attack is ongoing. Preliminarily, a 52-year-old woman sustained injuries,” Diakivnych stated.
Emergency responders, specialized firefighting brigades, and civil defense units deployed to the site of the hit to contain the blaze, secure the perimeter, and evaluate whether additional personnel or visitors were inside the facility during the impact.
The kinetic impact on the Epicentr hypermarket in Poltava follows a sequence of targeted Russian strikes against commercial retail sites, logistics facilities, and public infrastructure across Ukraine over the weekend.
On Saturday evening, Russian forces struck a commercial shopping center in the Osnovianskyi district of Kharkiv , igniting a major structural blaze, alongside strikes on a construction hypermarket and industrial facilities that wounded several civilians and three emergency rescue workers during follow-on secondary strikes.
Concurrently in Dnipropetrovsk region, a strike drone hit a residential high-rise in Synelnykove, killing four civilians and wounding 13 others.
Overnight into Sunday, Russian bombardments damaged critical infrastructure and municipal utility networks across nine regions , with impacts reported at thermal power plants, electrical substations, coal mining enterprises, grain storage facilities, and a postal depot.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Fresh Clashes Rock France as Protesters March On
body:
Clashes erupted across France on Saturday as protesters took to the streets, a week after marches that degenerated into violence and prompted a firm security backlash from French President Emmanuel Macron, who is scrambling to restore order.
Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers faced “an extremely elevated level of violence” from black-clad “ultra-left” extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes.
Two people were “seriously” injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case.
Authorities had deployed 70,000 security personnel across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living.
The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalized, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over the country six months before an election to choose Macron’s successor.
Nunez said Saturday’s outcome was more “positive” than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses.
But there was widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as an assault on the right to protest.
Saturday’s demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organizing CGT union.
The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources.
Macron’s government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centers, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones.
The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as “illegitimate”.
In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully.
The march had been pushed to the capital’s southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities.
Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing, with Nunez blaming “500 rioters” at the back of the march.
AFP journalists saw police charge several times, blasting tear gas and using batons against some, mostly young, protesters.
“They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters,” one demonstrator bleeding from a baton blow to his face, who gave his first name as David, told AFP.
Thousands of protesters in the western city of Nantes broke through lines of police firing tear gas and a water cannon to reach the city center, an AFP journalist witnessed.
Emma, 23, who came out in the northwest city of Rennes, denounced the bans on demonstrations and the “repression” of protests by high school students demanding better learning conditions.
Marching in the rain at the head of the protest in the northern city of Lille, 47-year-old Delphine insisted: “Neither the president, nor the weather will stop me from demonstrating.”
In Lyon, police used tear gas to disperse around 1,000 people gathered in the south of the city.
“If they ban protests, that means we’re heading more and more towards a regime that is fascist, that is dictatorial,” said one 20-year-old protester in Lyon, who gave only his first name, Silem.
Protesters face the police's water cannon near Porte de Vincennes during a demonstration in favor of purchasing power, the protection of public services, and fiscal and social justice, in Paris, Oct. 24, 2026 as part of a nationwide call for mobilisation bringing together former members of the Yellow Vest movement, labor unions, high school and university students. (Photo by Aris MESSINIS / AFP)
Protesters face the police's water cannon near Porte de Vincennes during a demonstration in favor of purchasing power, the protection of public services, and fiscal and social justice, in Paris, Oct. 24, 2026 as part of a nationwide call for mobilisation bringing together former members of the Yellow Vest movement, labor unions, high school and university students. (Photo by Aris MESSINIS / AFP)
In the southern cities of Cannes and Montpellier, far-right activists clashed with “ultra-left militants”, in what authorities said was an unprecedented development.
There was looting on the sidelines of the marches in Marseille and Grenoble, police said.
The Yellow Vests, who staged disruptive protests against Macron eight years ago, called for more demonstrations on October 31 for “the freedom to protest”.
Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who marched in Paris, said the movement “is going to repeat itself every week”.
Tensions were heightened by a rally in the city of Orleans by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally party to kick off her campaign for the presidential election.
Thousands of counter-protesters chanting anti-fascist slogans marched in the city.
The unrest across France highlighted the febrile political atmosphere ahead of the vote, in which Le Pen leads in surveys.
Inflation in France, particularly affecting the cost of fuel, has surged since the start of the Middle East war in February.
“I’m going to try and instill a bit of optimism,” said the four-time presidential hopeful, who has cast herself as the law-and-order candidate, ahead of her first major campaign speech on Sunday.
Protests have also broken out in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems.

title: Man Allegedly Kills Girlfriend in Edo
body: Operatives of the Edo State Police Command have arrested one Miracle Samuel, 21, over the alleged killing of his girlfriend, whom he met on social media, in the state. The state’s Commissioner of Police, Patrick Daaor, said the suspect and the victim met on social media and became friends after chatting for months. He said the suspect subsequently invited the victim to his house in the Ahor axis of Benin City, where he allegedly killed her with a knife. Daaor said the suspect was in police custody and would be charged to court after the completion of the investigation. Police Rescue Kidnap Victim in Delta Police Arrest 62-year-old with Gun, Recover Indian Hemp in Delta However, the suspect, in an interview, said the victim sustained injuries while he was struggling to retrieve a knife she allegedly intended to use against him following an altercation. “I didn’t mean to kill her, but she got injured in the process of struggling with her for the knife during an argument,” he said. He said he met the victim online and became friends with her, adding that after chatting for months, she decided to visit him. “On the day she came to my house, we were discussing, but the discussion snowballed into an argument. In the process, she picked up a knife and intended to stab me,” he said. He added that the victim sustained an injury to her neck while they were struggling over the knife. “I didn’t mean to kill her. I tried to save her after she was injured, but she died,” he said.

title: Italy places first order for Rheinmetall Panther-based main battle tanks in €3.7 billion deal, report says
body: Italy has ordered 30 Panther-based main battle tanks and 48 Lynx infantry fighting vehicles from Leonardo Rheinmetall Military Vehicles, according to Milano Finanza . The Italian financial daily reported on 22 October that the two contracts are worth a combined €3.7 billion. If confirmed, the tank deal would be the first production order for any version of Rheinmetall’s Panther KF51. Neither the joint venture, its parent companies Leonardo and Rheinmetall, nor the Italian authorities have confirmed the report. The tanks would be built to an Italian configuration under the New Main Battle Tank programme. No delivery dates have been given, and it is not clear how much development work is covered by the reported price. The 48 Lynx would add to 21 already ordered by the Italian defence ministry. Five of those were bought in an interim configuration based on Hungary’s Hiúz variant, and the other 16 were adapted to Italian requirements. The new batch falls under the Army Armoured Combat System (A2CS) programme. There is no word yet on when the vehicles will be delivered or whether they will differ from the Italian configuration already on order. Italy ultimately plans to buy around 1,050 Lynx ITA/A2CS vehicles in more than a dozen variants. The tank programme covers 132 main battle tanks and 140 support vehicles. Together, the two programmes are expected to cost around €23 billion. A2CS is due to run until 2040 and the tank programme until 2037. The Lynx will replace the Italian Army’s VCC-80 Dardo infantry fighting vehicles, while the Panther-based tanks will serve alongside its upgraded C2 Ariete fleet.

title: Maximalist US and Iran positions fuelling conflict, former Pakistani PM says
body: Maximalist negotiating positions by both the US and Iran have prevented an end to the Middle East conflict, amid worrying signs of the war escalating, a former prime minister of Pakistan told The National. “I think when you go for a maximalist position, that's a stumbling block,” Anwaar Ul Haq Kakar said in a rare interview from Islamabad. “I think both sides probably choose to remain maximalist, and that is the prime reason for [a lack of] progress on this account when it comes to the resolution of the conflict.” The US and Iran have disagreed on the scale and timing of commitments to end the war, including an end to the US blockade of Iran’s seaports, a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz , sanctions relief for Tehran and guarantees of an end to fighting across all fronts in the region. Pakistan brought together Iranian and US officials for the highest-level diplomatic contacts between the two countries in decades following the start of US-Israeli operations against Iran in February. In June, the two countries agreed in Islamabad on a plan to end the war, but the conflict continued, albeit at a lower intensity. Since then, mediators including Pakistan have been urging both sides to return to the negotiating table amid a deadlock over progress. Pakistan’s foremost aim is that military conflict should not resume, said Mr Kakar, who served as acting prime minister of Pakistan before incumbent Shehbaz Sharif took office in March 2024. “Well, this is a desire. This is a wish list. Whether we would be able to achieve that or not, that needs to be tested in probably few days or weeks from now,” he said. "US withdrawals of diplomatic staff from the region in recent days are an indication that the US and Israel could be preparing to resume military strikes," he added, "which is not a good sign." Already hit economically by energy price spikes caused by the war, Pakistan would be further squeezed by renewed fighting, as would other countries around the world, he added. The nation of 260 million people has already endured sharp fuel price increases following a surge in global oil prices prompted by the war. “It would hit us badly,” Mr Kakar said. “Whether it comes to inflation or levying the petrol and then its increased prices, which would be a trickle down effect on the rest of the commodities, we are expecting an adverse economic impact if that is resumed, if the escalation goes on.” US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have pointed to renewed military operations against Tehran in recent days, prompting a flurry of diplomatic activity to rein in any further conflict. “There is only one way to remove this threat once and for all: overthrow the regime in Iran,” Mr Netanyahu said on Thursday. “And that is my directive to the [military], the Mossad and the security branches.” The US has prepared for renewed strikes, US media have reported, although Washington has ruled out action before the midterm elections on November 3. The results of the coming Israeli elections on Tuesday will probably not change the country's appetite for conflict, Mr Kakar believes. "With or without Netanyahu, I do not see an alteration of the policies of that sense of continuous conflict with the region," he said. Pakistan is among the nations opposing any renewed escalation. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar joined meetings between counterparts from Turkey, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Europe in Istanbul on Friday, and the ministers said they would tell parties to the conflict not to escalate attacks. Islamabad has attempted to keep negotiations alive, and military chief Field Marshal Asim Munir travelled to Tehran this week for meetings with senior Iranian officials, including National Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei and Speaker of Parliament Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. Mr Ghalibaf told Mr Munir that the US could not win Tehran’s trust unless it implemented seven conditions put forward in a proposal in September, including an end to US military operations, a release of frozen Iranian assets and a lifting of the naval blockade, according to the Iranian National Security Council-affiliated Nour News outlet. That seven-point proposal put forward by Tehran last month to revive the Islamabad agreement was a “pure Iranian plan”, and Pakistan’s role had been limited to influencing, advising and making suggestions, Mr Kakar said. We are only doing the role of mediation, so the US and Iran are grown ups in the room. Anwaar Ul Haq Kakar, former caretaker Prime Minister of Pakistan “Primarily the two parties who are in conflict here are the US and Iran , not Pakistan,” he said. “We are only doing the role of mediation, so they are grown ups in the room. So they do their own proposals, both sides. We can only suggest to them what is reasonable and what should be accepted or not accepted, and the rest is their choice.” One complication in Iran is there are multiple schools of thought about what the country’s strategy should be. “You have a mix when you interact with the ruling elite. There are quiet pragmatists who are there, but then there are a bunch of ideologues also. So you have to cater for both the audiences,” Mr Kakar said. Iranians, who have struggled under sanctions for decades, have not had the same opportunities as people in neighbouring countries, he added. “Almost three to four generations have been bereft of their counterparts in the region, particularly the Gulf Co-operation Council [countries]. Their entire lifestyle has transformed, and they are on a different model of progress as compared to Iran,” he said. Born in Pakistan’s south-western Balochistan province, which neighbours Iran, Mr Kakar, who is also a current senator in Pakistan’s upper house, said there was room for political debate over a recent defence pact concluded with Saudi Arabia and Turkey, but that further political approval was not needed for it to enter into force. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the Makkah defence agreement in August, and have since co-ordinated to support Saudi Arabia in the face of attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen. Unlike Turkey, where parliamentary approval for the pact is required , Pakistan’s legislators can debate it, but the constitution does not require their green light. Pakistan already has troops and military equipment in Saudi Arabia under long-standing agreements, and any decision to send more “would be a conversation between the three sides” in the Makkah defence pact, Mr Kakar said. “The initial assessment definitely is this: that Pakistan would also be in the role of defending Saudi territories, anyone who violates the Saudi sovereignty or territorial integrity gets challenged. “No one can peek into the future, so there are no manifested clauses where it says that Pakistan would either go to Yemen or any other country, but I'm being very cautious. All I can say is that Pakistan is fully committed to defend Saudi Arabia, no matter what.” Defending the holy cities of Makkah and Madinah is key, he added. “If either Medina or Makkah is, God forbid, attacked by Houthi or by Israelis or by aliens - by anyone - I don't think that there would be a single soul in Pakistan or maybe around the Muslim world who would have a relaxed sleep during the night. That is the red line. Everyone knows that, and I think the Houthis would know that too.” With the US reducing its role as security guarantor in the Middle East, the Makkah pact is a key part of countries in the region finding a way of filling that “vacuum,” Mr Kakar said. Any future expansion of the pact - which he underlined was not just about the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, but about a long-term regional security architecture - would take place in a “very systematic manner,” he said. “They probably would receive applications from the interested parties in the region, and that would be deliberated over there in the newly built secretariat for Makkah agreement,” he said. “Then probably for a year or so, these applications would be tested as observant parties, and then a formal decision by all three would be made that on whom to give permission to enter the club.” Closer to home, Pakistan is currently engaged in a grinding conflict with insurgents in neighbouring Afghanistan, and a peace deal remains elusive despite fatal strikes on both sides this year. Mr Kakar said Pakistan's sole demand was an end to the presence of insurgents from the Tehrik-e- Taliban Pakistan (TTP), a group proscribed as a terrorist organisation by Islamabad, as well as the UK, US and other nations. "Once that is removed, I think so from Pakistan's side, the situation would normalize within 24 hours," he said. ar A major problem in Afghanistan was the lack of accountability for weapons following the fall of the country to the Taliban in 2021 and the withdrawal of US and Nato forces. Arms are now being sold across the region as well as in Afghanistan, he said. "All those small gadgets are now being sold in the black market, which is probably even available from Peshawar and Quetta to the Syrian capital and Yemeni capital and other areas," he said. "So that is the challenge in which Pakistan is being compelled to respond to the presence of TTP on the Afghan side, we go for the precision strikes against their presence on Afghan side." Asked about the UN and human rights organisations' criticisms of civilian killings in Pakistani strikes on Afghanistan, he said the TTP's wearing of civilian clothing did not mean its members were non-combatants. "You cannot determine just on the basis of clothes that they were not the legitimate targets," he said.

title: UN survey finds lasting trauma among El Fasher’s displaced women
body: Nine in 10 organizations supporting women and girls displaced from Sudan’s El Fasher reported persistent psychological distress a year after the city fell to paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), according to a UN Women survey released on Friday. The survey of 50 women’s organizations found that 45 reported continuing psychological distress among displaced women and girls, while 48 said women were unable to sleep because of trauma. El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur, fell to the RSF on October 26, 2025, after an 18-month siege marked by reports of killings, sexual violence, looting and disappearances. “One year on, the scars of the violence in El Fasher have not faded,” Anna Mutavati, UN Women’s regional director for East and Southern Africa, told a press briefing in Geneva. The survey found that 49 of the 50 organizations had observed signs of psychological distress among displaced women and girls, while nine in 10 described their living conditions as unsafe. About two-thirds knew of women or girls who had disappeared during or after the city’s fall. Access to assistance remains limited. Forty-three organizations had encountered distressed women and girls who had received no mental health, psychosocial or legal support since fleeing. Nearly half said few or none of the women they supported could access such services. Mutavati said service providers faced threats of arrest and harassment, while women and girls lacked adequate protection. Some residents have begun returning to El Fasher, but insecurity continues to restrict their movements. According to a 2026 Sudan needs assessment by the International Organization for Migration, 84% of 117 households surveyed said women avoided marketplaces, about two-thirds avoided collecting firewood, and half avoided social, community or religious spaces. Hospitals lack doctors and medicines, while food and other basic goods remain scarce, Mutavati said. She also warned of increasing drone attacks on displacement camps, markets and other civilian infrastructure across Sudan, including in Blue Nile, Khartoum, West Kordofan and Gedaref states and parts of Kassala state. Women and children were among those killed or injured, including people who had already fled violence, she said. The UN Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan has reported that 80% of hospitals in conflict-affected areas are not functioning, contributing to maternal deaths and restricting access to sexual and reproductive healthcare, Mutavati said. Despite insecurity and funding shortages, women-led organizations continue to provide assistance and support peace efforts, she said. Mutavati called for civilian protection, accountability for perpetrators and compliance with international humanitarian and human rights law. She also urged sustained support for women and girls and their meaningful participation in decisions on Sudan’s future. The post UN survey finds lasting trauma among El Fasher’s displaced women appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: What the hell is going on with Netanyahu? - opinion
body: If the original Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu were to hear what his current mutation said this past Friday – in an interview with a business news channel – he would likely call the district psychiatrist from a blocked number and suggest that he himself be brought in for a mental health evaluation.The Hebrew language lacks words sufficiently precise or potent to capture the sheer absurdity and madness embodied in the incumbent prime minister of Israel's recommendation to shift toward a “bypassing economy” or a “blockchain economy.” This goes far beyond merely crashing the stock market tomorrow morning; it amounts to bringing down the state itself.There are only two possibilities: either this fellow has completely detached from reality, or he is drifting further and further from sanity. I am neither a psychiatrist nor a physician, but the man who was once “Mr. Security” (before leading us into the greatest catastrophe in our history) – and who was also once regarded as “Mr. Economy” – is now preparing us to join the ranks of pariah, sanction-stricken states: Iran, North Korea, the Houthis in Yemen, and Israel. What an honor.The man has completely lost the plot – and he's doing it at 200 kph. Could Israel become a “bypass economy”? Could Israel shift from the international banking system to Bitcoin? Could the “Start-up Nation”, a cyber superpower, a country more dependent than most on global monetary systems and the digital flow of capital that fuels its start-ups and investments, transform into a Jewish mutation of North Korea?It's a good thing he didn't suggest we focus on drug trafficking. Then again, why not? The trade in Captagon sustained the Assad regime and Hezbollah for years. We could even try the slave trade, like in the old days. Netanyahu, after all, has a substantial supply of utterly subservient “slaves” available for hire. There's a market for that, too.From saving Israel's economy to calling for a 'bypass economy'To think that this is the same man who, at the turn of the millennium, saved Israel's economy. This is the man who, during his first term in the 1990s, spearheaded the rapid privatization of the Israeli economy. This is the man who taught us the parable of “the fat man and the thin man.” Now, he tells us that “America has changed,” that we can forget about tens of billions of dollars in security aid, and that we need to “reorganize” for what he calls a “bypass economy.”You don't need to be an economist or a tech investor to realize that Benjamin Netanyahu's remarks on this subject border on insanity. I don't really... It is hard to tell whether this is just another linguistic slip-up by Netanyahu – a hysterical gaffe intended to instill fear and convince us that only he can save us – or if he actually believes his own preposterous nonsense.Let's set the record straight: let's start with American aid. America has changed, but not fundamentally. The same Republicans and Democrats are still there. While the extreme fringes of both parties have expanded, the core values remain unchanged. It is Israel that has changed.It's no coincidence that we have been warned for months that American sanctions may follow the US elections. This is not because of the war – the war in Gaza is something they can manage. If sanctions are imposed, it will be because of the government – specifically because the most extreme, the most unhinged, and the most widely recognized anti-democratic figures in the world hold key positions within Netanyahu's government.If this happens, it will be because of National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, and because of the continued rampaging of hundreds of Jewish rioters in Judea and Samaria – who attack, unimpeded, anyone who crosses their path, including Western diplomats. If this happens, it will be because of the person who built this anti-Zionist construct: Benjamin Netanyahu.Take note of how he phrased things in an interview: “I brought in tens of billions of dollars – twice.” He is taking credit for American aid. Well, spoiler alert: American security and economic aid to Netanyahu began long, long before his time. He didn't establish it; he destroyed it. That is a fact.Israelis stand to lose much under 'alternative economy'Let's turn to the concept of an “alternative economy.” First, one must grasp the implications of the warning he issued: We will lose our pensions. We will lose the bulk of our money. Most of us will no longer be able to travel abroad or purchase goods from AliExpress. Our savings will go up in smoke. We will be unable to use international credit cards. The high-tech, cyber, technology, and industrial sectors will collapse.Most entrepreneurs will leave the country, and the remaining investors will vanish. Academia will wither and die. Researchers will move abroad. I suspect the only ones who will remain are the members of the Kohelet Forum. Then again, once the money disappears, they'll likely vanish with it.It is truly unbelievable that Netanyahu actually said these things himself. What was going through his mind? Has he lost touch with what he's saying, or has he lost control of the “gems” tumbling from his mouth? Does he fail to grasp the implications of his words for the international markets? Does he genuinely believe that Israel can achieve self-sufficiency – in munitions, for instance – while operating under a “blockchain economy”?Can a nation survive on Bitcoin when it lacks endless oil reserves and remains 100% dependent on the Western economy and the international banking system? Tell me, has he lost his mind? I'm not entirely sure he hasn't.Let's look at who else in the world relies on an alternative, bypass-style economy: North Korean Supreme Leader Kim Jong Un, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, and now Netanyahu. Is this an inevitable fate? No. It is a “Netanyahu-fate.”This is the future that awaits us if he and his cronies remain in power. This is the destiny that lies in store if this band of opportunists – some of whom aren't even Zionists – continues to hold the State of Israel by the hair and drag it toward the abyss. This can be reversed. This can be stopped.This is not an impossible task... It is possible. On the contrary. All that is required is a return to sanity – to protect democracy, restore law and order, rebuild our public diplomacy apparatus, and fight for our truth and our cause. We must do this intelligently, with good taste, and with sound reason.This is how we have operated since the founding of the state, and we have achieved great success. There is no reason for us to abandon what has been built here. Our ship is speeding toward an iceberg, but we still have time to change course, take the helm, and return to safe waters.

title: Saudi Arabia intercepts barrage of Houthi missiles and drones
body: Saudi Arabia intercepted a series of missiles and drones, including over its capital, Riyadh, on Sunday as the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen continued to counter attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthi rebels. The attacks came as authorities prepared to reopen two terminals at Riyadh’s main international airport following a deadly strike earlier this month. The Saudi-led coalition said air defences intercepted and destroyed 10 ballistic missiles launched towards the kingdom’s southern region. It also reported intercepting a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh and destroying a drone aimed at the capital. The coalition fighting the Houthis separately said it had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched towards Khamis Mushait in southwestern Saudi Arabia. The Saudi Civil Defence issued warnings through its National Early Warning Platform about potential danger in Abha city and Khamis Mushait governorate. The Khamis Mushait warning was the second issued for the area on Sunday morning. The Civil Defence later said the danger had passed, urging residents to follow safety instructions and avoid gatherings and filming. The coalition said interceptions of two ballistic missiles on Saturday had resulted in debris falling in Makkah, Jeddah, Taif and Rabigh. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia was reopening two terminals at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Sunday, about two weeks after the airport was closed following a Houthi missile attack that killed 13 people and injured more than 300. Terminal 1 will handle domestic flights, while Terminal 2 will serve international flights. The Houthis repeated their threats to airlines, airport staff and travellers against using the airport. The rebels' spokesman, Yahya Saree, described the site as unsafe and said it remained a “military target”, warning that the group would continue operations against it. He said Saudi Arabia would bear responsibility for the consequences of resuming airport operations. As the situation escalated, the US on Saturday warned its citizens against travelling to Saudi Arabia and several other countries in the region, including Bahrain, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Kuwait, Oman, the UAE, Qatar, Syria, Yemen and Israel. The advisories cited the threat of terrorism. Washington urged people to reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia because of threats including the “risk of drone and missile targeting of American interests by Iran and the Iranian-supported Houthis”, as well as armed conflict and terrorism. “Do not travel to the Yemen border due to terrorism,” the US advisory for Saudi Arabia said. The US warned that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia “have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area”. A Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen’s civil war in 2015 at the request of the internationally recognised government, after the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa. A UN-brokered truce in 2022 helped maintain a fragile peace between the warring sides until this year. The coalition resumed its military campaign in Yemen in support of the internationally recognised government last month, seeking to reverse the Houthis’ advances, after the rebels moved along the Red Sea coast towards the strategic Bab Al Mandab strait.

title: 4 ways US foreign policy could change if Democrats win in November
body: WASHINGTON, USA – Nonpartisan analysts say Democrats stand a good chance of winning the US House of Representatives and possibly the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections , which would give them a slice of power in Washington after two years of Republican control. Democrats argue that Republicans have allowed President Donald Trump ‘s administration to declare war and control spending, even though the US Constitution reserves those powers for lawmakers. Here are some ways a Democratic Congress could hem in Trump’s foreign policy. Curb the Iran war Trump did not secure approval from Congress before he launched the war with Iran on February 28 , and Democrats have voted repeatedly to end the fighting unless he does so. One of these resolutions passed with support from a handful of Republicans, but Trump’s administration ignored it. With control of the House or the Senate, Democrats could cut defense spending to pressure Trump to obtain permission from Congress to continue the war. They could also require administration officials to testify publicly about their plans. Fresh support for Ukraine Trump has largely halted direct US financial and military aid to Ukraine, despite broad support from Democratic and Republican lawmakers as it fights a Russian invasion . Most recently, he has angered members of Congress, including many Republicans, by lifting sanctions on Russian diesel and waiving sanctions on Russian energy only weeks after signing them into law. With a victory in both chambers in November, Democrats would be able to decide what gets voted on and when. That could allow them to approve new aid to Ukraine, which likely would pass with the two-thirds majorities needed to overcome a Trump veto. They could also target other Trump activities. For example, Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, who could head the House Foreign Affairs Committee if Democrats win control, has introduced bipartisan legislation to block Trump’s plan to bring Russian diesel back into the global market. End military aid to Israel Support for Israel has plummeted among Democrats over its conduct in the Gaza war, which has killed tens of thousands of Palestinian civilians. The ongoing violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s close alliance with Republicans have also been factors. Democrats could limit or end military aid to Israel, which amounted to $3.8 billion in the most recent fiscal year. That is more than was provided to any other country. Must Read Obama unloads on Trump while stumping for Democrats ahead of midterms Nearly half of House Democrats voted this summer to ‌cut off aid to Israel. Some of those who voted against that effort, such as Meeks, have backed limits on providing weapons like heavy bombs to Israel. Limit military spending and restore foreign aid Democrats are far more likely than Trump’s Republicans to limit military spending. Trump asked for an unprecedented 67% increase in the military budget this year, to $1.5 trillion, but Democrats blocked it in the Senate, citing his refusal to consult Congress about the Iran war and his steep cuts to social programs. Trump has also withheld or canceled billions of dollars in foreign aid approved by Congress. Many Democrats have been angered by the cuts and say they will try to restore funding. – Rappler.com

title: Up to two billion pounds to replace the SA80 rifle
body: The programme to replace the SA80 family of weapons carries an estimated value of £2 billion including VAT, and the contract is expected to run from July 2029 until the end of March 2045, according to a contract notice published by the Ministry of Defence. The notice, issued by the National Armaments Director Group on 23 October, announces an industry day for Project GRAYBURN, which is considering the future replacement of the SA80 and the provision of associated small-arms capability for defence as a whole. The estimated value excluding VAT is given as £1,666,666,666.67, and the tender notice itself is not expected until 2 July 2027. The notice states that the authority “is at an early stage of developing the requirement and is using this engagement to inform its understanding of the market and potential delivery approaches” , and that “the scope and approach to any future procurement remain subject to further development and approval.” It adds: “This notice does not constitute a call for competition, an invitation to tender or a commitment by the Authority to commence a procurement. The Authority has not selected a preferred procurement route, delivery model, supplier, product or contractual structure.” Maria Eagle, then Minister of State for Defence, told Parliament in April 2025 that “due to the current phase of the project, we are unable to provide a formal cost estimation yet” , and said a figure would follow once the scope, timeline and complexity were confirmed. A senior defence official told reporters in July this year that the programme “is funded” while adding “I don’t think we’ve got the specific line in the document” , referring to the Defence Investment Plan, as this publication reported at the time . The notice now puts a number on it. The dates have moved as well, and a procurement pipeline notice issued by Defence Equipment and Support in January gave indicative contract dates of 2028 to 2045 and carried no value, and this publication reported then that those dates were notional and should not be taken as a commitment to enter production at that point. The start has moved to July 2029, and a date has been attached to the tender notice for the first time. The life of the weapon being replaced has stretched over the same period. Ministers gave the L85A3’s projected out of service date as 2030 through 2025 and into this year, including when Eagle told Rebecca Paul, the Conservative member for Reigate, that “the L85 rifle (‘SA80’) will be replaced over the coming decade through Project GRAYBURN” . By July officials were saying the rifle is expected to remain in service into the early 2030s. A contract starting in July 2029 and running to 2045 leaves the existing weapon carrying the load into the period the replacement is being delivered. The January notice set out five planned variants, likely built on a common lower receiver: a standard dismounted close combat rifle to replace the SA80A3, a short dismounted close combat variant, a personal defence weapon to replace the L22 carbine, a generalist rifle to replace the SA80A2 and a cadet rifle to replace the L98. Requirements listed in that notice included United Kingdom manufacture to strengthen sovereign supply chains, a possible long-term strategic supplier relationship covering delivery, support and spiral development, the ability to defeat current and emerging adversary body armour, day optics as standard with rapid acceptance of in-line night vision systems, signature reduction on selected variants and reliability across all climatic and environmental conditions. Luke Pollard, the Minister of State for Defence, confirmed in January that the programme covers the whole dismounted close combat weapons portfolio, from pistols to machine guns, and said it is “desirable for the project to create skilled employment in the UK” in line with the Defence Industrial Strategy. Answering Ben Obese-Jecty in February he said the department has “set clear expectations that Project Grayburn will be manufactured in the UK to enhance sovereign industry” , while “there is currently no specific definition for the future export potential of Project Grayburn.” The industry day will be held as a hybrid event, with organisations attending in person or over Microsoft Teams, and each will be offered a single one-to-one session of no more than fifteen minutes. Attendance is by invitation only, organisations must register by five o’clock on 30 October, and the department intends to confirm attendance by 6 November. The engagement deadline is 27 November. The notice flags the opportunity as particularly suitable for small and medium-sized enterprises, and the one-to-one sessions will not be used to evaluate or down-select suppliers or solutions. The SA80 entered service in the 1980s and has been through two major upgrades, the A2 rebuild carried out by Heckler & Koch and the A3 configuration that brought a new upper receiver and mounting arrangements. The calibre of the new weapon remains open, with performance, interoperability with allies and technological complexity among the factors under consideration, and approvals will run through the Combined Operational Effectiveness and Investment Appraisal process. The project takes its name from Lieutenant John Grayburn of the 2nd Parachute Battalion, who was awarded a posthumous Victoria Cross for his actions at the Arnhem road bridge in September 1944. The post Up to two billion pounds to replace the SA80 rifle first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Two German suspects arrested after being seen photographing entrance to Damon Prison
body: The Haifa Magistrate's Court extended the detention of the two German nationals arrested on suspicion of photographing security facilities and security-related activities near Damon Prison by 24 hours on Sunday evening. Their hearing was held behind closed doors.The two were arrested on Saturday night after being spotted near the entrance to the facility and photographing it with their cellphones, prompting the dispatch of additional prison officers, who approached the two men and conducted an initial inspection.An examination of their cellphones revealed the images, raising further suspicions about why they were at the location and why the took the photos.Following the discovery, the case was handed over to Israel Police, which launched an investigation into the circumstances of the incident.At this stage, the purpose of the photographs remains unclear, as does whether the incident involved security-related activity or whether the photographs were taken for another reason.Damon Prison is a security facility where security prisoners and detainees, including female prisoners and minors, are held.Recently, a special wing was established at the facility for dozens of defendants and detainees involved in espionage cases in recent years.Police arrest tourist who stated intent to commit terror attack at IDF's Kirya complexIn early October, N12 News reported that an American tourist was arrested outside of the IDF's Kirya complex in Tel Aviv after taking photos of the surroundings and announcing his intention to carry out a terror attack.He was subsequently arrested and reportedly sent for a psychiatric evaluation.Israel Police confirmed the arrest in its own statement, though it did not name the security site, nationality, or the reason for the tourist's arrest beyond their "suspicious" behavior at the site.

title: Russian drone strikes Epicenter shopping center in Poltava, injuring one person
body:
Vitalii Dyakivnych, head of the Poltava Regional Military Administration, reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
"In Poltava, an enemy UAV struck a shopping center. Details are being clarified," the statement reads.
He later added that a fire broke out as a result of the attack.
“Information regarding the extent of the damage is being clarified. Cleanup efforts following the attack are ongoing. Preliminary reports indicate that a 52-year-old woman was injured,” the statement reads.
As reported by Ukrinform, Russian drones damaged 25 private homes , a business, and educational and medical facilities in Poltava.

title: Mother, child die as two container trucks overturn in Lagos
body: By Efe Onodjae A mother and her child have died after two heavily laden 20-foot container trucks overturned at Mile 2, near Freeman Market, inward Apapa, Lagos. The victims were trapped beneath the overturned trucks and their containers during the incident, which occurred over the weekend. The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, said its rescue and recovery personnel responded to the scene to evacuate the victims and remove the wreckage. According to the agency, the road was temporarily cordoned off, while traffic was diverted through an adjoining service lane to ease congestion and prevent further accidents. LASTMA deployed a crane and a high-capacity tow vehicle to remove the overturned trucks and their cargoes, while officers of the Nigeria Police Force provided security during the operation. The remains of the victims were subsequently conveyed to the police mortuary in Yaba for necessary procedures. The General Manager of LASTMA, Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, expressed sadness over the incident and called for a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident. He urged relevant security agencies to determine whether mechanical defects, excessive loading, improper cargo distribution, driver negligence or other factors contributed to the incident. Bakare-Oki also called on truck operators to ensure their vehicles were roadworthy, secure their cargoes properly and comply with established road safety regulations. He stressed the need for regular vehicle inspections and responsible driving, particularly among operators of heavy-duty articulated vehicles, to prevent avoidable road crashes The post Mother, child die as two container trucks overturn in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Vulnerable residents in Malakal receive 30 land registration documents
body: A civil society coalition has handed over 30 land registration documents to vulnerable residents who lost their papers during conflict and displacement in Upper Nile State, as part of efforts to strengthen property rights and reduce land disputes. The Coalition of Civil Society on Natural Resources (CSCNR), in collaboration with Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA) and state authorities, launched an awareness campaign in Malakal to educate residents about land ownership, registration and their legal rights. The programme targeted widows, orphans, older people, internally displaced people, returnees and people with disabilities, the coalition said in a statement. Charles Judo, the coalition’s chairperson, said 30 eligible residents who had lost their land registration documents during conflict and displacement had been identified and their paperwork processed before the documents were handed over. He said the initiative aimed to improve land tenure security, prevent disputes and promote peaceful coexistence in communities affected by years of conflict. Upper Nile State, like neighbouring Unity State, has been affected by conflict since 2013, Judo said. Chukwan Philip, a director general at the Ministry of Roads, Bridges and Physical Infrastructure, welcomed the initiative and outlined provisions of the Land Act 2009 governing land acquisition, ownership and access. He said the law recognises customary, freehold and leasehold land tenure and provides for access to land for housing, cultivation, grazing and other uses, subject to legal regulation. Philip also cited Section 78(1) of the Land Act, which addresses the restitution of land rights lost through involuntary displacement associated with the civil war that began in 1983. The campaign included an awareness session attended by 44 people, including community leaders, internally displaced people, returnees, young people and women’s groups. Participants discussed land ownership, land management and mechanisms for resolving disputes. Residents seek further assistance Participants called on the coalition and its partners to extend assistance to more residents who had lost land registration documents. They also urged the ministry to reduce registration fees to make it easier for landowners to formalise their documents. Martin John, a beneficiary of the programme, welcomed the assistance but said a lack of money continued to prevent residents from building permanent homes on their plots. He called on non-governmental organisations to support house construction and clear roads in the Luakat area to improve access and security. Participants also recommended expanding land rights awareness campaigns, building shelters for vulnerable households, establishing additional police posts and providing surveying equipment to strengthen the ministry’s land administration capacity. title: NDLEA arrests US-based grandma, South African woman with large cocaine, loud shipments
body: By: Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) disclosed on Sunday that it’s operatives have arrested a 62-year-old Nigerian-American grandmother, Anetor Gloria Ubong, with 9.45kg of high-grade cannabis, loud, imported from the United States and a 34-year-old South African woman, Qhina Beauty, with 36.65 kilograms of cocaine at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos. The agency added that in separate operations across the country, NDLEA officers also recovered tons of illicit drugs in Kano, Lagos, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta states. Spokesman of the agency, Femi Babafemi said, “Qhina, the South African, was arrested at the departure hall of the Lagos airport on 7th October 2026 while trying to board a Qatar Airways flight to South Africa via Doha. “A search of her two travelling bags led to the recovery of 30 blocks of cocaine weighing 36.65kg, laced with dried pepper, wrapped in cello tape and packed into seven separate parcels. “During her interview, she told operatives she arrived in Nigeria on 30th September specifically to pick up the consignment. She said she was recruited by another South African lady, who promised her R20,000 on successful delivery. “She claimed she was introduced to two other members of the syndicate: one based in the United States and the other a Lagos-based car dealer. “Investigations later led to the arrest, on 14th October, of the 46-year-old car dealer Uchenna Victor Umunnakwe, who was intercepted at Apple Junction, Ago Palace Way, Lagos, after days of surveillance at his Shasha residence. “He admitted receiving Qhina at the airport, lodging her at Santiago Hotel in Amuwo-Odofin, and later moving her to Cynarisso Hotel near the airport, ahead of her departure. “In another interdiction operation at the Lagos airport, NDLEA officers on Wednesday, 21st October, arrested a 62-year-old grandma Anetor Gloria Ubong, a realtor based in Richmond, Texas, who holds both Nigerian and US passports. “She was arrested following her arrival on a United Airlines flight from Houston. A search of her two checked-in boxes uncovered 18 parcels of loud, a synthetic cannabis weighing 9.45kg, concealed with gift wrapping paper in a box. “She claimed the box was delivered to her home in the US by her daughter and the daughter’s future brother-in-law, for onward delivery in Nigeria to her daughter’s fiancé, Jibola. Meanwhile, operatives of a special operations unit in NDLEA on Friday, 23rd October arrested Eletu Rasheedat, 41, at Eti Osa in area of Lagos where they recovered 5,820 pills of diazepam, 780 tablets of tramadol, 3.7kg skunk and 230.25 litres of skuchies. In Delta, a suspect Peter Ugochukwu, 51, was arrested in Warri with a huge cache of pharmaceutical opioids including 29,350 capsules of tramadol; 6,620 tablets of tramadol 200mg; 4,116 bottles of codeine syrup; 11,340 tablets of Rohypnol; 3,500 tablets of diazepam; 300 ampoules of pentazocine injection, 200 ampoules of diazepam injection, and quantities of tramadol 225mg, Molly and Cocodamol. He was transferred along with a white Hummer bus from the Nigeria Police Force, Delta State. In a separate arrest at Enhere Junction, Warri, a 46-year-old physically challenged woman, Helen Bakporo Samson, was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Monday 19th October with 6.0kg of skunk. A 41-year-old suspect Fajana Dada Oluwaseyi, was arrested on Monday 19th October in Adamasingba, Ibadan, following his initial escape from arrest when NDLEA officers seized 197.8kg of cannabis sativa from his house on 16th September. The agency said a raid in Gerawa area of Kano on Thursday 22nd October led to the arrest of Murtala Lawan, 30, and seizure of 159 blocks of cannabis sativa weighing 97.2kg, NDLEA officers at the Lankaviri checkpoint, Yorro LGA, Taraba on Friday 23rd October arrested Raiyanu Misa, 39, with 95 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 60.175kg. The same day, the Nigeria Police Force handed over a suspect arrested at Dakka village, Bali LGA, with 112 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 81.49kg. In Niger state, Emmanuel Ekene, 26, was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Monday 19th October on the Sabo-Kainji road, Borgu LGA, with 64,000 pills of opioids including tramadol and diazepam, while officers arrested Jamilu Mustapha, (aka Last Card), 45, on Wednesday 21st October at Nasaru Town, Ningi LGA, Bauchi state where they seized 379kg of cannabis sativa packed in seven jumbo sacks. Acting on intelligence, NDLEA officers on Tuesday 20th October raided a farm at Board-Ala, Akure South, Ondo state and recovered 56 bags of abandoned cannabis sativa weighing 583kg. Two cannabis farms in Ugbada Forest, Uzebba, Owan West LGA, Edo state, with an estimated yield of 2,023.14kg, were destroyed on Sunday 18th October by NDLEA operatives who also burnt 450kg of processed cannabis at the site and took 97kg as exhibit. In a related operation at Ewe community, Owan West, Mary Edokhai, 42, was arrested with 35kg of same psychoactive substance. With the same vigour, Commands and formations of the Agency across the country continued their War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitization activities to schools, worship centres, work places and communities among others in the past week. These include: WADA enlightenment lecture to students and staff of Oje Grammar School, Ibadan, Oyo state; Government Day Secondary School, Kwamba, Niger state; Baptist Primary School, Olorunda, Ogun state; Government Secondary School, Yalea, Kano; Community Secondary School, Igogoro, Enugu; Urban Girls Secondary School, Onitsha, Anambra; and Kelebe Community Grammar School, Osogbo, Osun state, among others. While commending the officers and men of MMIA, Kano, Lagos, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta Commands for their vigilance, diligence, professionalism and intelligence-driven approach to the various successful operations, Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of NDLEA, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (rtd) urged them and their colleagues across the country to sustain the tempo of the war against drug trafficking and substance abuse. title: Nvidia open-sources Flora to make robot video labeling 125x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra
body:
Labeling one hour of robot video for 72 cents instead of $88 is what Nvidia promises with Flora, its open data engine. But the comparison with GPT-6 Astra isn't quite as lopsided as the price tag suggests.

Large AI models for robots learn from videos that need text annotations, and according to Nvidia's GEAR research lab, this requires three types of labels. First, descriptions of what action happens when in the video, used to select training data. Second, ratings of how well a robot progresses step by step, so it can learn through trial and error. And third, judgments on whether a task was completed successfully, used to monitor robots during deployment. Most existing tools only provide one of these types. Large language models like GPT-6 Astra can generate several, but they're too expensive for the massive volumes of video involved.

[caption id="attachment_41978" align="alignnone" width="1800"] Flora breaks videos down into time segments, describes each action, and evaluates the execution and outcome of an episode. | Image: Nvidia[/caption]

According to the paper, Flora covers all three. Nvidia says the system is already running during training of its GR00T models, annotating up to 200,000 hours of video per day across 512 GB300 GPUs. The models are available on Hugging Face.

[video width="1280" height="720" mp4="https://the-decoder.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/nvidia-flora-720p.mp4" poster="https://the-decoder.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/nvidia-flora-hero-title-1.jpg"][/video]

Flora consists of three fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models. A 9B model splits videos into action segments, and a 27B model describes them while factoring in what happened before and after each action. A second 27B model called Flora-Rewarder takes on three roles depending on the prompt. It rates an episode's success on a scale of 1 to 5, classifies each half-second step as normal, suboptimal, or failure, and assigns scores based on self-defined rubrics.

[caption id="attachment_41977" align="alignnone" width="1800"] A segmentation model and a captioning model produce timestamped descriptions, while a single reward model generates all three types of ratings. | Image: Nvidia[/caption]
Up to 125x cheaper by Nvidia's own estimates
In a test with 50 videos, Flora scored slightly better than GPT-6 Astra according to Nvidia, even though OpenAI's model was allowed to use its full reasoning capacity. Labeling one hour of video runs about 72 cents with Flora by Nvidia's estimate, compared to roughly $88.50 with GPT-6 Astra. Claude Opus 5 scored much worse in the same test and still cost about $42 per hour.

[caption id="attachment_41976" align="alignnone" width="1800"] Flora hits 57.1 percent annotation quality at $0.72 per video hour according to Nvidia, while GPT-6 Astra reaches 53.7 percent at $88.49. | Image: Nvidia[/caption]

The Flora cost figures are projections, though, not production measurements. Nvidia calculated them based on an assumed rental price of $10 per GPU per hour.
Flora finds actions better, but Astra often describes them more precisely
On the public WGO-Bench, Flora is best at detecting action boundaries but trails Astra in overall score and falls behind Gemini 3.8 Flash in pure description accuracy. According to the researchers, the gains come mainly from temporal localization.

On Nvidia's own DenseCaptionBench, Flora leads across all metrics for human recordings, but for robot videos the model comes in second behind Astra. There's a methodological catch the researchers acknowledge, too. GPT-6 Astra evaluates the descriptions while also being one of the models under test.

[caption id="attachment_41975" align="alignnone" width="1800"] Flora leads on human recordings, outcome scoring, and step-by-step ratings, while GPT-6 Astra wins on WGO-Bench, robot videos, and rubric scoring. | Image: Nvidia[/caption]
Almost no other model catches mid-episode errors
On RoboRewardBench, Flora's error rate is 27.8 percent lower than Astra's. The paper attributes the gap to partially completed tasks. When a robot only tips a bottle over instead of knocking it off the table, Flora assigns 3 out of 5 points to match the human reference, while Astra gives just one.

Flora-Rewarder catches 53.3 percent of failed steps within an episode, while no competitor gets above 11.7 percent and Astra doesn't catch a single one. The tradeoff is that Flora falsely flags about 11 percent of normal steps as errors. Astra still leads on rubric-based scoring and trajectory ranking.

In a video with many short hand movements, Flora identifies 34 of 37 individual actions, while Astra catches only four. On the flip side, Flora sometimes splits longer actions into too many small steps and occasionally gets descriptions wrong. In one video, a robot hand wipes a plate with a cloth, but Flora describes it as folding a napkin.

[caption id="attachment_41974" align="alignnone" width="1800"] In one example episode, Flora identifies 34 of 37 reference actions, while GPT-6 Astra catches only four. | Image: Nvidia[/caption]

Nvidia positions Flora as an open alternative to commercial services like Scale AI's Physical AI Data Engine. Researchers can use it to scale their own robotics datasets and test approaches like transferring human demonstrations to robots. Nvidia is investing billions in open AI models to keep developers in its hardware ecosystem and drive demand for its chips, and Flora serves that same goal.

The company has also been working for some time to offset the shortage of robotics training data through simulation and automated data processing. At GTC earlier this year, Nvidia showed a data pipeline that automatically prepares, multiplies, and scores training material. Flora adds detailed labels and reward signals from video to that pipeline.

All of this feeds into Nvidia's strategy of covering the entire robotics value chain, from hardware and training data to simulation and the AI models themselves. Google's recently announced Gemini 4 Argon targets a similar part of the robotics training process, also identifying work steps in training videos and flagging failed actions.

title: Serbia Votes as Student Movement Mounts Major Challenge to Vučić
body:
Serbia is voting on Sunday as a mass student protest movement seeks to unseat long-time populist leader Aleksandar Vučić in the biggest challenge to his rule for more than a decade.
The snap parliamentary elections, called by Vučić in September, come after almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024. The students have since gained widespread support.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Unusually long lines formed at polling stations in Belgrade and Novi Sad before the start of voting at 7 a.m. local time. Voting ends at 8 p.m. with first indications of results expected around two hours later.
A student victory would be a profound political shift in the Balkan country of some 6 million people, reminiscent of the defeat of Hungary’s Viktor Orban in April. It also potentially offers a blueprint for other student movements across Europe, which have taken to the streets in recent weeks to protest, in some cases violently, against poor education standards and a lack of prospects.
But Vučić, who resigned from his second term as president to run again for prime minister, is a strong incumbent. Many voters thank him for pulling Serbia from economic obscurity and orchestrating a period of sustained modernisation including new highways, railways, schools and hospitals.
“I came out early today because the students called us,” said Ana, 30, at a polling station in Belgrade.
Domestically, Vučić has pledged higher pensions and public sector salaries, investment in state healthcare and subsidies for young couples. On the international stage, he has balanced closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia’s traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, while leaving the door open to joining the European Union.
The students’ domestic agenda aims to root out graft and improve schooling, but they have been quieter on their international ambitions. Their list of 250 largely unknown candidates includes university professors, actors and farmers, and is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic.
Opinion polls predict a tight race. In an Ipsos poll published on Thursday, Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) is seen leading with 47% of votes versus 40% for the students. But other polls have put the students in the lead.
The student-led street protests sparked by the station disaster quickly became the biggest in a generation, calling for Vucic to step down. Rights groups and activists say repression has worsened in the period since.
Bogdan Pavkovic was one of thousands in central Belgrade for a final student rally on Thursday. He said he wants to change “this awful, horrendous system which cheats on us, which spies on us, which beats us.”
Vučić’s office and the Interior Ministry did not respond to requests for comment. Vučić and the SNS have repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents. He says the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students dismiss.
“This has been one of the most difficult but the most emotional campaigns,” Vučić told his supporters on Thursday. “We stood against those who wanted to destroy Serbia.”
Relations with the EU have frayed as the bloc has become increasingly frustrated with Serbia’s lack of reforms over the judiciary, rule of law and corruption.
In a report this month after a visit to Serbia, a delegation from rights body the Council of Europe noted the “hostile and aggressive rhetoric” against opponents.
And in September, EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the huge public funeral of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic held in Belgrade, saying it contradicted “the values underpinning Serbia’s path towards the European Union.”

title: Israel on alert for renewed attacks on Syria's Druze, security source says
body: Israel is concerned that operatives acting on behalf of the Syrian regime intend to renew attacks against the Druze population in the Sweida province of southern Syria, a security source told Walla on Sunday morning.As a result, the IAF has increased activity in the area, sending a warning to Damascus that Jerusalem will not tolerate attempts to harm its Druze allies.The security source told Walla that Israel is monitoring developments in Syria around the clock and has no intention of easing the Israeli government's policy of assisting the Druze against any attempts to carry out massacres or abductions by operatives acting on behalf of the Syrian regime, including Bedouin factions coordinated with Syrian security agencies, or by regime personnel directly.According to the source, the issue has received extensive coverage in media outlets affiliated with the Syrian regime. These outlets have accused Israel of supplying weapons, ammunition, money, and intelligence to Druze factions in Sweida province operating under the name "National Guard," allegedly to enable them to attack Bedouin tribes or Syrian military positions in the area.According to reports published in Syria, some of the equipment is being airdropped.Syria insists actions intended to establish sovereignty, not target civiliansDamascus has conveyed messages to Jerusalem asserting that its actions are intended to establish sovereignty over all Syrian territory rather than target civilians. However, Druze members of the National Guard oppose these efforts and refuse to place their forces under the command of the Syrian military.The Syrian regime views this refusal as a direct threat to the country's territorial integrity. In addition, the regime has been using Bedouin groups that are engaged in longstanding historical land disputes with the Druze.The security source said that in some cases, Bedouin groups operate independently, without coordinating with the regime's security agencies.In other cases, Bedouin groups have attempted to attack Druze communities, block supply routes, and damage water and electricity infrastructure.According to reports from Syria, including Al Jazeera, the IAF has maintained an increased presence over the Daraa and Sweida areas, particularly over the past week, deploying attack helicopters, fighter jets, and remotely piloted aircraft.

title: Augie Wins Court-Ordered APC Primary for Argungu/Augie Constituency
body: Umar Hassan Augie has emerged as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for the Argungu/Augie Federal Constituency in Kebbi State after winning the party’s fresh primary election ordered by a Federal High Court. Augie polled 33,013 votes to defeat his challenger, Samir Salihu Felande, who secured 1,319 votes in the election held on Saturday across the constituency’s 21 political wards. Announcing the results, the Chairman of the APC National Committee, Shehu Kawu Damina, said the constituency had 44,784 registered delegates, and that 34,332 votes were cast. Damina, who also served as the returning officer representing the party’s national headquarters, formally declared Augie the APC candidate for the House of Representatives seat. The fresh primary followed a Federal High Court judgment delivered in Birnin Kebbi last week, which nullified the earlier primary election and directed the party to conduct a new exercise within two weeks. The latest exercise was conducted in compliance with the court order, with Augie emerging as the party’s candidate for the constituency. The post Augie Wins Court-Ordered APC Primary for Argungu/Augie Constituency appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Why aren’t African economists winning Nobel Prizes?, By ‘Tope Fasua
body:
There are many observations around the subject of economics that African economists are better suited to understand. We could write about informality, for instance, for we have the world’s largest informal economies, products of past dislocations and distrust of imported systems of government. We could write and research around the impact of history on economies, or the paucity of data to make economic decisions. What about the calculation of domestic investment in informal economies, where capital formation at the informal level is more rapid and exceedingly more robust but largely ignored?
I had it in mind to question why there have been no Nobel Prize winners in Economics from Africa, ever. Is it because most of the economies in Africa are underdeveloped, going by the standards set by top global economies and so the Nobel committee thinks we have nothing to offer? Is it because the economies of Africa are mostly not industrialised? Or are they considered not to be complex enough? Just what does it take for economists in Africa to get noticed, and for some of their work to be taken seriously? Perhaps African economists themselves are not doing enough intellectual work, which they can put out there in top journals. Another problem could be around the fact that those same journals are involved in hard gatekeeping, which can sometimes be termed as discriminatory. African economists themselves must be daring, and articulate. They must be proud of their work too and depend less on foreign funding. A lot can even be done with little local funding in the field of Economics. I believe that what matters for global recognition, whether at the level of the Nobel Prize or other genuine platforms, is the profundity of the work that economists do.
Or maybe Africa and the global South may create their own equivalents of the Nobel Prize that recognises their work and encourages economists – we could even include other sciences – along the lines of impact and excellence. I believe we have enough private sector entities that can take this opportunity and etch their names in the annals of history just like Alfred Nobel and – for the purpose of Economics – the Sverige Riksbank (Swedish Central Bank) have done. We have successful banks, mining and oil companies in Africa – even Nigeria – that can occupy this space if, as it now seems, African scientists, and economists are not considered worthy of the Swedish Prize. But that could be termed reactionary. Let us stick to the 131 years old Nobel Prize for science, and the 58 years old Swedish Central Bank prize for economics, for now. I hope we know the importance of Economics in Africa? It affects everything. Like Lord Maynard Keynes once wrote, no field of human endeavour is beyond the contemplation and influence of an economist. So, creating awards that recognise the profundity of thought and research that inches the continent forward, or that makes a case for recognition at extant platforms, is no waste of time at all.
These thoughts came rushing back to me recently at the Bank of Industry annual economic lecture when Professor Asad Alam presented Robert Solow’s Total Factor Productivity function, which explains the part of an economy’s output that is not explained by labour and capital. I was quick to point out the fact that Nigerian scholars should be interrogating Solow’s formula to see how we can decompress the residual that is known as Total Factor Productivity – which is a larger residual for countries like Nigeria, where so many interactions and activities that lead to growth go uncaptured because of our large informal economy, and cultural differences that Solow and other Economic greats may not have contemplated. Now, this takes us back to the four factors of production that we were taught in secondary school – land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship – and which is still being taught the same way today, up to university level. In fact, some PhDs in Economics will swear by that formula till today. In previous articles, I had challenged this theory developed in the times of Adam Smith and proposed that there are other productivity functions in today’s world, which can stand on their own, and which are often more powerful than the usual land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship. These include factors such as technology, information, data, knowledge, and even now, AI. Some of these could stand alone, in terms of their impact. So, the understanding of factors of production in economics must change.
The above example is just one instance in which we can successfully challenge some economic theories using African peculiarities and experiences. There are many other instances where the kind of complexity that adds to the body of knowledge will come from Africa, and among the deluge of economists that saturate Africa, I believe there are many notable, hardworking, and smart ones who have dedicated their researches to such good causes. We have an overhang of economic shock (the sudden shift from our traditional systems to the modern system via colonisation), we have the phenomenon of slavery that emptied our population into the Caribbeans, the Americas and elsewhere (who knows what we could have been without that happening), we have our abundant resources, which has often been blamed for our legendary complacency, we have our cultures, we have espionage, the Cold War, etc, as well as geopolitics (the China-Western play), to analyse as variables when we discuss our economies and project into the future. Some of these factors are difficult to quantify and this is what makes them more fascinating and tough to explain. And if we don’t write about what makes our economies peculiar and our honest challenges at advancing our economies, certainly nobody will.
We could even research about how relatively low levels of literacy and underdeveloped political systems affect economics or conduct new research around resource dependency. The point is that we must never assume that all the research work relevant to our situation and to the study of economics have already been done, or that only non-Africans are better suited to think and postulate about peculiar issues. That will be the worst defeat that we would have conferred upon ourselves. African economists must be bold, must be articulate, and daring.
We had an example in the health sector of what I am talking about. The biggest tragedy of the COVID-19 era was how African scientists and African opinions were totally rejected, minimised, silenced, ignored, denigrated, pooh-poohed. The other day I ran into videos of African leaders fearfully agonising about how we were going to find vaccines to prevent whole populations from dying. In the beginning of the pandemic, what we had were Western scientists and leaders projecting that poverty-laden Africa was going to be the worst hit continent, after all, in their heads, we were already disease-ridden. The few who thought differently, who tried to think through the pathology of the flu or postulated about local remedies or lifestyle advantages that Africans had, were labelled as conspiracy theorists, crazies, and frauds. But by the time the world was tired and needed to move on, Africa had the lowest numbers of casualties in all the continents. A country like Nigeria had less than 5,000 deaths, even though I saw with my own eyes on TV when Mrs Bill Gates said we would have so many deaths, such that we will have to leave corpses on the streets!
