title: Xi's remarks on upholding authority, role of UN
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Saturday marked United Nations Day, commemorating the anniversary of the UN Charter's entry into force in 1945.
On multiple occasions in recent years, Chinese President Xi Jinping has reiterated China's support for the international system with the United Nations at its core, and called for upholding the authority of the United Nations, practicing true multilateralism, and observing the purposes and principles of the UN Charter.
The following are some highlights of his remarks.
At the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Xi said all countries, regardless of their size, strength or wealth, are equal members of the international community.
"Global South countries should hold high the banner of multilateralism, uphold the authority and role of the United Nations, support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency, and ensure the equal participation of all countries in international affairs," he said.
At the opening ceremony of the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance held in Shanghai, Xi said that AI is an invaluable asset that encapsulates humanity's collective wisdom.
"We should practice true multilateralism and recognize the important role of the United Nations," he said. "We should enhance alignment and coordination on AI development strategies, governance rules and technical standards, so as to form a consensus-based global governance framework at an early date to make this frontier technology better benefit humanity."
At the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus" Meeting in north China's port city of Tianjin, Xi said the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and other universally recognized basic norms of international relations must be observed comprehensively, fully and in their entirety.
"We should firmly safeguard the status and authority of the United Nations, and ensure its irreplaceable, key role in global governance," he said.
When meeting with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on the sidelines of the SCO Summit 2025, Xi said that China will always be a trustworthy partner of the United Nations.
China is willing to deepen cooperation with the United Nations, support the United Nations in playing a central role in international affairs, and jointly shoulder the responsibility of safeguarding world peace and promoting development and prosperity, Xi told Guterres.
At the conference marking the 70th anniversary of the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence held in Beijing, Xi said that in the face of new developments and challenges, "the authority and central role of the United Nations can only be strengthened rather than weakened."
"The purposes and principles of the UN Charter are never outdated, and they are getting ever more important," he said. "China advocates the vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit, and China believes in true multilateralism."

title: China's Long March legacy through Turkish eyes
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March and the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Türkiye.
Turkish scholars, students and political figures say the military odyssey offers insights into China's revolutionary history and development path, while calling for deeper cultural and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries.
The Red Army, led by the Communist Party of China (CPC), was mainly made up of soldiers from peasants' and workers' families during the Chinese revolution. Between 1934 and 1936, the army trekked roughly 12,500 kilometers to break through the encirclement of the Kuomintang forces, a journey later known as the Long March.
Murat Tamer, a Turkish scholar specializing in cultural exchanges between China and Türkiye, said the Long March deserved greater recognition in Türkiye. More than a historic march, it demonstrated the CPC's determination, organizational strength and strategic thinking in the face of formidable challenges, he said.
The great spirit of the Long March, Tamer added, could help Turkish people better understand how China overcame difficulties and forged its own path of development.
For Turkish students in China, the Long March also offers lessons that resonate with their own experiences.
Berfin Adiyaman, a master's student in applied economics at Northwestern Polytechnical University, said learning about the Long March had deepened her understanding of the importance of perseverance.
While studying in China, she has faced challenges including language barriers and homesickness. Her involvement in exchanges between Chinese and Turkish businesses, as well as her work at a logistics company in Xi'an, northwest China, enabled her to gain a closer look at Chinese society, she said.
"Whether it is a country or an individual, courage and perseverance are essential in the face of adversity," Adiyaman said, adding that she hoped to contribute to China-Türkiye economic cooperation and youth exchanges.
Yuksel Mansur Kilinc, a member of the Türkiye-China Interparliamentary Friendship Group of the Grand National Assembly of Türkiye, said China's development path has attracted attention in Türkiye, particularly its focus on common prosperity, harmony between humanity and nature, and the coordinated development of material and spiritual civilization.
Kilinc said China and Türkiye have new opportunities to deepen bilateral ties. Events marking the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations have been held across Türkiye this year, reflecting interest in expanding exchanges between the two countries.
Describing cultural exchanges as an important foundation for bilateral relations, he called for closer cooperation in the media and cultural sectors alongside economic and technological collaboration, saying such efforts could promote mutual understanding and support the long-term development of China-Türkiye relations.

title: 14 Bandits Killed As Community Hunters Foil Kidnap Plot in Katsina
body: The Katsina State Government says community hunters foiled a planned mass kidnapping in Gidan Wawo village, Kakumi Ward, Bakori Local Government Area, following a gun battle with suspected bandits that left 14 of the attackers dead. According to the government, intelligence received at about 1:28 a.m. on Friday indicated that 26 heavily armed bandits riding on 13 motorcycles were heading towards Dawan Laila Forest ahead of planned attacks on neighbouring communities. They were reportedly led by a suspected kingpin, Isiya Kwashen Garwa. Security agencies subsequently placed all operational assets in Bakori Local Government Area on high alert, disrupting the planned abduction. However, at about 1:31 p.m. the same day, the bandits attacked a private vehicle conveying four passengers from Kakumi Ward to Illela Market in Sokoto State and set it ablaze, trapping the occupants. Community hunters from Gidan Wawo were mobilised and engaged the fleeing attackers in a gun battle, killing 14 suspected bandits and rescuing three passengers alive. The incident claimed the lives of two people: 29-year-old community hunter Mohammed Ibrahim Jidda, who was killed while defending the community, and 50-year-old traveller Jamilu Lawal, the fourth passenger, who died from burns sustained in the vehicle fire. Another hunter, 25-year-old Usman Sunday, sustained minor gunshot injuries and is receiving medical treatment. Resident Urged To Remain Calm The government said intelligence reports indicated possible reprisal following the bandits’ losses. It added that countermeasures had been activated in collaboration with security agencies to prevent further threats. Commending the security personnel and community hunters for their intervention, the government said their actions prevented what could have been a devastating mass kidnapping. In a statement signed by the Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Dr Nasir Mu’azu Danmusa, the government urged residents to remain calm and vigilant and to continue providing timely, credible intelligence to security agencies. It also reaffirmed its commitment to protecting lives and property across the state. The post 14 Bandits Killed As Community Hunters Foil Kidnap Plot in Katsina appeared first on Channels Television .

title: More relief supplies allocated to quake-hit area in Xizang
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – The Red Cross Society of China has allocated additional supplies, including 50 emergency toilets, 500 family relief kits, 500 warm packs and more than 1,000 boxes of food, to the quake-hit area in southwest China's Xizang.
As of 1 p.m. Friday, 16 people have been killed and 76 others are injured following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Baqen County of the city of Nagqu in Xizang at 10:33 p.m. on Thursday.
The RCSC Yunnan Branch also dispatched a public health emergency response team to the affected areas as part of the latest relief efforts.
The RCSC previously dispatched a working team to the disaster-hit area to guide local relief efforts and allocated 3,800 sets of supplies, including family relief kits, hygiene kits, heaters, tents, jackets, folding beds and quilts.
The Western Theater Command of the Chinese People's Liberation Army has coordinated ground and air forces to assess the damage and carry out search-and-rescue operations. More than 400 service members and militiamen from the local subcommand and police have been deployed, helping relocate and resettle nearly 500 affected residents as of 5 p.m. Friday.
The theater command has also deployed military drones in the quake-hit area to conduct aerial surveys of several villages within a 20-km radius of the epicenter as well as inspections for potential secondary disasters.
As of 6 p.m. Friday, no missing persons have been reported so far following the earthquake, local authorities said.
An analysis by experts at the China Earthquake Networks Center showed that the earthquake was an extensional fracture, basically consistent with the regional tectonic characteristics.

title: China announces actions to further improve global governance
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Friday announced that China will take practical actions to help build a more just and reasonable global governance system.
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when attending the opening ceremony of the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan).
China aims to successfully host this year's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and will continue to deeply participate in and promote the UN reform, he said.
China will give full play to the role of the Group of Friends of Global Governance, said Wang, adding that the country will promote the full and effective implementation of the Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction.
He said China will promote the rectification of global human rights governance and place the right to development in a prominent position, and release its position paper on strengthening outer space governance and advance rules of governance in pace with space exploration.
China will also deepen international cooperation in artificial intelligence and establish a global governance research center, Wang said.

title: OpenAI offers discounts up to 90 percent to poach Anthropic's biggest customers
body:
OpenAI is reportedly pulling major customers away from Anthropic with aggressive discounts, and the strategy is working. Companies like Rippling, Replit, and DataCamp are shifting more of their AI spending to OpenAI, The Information reports . Rippling CEO Parker Conrad said his company boosted OpenAI's share of its coding workload from 16 to 52 percent, while Anthropic's share fell from 57 to 18 percent.
Replit switched after OpenAI offered more than 30 percent off a contract worth over $100 million a year. DataCamp CEO Jonathan Cornelissen said OpenAI's pricing cut his costs by 80 to 90 percent. A US bank with more than $7 billion in assets got its ChatGPT seats doubled to 500 employees at no extra charge, paying under $7 per user instead of the usual $20 or more.
OpenAI is partly buying market share at the expense of its own margins, but it has also achieved real price cuts through its Sol and Luna model lines thanks to more efficient models and infrastructure. Anthropic's growth slowed from Q2 to Q3 , according to an investor memo. Both companies also face growing price pressure from China, where new models by Deepseek and Kimi deliver comparable performance for a fraction of the cost. Ad Ad

title: Russian drone strikes five-story apartment building in Vinnytsia, six injured
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Vinnytsia Regional Military Administration reported this on Facebook .
Regional Governor Nataliia Zabolotna said that early this morning, Russia struck a five-story residential building in Vinnytsia with a drone. The impact caused structural damage between the second and third floors. Four apartments were completely destroyed, and cars parked nearby were damaged.
"Six people have been injured. One person has been hospitalized," Zabolotna said.
The massive attack also damaged critical and civilian infrastructure in the region, as well as private homes. All fires have been extinguished. Rescue workers are continuing to clear the rubble. More than 60 emergency personnel and 14 units of equipment have been deployed at the site.

title: Xi sends message to 2026 Global Governance Forum
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a message to the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan) on Friday.
The world is undergoing accelerated transformation unseen in a century, and the deficits in peace, development, security and governance are growing rather than diminishing, Xi said.
"I have put forward the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) to promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system and a better world," he said.
China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold the vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits, pool strength through confidence-building and tackle challenges through cooperation, Xi said.
He called for efforts to promote the implementation of the GGI to inject more certainty and positive energy into a world of turbulence and transformation, and jointly move toward a community with a shared future for humanity.
The forum opened on the same day in Xiongan New Area, north China's Hebei Province. Hosted by the Chinese People's Institute of Foreign Affairs, it is themed "Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Reforming and Improving Global Governance in a Transforming World."

title: Rubio Defends Trump Diesel Sanctions Relief as ‘Very Wise’
body:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has defended US President Donald Trump’s decision to ease sanctions restrictions on Russian diesel exports as “very wise,” stating the policy aims to boost global energy supply and stabilize international fuel benchmarks, German news outlet N-TV reported.
Speaking on the administration’s energy and foreign policy strategy, Rubio emphasized that the White House remains focused on mitigating the wider macroeconomic fallout of global conflicts on fuel prices, arguing that the temporary accommodation serves both American and international economic interests.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“We recognize the impact of this war on the global economy,” Rubio said.
“That is why I consider the president’s decision to temporarily permit additional energy supplies onto the world market to be very wise. This will benefit not only us – though, of course, it will also help the US – but it is also an important factor given high diesel prices worldwide.”
Rubio explained that increasing physical volumes of diesel fuel transiting international maritime trade routes is essential to containing price spikes that have affected transportation networks, agricultural producers, and consumer energy benchmarks across global markets.
The secretary of state’s remarks follow the announcement of a bilateral commercial diesel arrangement unveiled by the White House following an Oct. 9 telephone call between Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin .
Under the framework, Moscow agreed to deliver commercial diesel fuel onto international markets through 2027 to ease consumer fuel inflation. To facilitate the initial and subsequent shipments, the US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a temporary general license authorizing transactions involving Russian refined diesel through April 7, 2027.
The commercial arrangement was reinforced on Oct. 16, when Trump signed an executive order invoking Section 115 of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 .
The executive action waived mandatory statutory penalties – including 500 percent tariffs on Russian imports and 100 percent secondary duties on foreign purchasers of Russian crude oil and natural gas – just 48 hours before the measures were scheduled to take effect.
Rubio previously defended the statutory suspension as an analytical pause of up to 60 days to evaluate the broader economic impact of tariffs and sanctions on global markets and American domestic supply chains, pointing to dependencies among key international partners such as India’s reliance on Russian crude.
The administration’s energy accommodations have provoked a pushback from Ukrainian leadership and bipartisan lawmakers in Washington.
President Volodymyr Zelensky characterized the diesel arrangement and the executive waiver of the Graham Act as grave strategic errors that provide hard-currency revenues directly underwriting the Kremlin’s wartime budget.
Zelensky argued that retail diesel inflation is driven primarily by armed conflict in the Middle East rather than Ukrainian long-range drone interdictions against Russian oil refineries, maintaining that granting Moscow market access signals that attacks against Ukrainian civilian infrastructure carry no economic penalty.
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha similarly cautioned that lowering the cost of Russian aggression while Moscow sustains standoff missile and drone strikes against Ukraine’s power grid undermines international deterrence ahead of winter.

title: Collapse and outbreak of civil war waiting for Israeli regime
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – A set of political, economic, social, and security crises has placed the Zionist regime in a situation where the future of its internal stability has become a subject of discussion among analysts more than before.
The continuation of the consequences of the Gaza war, military confrontation with Iran, insecurity on the northern front, disputes over the performance of Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet, and the increase in military costs have raised serious questions about Zionist regime's ability to simultaneously manage internal and external crises.
The Daily Telegraph newspaper, also referring to the social and political fissures in occupied Palestine, has raised the possibility of intensified internal instability.
Political Fissure; A Crisis Beyond the Dispute Over Netanyahu
One of Israel's most important challenges is the deep disagreements among political and social currents over the nature of governance, security policies, and the manner of running the occupied territories. The dispute between religious and secular parties, the controversy over judicial reforms, the issue of military service for Orthodox Jews, and criticisms of the cabinet's performance regarding the attack of October 7, 2023, are among the factors that have made political cohesion difficult.
According to a report by the Israeli Institute for National Security Studies (INSS) in June 2026, only 25 percent of respondents had high trust in the cabinet; in contrast, 73 percent rated their level of trust as low. Also, high trust in Benjamin Netanyahu was reported at 31 percent and low trust in him at 67 percent. These figures indicate a considerable gap between the cabinet and parts of Israeli society; although they alone cannot be considered a definitive sign of political collapse.
Under such circumstances, the election result and the manner of forming parliamentary coalitions can affect the intensity of disputes. Netanyahu's competition with opponents, including the political current associated with Gadi Eisenkot, is not merely a competition over seats of power; rather, it also includes disagreement over political accountability, the future of the governance structure, and security priorities.
The Costs of War; Pressure on Israel's Economy
The economic consequences of the war are another important axis of this crisis. According to the annual report of the Bank of Israel, the financial cost of the war that began in October 2023 has been estimated at about 350 billion shekels for the years 2023 to 2026; a figure that does not include the decisions and costs related to military operations against Iran from late February 2026.
Also, Israel's public debt-to-GDP ratio rose from about 60.5 percent at the beginning of 2023 to 68.5 percent at the end of 2025. The Bank of Israel has identified military costs, civilian expenditures related to the war, and their financing through debt as important factors of pressure on the regime's financial situation.
These figures show that even if economic growth is maintained, the continuation of conflicts can restrict the regime's financial resources and increase the opportunity cost of investment in construction, education, and social sectors. However, Israel's economy still has capacities for adaptation, and one cannot speak of economic collapse merely on the basis of rising debt.
The Gaza War and the Northern Front; The Issue of Realizing Strategic Objectives
One of the fundamental questions about Israel's military performance is the possible gap between operational achievements and the realization of the political objectives of the war. Extensive military attacks and the destruction of Gaza's infrastructure have imposed a heavy human cost on the Palestinians; but assessing the strategic success of such operations is not possible merely by the extent of destruction or the number of attacks.
The continuation of the security issue, the future of Gaza's administration, and the dispute over the fate of prisoners and captives are among the issues that are important in evaluating the performance of the Israeli cabinet. The International Institute for Strategic Studies, in an analysis in August 2025, had also referred to the difficulty of the Netanyahu cabinet in converting military achievements into a sustainable political result. At the same time, this institute has also spoken of Israel's military achievements against Hamas, Hezbollah, and Iran.
On the northern front as well, the return of residents of evacuated areas and the rebuilding of economic activities have become an important issue. Reports published in October 2026 about Kiryat Shmona indicate continued security concerns, damaged economic activities, and the dissatisfaction of part of the residents. This situation shows that military operations alone do not necessarily lead to the sustainable return of security and normal life.
Confrontation with Iran; A Test of the Cost and Benefit of the Military Strategy
Direct war with Iran has been one of the Zionist regime's most important security challenges in 2026. American and Israeli attacks on Iran from February 28 were accompanied by Iran's retaliatory attacks and the expansion of the scope of war in the region. A report by the US Congressional Research Service in September 2026 shows that this war, in addition to the Israeli regime and Iran, has also affected American military bases, regional infrastructure, and commercial shipping.
According to the same report, the April ceasefire and the June 2026 memorandum of understanding could not lead to a sustainable agreement, and the conflicts resumed afterward. This process indicates the difficulty of converting military pressure into sustainable political and security arrangements.
From a strategic perspective, the main issue for Israel is not only the extent of damage inflicted on the opposing side; rather, the ability to achieve the declared objectives, maintain deterrence, manage reciprocal attacks, and prevent the expansion of war is also important. In contrast, Iran has also faced heavy human, economic, and infrastructural costs; therefore, assessing this confrontation without taking into account the costs of both sides provides an incomplete picture.
Overall, economic pressures, political disputes, the consequences of the Gaza war, insecurity on the northern front, and the costs of confrontation with Iran have placed a set of interconnected challenges before Israel. The simultaneous intensification of these pressures can reduce the Israeli regime's room for maneuver, deepen social fissures, and provide the ground for new political crises.

title: PROFILES: The men, women seeking to be Nigeria’s president in 2027
body:
T he Independent National Electoral Commission recently released the list of cleared presidential candidates and their running mates for the 16 January 2027 election.
Of the 22 registered parties in Nigeria, the commission cleared the candidates of 18 of them. The three parties without candidates are the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) and the Youth Party (YP).
While APGA and YP did not nominate presidential candidates for the 2027 general elections, the NNPP withdrew its presidential nomination during the substitution window.
Prominent among the candidates whose names were listed are President Bola Tinubu of the APC, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar (ADC), former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi (NDC), Oyo State Governor Oluseyi Makinde (APM), former Cross River State Governor Donald Duke (PRP) and former Senator Sandy Onor (PDP).
Although INEC listed 18 candidates, there are indications that it will expand the list to include the candidate of the Accord Party, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, who was cleared by the court, bringing the number to 19.
There are only two female candidates in the list: Ada Okwori of the National Democratic Party (NDP) and Esther Okereke of the National Rescue Movement (NRM).
Four women are listed as vice-presidential candidates. They are Peace Egobia (APP), Nafisat Usaku (DLA), Hanna Konto (LP), and Patience Key (YPP).
According to the list, the presidential candidates are aged between 35 and 79, while the vice presidential candidates are between 35 and 80.
The oldest presidential candidate, Atiku of the ADC, is 79, while Moses Adebisi of the DLA, 35, is identified as the youngest candidate.
PREMIUM TIMES brings you the brief profiles of the candidates.
President Bola Tinubu, 74, is seeking a second term after winning the 2023 presidential election with 8,794,726 votes.
Born on 29 March 1952, Mr Tinubu graduated from Chicago State University in the United States in 1979 and worked in accounting and the oil industry before entering politics. He was elected senator for Lagos West in 1992, participated in the pro-democracy movement during military rule and served as Lagos State governor from 1999 to 2007.
He subsequently helped build the opposition coalition that formed the APC in 2013.
Since assuming office in May 2023, Mr Tinubu has removed the petrol subsidy, introduced foreign-exchange reforms and pursued changes in taxation and public finance. His administration has recorded improvements in some economic indicators, with the World Bank reporting 4.2 per cent growth in the first half of 2026 . However, high food and transport costs continue to affect households, while insecurity persists in several parts of the country.
His personal background and financial history have also attracted scrutiny, including a 1993 United States civil forfeiture settlement involving a drug case that did not result in a criminal conviction.
Mr Tinubu secured the APC presidential nomination in May 2026 and retained Vice President Kashim Shettima as his running mate.
On 14 October, he inaugurated the party’s Presidential Campaign Council, calling on supporters to defend his administration’s record. His campaign centres on consolidating the Renewed Hope economic reforms, expanding infrastructure and improving security. The election will test public confidence in those reforms and whether their reported economic gains have translated into improved living conditions.
Atiku Abubakar, 79, is a businessman, former customs officer, and Nigeria’s vice president from 1999 to 2007. Born on 25 November 1946 in Jada, Adamawa State, he obtained a diploma in law from Ahmadu Bello University. He worked in the Nigeria Customs Service from 1969 to 1989, retiring as a deputy director.
He entered politics through the movement associated with Shehu Yar’Adua and won the Adamawa governorship election in 1998 but did not assume office, becoming Olusegun Obasanjo’s running mate instead.
As vice president, Atiku chaired the National Council on Privatisation, overseeing policies implemented by the Bureau of Public Enterprises (BPE). The privatisation programme subsequently attracted criticism over the disposal and management of public assets.
More recently, a September 2026 international arbitration ruling raised questions about a $500,000 payment to his then-wife in connection with the Mambilla power project dispute. The tribunal, however, found no evidence before it that Atiku had used his official duties to facilitate the contract award. Atiku denied wrongdoing. He contested the presidential elections of 2007, 2019 and 2023, finishing second in the last election with 6,984,520 votes.
Atiku secured the ADC presidential nomination in May 2026, defeating former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi and Mohammed Hayatu-Deen. Mr Amaechi subsequently became his running mate after withdrawing a legal challenge to the primary.
His campaign focuses on economic recovery, insecurity and electoral reforms, including a proposal for targeted support for domestically refined petroleum products. The ADC’s internal disagreements and efforts to unite opposition forces remain important challenges to his latest presidential bid.
Peter Obi, 65, is a businessman and former governor of Anambra State.
Born on 19 July 1961 in Onitsha, he hails from Agulu in Anaocha Local Government Area and studied Philosophy at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka. Before entering politics, he worked in commerce and banking, including serving as chairman of Fidelity Bank. He became Anambra governor in March 2006 after successfully challenging the 2003 governorship election result. His tenure was interrupted by impeachment and litigation before he completed his second term in March 2014.
Mr Obi’s administration invested in education, returned some schools to missionary management and promoted fiscal restraint. His claim of leaving substantial savings has remained controversial, with the Anambra government questioning aspects of his financial record , particularly outstanding liabilities. A 2021 PREMIUM TIMES Pandora Papers investigation also raised questions about his offshore business arrangements and asset declarations, which he denied violated Nigerian law.
Mr Obi was Atiku’s running mate in 2019 before contesting the 2023 presidential election on the Labour Party platform, securing 6,101,533 votes and finishing third.
He emerged as the NDC presidential candidate in May 2026, with former Kano Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate. Their alliance brings together politicians who received more than 7.5 million votes separately in 2023, although those votes cannot be assumed to transfer automatically to their joint ticket.
Mr Obi has promised to prioritise security, agriculture, manufacturing, education and healthcare, while maintaining his pledge to serve only one four-year term if elected.
Seyi Makinde, 58, is an engineer, businessman and two-term governor of Oyo State.
Born on 25 December 1967 in Ibadan, he studied Electrical Engineering at the University of Lagos and established Makon Engineering and Technical Services after working in the oil and gas industry.
He unsuccessfully contested the Oyo governorship in 2015 before winning on the Peoples Democratic Party platform in 2019 and securing re-election in 2023.
His administration abolished a ₦3,000 secondary school levy, supported the transfer of Ladoke Akintola University of Technology to sole Oyo State ownership and pursued road construction and rehabilitation projects. His government also reported increased internally generated revenue, although the relationship between rising revenue and improvements in public services requires assessment.
Mr Makinde’s presidential ambition emerged amid disagreements within the PDP, leading him to accept the APM nomination on 30 May 2026.
His running mate is Lawal Daura, a former director-general of the State Security Service (SSS), who was dismissed in August 2018 following the blockade of the National Assembly by armed security personnel.
Mr Makinde has promised to decentralise security management, improve economic governance and establish a four-year transitional Government of National Unity. His candidacy faces the challenge of translating his electoral success in Oyo State into national support through the relatively smaller APM.
Sandy Onor, 60, is a historian, university professor and former senator from Cross River State.
Born on 14 February 1966, he studied History at the University of Calabar, obtaining a doctorate in 1993. He served as chairman of Etung Local Government Area from 1999 to 2002 and subsequently held state government appointments, including commissioner for agriculture and environment. He won the Cross River Central senatorial election in 2019 and served in the Ninth Senate.
During his legislative tenure, Mr Onor served as deputy chairman of the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund and sponsored legislation, including the Advanced Healthcare Development Fund Bill.
He subsequently contested the 2023 Cross River governorship election on the PDP platform but lost to Bassey Otu of the APC, who received 258,619 votes against his 179,636. Mr Onor challenged the outcome, but the Supreme Court upheld Mr Otu’s election in January 2024.
Mr Onor emerged as the presidential candidate of the PDP faction aligned with Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike in May 2026, with Babangida Umaru as his running mate. INEC subsequently listed him as the party’s candidate, although a rival faction led by Tanimu Turaki nominated former President Goodluck Jonathan and pursued legal recognition.
Mr Onor has identified local government autonomy, rural development, employment and security as campaign priorities. The unresolved divisions within the PDP remain a major obstacle to his campaign.
Donald Duke, 65, is a lawyer and former governor of Cross River State.
Born on 30 September 1961 in Calabar, he studied Law at Ahmadu Bello University and obtained a master’s degree from the University of Pennsylvania. He served as Cross River State commissioner for finance and planning before winning the governorship in 1999 on the PDP platform and securing re-election in 2003. His administration promoted tourism through Obudu Mountain Resort, Carnival Calabar and the Tinapa Business and Leisure Resort.
While Carnival Calabar became an established annual cultural event, Tinapa struggled to attract the anticipated commercial activity and became associated with disputed financial obligations.
In September 2026, former Governor Liyel Imoke questioned liabilities inherited from the Duke administration, while Mr Duke defended aspects of the project’s financing. Cross River’s 2024 audited accounts valued its investment in Tinapa at ₦58.7 billion, an accounting figure rather than its original construction cost.
Mr Duke previously contested the 2019 presidential election on the SDP platform, receiving 34,746 votes nationwide.
He won the PRP presidential primary in May 2026, with Rabiu Kabiru as his running mate.
A Federal High Court dismissed a challenge to his nomination in September, although the defeated aspirant subsequently appealed.
Mr Duke has promised improvements in security, education, healthcare and economic management, including reducing petrol prices to about ₦300 per litre . His previous presidential result highlights the challenge of building nationwide electoral support.
Omoyele Sowore, 55, is a journalist, activist and founder of SaharaReporters.
Born on 16 February 1971, he hails from Ondo State and studied Geography and Regional Planning at the University of Lagos, where he participated in student activism. He subsequently obtained a master’s degree in Public Administration from Columbia University in the United States.
In 2006, he founded SaharaReporters, an online news organisation known for reporting on corruption, governance and human rights abuses.
Mr Sowore established the AAC in 2018 and contested the 2019 and 2023 presidential elections, receiving 33,953 and 14,608 votes respectively.
His activism, including the #RevolutionNow movement, has repeatedly brought him into conflict with security agencies. In 2019, he was arrested and prosecuted for treasonable felony, but the Federal High Court struck out the charges in February 2024 after the federal government discontinued the prosecution. He also faces a separate cybercrime prosecution over social media posts about President Tinubu, to which he pleaded not guilty.
Mr Sowore emerged unopposed as the AAC presidential candidate in May 2026, with Kano-based lawyer Haruna Magashi as his running mate. His campaign promises include a ₦500,000 monthly minimum wage, free education, one million public homes, restoration of petrol subsidies and improved electricity supply.
He estimated that the wage proposal would add about ₦7.1 trillion to the annual federal wage bill, raising questions about its financing. His third presidential bid will test whether his public prominence and political activism can attract substantially more votes than in previous elections.
Rufai Adekunle Omo-Aje, 71, is a businessman and national chairman of the Action Alliance.
Born on 15 January 1955, according to published biographical accounts, he hails from Ede in Osun State.
INEC’s candidate list records his declared qualifications as primary and secondary school credentials. His political experience has centred on party organisation rather than elected public office, and independently verified information about his business activities remains limited.
Mr Omo-Aje emerged as AA national chairman following a convention in Osogbo in 2020, but his leadership has been challenged by a rival faction associated with Kenneth Udeze. The dispute has produced competing court decisions and disagreements over which faction is entitled to represent the party. INEC subsequently recognised Mr Omo-Aje’s leadership following a court order. However, the dispute extended to the presidential nomination, with Joseph Faduri challenging INEC’s recognition of Mr Omo-Aje as the party’s candidate.
Mr Omo-Aje secured the AA presidential nomination through a consensus arrangement in May 2026, with Zamfara politician Shehu Hussaini as his running mate.
His campaign has promised improvements in security, economic management, national unity and grassroots participation. The party received 14,542 votes in the 2023 presidential election under its previous candidate, Hamza Al-Mustapha.
Mr Omo-Aje therefore faces the challenge of resolving competing nomination claims and expanding the AA’s limited national electoral support.
Aliyu Abbas, 44, is a political organiser and former aide to ex-Vice President Atiku Abubakar seeking Nigeria’s presidency on the ADP platform.
From Borno State, he says he grew up as an Almajiri pupil in Kano before pursuing further education.
INEC records his qualifications as the First School Leaving Certificate, Senior School Certificate and a bachelor’s degree.
In December 2018, Atiku appointed him Special Assistant on Youth Support Groups during his presidential campaign. Mr Abbas subsequently founded the National Youth Alliance, which reported inaugurating hundreds of coordinators across several geopolitical zones in 2026, although its claimed nationwide operational reach has not been independently established.
Mr Abbas has no documented record of holding elected public office. His political experience has centred on campaign organisation, advocacy and youth mobilisation.
He emerged as the ADP’s consensus presidential candidate at its national convention in Abuja on 30 May, with Ike Chinazam, 50, as his running mate.
INEC subsequently listed the pair among the candidates for the election.
However, another aspirant, Johnson Chukwuka, challenged his nomination at the Federal High Court in Abuja , alleging that the party failed to conduct a valid primary.
His campaign emphasises youth participation, national unity, security, education and economic development. During his nomination, he proposed deploying artificial intelligence to address national challenges, while his eight-point agenda includes food security, transport, wealth creation and land reform.
However, a detailed, independently authenticated and costed manifesto was not available by the research cut-off.
The ADP received 43,924 votes nationwide in the 2023 presidential election, approximately 0.18 per cent of valid votes. Mr Abbas therefore faces the challenge of translating his youth mobilisation activities into electoral support while defending his nomination against the pending legal challenge.
Yusuf Kabiru, 54, is the presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Party (APP), with Ofordile Egobia, 47, as his running mate.
INEC records Mr Kabiru’s qualifications as the First School Leaving Certificate, Senior School Certificate and National Diploma. However, his state of origin, professional background, educational institutions and previous political appointments could not be independently established from the public records reviewed. No reliable account was found of his participation in an earlier presidential, governorship or legislative election.
Mr Kabiru’s emergence as the APP candidate is also sparsely documented. Although the party reportedly scheduled its presidential primary for 27 May, an authenticated primary result or detailed convention report explaining his nomination was not located. His inclusion on INEC’s final list establishes his recognition as the party’s candidate but does not explain whether he faced other aspirants or emerged by consensus.
His running mate, Ms Ofordile, is among the women contesting the vice presidency in 2027, although her professional and political background could not be independently verified. Similarly, no authenticated presidential manifesto or detailed policy programme issued in Mr Kabiru’s name was located by 17 October.
The APP previously contested the 2023 presidential election with Charles Nnadi as its candidate, securing 12,839 votes nationwide , approximately 0.05 per cent of valid votes. The party recorded its highest state total in Oyo, with 1,985 votes, according to an election database . These results provide historical context but do not measure Mr Kabiru’s current electoral support. His candidacy is formally established, yet important questions remain about his professional and political experience, the process through which he secured the nomination and the policies he intends to pursue if elected.
Sunday Adenuga, 52, is the presidential candidate of the Boot Party (BP), whose name stands for “Because of Our Tomorrow”. A native of Ogun State, he holds a master’s degree in Project Management from Northumbria University and professional certifications in information technology governance, risk and security.
While he has never held public office, Mr Adenuga has been involved in the Boot Party since its formation in 2016. The party was registered by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in 2019 following a legal dispute.
He has served as the party’s national chairman since 2020 and was its presidential candidate in the 2023 election, in which he secured only 16,156 votes, representing 0.07 per cent of the total valid votes.
Mr Adenuga is seeking the presidency again after emerging unopposed in the party’s 2027 presidential primary. His campaign is anchored on the “One Working Nigeria” (OWN) agenda, drawing heavily from his professional background in IT risk and governance; he focuses on using technology, transparency, and institutional reform to solve national issues.
He is running alongside a 40-year-old Usman Mustapha.
Moses Adebisi, 35, a native of Osun State, is the presidential candidate of the Democratic Labour Alliance (DLA). He is the youngest of the presidential candidates, according to the INEC’s list.
Mr Adebisi grew up in Gbongan, in Aiyedaade Local Government Area of Osun State, where he attended his primary and secondary education. While he attended District Council (D.C.) Primary School, Oke Offa, he obtained his junior and senior secondary certificates from Olufi High School and Ayodele Citadel College respectively, both in Gbongan.
He subsequently said he obtained a diploma from the Global Distance Learning Institute in Abuja and a degree in Human Resource Management from ISCG University in the Benin Republic.
Mr Adebisi emerged as the DLA’s presidential candidate at a substitution primary held on 20 August 2026, following the withdrawal of the party’s national chairman, Samuel Memeh, who had initially been listed as its candidate.
His emergence has attracted controversy as a forum of the party’s governorship candidates withdrew their support, saying the party has no presidential candidate.
Mr Adebisi is running alongside Abubakar Nafisat, also 35. Their campaign is built around a blueprint titled “The Divine Order for a New Nigeria,” which promises structural reforms in governance, the economy and national security.
Okereke Okereke, 43, is the Labour Party’s presidential candidate. A native of Abia State, he is a legislative governance expert, policy analyst and political consultant whose work focuses on public institutions and legislative processes.
He emerged as the party’s presidential flag-bearer through a consensus arrangement among party stakeholders at a convention in Abuja on 30 May. The party subsequently reaffirmed his nomination.
Mr Okereke holds a PhD in Legislative Governance Studies from the Federal University Lokoja. He also has master’s degrees in Legislative and Democratic Studies from the University of Benin and the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies, and in Public Administration and Policy from Baze University. He obtained his first degree in accounting from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka.
He is president of ERGAF-AFRICA Legislative Governance Innovation and Policy Hub and works as a legislative consultant to committees and members of the National Assembly. He also serves as a resident lecturer in public policy and administration at Miva Open University in Abuja.
His campaign focuses on institutional restructuring and shifting Nigeria from a consumer/distribution-based model to a highly productive economy. He is running alongside Hanna Konto, 54.
Adewole Adebayo, 54, from Ondo State, is a lawyer, businessman and media entrepreneur seeking the presidency for a second consecutive election cycle under the Social Democratic Party (SDP). He contested the 2023 election on the same platform, securing 80,267 votes.
A longstanding member of the SDP, Mr Adebayo attended St Stephen Primary School and St Joseph College, where he completed his secondary education in 1989. He obtained a law degree from Obafemi Awolowo University in 1997 and was called to the Nigerian Bar in 2000.
He subsequently expanded his legal practice internationally, qualifying for the New York Bar and the State Bar of California. He holds licenses or affiliations allowing him to practice across multiple global jurisdictions, including federal courts in the US, the UK, Australia, and Canada.
In 2006, he was appointed a commissioner on Liberia’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission through the United Nations and ECOWAS. The commission was established to address the legacy of the country’s civil conflict.
Mr Adebayo also founded KAFTAN TV in 2016. The multilingual television channel operates in Nigeria and broadcasts internationally via satellite platforms.
Although he has not held an executive public office, he presents his candidacy as an alternative to the dominance of the APC and the PDP. His 2027 policy blueprint, titled “Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity”, focuses on clean government, food security, judicial independence and full employment.
He is running alongside Usman Bugaje, 74.
Peter Agada, 54, is the presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP). Born in Enugu, he hails from Ogbadibo Local Government Area of Benue State and is an architect and politician.
He emerged as the YPP’s presidential flag-bearer alongside his running mate, Patience Key, at a substitution primary held in Abuja on 21 August 2026. He replaced Anita Zugwai-Chukwu.
Mr Agada holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in Architecture from the University of Jos and a PhD in Architecture from the University of Lagos.
He previously served as a finance director in the Obidient Movement, a political support group for Peter Obi. In May 2026, he declared his intention to contest the presidency under the Labour Party, presenting himself as a potential conciliator amid the party’s internal divisions.
His bid was cut short when he was disqualified during the party’s screening exercise. Mr Agada criticised the party’s leadership, alleging betrayal, exclusion and regional bias.
He subsequently defected to the YPP in June 2026, citing his desire to pursue an economic and development agenda beyond political coalition-building.
Describing his approach as running Nigeria “like a project site”, Mr Agada says his governance model would prioritise direct labour, grassroots development and tighter oversight of public projects.
Dan Nwanyanwu, 66, is the presidential candidate of the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP). A native of Imo State, he has a long history in organised labour and Nigerian party politics.
He previously served as national chairman of the Labour Party from 2004 to 2014, during which the party expanded its national profile. Under his leadership, the party won the Ondo State governorship with Olusegun Mimiko as its candidate.
Mr Nwanyanwu left the Labour Party in February 2015 and later joined the ZLP, where he served as national chairman. He contested the 2023 presidential election under the ZLP platform, where he secured 77,665 votes, and is seeking the presidency again in 2027.
He holds a bachelor’s degree in Law, which he obtained in 1998, and a master’s degree in law from the University of Lagos.
He is running alongside Hassan Khalid, 37. Their campaign manifesto focuses on immediate national priorities, focused on fostering national unity, aggressively tackling insecurity, combating corruption through legal updates, expanding clean energy investment, and driving industrialisation.
Ada Okwori, 48, is the presidential candidate of the National Democratic Party (NDP) and one of the two women seeking Nigeria’s highest elected office in 2027. She hails from Benue State and holds a Higher National Diploma in Accounting.
Mrs Okwori is associated with grassroots political mobilisation. She previously coordinated Ward2Ward, a political support group that campaigned for former President Goodluck Jonathan’s re-election in 2015.
Her political activities also included involvement in the PDP before she moved to establish the NDP. The party’s registration followed a legal dispute with INEC. Its promoters challenged the commission’s initial refusal to register it, and the Federal High Court in Abuja ordered the commission to register the party in February 2026.
Mrs Okwori is running alongside Uchenna Chukwuemeka, 48.
Esther Okereke, 43, is the presidential candidate of the National Rescue Movement (NRM) and one of two women contesting the 2027 presidency, according to the INEC’s final presidential candidates list.
A native of Anambra State, Mrs Nkem spent her formative years and completed her secondary education in Niger State. She emerged as the NRM’s presidential candidate through a unanimous voice vote at the party’s national convention in Abuja in May 2026.
She holds a PhD and a master’s degree in International Relations, as well as a bachelor’s degree in Political Science from the University of Abuja.
She has worked as an actress and film producer and founded Kamdera Services Limited, a human resources and talent management company.
Mrs Okereke is running alongside Nasir Sulaiman, 35. Her campaign promotes what it calls the “ESTHER Agenda”, which proposes reforms in education, security, technology, housing, entrepreneurship and restitution. The agenda is presented as a response to institutional failures.
Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, 61, is a businessman, human rights activist and politician seeking the presidency under the Accord platform. Born in Kebbi State, he is known for his involvement in Nigeria’s pro-democracy movement and business interests in the energy sector.
His political activism dates to his student years, when he participated in student movements and anti-apartheid campaigns. He later became involved in national politics and was among the founding members of the Peoples Democratic Party in 1998, serving as its first deputy national publicity secretary.
He subsequently moved into opposition politics and contested the 2007 Kwara State governorship election under the Democratic People’s Party (DPP), finishing as runner-up.
Mr Olawepo-Hashim has also pursued presidential ambitions through smaller political parties. He contested the 2019 presidential election under the People’s Trust platform and has since been associated with efforts to build an alternative to Nigeria’s dominant political parties.
He holds a bachelor’s degree in Mass Communication from the University of Lagos and a master’s degree in Global Affairs from the University of Buckingham.
His 2027 candidacy under Accord became the subject of a dispute after the party’s national leadership said he had missed its nomination deadlines and that the party had not conducted the primary through which he claimed to have emerged as its presidential candidate.
However, on 5 October 2026, the Federal High Court in Abuja ordered Accord and INEC to recognise him as the party’s presidential candidate. According to the account of the ruling used for this report, the court held that the party had violated Section 86 of the Electoral Act 2026 by refusing to submit his name after the primary.

title: AI Detection Is Set to Transform Live Streaming
body:
AI in live streaming is unlocking new levels of automation, insight, and real-time responsiveness that were previously impossible. With Red5’s upcoming AI-detection service and real-time frame extraction, video content can now be analyzed, enhanced, and acted upon in milliseconds. In this blog, you’ll learn what we discussed at IBC 2025 , how Red5’s technology enables instant frame extraction across HTTP and XDN infrastructures, what new AI-driven use cases this makes possible, and how it transforms the speed and intelligence of live video streaming.
Our co-founder and CEO, Chris Allen, talked about ‘AI and the Next Wave of Real-Time Video Intelligence’ at the RTC.On conference in Poland this month. If you prefer video format, watch this recording on Youtube:
Barriers to getting the most out of AI-assisted per-frame applications tied to live-streamed A/V content are about to fall with Red5’s forthcoming introduction of a fully automated AI-detection service supporting the market’s first real-time frame extraction process.
The emergence of Generative AI supporting deep-learning Large Language Models ( LLMs ) has triggered a vast array of capabilities that can be used with the aid of hardware-accelerated cloud processing to activate streamed A/V use cases that once were out of reach. The full potential of what can be done with these tools has yet to be attained owing to the time consumed by pulling frames for AI processing.
Now, by enabling for the first time anywhere virtually instant extraction of A/V frames at any frequency down to sub-second intervals from content delivered over any supported by Red5 ingest protocol ( WebRTC / WHIP , SRT , Zixi , RTMP , RTSP ) going into Red5 Cloud streaming infrastructures, Red5 has opened a new perspective on what can be done in the live-streaming environment. The possibilities truly are unlimited, especially when combined with the capabilities unleashed by Red5’s Experience Delivery Network ( XDN ) Architecture on the Red5 Cloud real-time streaming platform.
Diagram illustrating real-time frame extraction and encoding for AI in live streaming using SRT
Some AI-related applications enabled by real-time A/V frame extraction relate to surveillance or other scenarios where there’s a need to detect specific objects or faces, variations in street and highway traffic patterns, fires and other emergency-related developments, criminal activity, and other types of developments in the live stream flow, including unwanted audio or video elements such as swear words or indecent exposure. Other applications have to do with pulling and formatting high-quality still images to capture key moments in sports competition, generate promotional thumbnails, or pinpoint defective parts in factory production, to name just some types of use cases that can benefit in ways far beyond what once could only be done by extracting screenshots from stored files.
While there are many frame-extraction solutions that have improved on the screenshot capture model, they typically lag real time by a few seconds or more, which delays the application of AI for whatever types of analysis, content manipulation and formatting are used with the extracted frames. In contrast, the Red5 solution extracts frames in milliseconds from high-latency HTTP-based streams as well as from streams delivered at real-time speeds (WebRTC typically) over XDN infrastructures implemented on the managed Red5 Cloud service.
When HTTP Live Streaming ( HLS ), MPEG-Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH) or another conventional streaming mode is involved, the post-production playout stream is delivered as usual over conventional CDNs to end users while, at the same time, the feed is ingested by the XDN Architecture for real-time frame extraction at whatever intervals users set on their Red5 extraction dashboards. In this approach, there’s no end-to-end distribution involving egress from a cloud XDN infrastructure to end users.
Instead, as dictated by the user, the extracted frames are pushed into S3 or another cloud-based object storage platform, where the user’s chosen AI mode of processing can be applied instantly to execute the relevant tasks. Depending on the speed of the AI processing, those tasks can often be completed before the HTTP-streamed primary content reaches end users, especially in cases where the streaming entity employs low-latency backend connections to the storage repositories. Moreover, the Red5 Cloud extraction process allows users to choose settings on their service portals that automate whatever transcoding and formatting is required to support their uses of the extracted frames, all in real time.
Alternatively, in instances where streamers have activated real-time streaming end to end over Red5 Cloud XDN infrastructures, there’s no need to push the extracted frames into storage. Instead, distributors can instantly apply the LLM solutions as part of the in-stream flow using AI tools that have been pre-integrated with the Red5 Cloud service or other options once they’ve been integrated through Red5’s open APIs for use on the platform. Depending on the use case, the AI-processed frames can be streamed in real time as part of the primary feed or sent separately over the XDN infrastructure to end users or whatever social media, website or other domain is used to display the output.
Critically, Red5 has taken an AI-agnostic approach to ensure the broadest range of applications are available for use cases with real-time frame extraction. As mentioned, Red5 is pre-integrating some LLM models for use on the platform and will continue doing so over time, based on our assessment of best-of-breed performance options. But, at the same time, users are free to bring other AI models into play based on our ability to integrate virtually any solution that employs open interfaces compatible with the industry standards used with our APIs.
As used here, real time refers to the fact that anything labeled as such is transpiring at latencies so low they are imperceptible, at least to us humans, in contrast to flies on the wall that perceive a millisecond as a long time. End-to-end streaming over XDN infrastructure doesn’t exceed imperceptible 250ms latencies at any distance so long as distance doesn’t push light-speed latency above that threshold, and, of course, frame extraction in just a few milliseconds meets that stipulation as well.
XDN latency parameters, which can drop into the 50-ms range when transport is limited to intra-regional distances, are unmatched by any other platform at any scale, let alone at scales into the millions of end users supported by XDN Architecture. This is because, as explained at length in ‘Keys to Optimizing End-to-End Latency with WebRTC ‘ blog, Red5 has gone well beyond the latency-reducing capabilities of WebRTC and the underlying Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) to cut latencies typically introduced by encoders, transcoding , stream mixing, multi-transport protocol ingestion and the delivery of personalized ads and content enhancements on a per-user basis.
Red5’s approach to frame extraction ensures the end-to-end latency remains very low when AI processing is employed with XDN streams. And, as noted earlier, when traditional higher-latency streaming is in play, Red5’s real-time frame extraction will enable AI processing on frames passed into storage to be conducted in tandem with or ahead of HTTP streaming latencies.
Beyond enabling the use of real-time frame extraction to support AI generation of standalone images, these capabilities will have a transformative impact on in-stream use cases wherever they’re put into play, thanks to the power of currently available AI solutions that can be programmatically applied on the Red5 Cloud platform to execute tasks at warp speed. For example:
All the capabilities stemming from Red5’s support for real-time frame extraction are made possible by the unique attributes of XDN Architecture as executed on the Red5 Cloud Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform. The full end-to-end real-time multidirectional streaming supported by Red5 Cloud is automatically implemented in accord with user requirements on the global Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), which spans 50 geographic regions on six continents.
OCI server instances dedicated to Red5 Cloud are automatically configured in hierarchical Origin, Relay and Edge Node clusters for each user based on numbers and locations of end users, streaming volume and other parameters input by users on their service dashboards. Everything that occurs on an XDN infrastructure, from how resources are configured and backed up to how they’re functionally orchestrated, is controlled by the pervasively deployed software stack comprising the XDN Stream Manager.
The architectural component serving both the users who want to perform real-time frame extraction on HTTP streams and those streaming end to end in real time over XDN infrastructures utilizes functionalities in and proximate to the Origin Nodes, where any incoming stream delivered from H.264 , H.265 , or VP8 encoders at resolutions all the way to 4K can be ingested. XDN ingestion, along with accommodating direct HLS and WebRTC streams, encompasses a comprehensive portfolio of transport modes used with playout contribution and camera feeds, including Real-Time Streaming Protocol (RSTP), Real-Time Messaging Protocol (RTMP), enhanced RTMP (eRTMP), Secure Reliable Transport (SRT), Zixi Software-Defined Video Protocol (SVDP), and MPEG Transport Stream (MPEG TS).
For streamers activating the Red5 Cloud real-time frame-extraction service on HTTP streams, it’s up to them what mode of transport they use to upload the frames to storage for AI LLM processing. In the case of users who are delivering streams to end users employing the real-time transport capabilities of RTP over the Red5 Cloud platform, the service automatically chooses whichever RTP-compatible framework is best suited to each user’s device.
WebRTC is the most used real-time streaming mode owing to the client-side support provided by all the major browsers, including Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and Opera, which eliminates the need for plug-ins or purpose-built hardware. Alternatively, if a mobile device with built-in client support for RTSP is receiving the stream, the platform transmits via RTSP. The client-optimized flexibility of XDN architecture also extends to packaging ingested RTMP , MPEG-TS and SRT encapsulations for transport over RTP when devices compatible with these protocols can’t be reached via WebRTC or RTSP.
In all instances involving HTTP- or XDN-based streaming, the Red5 Cloud frame-extraction service employs Red5’s unique cloud-hosted real-time transcoding process to deliver extracted frames in whatever resolutions and bitrate profiles users choose on the service portal. Our real-time Cauldron stream processor running on OCI commodity servers employs our native code modules or Brews to initiate and configure stream scaling and compression resources through a Multiple Independent Re-encoded Video (MIRV) processor.
These MIRV-configured resources allow us to decode and split a received asset for recompression into multiple bitrate profiles at negligible contributions to latency. By building our software transcoder from scratch rather than relying on FFMPEG or third-party solutions we’ve shaved hundreds of milliseconds off the typical latency performance using CPUs without additional hardware acceleration.
We’ll be posting many more details about the new Red5 Cloud real-time frame extraction and AI support service as we move to commercial launch, including listing of the compelling LLMs we’ll be integrating at the outset for specific use cases. At this point we can share that service availability will be facilitated by its inclusion as a Red5 Cloud application in the Amazon Marketplace.
But, there’s no need to wait in preparations for the official launch. Feel free to get started now by contacting us at [email protected] or scheduling a call.
