The UAE Foreign Ministry said the ministers discussed issues of mutual concern and ongoing efforts to strengthen security and stability while promoting development and prosperity in the region and internationally.
The available official accounts, however, did not disclose a joint position on any particular regional conflict, nor did they identify specific security commitments or a coordinated diplomatic initiative emerging from the talks.
A meeting alongside intensified India-US and India-UAE engagement
The Mumbai trilateral meeting took place amid a wider round of diplomatic engagement involving all three countries.
Rubio was in India for a visit that included discussions with Jaishankar on advancing the India-US strategic partnership. Their bilateral agenda covered trade, energy, technology, defence, people-to-people ties and regional developments. Both sides also highlighted energy security and defence cooperation.
The trade relationship was an important part of the wider discussions. Washington and New Delhi have been seeking to move forward with a trade agreement after negotiations encountered difficulties over tariffs and other economic differences. During his Mumbai talks, Rubio said the two countries were close to concluding an agreement, although the trilateral meeting itself was not reported to have produced a trade deal.
In parallel, Sheikh Abdullah held separate bilateral discussions with Jaishankar to review India-UAE cooperation under their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. The bilateral agenda included trade, investment, education, culture, technology and regional and international developments.
These parallel engagements gave the trilateral meeting a broader diplomatic context. India was able to pursue its bilateral priorities with Washington and Abu Dhabi while also exploring areas in which cooperation among all three could yield additional benefits.
The distinction is important: bilateral agreements and negotiations remain the principal channels for many areas of cooperation, while the trilateral format offers an additional platform for addressing shared interests that cross national and regional boundaries.
Strategic significance for India
The meeting’s importance lies less in any single announcement than in the opportunity to connect three substantial bilateral partnerships through a common agenda.
First, it gives India another avenue for pursuing energy security and economic resilience. Engagement with both the US and the UAE can help New Delhi explore a wider range of commercial, technological and investment opportunities without making trilateral cooperation a substitute for its established bilateral relationships.
Second, the meeting reinforces India’s diplomatic engagement with both Washington and Abu Dhabi at a time when economic security, technology and regional stability are increasingly interconnected. Maintaining constructive relations with both partners gives New Delhi scope to cooperate on common priorities while retaining the flexibility to address its national interests independently.
Third, the talks highlight the growing importance of the Gulf as a link between the Indian economy, Western markets and wider international supply chains. The UAE's role as an energy producer, investor and logistics hub makes it a natural partner in discussions involving India and the US.
Finally, the emphasis on trade, investment, technology and AI suggests that the three governments see opportunities to broaden their engagement beyond traditional diplomacy. Turning these opportunities into measurable outcomes, however, will require sustained follow-up by officials, businesses and relevant institutions.
From diplomatic dialogue to practical cooperation
The immediate outcome of the October 20 meeting was an exchange of views rather than the announcement of a new trilateral agreement. The public statements identified a broad set of shared priorities but did not outline a timetable for follow-up meetings, a formal implementation mechanism or specific joint projects.
The test of the engagement will therefore be whether the three governments can translate the discussion into tangible progress in energy cooperation, trade and investment, technology partnerships and regional connectivity.
For India, the trilateral format offers a useful supplementary channel for advancing its economic and strategic interests with two important partners. For the US and the UAE, it provides an opportunity to work with a major Asian economy on issues that extend across energy markets, technology and regional commerce.
The Mumbai meeting did not establish a new strategic bloc, nor did the official statements suggest that the three countries intend to coordinate their policies across every regional or international issue. Rather, it demonstrated an interest in identifying practical areas of convergence while preserving their individual bilateral relationships and wider diplomatic priorities.
The broader significance of the meeting will ultimately depend on implementation: whether the shared emphasis on energy security, connectivity, trade, investment and technology leads to concrete initiatives that strengthen economic links and contribute to regional stability.

title: Poison for profit: Why fake drinks are killing Nigerians and what must change now, By Chukwuemerie Uduchukwu
body:
The war against fake and counterfeit products cannot be left to NAFDAC alone. Manufacturers must invest in secure packaging and rapid verification tools. Traders must refuse to stock goods of doubtful origin. Consumers must demand proof of authenticity and report irregularities. Lawmakers must pass the necessary statutes, and enforcement agencies must receive the resources to sustain operations beyond individual raids. Only a coordinated effort across these groups can shrink the space in which counterfeiters operate and restore confidence in the everyday items that sustain households.
The recent surge in counterfeit and fake drinks and consumables across Nigeria has reached alarming proportions, as confirmed by successive enforcement operations that uncovered vast networks of the illicit production and distribution of these goods in major commercial hubs in the country. In Lagos, officials of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) discovered more than twenty illegal stores hidden within the International Trade Fair Complex, where operators blended and repackaged popular alcoholic brands, revalidated expired and unsafe beverages, and stockpiled banned imports on a massive scale. The haul exceeded ₦2 billion in value, with two suspects arrested amid equipment including drums, filters, heating devices, labels, corks, and bottles of whisky, wine, and energy drinks.
Parallel actions in Aba targeted five shops at Old Court Road Market, seizing counterfeit labels, corks, packs, and outer packaging materials worth hundreds of millions of naira that bore the names of well-known brands such as Jameson, Glenfiddich, Four Cousins, Lord’s Dry Gin, and Imperial Blue. A separate facility at Omenazu Street revealed an unhygienic setup for manufacturing spirits and herbal liqueurs, complete with a 200-litre drum of liquid ethanol stored in large containers, dirty sieves, sealing machines, tree barks, and bottles already marked with established labels. These discoveries form part of a broader weekly haul exceeding ₦5.3 billion in seized and destroyed counterfeit products spanning drinks, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, and food items. The pattern is clear: organised syndicates treat the health of the public as a commodity to be diluted, adulterated, or poisoned outright for profit, thereby flooding markets with products that can cause organ failure, chronic illness, or sudden death.
What drives individuals to pursue this murderous trade remains difficult to comprehend. The same people who mix industrial alcohol with flavourings, or who repackage expired stock under fresh labels, live in the same communities where their products circulate. They shop in the same markets, attend the same gatherings, and share the same water and food chains. Nothing shields them or their relatives from the very toxins they unleash. A child who drinks a counterfeit soft drink, a relative who takes a falsified medicine, or a friend who consumes adulterated spirits can die from the very enterprise that was meant to enrich the perpetrator. Greed appears to override even basic self-preservation. The calculation seems to rest on the assumption that the victims will always be strangers, the enforcement will always be temporary, and the profits will always outweigh the risk of detection. Yet, the raids demonstrate that the risk is real and growing. Traders who resisted evacuation of seized materials in Aba only underscored how deeply the trade has embedded itself, turning ordinary markets into nodes of organised harm.
Capital punishment for those who knowingly manufacture, package, or distribute fake drinks, foods, or medicines would signal that the state places the lives of citizens above the profits of syndicates. Such legislation would also equip investigators with stronger tools for asset forfeiture and for prosecuting financiers who never touch the products themselves but bankroll the operations.
The National Assembly must respond with laws that treat the counterfeiting of consumables as a capital offence. Existing penalties have proven insufficient to deter large-scale operators who calculate that fines or short prison terms are merely a cost of doing business. When the product itself can kill, the law should recognise the act as equivalent to premeditated harm against the public. Capital punishment for those who knowingly manufacture, package, or distribute fake drinks, foods, or medicines would signal that the state places the lives of citizens above the profits of syndicates. Such legislation would also equip investigators with stronger tools for asset forfeiture and for prosecuting financiers who never touch the products themselves but bankroll the operations. Delay only allows the networks to reorganise after each raid, relocating equipment and recruiting new fronts, while the public continues to bear the cost in hospital admissions and premature deaths.
The same legislative urgency applies to product authentication. The National Assembly should enact laws requiring NAFDAC to adopt systems already used by sister agencies in other countries. Every manufacturer selling products in Nigeria must include a barcode or pin code concealed beneath a scratch-off panel on the packaging. Consumers should be able to verify authenticity freely through both the manufacturer’s website and the NAFDAC portal, receiving immediate confirmation that the item is genuine and within its approved shelf life. Some pharmaceutical companies have already introduced comparable technology, proving that the infrastructure is feasible and that consumers respond when given a simple means of self-protection. The majority of companies marketing drinks, foods, cosmetics, and other consumables have not followed suit. This gap leaves the market open to counterfeiters who simply copy packaging without any corresponding digital trail. The present moment offers the clearest opportunity for action. Enforcement operations have exposed the scale of the problem, public awareness is rising, and the technical capacity exists. National Assembly members and the NAFDAC leadership can close the loophole by making the scratch-off code mandatory for all regulated products sold within the country, with clear timelines for compliance, and penalties for non-adherence.
The lives already lost or damaged by adulterated drinks and consumables make clear that half-measures will not suffice. The country can either tolerate a trade that treats public health as expendable or it can mobilise every available institution and citizen to end it. The choice will determine whether the next generation inherits markets filled with safe products or continues to navigate a terrain of hidden poisons.
While these measures take shape, ordinary Nigerians must protect themselves through deliberate purchasing habits. Products of any kind should be bought only from reputable stores whose ownership and supply chains can be traced. Medications, in particular, must be obtained solely from registered pharmaceutical outlets staffed by licensed professionals. Street vendors, informal markets, and unverified online sellers present the highest risk of receiving adulterated or expired goods. Checking packaging for signs of tampering, unusual pricing, or missing regulatory marks provides an additional layer of caution, yet the most reliable defence remains the choice of where to buy. Families can further reduce exposure by limiting bulk purchases from unknown sources and by reporting suspicious products or production activities directly to the relevant authorities. These steps do not replace systemic reform, but they reduce immediate harm, while stronger laws and authentication systems are put in place.
The war against fake and counterfeit products cannot be left to NAFDAC alone. Manufacturers must invest in secure packaging and rapid verification tools. Traders must refuse to stock goods of doubtful origin. Consumers must demand proof of authenticity and report irregularities. Lawmakers must pass the necessary statutes, and enforcement agencies must receive the resources to sustain operations beyond individual raids. Only a coordinated effort across these groups can shrink the space in which counterfeiters operate and restore confidence in the everyday items that sustain households. The lives already lost or damaged by adulterated drinks and consumables make clear that half-measures will not suffice. The country can either tolerate a trade that treats public health as expendable or it can mobilise every available institution and citizen to end it. The choice will determine whether the next generation inherits markets filled with safe products or continues to navigate a terrain of hidden poisons.
Chukwuemerie Uduchukwu writes from Abuja, Nigeria. He can be reached via [email protected]

title: Musk claims Ukraine violated Starlink terms of service, 'Flash' responds
body:
That is according to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty , Ukrinform reports.
According to the SpaceX owner, Ukraine had allegedly used Starlink for such strikes, and the relevant capability was restricted last week.
In a post on social media platform X, Musk stressed that "Starshield, a different system, is controlled by the U.S. government." At the same time, he pointed to the key role of the satellite network for Ukrainian troops.
"Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is not a threat, it is simply a statement of fact," the billionaire said, adding that SpaceX "has done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth by far."
In response, Ukrainian presidential advisor Serhii Beskrestnov, known by the call sign "Flash," said : "It is very strange that Elon Musk is unaware of the restrictions on Starlink operations in Ukraine."
He recalled that since February 2026, all Starlink terminals over Ukrainian territory, including the occupied areas, "have been subject to a movement speed limit of 70-90 km/h."
Starlink does not operate over Russian territory.
Therefore, Beskrestnov stressed, Ukraine is physically unable to use commercial Starlink for deep- and medium-range strikes.

title: ‘Israel needs a dramatic change’: Northern voters turn against Netanyahu
body: A “dramatic change” is needed in Israeli politics , which includes removing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from government, people living in northern Israel have told The National days before the country goes to the polls. Those who spoke included senior officers and soldiers who have been on active duty in Lebanon, who are angry over the damage caused by Hezbollah to the ecomomy and to Israeli communities. They called on Mr Netanyahu to take responsibility for the security failures of the October 7, 2023 attacks. After nearly 20 years in office his time was over, critics said, especially in view of the right-wing coalition that had, in their eyes, caused the country great harm. “For me, this is one of the worst coalitions that we have ever had in Israel,” said Eyal Dror, a lieutenant-colonel reservist in the army who just returned from a tour of Lebanon. “I pray and hope that there is a new government which makes this a very important election,” he said, speaking in Kibbutz Dafna, near the northern town of Kiryat Shmona. He believes a new government is needed to rebuild the country’s economy, especially in the north where nearly 70,000 people were evacuated for almost two years after a war with Hezbollah that followed the Hamas-led attacks on Israel. Opposition leaders Gadi Eisenkot and Naftali Bennett were “very professional people who might lead us to that road”, Lt Col Dror said. A voter for the left-wing Democrats Party, Barry Praag, also from Kibbutz Dafna, said a coalition government was inevitable but it was vital for the new government to work with the Israeli-Arab parties to address the Palestinian question. “I have no problem with the Democrats sitting with the Arab parties. It is a very complex problem but it must be tackled. We must face the idea of a two-state solution with the support of the surrounding Arab countries otherwise, it won’t work.” He added that Mr Netanyahu had "a lot to answer” for and that the “buck stops with him”. Lior Shelef, speaking at Kibbutz Snir, which is only about a kilometre from the Lebanese border, was on military operations in the north for much of the last three years. He was still unsure who he would vote for – a position he believed was shared by many Israelis – but said the country certainly needed a new government. “Israel needs a change, and I think this change should be very dramatic. There are quite a lot of things in the country now, the economy, the religious people not going into the army, that need to change dramatically.” Anyone who was part of government on October 7, 2023 should “be honest enough to say it’s time for change and understand it”, he added. Hezbollah threat To many in the north, the Hezbollah threat has not disappeared, and they fear that the Iran-backed group across the border in Lebanon is biding its time to attack again. Lt Col Dror stated that for the Lebanese government to “get their own country back they need to do some more against Hezbollah” but it was only Israel that “can make them weaker”. But like many in the north, he said he wants to live in peace so that tourism can return, the economy can be revived, and his children can be educated. “As long as I have to send my son to the school, which is 600 metres from Lebanon and Hezbollah have the ability to fly a drone across the school I'm not feeling safe,” he said. While he hoped that the politics and diplomacy of a new Israeli government might achieve that, he did not dismiss the possibility of further military action. Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv on Saturday night as part of the latest anti-government demonstration, with protesters calling for an inquiry into the failures surrounding the October 7 attack. Mr Eisenkot, the main rival to Mr Netanyahu, was greeted with cheers and chants from the crowd at the rally. Mr Netanyahu has refused to set up a commission of inquiry into the attack, arguing that it would be biased against his government.

title: Fasoranti’s Death: Why reconciliation in Afenifere will be difficult — Okurounmu, ex-Secretary
body: •Group’s future uncertain —Mogaji Adejumo By Dapo Akinrefon Tongues across the country are wagging over a possible leadership crisis within the once formidable pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, especially with the demise of its leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti . Fasoranti died on Tuesday at the age of 100 years. Before his death, the Yoruba group had been engulfed in leadership crisis. It is instructive to note that Afenifere hinges on a traditional, non-competitive succession process to choose its next leader. However, the body faces the critical task of unifying its historically fractured factions. While the old guards like Chief Olu Falae express hope that a new leader will emerge seamlessly through ancestral custom, key insiders paint a much bleaker picture of the group’s future. How division set in In 2023, its then Acting Leader, late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, rocked the boat by suspending two of its officials, the National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi and National Organising Committee, Abagun Kole Omololu. The suspension, however, led to a split and worsened the crisis. Both officials were removed from office and subsequently suspended for alleged uncouth activities and issuance of unauthorised statements, as well as constant denigration of the organisation. Recall that in November 2022, the late Afenifere leader, Pa Fasoranti, insisted that he remained the leader of the group. This was after he had named his deputy, late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, as the leader of the organization. Pa Adebanjo, who was taken aback over Fasoranti’s suddenly change of mind, had alleged that there was an attempt to split the organisation. Observers of events in the polity were of the view that he was not far from the truth. The split, however became a reality. It was as a result of the fact that during the 2023 electioneering campaign, then candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Asiwaju Bola Tinubu had visited Pa Fasoranti in Akure, where the former Lagos State governor was endorsed. The decision did not sit well with the Adebanjo group. How Fasoranti stepped down in 2021 It will be recalled that in March 2021, Pa Fasoranti stepped down as Afenifere leader, citing old age. While Adebanjo had endorsed Peter Obi, who was presidential candidate of the Labour Party, LP, the Fasoranti group, threw its weight behind Tinubu. Fasoranti had named the deputy leader, Chief Ayo Adebanjo, as the acting national leader of the group, while the former financial secretary, Oba Oladipo Olaitan, the Alaago of Kajola Ago in Atakumosa East Council Area, Ilesa, Osun State, was named the group’s deputy leader. Fasoranti had said: “The development became necessary as the group needs, more than ever before, to have an improved organisation with a more effective approach to combat the monstrous invasion of our culture and pride as a people. “Only a more alike and active leadership can achieve this. At 95 I am hardly able to provide such and so it is time for me to step aside. “At this junction, I am proud to announce Chief Ayo Adebanjo, a politician of the Awolowo school of thought, as Acting leader of Afenifere and Oba Oladipo Olaitan, the Alaago of Kajola Ago in Atakumosa East Local Government Area, as the Deputy Leader.” The late Afenifere leader, in a viral video had claimed: “I am still the leader of Afenifere. Afenifere has not endorsed Obi, we are endorsing Jagaban (Bola Tinubu) for the presidency. “You can see the trend, the approval and the acceptability. You could see what happened when Tinubu came to meet me in Akure. The media carried the whole thing. “Adebanjo cannot warn me not to welcome Tinubu. Can he do that successfully? “What happened was that Adebanjo took a stand and I took a stand. I didn’t call him and he didn’t call me. We never spoke about the visit. “As you can see, Jagaban is accepted and we approve of him. Obi has no stand in our mind at all.” Adebanjo counters Fasoranti But in a swift reaction, Ayo Adebanjo, known to be a staunch Awoist, faulted Tinubu’s visit to Pa Fasoranti, saying the comments trailing it were aimed at dividing the group. Adebanjo, who earlier endorsed Peter Obi, said: “Nothing is going on other than an attempt to split Afenifere to which I will not be a party. “It is a sort of conspiracy among those who want to see Afenifere divided. They have been on this plan for over a month ago and my members came to me to alert me about it and I said, ‘Don’t talk about it. It would be a diversion. All we want now is an election on issues.” He said Pa Fasoranti had called to inform him about Tinubu’s planned visit adding that the former Afenifere leader was initially not open to receiving the APC candidate but he persuaded him to do so. Adebanjo had said: “I will tell you the story and I won’t go further. Pa Fasoranti phoned me on Friday that Tinubu had phoned him and that he wanted to come and see him and he wanted to say no. I said no, don’t do that, you are an elder statesman. If he wanted to see you, why not? “As far as he is concerned, Obi’s endorsement is based on the principles of equity as the South-East has not produced a president since the return of democracy in 1999. Since the South-West and South-South have produced the president, he said it is the turn of the South-East. “South-South has had its own and I said it is remaining the South-East.” Adebanjo died and the once formidable Yoruba body became polarized. But with Fasoranti’s death, both camps are still laying claim to the leadership of the group. Falae speaks However, a former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Chief Olu Falae, dismissed concerns about a possible succession struggle in Afenifere, saying the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation has a tradition of producing leaders without contests or internal fights. Falae, who is now a monarch, rules out the possible division within the Yoruba fold. He said Afenifere was a self-perpetuating and self-regulating organisation in which leadership emerged through an established process rather than through competition for positions. “Leadership chooses itself. A new leader will emerge without any struggle. “It is obvious who the next leader will be, and I hope and pray it will be so this time,” he said. Is reconciliation a tall order? Vanguard was reliably informed that before Fasoranti’s death, there was underground moves to bring all Afenifere member under one roof. For instance, it Chief Sola Ebiseni, who was the General Secretary of the Adebanjo camp, had crossed over the Fasoranti camp. A senior Afenifere leader had confided in Vanguard that the reconciliation was to be unveiled immediately after the 2027 general elections. However, with Fasoranti’s demise, this may be turn out to be difficult to achieve. ‘No light at the end of tunnel’ Providing his perspective on the crisis and possible reconciliation, a former National Secretary of the Yoruba body, Senator Femi Okurounmu, said he does not see light at the end of the tunnel as far as reconciliation in Afenifere is concerned. Okurounmu, a former Senator from 1999-2003, said though it was too early to talk or reuniting the group, the two factions cannot be reconciled. In a chat with Vanguard, the former lawmaker said: “You see, it is difficult. Things are difficult. It is very difficult to unite the two groups. The Akure group supports Tinubu. You cannot criticise Tinubu in the presence of the Akure group.” Speaking further, he said: “Everything Tinubu does must be supported. That is the philosophy of the Akure group. “The Adebanjo group is very critical of Tinubu. That is an irreconcilable difference, and that is why the two groups cannot be reconciled.” Origin of crisis – Adejumo Giving his perspective on the crisis in Afenifere, Mogaji Gboyega Adejumo, a former Public Relations Officer of the body, traces the origin of the crisis. Adejumo, who is also the Gbonka Aare-Ona Kakanfo, said Afenifere’s future remains uncertain. Tracing the origin of the crisis within the fold, he said: “What happens to Afenifere after the departure of Pa Fasoranti? All I can say is that Afenifere lost its glory some time back. Perhaps it is as long ago as 2008, and I will explain. The momentum of the Afenifere as at the moment that the June 12 episode became a national movement, which Afenifere spearheaded by forming NADECO, the ascendancy of Afenifere was assured. “So it wasn’t in any way surprised that in 1999 Afenifere formed the Alliance for Democracy, AD, and the AD was able to sweep at least, all the southwest states. But that momentum faltered in 2003 due to so many reasons. “However, in 2008, when Pa Abraham Adesanya, who was not only Afenifere leader, but the leader of the Yoruba, that was proclaimed by every Yoruba group, apart from the fact that Afenifere leaders have always been known as Yoruba leaders, but Pa Adesanya enjoyed that, which was the spoken word of every other group appointing him as Yoruba leader. “So Pa Adesanya had suffered a stroke, and he felt it was time to anoint a new leader. As at that time, the foremost leaders were Pa Ayo Adebanjo, who actually started with them in 1951, and then there was Sir Olaniyun Ajayi, and the whole idea was Pa Adesanya asking the two of them to choose one among themselves. “So that he can then proclaim the choice of the two of them as the new leader. But Pa Adebanjo felt that, as at that time, Pa Adesanya, who was an Ijebu kan, who took over from Pa Adekunle Ajasin, who was from Owo in Ondo “And it just happened, there was nothing like Ijebu mafia, it just happened that Pa Ajasin and Pa Adesanya, and the mightier than the image of just a knighted man, somebody that was well loved, that is Sir Olaniyun Ajayi, they were all Ijebu; at least to that effect we could say that Pa Olaniyun Ajayi too, from Remo, is Ijebu.” How Fasoranti took over from Adesanya Mogaji Adejumo also spoke on how Fasoranti emerged of Afenifere and how the late Adebanjo convinced Adesanya to make him (Fasoranti) the leader of the group. He said: “So Pa Adesanya felt another Ijebu man to succeed Pa Adesanya might look like a reality, perhaps an accentuation of the idea that there was an Ijebu mafia. So he now suggested that Papa Fasoranti should be the new leader. Pa Adesanya didn’t quite even remember who Papa Fasoranti was. “Papa Fasoranti was the Commissioner for Finance during the time of Papa Ajasin as Governor of Ondo State, but he was not a member of the caucus of the Afenifere, and neither was he a participant in the struggle that followed after the June 12 1993 election, in which case Papa Fasoranti was not part of the Afenifere that fought for this democracy. He had more or less like retired from politics. So it was hard for Papa Adesanya to even remember him, let alone see him as the right kind of person. “But Papa Adebanjo went on to convince him that he is a very cool-headed man, and after all that happened between 2003 and 2008, quite a lot happened, because the Governor of Ondo State then, who campaigned on the platform of the AD in 2023, broke away and the Afenifere went into some serious crisis. It started from 2001 when Uncle Bola Ige died, mysteriously and unexpectedly. So what Papa Adesanya felt was that we needed a user-friendly leader, very cool and unassuming, somebody who will be able to pull everybody together, and they will support him. “And besides, he was older, joined the Afenifere in 1953 as what they called the Action Group Mosquito. As at that time, he was a student in the university, so he was recruited by Papa Adesanya himself. Anyway, that was how Papa Fasoranti was made the leader of the Afenifere, which eked Asiwaju Bola Tinubu, who was not even part of the Afenifere at that time, but had some influence here and there. There was even this Afenifere Renewal that had his signature all over it, but yet he was still interested in the leadership of the Afenifere. So, he went ahead and announced the late Senator Ayo Fasanmi as the leader, as against Papa Fasoranti. “And all of that happened. Papa Fasoranti, for about a year or more, was not even holding the Afenifere meeting at Akure. “In the tradition of the Afenifere, the leader becomes the rallying point, and meetings would be held in the leader’s house, and which means everybody should go to Akure. “Well, they started even at Ijebu Igbo for a while, and moved to the home of Sir Olaniyun Ajayi. “So it was, I should think, I should think, Professor Bolaji Akinyemi, who even suggested that, look, the leader is Papa Fashononji, and his home is Akure, why should we be having the meeting here? So somehow, that sank in, and then the meetings now moved to Akure. But in the true sense of it, Afenifere leadership has always been very energetic, very eloquent, and ready to engage anyone intellectually and forcefully to work on principles. And Papa Ajayi too was like that. “He gave late Sani Abacha some serious trouble, and even when he died, Abacha wouldn’t just have someone to come and preach. So it was Papa Ajayi who formed NADECO. And then Papa Adesanya, oh, well, a lawyer of note, he represented Papa Obafemi Awolowo everywhere. “And then, of course, he was a Senator in the Second Republic. He was yet in the same mould of the kind of leaders Afenifere have been able to produce. So he was just like Obafemi Awolowo and Papa Ajayi. “But by nature, his passion was not that kind of a Afenifere ready to fight, ready to carry the placard, ready to engage any one kind of leader. So that, again, would make the Afenifer to be a bit vulnerable and not to be as forceful, as pushful as Afenifere has been known to be. And sometime in 2015, Papa Ajayi actually wrote a letter and said he was resigning. “He didn’t want to carry on again as the leader of Afenifere. He was overwhelmed, really. The opposition came from everywhere and just couldn’t handle it. “And you won’t blame him because some are made very strong, some are mild-mannered. And he’s one of those mild-mannered, never-really-wanting-to-cause-any-trouble kind of gentlemen. So, but it was Pa Ayo Adebanjo again who said, no, you can’t just leave. “You won’t just succumb to pressure. Those who want Afenifere to die will really be happy if you suddenly just up and left. So he convinced him to stay on.” Afenifere’s rebirth under Fasoranti “And, yes, Afenifere went through some rebirth under Papa Fasoranti. He started to attract new members, too, and started to evolve as yet an offshoot of the original Action Group. They became involved in the 2019 elections. “From the 2015 elections, when Afenifere fully supported former President Goodluck Jonathan. Don’t forget that in 2014, there was the CONFAB organised by the Jonathan administration, which Afenifere had every signature of theirs in the preparation, the setting up, and even the exercise of having a conference of that nature happen. “Afenifere was there. It was well put together. That is, the framework was put together by Dr. Femi Okurounmu of Afenifere. “And co-chaired, well, Professor Bolaji Akinyemi was once a very active Afenifere member, was one of the co-chairs. So Afenifere rebirth, or let me say renewal and renaissance took place even at that time. Because when Afenifere had all the governors, yes, Afenifere was very solid. “But from 2005 to 2013, those were very trying years for Afenifere. But Afenifere was good to come together again. And in 2017, Baba Adebanjo called everybody and said, everything we said would happen with Buhari have started to manifest. “So what do we do? So Afenifere, by our tradition and principles and all that, is seen as a national movement. But then national movement with a particular principle, the Awolowo principle, which is so difficult for just anyone to pick up. So we decided we’ll pull in other Yoruba groups. “And many groups showed up, maybe about 70 or so, but 42 were chosen. And then we launched the Yoruba Summit Group. And that was how we came by the Yoruba Declaration of 2017. “I was made the National Policy Secretary of the Yoruba Summit Group. And that was when we even invited every other group in the Middle Belt Forum from the Southeast, the Ohanaeze Ndigbo, and from the South-South, the PANDEF. And we came together and formed the Southern Middle Belt Leaders Forum, SMBLF. “So all of this happened during the time Baba Fasoranti himself was thinking of, well, resigning. But he was buoyed, he was kept on by Baba Adebanjo and a few others, Chief Supo Shonibare and the rest, that, no, you go on. We will continue to fight. So all of this happened during Baba Fasoranti’s time. And in 2021, that was when the, would I say it was just some kind of innuendo, some, well, I wouldn’t know where it came from, that Baba was going senile. “And he moved against those who wanted to take an advantage of what they felt would make Anthony Ferry’s leadership come their way. So that was when Baba Fasoranti now decided, look, it’s time for me to truly bow out. And he made Baba Adebanjo the acting leader. “I wouldn’t know what exactly that meant. And then see Oba Oladipo as the deputy leader.” Vanguard News The post Fasoranti’s Death: Why reconciliation in Afenifere will be difficult — Okurounmu, ex-Secretary appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: VIDEO: Shooting at Florida State University, dozens injured
body: TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Shooting at Florida State University in Tallahassee has left several people reportedly wounded, prompting a campus-wide security alert. At least 12 people, including six minors and an 11-year-old, were injured in the incident.

title: Iran's 7-day plan set on Hormuz not yet conveyed to US side
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Iran has presented no new offers to the Pakistani mediator on reopening of the strategic Strait of Hormuz., categorically rejecting media claims that Iran has presented new proposals to the Pakistani mediator on the strait.
An informed source has said that Tehran’s existing seven-day plan outlining its conditions for reopening the strategic waterway was already conveyed to the Americans.
The source described reports by the Saudi news outlet Al-Arabiya as “a lie and fabrication,” consistent with what the source called the “quasi-media outlet’s” pattern of false reporting on Iran.
The Al-Arabiya reports alleged that Iran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the lifting of the US maritime blockade.
“Iran does not accept any arrangement based on the equation of the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the blockade,” the source said.
Tehran is instead circumventing the restrictions through its own methods and will ultimately break them, the source added.
The informed official emphasized that Iran’s seven-day plan, which includes Tehran’s demands for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, had previously been transferred to the American side through mediators.
Until all of Iran’s demands are met, one of which is the removal of disruptions to Iranian ports and shipping, the insecurity imposed by the American enemy in the Strait of Hormuz will not be eliminated.
“The whole world knows very well that the cause of insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz is the aggressive and interventionist actions of the United States,” the source stated. “For this reason, stopping these illegal actions is a common demand of the countries of the region and the world.”
The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding was reached in June after the US-Israeli aggression that began in late February. The agreement had called for an end to hostilities on all fronts, the lifting of the illegal US naval blockade on Iranian ports, restoration of commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and subsequent negotiations on other issues.

title: El Clasico: Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid look to spring a surprise at Camp Nou
body: Jose Mourinho returns to El Clasico on Sunday as his Real Madrid side take on Barcelona at Camp Nou, looking to close the gap on their fierce rivals at the top of La Liga. Barca have enjoyed a sensational start to the season, winning nine out of nine in the Spanish top-flight – scoring 39 goals in the process – including a 5-2 win at Real Betis last weekend. Madrid, meanwhile, hammered Sevilla 4-1 at the Bernabeu, which saw Kylian Mbappe score twice, lifting Mourinho's side to within a point of second-place Atletico Madrid, but still seven behind Barca. Mourinho, who will manage in his first Clasico since returning for a second spell as Los Blancos manager during the summer, will be without suspended attacker Vinicius Junior for a match in which his team are undoubtedly the underdogs. “The people who thought a week ago that Barca could thrash us still think the same now,” said the Portuguese, whose team defeated RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday to maintain their 100 per cent start in the Uefa Champions League. “I don't think that view will change. The fact that people speak highly of Barca doesn't affect me. To be honest, there are matches in which they obviously deserve plenty of praise because they do some very good things. “In our case, we're viewed as a finished product. Finished products are difficult to achieve in football. If you talk about us at an advanced stage of the process, we've been working for three months. If you exclude preseason and the international break, we've been working for a month and a half. Far from being a finished product, we're at the very beginning of the process. “Our manager is still getting to know the team, analysing things and establishing his approach. The players are still getting to know me, too. I don't think it's fair to compare a team like ours with one that has been together for longer.” Barcelona suffered their first defeat of the campaign on Tuesday when they lost to Champions League holders Paris Saint Germain 4-2 in a breathless clash at the Parc des Princes. “It was a fantastic game from both teams,” said manager Hansi Flick in Paris. “We made a few too many mistakes in possession. We have to analyse the game, but I also saw a lot great things. It was a great test for us today. We've seen what things we need to do better, and that's what we'll do. “What we've done over the last few weeks has been incredible. The attitude, the quality. We tried to play how we want to play, we pressed them very high. There were a lot of fantastic things on show today.” And now Flick's attention will be turned to Madrid and their wily coach, Mourinho, who will almost certainly relish being the villain of the piece for Barca fans. “I have a lot of respect for him,” said the German. “When you’ve managed for so many years and had so much success, it’s a testament to his talent. “When I was [Joachim] Low’s assistant, I met with him in Madrid. Every player who played under him speaks of him with great respect. He’s a colleague, and a very successful one at that. “They have players with great quality in the final third,” he added when asked about the threats his team will face from Mourinho's side. “They’ve shown that in recent matches. We have to be careful and prepared. “For us, the important thing is our positioning, with and without the ball. We need to maintain good distance between the lines and be compact. “This is important when playing with a high defensive line. [defenders Pau] Cubarsi and Gerard [Martin] are having a great season and they complement each other well; they are growing together.” While Barcelona's array of attacking talent in the likes of Lamine Yamal (eight goals and six assists), La Liga top-scorer Raphinha (12 goals and three assists) and summer signing Anthony Gordon (one goal and four assists) have been hogging the headlines, it was another recent arrival – midfielder Rodri from Manchester City – who has provided a bedrock for those forwards to blossom. “We always look at ourselves and the impact he has on Barca,” said Flick. “When the opportunity arose to sign him, we were all convinced he would improve us. He was a piece to take the next step,” he said. “We’ve seen that in the first few matches. I’m very happy he’s here. Alongside Pedri, there’s great quality in midfield. We’re all happy with him.”

title: Oil Spill in Delta: When environment is destroyed from within and without – black tide ‘swallows 216 communities’
body: By Egufe Yafugborhi The water at Odidi struggles to flow. It sits, thick, black, and dead. For seven months, the 28-inch Trans-Forcados Pipeline at the Kantu-Odidi axis, Warri South-West LGA has bled crude and associated gas into the creeks. What was sighted February 19, 2026 as a single rupture has become a black tide that has swallowed over 216 communities, according to their leaders. This is no longer just an oil spill. It is a war of narratives about who is destroying the Niger Delta — from within, or from without? On one side, the Joint Investigation Visit, JIV, of February 20-21, 2026, conducted by the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency, NOSDRA, officials and community representatives, gave a technical verdict: Corrosion and equipment failure. No sabotage. On the other side, voices from inside the Niger Delta say the truth is more uncomfortable. That Odidi has been a hub of illegal bunkering for 25 years and that hot-taps have turned the pipeline into Swiss cheese. Between those two truths, the environment dies. Seven months of nothing Odidi Federated Community is angry because containment has been a theatre. Comrade Justin Gbenekama, Chairman of the community, narrated: “This spill occurred on the 19th of February 2026, and up to this moment as we speak, the operator, Heritage Energy Operational Services, HEOSL, has not done anything properly to contain the spill. “As you can see within the environment, even their recovery activities is not effective.” He measured the scale of tidal spill: “And so six hours flow from this point, you get to Escravos area. And where we are standing is just five minutes drive to Forcados River, 10 minutes to the Escravos Bar. So the spill has spread very far.” For the people, the consequences are immediate. Drinking water is contaminated with hydrocarbons. Fishing and farming are dead. Cooking is a risk. Gbenekama added: “And most importantly, there is no medical attention to any of the affected communities. And even relief materials that were brought were not adequate.” He called the recovery method futile: “They will scoop, take it (spilled crude) back to their station in Isoko and inject it back to the same line, and the oil here will still come out in this point. That is an exercise in futility.” His demand: “There should be immediate shutdown of the Trans-Forcados Pipeline and carry out the complete repair before operation will commence.” It is a demand backed by law. Because the JIV ruled out third-party interference, HEOSL bears absolute liability under Nigerian environmental law. The operator must fund 100 percent of clean-up and compensation. And the Federal High Court in Port Harcourt, in Suit No. FHC/PH/CS/132/2026, HRM Udogri Isaac I v. Heritage Energy & NOSDRA, ordered a mandatory injunction to cease discharge and clean up all impacted ecosystems. No more business as usual Ijaw Youth Council, IYC, says it has had enough. Its President, Dr. Doubra Collins Okotete, led youths to threaten total shutdown of OML 42, OML 30 and the Forcados Terminal. “Today we are here not for jokes, but to shut down the operations of the Heritage Oil and Gas Services. This spill has been on for over seven months. The operators of Heritage are heartless, wicked,” Okotete declared. He dismissed the sabotage argument: “This is not sabotage. This is pure equipment failure. And we all know this oil activity has been going on for a very long time. “And this pipeline has been damaged for over six, seven months, yet no tangible has been done.” He alleged: “All they do is to employ contractors to come and curtail oil, yet the contractors they have employed could not contain this oil because, what as the community chairman said, they come here scoop the oil, take it back to their station, inject it back to the same Trans-Forcados Pipeline, and this oil keep popping out, destroying our ecosystem, creating health hazard for our people.” Okotete linked Odidi to the wider Niger Delta crisis, including Bille in Rivers State: “The same thing is happening to Alakiri, Rivers State, same thing that happening to Bille, Rivers State, and other communities across the Ijaw nation that are being threatened, that today life expectancy has dropped.” His message to Abuja was blunt: “President Tinubu, you are the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. The Minister, Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, this is under your watch and today our river has been bastardized.” And to the companies: “If they are tired of exploiting our oil, they should leave our environment.” Uncomfortable truth from within But long-time environmental monitor and Coordinator, Niger Delta Peace Coalition (NDPC), Zik Gbemre, offers a counter-punch that many in the creeks do not want to hear. He said Odidi’s black tide is also self-inflicted. “The Odidi axis in OML 42 has served as an active hub for illegal bunkering for over 25 years. What is happening there today is not a new development”, Gbemre said. “The ongoing environmental degradation is largely artificial and directly tied to pipeline sabotage. “Even after comprehensive cleaning and proper remediation, fresh spills reoccur within days because the root cause remains unchecked.” According to him, the pipeline is being killed by repeated hot-taps: “What is unfolding across the Odidi and Egwa fields is the direct impact of illegal bunkering operations. “Repeatedly placing hot taps on the same pipeline segments severely compromises structural integrity over time. “Even when damaged points are clamped and repaired, the weakened metal around the hot taps continues to deteriorate, making future leaks inevitable.” Gbemre, who has flown with Shell’s spill team over Odidi, said complicity is local: “A total stranger cannot enter a community, transport heavy equipment, and place hot taps on high-pressure pipelines without the knowledge, authorization, or passive approval of host community leaders and influential actors.” He listed it clearly: “Illegal bunkerers: Physical installation of hot taps, line breaching, and crude siphoning. Host Community leaders: Granting access, and providing cover.” His warning is moral: “You cannot destroy infrastructure, profit from illegal trade, and present yourself purely as an innocent victim. “You cannot demand millions in cleanup funds while harboring the very individuals who will re-break the pipes tomorrow.” He also punctured the IYC claim that surveillance by Tantita and others has ended vandalism: “It’s funny to hear the IYC boss claiming ‘no more vandalism in the operations space because TANTITA and other surveillance contractors are securing the space. “That is joke of the year and media gymnastics to justify sustenance of the multi-thrillion naira surveillance contracts. Oil theft still thrives.” Both sides in order Media consultant and Coordinator, Journalists for Just Development of the Niger Delta, Austine Aghomi, says both narratives must be held together to understand the ticking bomb. “Yes, NOSDRA is bound to do its work without bias when there are eventualities, just as oil and gas operators need to take responsibility on routine maintenance of their assets, particularly ageing pipeline from failure,” Aghomi said. He added: “What is equally concerning, however, is the realisation that unrestrained assets vandalism, particularly tapping into oil wellheads, flowlines and pipelines to steal crude oil now helps to hasten the ageing of pipelines beyond manufacturers’ set lifespan. “The lines suffer repeated cuts from oil thieves. Over time, assets operators get overwhelmed by repeated repairs and ultimately forced replacement earlier than normal.” Heritage Energy, through its Community Relations Manager Jeremiah Oharisi, told protesting women: “Heritage is more than willing to do the right thing.” But trust is gone. The pipeline is 50, its life was 25 The hard fact remains. Most trunklines in the Niger Delta, including Trans-Forcados, were laid in the 1970s with a 20-25-year design life. They have done double that, battered by corrosion outside and hot-taps inside. Whether the cause is rust or bunkering, the effect is the same: Odidi is dying. And if Odidi is not clamped permanently, if Bille’s gas leaks are not stopped, if the Trans-Forcados is not replaced, the black tide will come to the next community. The environment is being destroyed from without by ageing assets and corporate negligence. And it is being destroyed from within by an illegal economy that feeds on the same pipes. Until both are stopped, no clean-up will be final. Vanguard News The post Oil Spill in Delta: When environment is destroyed from within and without – black tide ‘swallows 216 communities’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: France faces new wave of nationwide protests
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said that nearly 1,000 people were arrested in France during demonstrations on Saturday, on the second straight weekend of mass protests.
Nearly 1,000 people have been arrested across France during Saturday's demonstrations over rising living costs and poor education standards, with the figure expected to rise, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.
He urged operators to be ready to suspend access to platforms including TikTok, Instagram, and X in the event of what they call violence during Yellow Vests protests, Anadolu Agency reported.
Around 410,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday, according to the Interior Ministry, while the CGT trade union put the nationwide turnout at 800,000.

title: iPhone Duo buyers complain of cracks and display failures after just days of use
body: Apple is facing complaints of damaged screens on its newly launched iPhone Duo , with some early buyers reporting cracks and display failures only hours after using the company’s first foldable smartphone. Images shared on Reddit appear to show damage concentrated around the hinge of the device’s inner display, with vertical cracks running down the centre and bright lines extending across the right side of the screen. Some affected devices also reportedly have dead pixels, raising concerns about the durability of the foldable display, which is one of the phone’s biggest selling points. The complaints come as the iPhone Duo officially goes on sale, following strong pre-order demand that saw initial stocks sell out rapidly and delivery dates for some customers pushed into next year. The Duo's prices in the UAE range from Dh8,499 to Dh13,599, and there are extended shipping times due to overwhelming demand. Dang these iPhone Duo screens can't be fixed til January! 😂💀💀💀 pic.twitter.com/ZsZX5l42mp — TexasTSLA (@TexasTSLA) October 24, 2026 Apple has reportedly been providing replacement devices to some affected customers despite limited retail inventory. However, a customer who received a broken Duo in the US said in a post on X that T-Mobile said it couldn’t replace any parts for the Duo until January. The iPhone maker is also reportedly planning to send damaged units to its engineering teams in California for examination to determine what caused the failures and whether changes are needed in future models. However, the extent of the problem remains unclear, and it is not known whether reports of broken Duo screens indicate a widespread manufacturing or design defect. The complaints add to the challenges Apple faces as it enters a foldable smartphone market already occupied by Samsung and Google, both of which have several years' experience developing devices with flexible displays.

title: Denis Ten Memorial Challenge: How Tournament Keeps Olympic Champion’s Legacy Alive
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ALMATY – When Denis Ten became Kazakhstan’s first Olympic medalist in figure skating, winning bronze at the 2014 Winter Games in Sochi, he showed a generation of young athletes that they could compete with the world’s best. More than a decade later, a tournament established in his memory is helping turn that ambition into opportunity, bringing international competition to Kazakhstan and giving emerging skaters a chance to develop on home ice. Photo credit: Aziz Erkebulan. The Denis Ten Memorial Challenge was created to carry forward the work of one of Kazakhstan’s most celebrated athletes. Beyond commemorating his achievements, the tournament seeks to strengthen professional figure skating in the country, support young athletes and foster connections within the international skating community. The event is organized by the Denis Ten Foundation, a public foundation established in 2018 to preserve the skater’s legacy, continue his projects and support young athletes and creative talent. Since 2019, the foundation has organized the memorial tournament, with Denis’s mother, Oksana Ten, serving as its president. Denis Ten’s mother, speaking at a press conference. Photo credit: Aziz Erkebulan. “On behalf of Denis’s dream, this international tournament was organized. Its goal is to develop professional figure skating in Kazakhstan and popularize this wonderful sport,” Oksana Ten said in 2025. From an Olympic breakthrough to a platform for young skaters Denis Ten’s achievements helped put Kazakhstan on the international figure skating map. He won his first major international title at the 2008-2009 ISU Junior Grand Prix event in Belarus, becoming the first Kazakh skater to win an International Skating Union competition. He was 16 at the time. His progress had begun even earlier. At 12, he competed against senior skaters at the Kazakhstan Championships and won. In 2013, he earned silver at the World Figure Skating Championships, followed by bronze in 2015. His Olympic bronze medal in Sochi in 2014 was a historic first for Kazakhstan. Ten was also known beyond the rink for his artistic interests, language skills and commitment to learning. His career demonstrated how an athlete from Kazakhstan could reach the highest levels of international sport while building a broader cultural and intellectual life. The Denis Ten Memorial Challenge continues to inspire the next generation of figure skaters in Kazakhstan. Photo credit: Aziz Erkebulan. His death in 2018 was a profound loss for Kazakhstan and the international figure skating community. The memorial foundation was established that year to ensure his projects and ambitions would continue beyond his lifetime. The tournament that followed became one way to put that commitment into practice. Rather than limiting the memorial to an annual tribute, the foundation created an event where young skaters could compete against international opponents, gain experience and develop their skills without having to travel abroad for every major opportunity. Why the tournament matters for Kazakhstan International competitions play an important role in developing athletes. They allow skaters to test their preparation against competitors from other countries, perform before international judges and audiences, and build the experience needed to progress through the sport’s competitive levels. The Denis Ten Memorial Challenge is part of the ISU Challenger Series, an international circuit for senior skaters that offers competition between national events and the Grand Prix series. Results from eligible competitions contribute to the ISU World Standings, helping athletes build their international rankings. The series also gives Kazakhstan an opportunity to host high-level skating and bring the international figure skating community to the country. Challenger events must meet ISU requirements for participating countries and disciplines, placing them within a broader international competition structure. According to the organizers, the growth of the memorial tournament has coincided with the development of new figure skating schools and the establishment of a figure skating academy in Kazakhstan. Domestic competitions with international participation have also given Kazakhstani athletes more opportunities to earn ISU ranking points on home ice. The significance of that development became especially visible with Kazakhstan’s success at the 2026 Winter Olympics, where Mikhail Shaidorov won gold in men’s singles. His achievement marked a major milestone for the country’s figure skating community and brought renewed attention to the importance of sustained athlete development. Oksana Ten reflected on that progress, noting the growth of the sport in Kazakhstan and the country’s Olympic success. “I realized how necessary this tournament is for Kazakhstan. You can see how much the number of figure skaters in our country has grown, both in quality and quantity. We finally have Olympic gold. This is a huge achievement not only for our country; the whole world admires it. That is why I think holding this tournament is worthwhile,” she said during a press conference ahead of the tournament’s 2026 edition. The memorial has also welcomed skaters who later achieved international recognition. Over the years, its winners have included Shaidorov, Russian skater Petr Gumennik, Belarusian skater Viktoria Safonova and Japanese figure skating legend Daisuke Takahashi. Their participation has helped connect younger competitors with athletes at different stages of their careers. Held in Almaty and Astana over the years, the tournament has featured singles skating and ice dance, as well as pair skating in some editions. Its broader purpose remains consistent: to create opportunities for athletes to compete internationally while strengthening Kazakhstan’s figure skating community. The 2026 edition brings together more than 20 countries The eighth Denis Ten Memorial Challenge took place at Halyk Arena in Almaty from Oct. 7 to 10, bringing together around 150 athletes from more than 20 countries. Senior and junior athletes competed in six categories: Junior Men, Junior Women, Women, Men, Junior Ice Dance and Ice Dance. In women’s singles, Alexandra Ignatova won gold with 226.01 points. South Korea’s Kim Yu-jae took silver with 209.20 points, while Kazakhstan’s Sofia Samodelkina claimed bronze with 204.36 points. Vladislav Dikidzhi won the men’s competition with 312.79 points, followed by Gleb Lutfullin with 277.23 points and Petr Gumennik with 261.76 points. In ice dance, Finland’s Juulia Turkkila and Matthias Versluis took gold with 191.32 points. Vasilisa Kaganovskaya and Maxim Nekrasov finished second with 187.20 points, while the United States’ Caroline Green and Michael Parsons won bronze with 180.37 points. For Samodelkina, the atmosphere in Almaty was an important part of the experience. The participant in the 2026 Winter Olympics and silver medalist at the ISU Grand Prix event in Osaka said the crowd’s support gave skaters an additional source of energy. “The audience applauds so loudly that you feel as if you’re on a whole different level. They give you incredible energy and strength, and that helps you skate,” she said. Remembering Denis Ten through sport and art The memorial’s purpose extends beyond competition. Each edition also creates space to remember Ten’s personality, artistic interests and influence on those who knew him. The highlight of the 2026 event was the gala show, “The Ice That Remembers,” which brought together competition medalists, invited skaters and athletes from the Denis Ten Academy. The program combined figure skating with music and aerial acrobatics. Marie-Pierre Leray, a French figure skater and longtime friend of Ten, took part in the show. She had also performed in the “Denis and Friends” program in 2013. Vocalists Daniil Yun and Sanat Asuat presented songs dedicated to Ten’s memory. The evening also featured a specially composed tournament anthem, an AI avatar of the skater and excerpts from his poetry. The Denis Ten Memorial Challenge continues to serve two connected purposes: honoring an athlete whose achievements changed the history of figure skating in Kazakhstan and creating opportunities for the next generation to pursue their own ambitions. The event is organized by the Denis Ten Foundation, with the assistance from Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Tourism and Sports, the Almaty city administration and Samruk Kazyna. The post Denis Ten Memorial Challenge: How Tournament Keeps Olympic Champion’s Legacy Alive appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: US intelligence agencies aware of Zelensky’s embezzled billions — Russian lawmaker
body:
MOSCOW, October 25. /TASS/. Vladimir Zelensky’s shift in rhetoric on claims to Russia’s historical territories is apparently linked to his fear of losing his embezzled assets, which are known to US intelligence agencies, lawmaker Viktor Vodolatsky told TASS.
Zelensky previously stated on Fox News that Ukraine was ready to accept a peace deal involving the loss of some of its territory, while retaining 75%. However, he had previously ruled out any discussion on the ownership of territories lost by Ukraine.
"Only the US intelligence agencies could have radically changed Zelensky’s rhetoric. They have clear, verified information about Zelensky's whereabouts and the location of the billions he has stolen. Some European politicians are now saying that Zelensky is the richest man in Europe, with a fortune estimated at several billion dollars. All of his accounts are under the control of not only the UK, but also the US. They calmly explained to him that if he continues to challenge [US President Donald] Trump, all of his stolen assets will be seized by the US," the lawmaker noted.
At the same time, London’s policy toward Russia remains unchanged, Vodolatsky pointed out. "London will delay intervention until a certain point, just as it did with the very first working group in Istanbul, when [former UK Prime Minister] Boris Johnson arrived and completely changed the situation, forcing Ukraine to back out of the agreed-upon terms. The same situation could repeat itself here," Vodolatsky emphasized.
Only a change in power in Kiev can alter the situation, the lawmaker noted. According to him, Ukraine’s new leader should not be another pro-Western figure.
Earlier, Crimean State Council Chairman Vladimir Konstantinov told TASS in an interview that Zelensky’s personal fortune is estimated at nearly $5 billion. He is unofficially considered the richest person in Ukraine and one of the wealthiest in Europe. According to Zelensky’s official 2025 asset declaration, which was reviewed by TASS, his family's total assets exceed $1 million, including $595,000 in cash. The remaining funds are distributed across various bank accounts, including one in Zurich with 346,483 euros.

title: Before the Philippines even had a name, it had gold
body: Gold is a patient metal. It does not rust or decay. It can be melted, worn, used, and reused from one generation to another, surviving long after the hands that first fashioned it have turned to dust. And more than a thousand years ago, long before these islands were called the Philippines, our ancestors were already working gold into exquisite ornaments, delicate chains, and elaborate vessels. Some of these treasures have survived to the present day; in them, we see a glimpse of a civilization nearly forgotten. Their rediscovery was a golden accident. On a sunny April day in 1981, Edilberto “Mang Berto” Morales was operating heavy machinery for a government irrigation project in Surigao del Sur. Something glistened in the mud. What he mistook for a helmet turned out to be a partly crushed gold bowl. Suspecting more, he shooed away his coworker and searched alone, combing some 300 feet of earth until late afternoon. By day’s end, he had recovered around 22 pounds of ancient gold, including an extraordinary necklace he called kuwintas ni nanay (mother’s necklace.) He hid the long chain around his waist, beneath his shirt, away from curious eyes. Now in the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) collection, it consists of 12 individual kamagi necklaces joined end to end, their intricate links resembling one woven cord. Photo from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas But the treasure began to scatter almost as soon as it emerged. Treasure hunters recovered more gold, dispersing objects among collectors and separating pieces of the same ornament. Then-central bank governor Jaime Laya and collectors Leandro and Cecilia Locsin helped preserve significant portions, which entered the collections of the BSP and Ayala Museum. Must Read ‘Holy grail’: Juan Luna’s lost masterpiece revealed after 132 years Bahandi sa Atong Kagahapon Florina Capistrano-Baker, the scholar behind the newly launched book Bahandi , calls the two collections as “twins separated at birth.” “They preserve different parts of a shared history and even different parts of what was once one object,” she said on Thursday, October 22, during the book’s launch at the BSP. In 2024, selected pieces were reunited at Ayala Museum, where the exhibition is scheduled to run until 2027. And what a magnificent history they reveal. Ancient goldsmiths mastered techniques involving minute golden beads, delicate filigree, and interlocking chains so precise that the finished jewelry could resemble cloth. “Even today, they cannot [recreate] some of it,” historian Ambeth Ocampo told Rappler in an exclusive interview, saying that ancient Filipinos possessed such a sophisticated understanding of gold that they even had distinct terms for its purity, including 24-carat and 20-carat gold. Gold also proclaimed status. The wealthy could wear numerous chains around their necks, with some ornaments so heavy that their wearers were said to stoop beneath their weight, BSP Deputy Governor Bernadette Romulo-Puyat recounted in a separate interview with Rappler. Yet these were more than displays of extravagance. PAST. Florina Capistrano-Baker tells the crowd about the treasures that help us understand what a pre-colonial Philippines was like. Photo by Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler “These are not just splendid ornaments. They’re evidence of social stratification, craft specialization, technical knowledge, and affluent individuals who had the means to commission these luxury goods,” Capistrano-Baker explained. The treasure also points toward ancient Butuan, whose communities traded across the seas long before Spanish colonization. Their surviving goldwork bears influences shared with Java and other parts of South and Southeast Asia, suggesting a world of exchange far richer than conventional colonial histories might suggest. For Ocampo, the gold offers a rich rebuttal for Filipinos raised on histories that often begin with the arrival of foreigners. “When you look at this gold jewelry, you realize that once upon a time we had a golden age,” he told Rappler. “So it gives you a sense of pride, gives you a sense of what was pre-colonial culture.” At the launch of Bahandi , BSP Governor Eli Remolona likened the generations who made, discovered, and preserved the treasure to links in a kamagi . “May future generations find their place in the chain and ensure it never breaks,” he said. – Rappler.com Must Read [Time Trowel] The precolonial Filipino you’re looking for never existed

title: Serbia to hold early parliamentary elections
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Early elections to the National Assembly (unicameral parliament) will be held in Serbia.
The Republic Electoral Commission has registered 6,451,292 voters who will elect 250 lawmakers to serve four-year terms.
Polling stations will open at 7:00 a.m. local time (6:00 a.m. GMT) and close at 8:00 p.m. (7:00 p.m. GMT). According to the REC, more than 16,000 observers, including 622 foreign observers, will monitor the voting process.
The ballots will feature 18 electoral lists. The main contenders are expected to be the United Serbia list of the ruling Serbian Progressive Party, led by Aleksandar Vucic, who stepped down as the country’s president on September 27, and the Student List coalition.

title: About 63% of Germans support maintaining or increasing military aid to Ukraine
body:
This is according to a ZDF-Politbarometer poll published on the website of German broadcaster ZDF, Ukrinform reports.
"Solidarity with Ukraine remains strong in Germany: 30% of respondents favor increased military support for Ukraine from European countries, 33% approve of the current level of European support, and 32% call for military aid to be reduced," the report reads.
According to the poll, the overwhelming majority of Germans (79%) doubt that Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin is willing to end the war.
"Only 16% of Germans, including nearly half of Alternative for Germany (AfD) supporters (49%), believe that Putin is genuinely interested in a lasting ceasefire. Overall, 79% of respondents, along with the overwhelming majority of supporters of all other parties, doubt this," the report said.
Regarding U.S. President Donald Trump's position on Russia's war against Ukraine, 38% of respondents believe he is on Russia's side, only 1% think he is on Ukraine's side, while 57% are convinced that the U.S. president supports neither side.
Germans are divided over the possibility of Russia attacking eastern NATO member states, particularly Poland and the Baltic countries. Some 46% of respondents consider such a threat realistic, while 48% do not expect such a development. Among residents of Germany's eastern federal states, 57% do not expect such an attack, compared with 46% in the western states.
According to the poll, if Bundestag elections were held next Sunday, 26% of voters would cast their ballots for the Alternative for Germany (AfD), down 2 percentage points from the previous poll. The Christian Democratic Union/Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) bloc led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz would receive 23%, up 2 points. The Social Democratic Party would garner 14%, the Greens 13%, and the Left Party 11%.
The poll was conducted by Forschungsgruppe Wahlen on October 20-22, 2026, among 1,225 eligible voters in Germany by telephone and online. The margin of error is approximately 2-3 percentage points.

title: Thousands protest against Netanyahu ahead of elections
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Thousands of Israeli settlers protested in Tel Aviv against prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet on the eve of parliamentary elections.
Thousands of Zionist protesters took part in a demonstration in Tel Aviv against Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet on the eve of the Zionist regime's parliamentary elections, Al-Manar reported.
The rally was organized by families of Israeli captives and those killed during Operation Al-Aqsa Flood, and participants demanded that regime officials be held accountable for the failure against the operation.

title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Omsk Region injures three — governor
body:
OMSK, October 25. /TASS/. Three people were injured as a result of a Ukrainian drone attack on the Omsk Region in south-central Russia, Governor Vitaly Khotsenko reported.
