title: Series of explosions rock Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh — news agency
body:
DOHA, October 25. /TASS/. A series of explosions occurred in the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh, AFP reported.
According to the news agency, at least three explosions were heard.
At the same time, Saudi Arabia’s General Directorate of Civil Defense activated the National Early Warning Platform for Emergencies, alerting Riyadh residents of a potential threat. The agency later announced that the alert had been lifted.

title: Senators chalk up win to maturity, systems
body:
OTTAWA – There are lessons to be learned in every game and the Ottawa Senators, so far, are proving to be good students.
Now three years under head coach Travis Green, the Senators (8-4-0) have fully bought into his system and are reaping the rewards.
A perfect example was Saturday’s night’s 7-4 win over the New York Rangers.
Ottawa jumped out to a 3-0 lead early in the second and by the end of the period found themselves clinging to a 4-3 lead.
Green admitted he felt a shift in the team’s play when it went ahead 3-0.
“We got like five per cent loose or less competitive, and that happens a lot when you get a lead, and it’s something you have to guard against, especially against a hardworking team,” Green said. “Sometimes it’s that five or 10 per cent that just kind of turns the table a little bit, and you can feel the game turning a bit.”
The Rangers pressed hard in the final frame, but the Senators stuck to their system and didn’t try to press the game. They blocked shots and kept New York’s chances to a minimum.
“I think you know, game’s never over ’til it’s over,” said Jake Sanderson. “You saw they had their push, they had their chances, and you know, I think credit to us not to give up and cave, and just keep pushing through ’til the end.”
Sanderson spoke about it being an indication of the team’s growth and maturity. He admitted it would have been easy to get frustrated at the way things turned around in the second.
“I think when you talk about the growth of this group, you know, bearing down, knowing how important these games are early in the season because you know a win’s a win whether it’s at the start of the season or at the end,” he said. “So you know, I’ll take it.”
The Senators are heading out on a five-game, 11-day road trip and will likely need to rely on backup goaltenders Samuel Ersson and Jonas Johansson for much of it. Linus Ullmark was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week and is expected to miss at least a couple games. The earliest he could return is Thursday.
Johansson made his Senators debut Saturday and held his own when it mattered most.
Acquired in late September, the 31-year-old has been with the team’s American Hockey League affiliate in Belleville, Ont., and isn’t well acquainted with many players, but made a solid first impression.
“I thought he did a real good job getting out of the crease and stopping some of their rims,” Green said. “You know, rim forecheck is hard to defend against, and he did a real nice job.”
Sanderson was impressed with Johansson’s puck handling.
“I think it’s pretty gutsy for a goalie to do, especially his first game with an organization,” he said. “It was a huge help tonight.”
With more than 100 NHL games to his credit, Johansson has been around long enough to understand the impact a solid first performance can have on new teammates.
“I just try not to change the way I play, I just try to do my best out there for whatever team I play for,” said Johansson. “I mean, I’m really happy to be here. There’s a great group of guys in here, and a really good team.”
Johansson is in good company with two fellow Swedish goaltenders. He previously played with Ullmark in Buffalo and trained with Ersson for much of the summer so there’s a familiarity that helps.
Thomas Chabot will travel with the team and Green is hopeful he could be ready to play at some point on the trip.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 24, 2026.

title: Tinubu blames opposition for hunger, poverty in Nigeria; Atiku kicks, says president delusional
body: President Bola Tinubu has accused opposition politicians of causing the hunger and poverty Nigerians are experiencing, insisting that his administration is working to address the problems as he formally launched his 2027 presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday. Mr Tinubu made the remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off at Ranchers Bees Stadium (also known as Kaduna Township Stadium), ahead of the 2027 general elections. I have heard the opposition talking about hunger and poverty. Who caused them? They did! They caused hunger and poverty. We are trying to eliminate them,” the president said. He also urged his supporters to be wary of statements from the opposition, particularly criticism of his decision to remove the petrol subsidy, insisting that the country would not return to the previous system. “Be careful; watch them. Don’t let them lie to you. What is past is in the past. “Fuel subsidy is in our past: no more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies, no more smuggling of fuel,” Mr Tinubu told supporters at the rally. The president’s remarks come amid persistent public concerns over high food prices, inflation and declining purchasing power, issues expected to feature prominently in political debates ahead of the 2027 elections. In a swift reaction to the president’s remarks, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, described President Tinubu’s claim “as a delusional, shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery his own government has inflicted on Nigerians.” He said a president cannot light the fire of hardship with his own policies, then blame the neighbours for the smoke. Tinubu defends petrol subsidy removal Since assuming office in May 2023, the Tinubu administration has implemented major economic reforms, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange regime. The government has defended the measures as necessary to reduce public expenditure, tackle alleged corruption associated with the subsidy system and establish the foundations for sustainable economic growth. While Mr Tinubu insists that the removal of the subsidy is irreversible, critics continue to demand evidence that the savings and additional revenue generated by the reforms are translating into improved living conditions for ordinary Nigerians. At the rally, the president also said salaries were being paid on time and praised APC governors for their development projects. Tinubu thanks Kaduna residents At the rally, Mr Tinubu thanked the people of Kaduna State for supporting him in the 2023 presidential election, saying their backing contributed to his victory. “You gave me the joy of remembering the victory you gave me to become president. I have returned to thank you once again,” he said. He urged Nigerians to give him another opportunity in 2027, promising to continue pursuing his agenda of prosperity, development and national growth. Tinubu has a long history of supporting the North – VP Shettima Vice President Kashim Shettima defended Mr Tinubu’s political relationship with northern Nigeria, saying the president had supported politicians from the region for years, including those who contested the presidency in previous elections. Mr Shettima cited Mr Tinubu’s political relationships with former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the late President Muhammadu Buhari to argue that the president had consistently supported northern political figures. “President Bola Tinubu is one person who has fiercely identified with the North over the years. It is pertinent to mention that when former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased off the PDP with his tail between his legs, he ran to the Lion of Bourdillon, who gave him political succour, support and a platform to contest for the presidency of this country in 2007. “In 2011, Asiwaju supported another northerner, Nuhu Ribadu, and in 2015 and 2019, he supported our late President Muhammadu Buhari,” Mr Shettima said. The expression, “Lion of Bourdillon,” refers to Mr Tinubu, whose residence on Bourdillon Road in Lagos has become associated with his political influence. Atiku contested the presidency under the Action Congress (AC) in 2007 after leaving the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), with support from Mr Tinubu and other party leaders. In 2011, Mr Ribadu contested the presidency under the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN), a party led by Mr Tinubu. In 2015 and 2019, Mr Tinubu supported Mr Buhari’s presidential bids under the APC. However, Mr Tinubu and Atiku subsequently became political opponents, particularly during the 2019 and 2023 presidential elections, when the former vice president contested under the PDP while Mr Tinubu was in the APC. Mr Shettima’s remarks were part of the APC’s effort to highlight Mr Tinubu’s history of political alliances and support for politicians from Northern Nigeria as the party seeks another presidential term for him in 2027. Top government officials attend the rally The event attracted senior federal government officials, APC governors and party leaders from different parts of the country. Those in attendance included Vice President Kashim Shettima and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani, who received Mr Tinubu upon his arrival in the state. Secretary to the Government of the Federation George Akume was also among the senior officials at the event. Other attendees included ministers, senators, members of the House of Representatives, APC governors and prominent party figures. APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda and Abdulaziz Yari, director-general of the party’s presidential campaign council, were among the party leaders involved in preparations for the rally and efforts to mobilise support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election. The event marked the official launch of the APC’s presidential campaign, as the party seeks to consolidate its support base ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: Ukraine switches to standard time tonight
body:
As a result, the day will automatically be extended by one hour, according to Ukrinform.
Daylight saving time and standard time were first introduced in the United Kingdom in 1908 to conserve energy and ensure a more efficient distribution of electricity throughout the day.
For decades, the switch to standard time and daylight saving time in Ukraine has taken place on the last Sunday in October and the last Sunday in March, respectively.
This procedure is regulated by Resolution No. 509 of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated May 13, 1996, “ On the Procedure for Calculating Time on the Territory of Ukraine.”
On July 16, 2024, the Verkhovna Rada adopted the law on the calculation of time in Ukraine (Bill No. 4201) in its entirety, abolishing the switch from daylight saving time to standard time and vice versa.
According to this document, a single Kyiv time zone—UTC+2—was to be established throughout Ukraine. Therefore, in 2024, on the last Sunday in October, Ukrainians were supposed to set their clocks back to standard time for the last time, and starting in 2025, there were no plans to switch to daylight saving time in Ukraine. However, President Volodymyr Zelensky has not yet signed this law.

title: Conflict with Russian to cost Ukraine over $470 million per day in 2027
body:
MOSCOW, October 25. /TASS/. Ukraine’s military spending in 2027 will amount to $473 million per day if the conflict with Russia continues, according to TASS calculations based on the Ukrainian Finance Ministry’s reports.
This figure refers solely to military expenditures, that is, costs related to payments to active-duty service members and the procurement of military equipment, ammunition, and gear. It does not include social spending to support former servicemen and the families of those killed in action, the construction of fortifications (if not carried out by the Defense Ministry), or any other government expenditures. Total military spending for the year will amount to nearly $173 billion.
In 2026, Ukraine’s military spending averaged about $300 million per day, excluding the Defense Ministry's additional requests at the end of the year. If these requests are included, the total rises to $370 million.

title: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
body: Former President Barack Obama has attacked the Trump administration over the Iran war and high consumer prices as he hit the campaign trail for Democrats ahead of the US midterm elections. “This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration,” Obama told crowds in Ohio on Saturday. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump touted his administration’s immigration and tariff policies at a rally in Georgia, telling supporters “we’re in the golden age of America”. The midterm elections on 3 November will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump’s term, and therefore how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans. Early voting has already begun and Trump cast his ballot on Saturday in Florida alongside his wife First Lady Melania Trump. Speaking on Saturday in Ohio and Michigan, Obama targeted Trump and his cabinet members, at one point mocking the president’s attempt to redecorate the White House. “After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘enough is enough,'” the former president said in Cleveland. Obama said he sympathised with voters who rejected Democrats in 2024 over economic and inflation concerns following the Covid pandemic. But he said Trump had only himself to blame for the current state of the economy. “If you thought everything was too expensive before ‘you know who’,” he said, referring to Trump without using his name, “everything is more expensive now”. Trump, meanwhile, acknowledged that oil prices were “temporarily high” but said “our country is getting stronger and stronger all the time, and those pump prices are going to come down”. The Republican president has faced significant pressure to lower fuel prices, which have jumped due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Talking up the economy, Trump told the crowd in Perry “we’re taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs”, and repeated his pledge to offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress. He also took aim at the Democrats, telling the crowd they would “loot your wealth” and “annihilate your borders”. Using derogatory language, he accused the Democrats of trying to open up immigration from Libya, Yemen, Haiti and Somalia – countries which he described as “terror-infested”. Describing a previous meeting with several senators, he recalled: “I said, ‘Why do we always have to take people from shithouse countries? Why can’t we take people from, like, well… Norway, Sweden? Why not Denmark?'”

title: Energized Leafs continue hot roll with 7-2 win
body:
EDMONTON – Picking the Toronto Maple Leafs to win in Edmonton has become a safe bet in recent years.
William Nylander had two goals, including the 300th of his career, as the surging Maple Leafs scorched the Edmonton Oilers 7-2 on Saturday.
No team has had more success in Rogers Place in Edmonton than the Maple Leafs. Since the Oilers moved into their new arena, Toronto has gone an impressive 12-2-1.
Jack Roslovic, Auston Matthews, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri also scored for the Maple Leafs (7-4-2), who have won four straight and are getting a complete team effort.
Matthews said the atmosphere on the Leafs is incredible at the moment.
“I just think the energy in the locker room day in and day out has been great,” he said. “I think the guys, the environment that we’re in, it’s so much fun. It’s competitive, you know. Guys, a lot of joking around, a lot of chirping one another. It’s just been a lot of fun, and I think that emotion, that energy carries over in the games, and it doesn’t matter who scores, everybody’s excited, everybody’s happy.
“It’s just everything’s about the team, and the team’s been first all this time, and that’s what is most important. That’s what I feel like is kind of driving us right now.”
Matthews and Kirill Marchenko (two assists) both extended their season-opening road point streak to five games. Matthews now needs just one point to reach 800 in his career, which will make him the fastest player in franchise history to reach the milestone, in addition to the NHL’s third-quickest American skater to hit the mark.
When asked about trying to contain Oilers Connor McDavid, who had two assists to pad his season-starting points streak to 11 games and 33 points, and Leon Draisaitl who recorded his third consecutive two-goal game to give him a league-leading 12 on the season, Matthews said it took “all hands on deck.”
“You recognize the challenges that you’re going up against, and obviously you need everybody to meet that challenge, and you know it’s not pretty at times,” Matthews said. “But I thought we stuck with it. Penalty kill was great. Defence was great. (Goalie Anthony Stolarz) was great, and we were able to put the puck in the net when we needed to.”
Stolarz made 30 stops to earn the win for Toronto.
Toronto head coach Jim Hiller said everyone in his team’s locker room can hold their heads high.
“It’s not just Matthews. It’s not just Nylander. It’s not just (John) Tavares. It’s going through the lineup, and that gives you a chance to win every night,” Hiller said. “And so as much as I’m happy for those guys, I’m happy for our team that they can feel there’s other guys there to support, and that’s a pretty good feeling right now.”
Toronto got goals from a couple unlikely sources as MacEwen scored his first goal since Oct. 14, 2024, and Lettieri hadn’t found the back of the net since April 1, 2025.
Nylander hitting 300 goals was significant in a number of ways. He became the fourth fastest player in franchise history to the milestone as well as the fourth fastest Swedish player and passed Rick Vaive for sixth in Maple Leafs history. It was also his 45th career multi-goal game, putting him 10th on the Toronto all-time list.
The Maple Leafs have been superb this season on the penalty kill. They had killed off 40 of 41 opposition power plays and 30 in a row until Edmonton got one late in the game.
The Oilers (8-2-1) had a three-game winning streak halted.
“They were just better than us. They were more competitive and won more battles,” said Oilers forward Zach Hyman. “They just beat us in every area today.”
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 24, 2026.

title: Convicted murderer attending McGill law school back in custody Saturday
body:
Warning: This story contains graphic descriptions of violence that may be disturbing to some readers.
A convicted killer from B.C. who had been attending law school in Montreal was back in custody on Saturday.
The Correctional Service of Canada said in a statement that a warrant was issued for Jeffrey Ewert and his conditional release has been suspended.
Officials said that type of warrant is issued when “there are reasonable grounds to believe that the offender has breached a condition of release or that the risk they present can no longer be safely managed in the community.”
“Following a suspension, the case is reviewed in accordance with the established post-release decision-making process, which may include further consideration by the Parole Board of Canada,” the statement read.
Ewert was recently back in the news because it was revealed he was attending law school at McGill University .
Ewert, now in his 60s, was convicted in the 1980s of second-degree murder and attempted murder involving violent attacks committed in British Columbia on two female victims, one of whom was 15 years old.
Ewert spent 40 years in federal prison and was granted day parole in 2025. News of his studies spread in early October and he has since been barred from campus.
Former prosecutor and retired judge, Rick Miller, told Global News in an interview that Ewert is “as bad as they come.”
“This guy was the most brutal and evil that I dealt with,” he said.

title: Sultan Sooud Al Qassemi on art: How an Egyptian weaving village became a lesson in the power of giving
body: A busy village scene in the Upper Egyptian Delta depicts a crowd of men harvesting corn and placing it on the backs of animals of burden, while women look after the children nearby. In the bottom-left corner, four men gather around a fire, possibly hinting that the scene is set in the autumn months, coinciding with the end of the corn harvest season in Egypt. The background is peppered with dome-topped houses, palm trees and birds. This scenic tapestry was created by Garya Mahmoud, one of the Ramses Wissa Wassef Art Centre’s first-generation weavers. The centre was founded by the prominent architect Ramses Wissa Wassef and his wife, Sophie Habib Gorgi, in 1951, and it initially employed 45 women and men in weaving, stoneware and batik painting. Ramses was behind several major projects, such as the Mahmoud Mokhtar Museum, opened in Cairo in 1962, and a string of churches and private residences across Egypt. Through the art centre, Ramses and Sophie envisioned a unique space that would give others opportunities that would allow them to earn a livelihood. In a 2018 interview with Masrawy , Sophie, recalling the conversation that prompted the creation of the centre, stated: “One day [Ramses] said to me, 'Why don’t we look for a simple village with quiet people and start a project that brings the place to life and helps the villagers learn something different?'” That village would be Harraniya, 15km south-west of central Cairo, not far from the Giza Pyramids. The couple could have simply opted for charity, but they chose to empower this “simple village” and “bring the place to life”, an act that embodies the proverb “give a person a fish and you feed them for a day; teach them how to fish and you feed them for a lifetime”. This spirit of generosity, selflessness and encouragement towards independence must be celebrated and commended whether it comes from an individual, a corporation or a country. The Arab Gulf states, too, have historically been among the most generous in terms of global aid. For instance, the Kuwait Fund for Development was founded in 1961 under Emir Sheikh Abdullah, as the world’s first development fund established by a developing country. Since its founding, it has extended loans to build schools and other infrastructure in more than 100 countries, continuing work even during Kuwait’s occupation in 1990-1991. Similarly, the UAE has been one of the world’s most generous countries relative to its size, contributing 0.61 per cent of its GDP, according to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, to developing and disaster-stricken nations. Last November, the UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs ranked the UAE as the third-largest donor of humanitarian aid globally for 2025, after the US and the EU. Since its founding in 1971, the UAE has delivered close to $100 billion in foreign aid, and today it is the world’s largest humanitarian donor to Gaza, providing $3.9 billion in aid, or close to half the global assistance, including the building of field hospitals and desalination plants. That said, not all acts of kindness are measured in billions or even millions of dollars. Often, small acts of generosity go a long way and lead to lifelong bonds. Mahmoud developed a close friendship with the founders, and when their daughter Suzanne, herself a stoneware ceramic designer, became engaged in 1972, the weaver created a tapestry to celebrate the occasion, depicting the couple and other family members. Since its establishment, scores of artisans and artists have benefitted from the Ramses Wissa Wassef Centre, and some, such as Mahmoud’s own daughter, Naglaa, have continued the legacies of their mothers and fathers long after they were gone. Today, tapestries from the centre are collected globally, and have appeared at auctions in Lebanon, the US, the UK and Sweden. The precedents set by Ramses and Sophie in 1951, Kuwait in 1961 and the UAE since 1971 are examples for us all. Giving back to our communities, whether it is at the state, corporate or individual level, should not merely be seen as an act of charity and kindness, but rather as a long-term investment in less-developed parts of our communities that can potentially bring the place to life.

title: Republic Day Is Reminder That Kazakhstan Belongs to Its People
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. Every year, as Kazakhstan marks Republic Day on Oct. 25, we return to a moment in our history that is easy to describe in legal terms but harder to appreciate in its broader meaning. On Oct. 25, 1990, the Declaration of State Sovereignty of the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic laid the foundations for the country’s future statehood, establishing principles of territorial integrity, political self-determination and national identity that would become central to independent Kazakhstan. The cover of the Declaration on the State Sovereignty of the Kazakh SSR. Yet this date’s significance extends beyond the document itself. It invites us to consider what it means to be a republic, not simply as a form of government, but as a country whose future cannot be separated from the people who inhabit it. In June 2022, at the first meeting of the National Kurultai in Ulytau, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed restoring its status as a national holiday. Parliament passed the relevant amendments on Sept. 29, 2022, and the country celebrated Republic Day again that October. For much of Kazakhstan’s post-independence history, the story of the state was closely tied to the figure of its first president. This made sense in a country undergoing profound political and economic transformation, where building new institutions and seeking stability became defining priorities. But a state is larger than any individual’s political career, however consequential that career may be. Leaders come and go, political narratives change, and the durability of a country ultimately depends on its institutions, shared values and the strength of its civic life. Seen in this light, the return of Republic Day means more than restoring a holiday. It brings the idea of the republic itself back into focus: the country as a shared political space, rather than an extension of any one person’s legacy. Perhaps Tokayev was guided by precisely this understanding when he proposed restoring the holiday, recognizing that the idea of statehood must ultimately rest on something greater than the legacy of an individual leader. A republic derives its strength not from any one political figure’s permanence, but from the people who sustain it, the institutions they build and their commitment to a common future. This also carries deeper historical resonance. The steppe that shaped Kazakh society was vast, and survival across it required more than individual strength. Communities depended on agreements, customary law, mutual obligations and an understanding that disputes had to be resolved within a shared social order. These traditions should not be romanticized as a history without conflict or inequality, but they do remind us that collective life has always required rules, negotiation and an ability to find common ground. Modern Kazakhstan is, of course, a very different society. Its citizens live in cities and villages, work in a highly connected economy, participate in institutions and increasingly engage with the world beyond their borders. Yet the underlying question remains familiar: what holds a community together, and what makes its members feel that the place they inhabit is genuinely theirs? Patriotism is often expressed through symbols, ceremonies and declarations of loyalty, but its more meaningful test lies in everyday choices. It is reflected in whether we respect the law when doing otherwise would be easier, whether we demand accountability from public institutions, whether we treat public property as something we share rather than something that belongs to nobody, and whether we contribute to the communities in which we live. It also requires us to recognize that we cannot delegate the country’s future entirely to the government, just as we cannot simply blame those in power for every problem. This does not diminish the role of the state. On the contrary, public institutions must create the conditions for citizens to participate meaningfully, exercise their rights and see that their voices matter. The relationship between the state and society cannot be one-sided: a government may set priorities and introduce reforms, but their success depends in large part on whether people trust institutions, take part in public life and believe that their actions can make a difference. Republic Day also reminds us that sovereignty has a geographical dimension. Kazakhstan’s territory, stretching across the steppe and connecting different parts of Eurasia, is not merely a feature on a map or an economic asset. It is the space within which a political community can determine its own future. Preserving that sovereignty requires capable institutions and sound strategic decisions, as well as a shared sense of belonging and an understanding of what is at stake when the country’s long-term interests are discussed. National identity, meanwhile, should not be understood as something fixed or inherited without question. It is shaped by the way we understand our history, preserve our cultural heritage, relate to one another and imagine the country we want to leave to the next generation. It can accommodate different backgrounds, languages and experiences without losing its central commitment to a common future. Perhaps this is the most important meaning of Republic Day today. The 1990 declaration marked a decisive step toward sovereignty, but the work of building a country did not end with independence, nor can any single generation or political leader complete it. Statehood endures through functioning institutions, communities that support one another, and citizens who understand that the country’s future is not something that happens to them, but something they help shape. On Oct. 25, we celebrate not only a defining moment in Kazakhstan’s journey toward independence, but also the idea that this country belongs to all of us. The post Republic Day Is Reminder That Kazakhstan Belongs to Its People appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: [Two Pronged] My love and sex life are complicated, and I want a committed relationship
body: Rappler’s People section runs an advice column by couple Jeremy Baer and clinical psychologist Dr. Margarita Holmes. Jeremy has a master’s degree in law from Oxford University. A banker of 37 years who worked in three continents, he has been training with Dr. Holmes for the last 10 years as co-lecturer and, occasionally, as co-therapist, especially with clients whose financial concerns intrude into their daily lives. Together, they have written two books: Love Triangles: Understanding the Macho-Mistress Mentality and Imported Love: Filipino-Foreign Liaisons. Dear Dr. Holmes and Mr. Baer, I wonder these days why people enter relationships. While getting in one is not the center of my life, I have questions about the intersection between desire, life direction, and relationships. I’m now at a point where I’ve experienced the most satisfying sex I could ever imagine with someone but he will not live in the Philippines permanently and when he leaves he knows he cannot maintain an LDR (long distance relationship). I found myself in another two month relationship with a man with a volatile libido. I ended up walking on eggshells, crashing my libido badly. I reconnected with the first guy. I was able to let my guard down and bare my raw self and act in a way that I’ve never been before. Right now, this man is someone I can’t let go of but still I can’t just plan my life around him, so it’s a dilemma, a floating connection. I now allow myself to talk to anyone that makes me happy. I don’t become loyal anymore to anything hypothetical and I have more reservations now. I’m also deeply aware and learned the hard way that I don’t want to feel ever again that I’m good enough to f*** but not worthy enough to commit to. – Anna Dear Anna, Relationships are complex and come in many forms, as it is clear you already know. You ask why people enter them yet in reality you have answered your own question already. A relationship offers the opportunity to reveal yourself fully and safely with someone else without having to sacrifice your own dignity and integrity, an aim that is achievable but often only partially. The two relationships you describe illustrate this. The “eggshell” one showed you what happens when there is no safety — having to deal with mood shifts can kill desire. The “reconnection” one demonstrates the effect of safety – you can reveal your true self. The contrast is critical and can usefully inform your future. However, the way you describe your current attachment is scarcely ideal. He is someone you cannot let go of but cannot plan a future with either, or as you label it, this is a floating relationship. That the sex is extraordinary is a bonus but also a distraction. After all, great sex doesn’t mean that he is the right partner for you any more than a missing label means that he isn’t. The real issue is: is he willing to move forward and label your relationship or are you shoring it up with hope that may be misplaced? A way forward would be to ask him: what does he want from the relationship? Is he willing to build something? His answer, or avoidance, will tell you much more than any guesswork on your part and if in the final analysis he wants intimacy without commitment, at least you will know where you stand. Best wishes, – JAF Baer Dear Anna: Thank you very much for your letter. You ask a very important question: Why do people get into relationships? A cursory search will give you a plethora of reasons, but in truth one can probably divide said reasons into two: neuroscientific ones — mirror neurons, oxytocin, etc. but one of the simplest ways to describe this is that we are social beings that need relationships because our brains are wired to connect with others; and practical and social reasons, such as when relationships result in children, it is much easier to raise the kids when said relationships continue; to avoid loneliness, etc. From the theoretical standpoint above, let us now proceed to a more personal level and try to gain a larger perspective on your love and sex life. At the moment, you seem to not just want, but actually need relationships with the opposite sex. In the last four months, you have been in a relationship first, with man A, whom you felt safe enough to have terrific sex with; but when his lack of commitment hurt you so much, you went to volatile man B who, thankfully, you realized after 2 months was not the sort of man you wanted in your life. The following (4th) month, you went back to man A, not just because the sex was, once more, absolutely fantastic, but because you reveled in being the woman you felt you truly were (and you could well be right) when with him. And because you felt complete, cherished and truly seen by him, you wanted the relationship to continue. Yet even as the relationship continued, man A was honest enough to say it couldn’t last forever because for whatever reason, he could not or would not stay in the Philippines forever. Man A, despite knowing that you could end the relationship prematurely (in his eyes-because I have a feeling not just the sex, but the while experience of being with you was also mind boggling for him), was honest enough to continue telling you the truth. Some writers divide people into two types : “Those who run away from something” or “Those who run towards something.” Actually, I would include a third type of person: those who run towards something (like a seemingly perfect relationship with man A) but then realize it is best for their mental health to run away from that same something. I would like to say that your last two paragraphs show what a mature person you have become. And this is true but, perhaps, not the complete truth. If you can hold off from sex with someone you genuinely like whom you know also genuinely likes you, is willing to commit to you but is honest enough to say, but I am not sure if this commitment will be forever, then terrific. You can still have a warm, funny, fulfilling relationship with him but not have sex. Another option is to believe that just because a relationship (with sex) doesn’t last forever, it does not mean it is empty or worthless. If you can truly manage one of these two options, then I say, “you go, girl!” But I am not sure you can. This is not to demean you in any way. This is merely a recognition that people are different and some feel they need sex more than others. If one is particularly blessed with the right experiences and/or the right therapy, one’s needs and one’s wants can live together harmoniously OR this can be a goal worth aspiring to. And if one is self compassionate enough to forgive oneself for the same “mistakes” with the same generosity one could forgive one’s best friend, then each relationship you have can be a learning experience. Hopefully, each relationship can also have more positive than negative elements in them. That way, in time, you might agree with what the brilliant psychoanalyst and humanistic philosopher Erich Fromm once wrote in his 1956 book The Art of Loving: Immature love: I love you because I need you. Mature love: I need you because I love you. The best of luck to you – to US! — my fellow work in progress – MG Holmes – Rappler.com Life got complicated? Write to our Two Pronged duo at twopronged@rappler.com .

title: Cognition Open-Sources an Agent Plugin that Helps Secure Systems against Recent Cybersecurity Threats
body: Cognition has released the Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin , a free, open-source set of agent skills. It targets three critical remote code execution (RCE) advisories. They cover PHP2Shell , the Node.js October 21, 2026 security release and a CVSS 10.0 self-managed GitLab bug . The skills run in Devin and in any coding agent that reads SKILL.md files . Cognition packaged the remediation workflow it used internally . Developers can do inventory, approve, patch, test, then ship 1 pull request per repository. TL;DR Size: Three skills ( fix-php-vuln , fix-node-vuln , fix-gitlab-vuln ), MIT license. Runs on: Devin, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Factory Droid, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Windsurf. Needs git, a shell, Docker and registry access. The npx skills install needs Node.js 22.20 or later. Performance: No remediation benchmark or fix-rate number is published for the plugin. Best: Covers the week’s most severe bug, GitLab CVE-2026-110264, rated CVSS 10.0. Worst: Validation is only as strong as your tests. Managed runtimes, appliances and Electron apps are flagged, not patched. What is the Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin? The Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin is a set of three Agent Skills from Cognition. They find and patch vulnerable PHP, Node.js and self-managed GitLab deployments. The source is on GitHub under the MIT license. Cognition’s product page lists it as free and open source. Which vulnerabilities does it fix? PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) : PHP rates both flaws CVSS v4.0 9.2 . The first corrupts memory after an out-of-memory condition. The second lets stale global state from one request reach the next. PHP says every web-serving setup is at risk , with mod_php rated highest risk. Fixed versions are 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. PHP 8.1 and older get no releases, only source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. Node.js October 2026 release : It fixes 10 CVEs, 4 rated High . The lead bug, CVE-2026-111497, is a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that can enable RCE. Fixed versions are 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1. Node.js 20 and older are end-of-life and get no fix. GitLab CVE-2026-110264 : An integer overflow in the regular expression compiler allows unauthenticated code execution . It affects GitLab CE/EE from 7.0 onward and scores CVSS 10.0. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched. How does the plugin work? Every skill follows the same five-step shape : Read-only inventory : The agent scans Dockerfiles, base images, distro packages, CI, Helm, Terraform, Packer, Lambda and config management. Approval gate : Nothing changes until you pick repos. Riskier minor or major upgrades are called out first. Verified target : Every tag, digest, package version and checksum is confirmed against the official source before editing. Test before and after : The suite runs on the current version, then inside the new production image. Regressions stop the run. One PR per repo : Each PR carries versions, test results, runtime diffs, a risk label and a rollback plan. The skills also encode known patching traps. Debian and Ubuntu backport fixes without changing upstream versions, so php -v can mislead. Ubuntu 24.04’s fixed package is 8.3.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.13 . Digest-pinned images need a new digest. Changing Composer’s require.php patches nothing. window.addEventListener("message",function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.mtpEmbedHeight){var f=document.getElementById("mtp-dvf-frame");if(f&&e.source===f.contentWindow){f.style.height=e.data.mtpEmbedHeight+"px";}}}); How do you install and run it? In Devin, open Customize, then Plugins, then Browse Marketplace, and search for Vulnerability Fixes. The Devin CLI uses devin plugins install CognitionAI/devin-marketplace#plugins/devin-vuln-fixes . For other agents, run npx skills add CognitionAI/devin-vuln-fixes . Claude Code users can add the marketplace and run /plugin install vuln-fixes@cognition-skills . Then ask in plain language, such as ‘Please fix my PHP vulnerability.’ Slash commands also work: /fix-php-vuln , /fix-node-vuln and /fix-gitlab-vuln . How does it compare with Dependabot, Copilot Autofix and Snyk Agent Fix? Feature Devin Vulnerability Fixes Dependabot security updates GitHub Copilot Autofix Snyk Agent Fix What it fixes PHP, Node.js and self-managed GitLab versions for 3 advisories Vulnerable dependencies with an available patch, plus GitHub Actions Code scanning alerts Snyk Code findings Where it edits Dockerfiles, images, distro packages, CI, Helm, Terraform, config management Manifest and lock files Code suggestions in the repo Local-file code fixes; no complex inter-file logic Approval before edits Yes, read-only inventory first No: opens PRs automatically once enabled Not disclosed User clicks “Generate AI fix” and reviews Validation Tests before and after inside the new production image Compatibility scores from public CI runs Not disclosed Retests fix with the Snyk Code engine Runs where Any agent that reads SKILL.md GitHub GitHub Snyk web UI and IDE plugins License MIT, open source Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed Cost Free Available for all GitHub repositories Free on public repos; private repos need GitHub Code Security Requires Snyk Code; price not disclosed These tools solve adjacent problems. Dependabot and the code-fix agents work on application dependencies and source code. Cognition’s plugin targets the runtime layer: base images, OS packages and infrastructure-as-code. Key Takeaways Three MIT-licensed skills patch PHP2Shell, Node.js and GitLab CVE-2026-110264. Read-only inventory and an approval gate come before any edit. Tests run before and after inside the new production image. Works across Devin, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other SKILL.md agents. No published fix-rate benchmark; results depend on your test coverage. Check out the GitHub repo , the Cognition blog post and the plugin page . Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter . Wait! are you on telegram? now you can join us on telegram as well. title: Luv FM journalists sweep top honours at GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards
body: Journalists from Luv FM, a subsidiary of the Multimedia Group Limited, have won multiple awards at the 2025 Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards. Four journalists from the Kumasi-based station received honours across several categories, with Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe taking the night’s top prize as Ashanti Regional Journalist of the Year. Mr Quaicoe also won Best Feature Production, Best Agriculture Reporter, and placed second in Best Entertainment Journalism. Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe Clinton Yeboah secured first place in both Best Health Journalism and Best Business and Economy Journalism. Clinton Yeboah Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom won first place in Best Community Impact Journalism, placed second in Best Health Journalism and finished third in Best Environment, Science and Climate Journalism. Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen also swept awards, including Best Science, Climate and Environment Reporter, and placed third in the Best Feature Production Category The awards recognise journalistic work across different beats, including health, business, entertainment, environmental reporting and community impact. Mr Quaicoe’s overall regional award, alongside the category wins secured by his colleagues, highlights the range of reporting represented by the Luv FM team. The GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards celebrate journalists whose work contributes to public understanding of issues affecting communities across the region. Luv FM, based in Kumasi, is part of the Multimedia Group’s network of radio and television stations in Ghana. The regional winners are expected to feature in the broader national awards calendar, although their participation and final standings at the national level will depend on the applicable GJA arrangements.

title: Multimedia’s Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe wins 2025 GJA Ashanti Regional Journalist of the Year award
body: Luv FM journalist, Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe, has been crowned the 2025 Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Ashanti Regional Journalist of the Year, the highest individual honour at the regional media excellence awards. His award was announced at the GJA Ashanti Media Excellence Awards, which recognises outstanding journalistic work across the region. Mr Quaicoe secured three additional honours on the night, winning Best Feature Production, Best in Agriculture reporting and placing second in Best Entertainment Journalism. The three awards recognise his work across different areas of journalism, including feature production and entertainment reporting. His story titled “Broken Chain: Delayed rains, poor sales discouraging Ejura maize farmers from planting next season” won the agriculture category while a story he published on “Illicit flows bleed Ghana dry: How billions lost are crippling science education and local research” won the Best Feature Production category. A story acknowledging the unique hairstyle of Asantehemaa’s maidens, “Braids of Loyalty: Asantehemaa’s maidens honour her legacy with unique hairstyle,” secured second in the Entertainment category. The 2025 Ashanti GJA Media Excellence Awards was held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Championing Credibility: Journalism in the Age of AI,” which highlights the importance of professional standards, credibility, and ethical reporting amid the growing influence of artificial intelligence in news production and distribution. The Journalist of the Year title places Mr Quaicoe among the region’s recognised media practitioners, while his category awards acknowledge his work in specific areas of reporting. He works with Luv FM, a Kumasi-based station under the Multimedia Group Limited. The GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards celebrate journalistic contributions to public information and coverage of issues affecting communities across the region. Mr Quaicoe’s performance at the regional awards could also place him in contention for national recognition, depending on the arrangements for the GJA National Awards.

title: Audi to invest $4.2 billion in building car plant in US — Trump
body:
WASHINGTON, October 25. /TASS/. German automaker Audi, which is part of the Volkswagen Group, plans to invest $4.2 billion in the construction of a plant in the US state of Georgia, President Donald Trump announced.
"Audi has just committed to invest 4.2 billion dollars in nearby Macon, Georgia, to begin the construction next month on a massive plant that will produce 200,000 cars a year," the US leader told Republican Party supporters at a rally in Georgia ahead of the November 3 midterm congressional elections. According to Trump, "this will be the single largest investment in modern US auto industry history."
The German automotive industry is facing a severe crisis. This crisis is caused by both rising costs, particularly high energy prices, and increased competition in the market.

title: Tinubu: I’m Working to Eradicate Inherited Hunger and Poverty
body: •Shettima: President has consistently supported northern political interests •Blaming opponents for hunger shameless attempt to dodge responsibility, Atiku replies Tinubu • ADC mocks APC campaign flag-off over empty seats, rented crowd, recycled promises • Tinubu’s Kaduna campaign flag-off ‘political theatre’, says Makinde Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and John Shiklam in Kaduna President Bola Ahmed Tinubu yesterday flagged off his 2027 re-election campaign in Kaduna State, declaring that he was working to eradicate inherited hunger and poverty created by his political opponents when they were in power. Tinubu, who spoke at the Ranchers Bees Stadium, the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) rally, promised that his administration would create prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity. This comes as Vice President Kashim Shettima declared that President Tinubu has consistently supported northern political interests, citing historical instances when the president provided vital political backing to major northern figures facing political adversity. Meanwhile, Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State has challenged opposition figures presenting themselves as northern candidates to show their track record. Reacting to Tinubu’s claim that the opposition created hunger and poverty, African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku described it as a delusional and shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery Tinubu’s government has inflicted on Nigerians. The ADC Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has also described the APC campaign flag-off in Kaduna as a monumental disappointment, accusing the ruling party of relying on rented crowds, empty seats and recycled promises. Similarly, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has dismissed President Tinubu’s campaign flag-off as political theatre, accusing his administration of failing the North on security, economic welfare and political inclusion. Speaking at yesterday’s campaign rally, Tinubu accused his political opponents of creating hunger and poverty, which his administration was tackling. Tinubu stated: “I must thank you for your participation in the past elections. You gave me joy, and I will always remember the victory you gave me to become President. I have come again to thank you and seek your mandate for a second term to fulfill our promise of prosperity, continuity, progress and development. “I hear my opponents talking about hunger. Who created it? They did. They created hunger and poverty. We are trying to eradicate them. We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working, and I am proud of them. They are developing their states. “To you, the children of our country, we promise prosperity in our second term. You will not regret going to the polls. “Do you have your PVC? This is not a matter of anger either. Our opponents are angry… They have nothing to offer you but heckling. We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity. I assure you of that.” The president urged voters to vote for all the ruling party’s candidates during the election. He noted: “Your prosperity is here. Your good fortune is in your hands. Your fingerprints will reflect this. Be careful. Watch them. Do not let them lie to you. “What is past is past. Fuel subsidy is in our past. No more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies and no more smuggling.” Shettima: Tinubu Had Consistently Supported Northern Political Interests Also speaking at the rally, Vice President Shettima stated that President Tinubu had consistently supported northern political interests. “And I want us to bear in mind and go back to the past. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has fiercely identified with the North over the years. It is pertinent to mention that when former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased out of the PDP, with his tail between his legs, he ran to the land of the Jagaban, who gave him political succour, support, and a platform to contest the presidency in 2007. “Again, in 2011, President Tinubu supported another Northern man, Malam Nuhu Ribadu, to contest for the presidency of this country. You can also see that in 2015 and 2019, President Tinubu stood solidly behind the late President Muhammadu Buhari, who secured his first- and second-term victories. This is why we have all stood with him. This is a mark of honour, and our faith in a man of honour.” Shettima said Tinubu’s administration had also kept the country together despite predictions of failure and had delivered on key promises. Shettima also cited several projects delivered by Tinubu’s administration. Gov Sani Challenges Northern Candidates to Show Records Kaduna State Governor Senator Sani challenged opposition figures presenting themselves as northern candidates to show their track record, stressing that Tinubu had fulfilled key campaign promises made to Kaduna State in 2022, particularly on road reconstruction and security in Birnin Gwari. He recalled Tinubu’s visit to Birnin Gwari LGA on December 22, 2022, when the area was the epicentre of insecurity in the North-west. Addressing the President, Sani said: “At that time, a very senior officer advised you against going to Birnin Gwari because of security concerns. You instantly rejected the advice and travelled to Birnin Gwari with 27 armoured vehicles.” According to the governor, two promises made during that visit have been met, adding that the 123km Kaduna-Birnin Gwari Road abandoned for over 40 years was under reconstruction. Sani said the government had released N117 billion to the contractor. He noted: “Today you can travel to Birnin Gwari with your eyes closed without a single police escort. That is progress.” The governor challenged opposition figures to show their track record. “When someone came to us and said we should vote for him simply because he is a northerner, we asked him, can you show us a track record?” Sani said. Also, the Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, said the campaign would be based on records in the economy, infrastructure, health, education and cash transfers. “We have been engaging all and sundry, our traditional rulers, our ulama and our imams, to understand the importance of your return in 2027 for continuity, for the peace of this country.” He added: “The opposition have now upgraded their campaign from Facebook and Twitter to AI. So, I want to call the attention of our supporters to prepare, be watchful and be vigilant.” For his part, the National Chairman of APC, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, declared that Tinubu has earned the confidence and support of Nigerians through his courageous leadership, commitment to national development, and promise of greater prosperity for the country. Blaming Opposition for Hunger Shameless Attempt to Dodge Responsibility, Atiku Replies Tinubu Meanwhile, Atiku has described Tinubu’s claim that the opposition created hunger and poverty as a delusional and shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery his own government has inflicted on Nigerians. In a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the former Vice President argued that a President cannot light the fire of hardship with his own policies, then blame the neighbours for the smoke. “Mr President, blaming the opposition for hunger is either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia. The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record. “The hardship your administration has brought upon Nigerians is real. You cannot deny it by blaming others. “Your decision to commission the unfinished Abuja to Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium shows how far removed you are from the daily reality of Nigerians. A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon-cutting ceremony,” Atiku added. ADC Mocks APC Campaign Flag-off Over Empty Seats, Rented Crowd, Recycled Promises Reacting to the rally, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Mr. Kola Ologbondiyan, said an event intended to demonstrate the APC’s political strength across the North-west had instead exposed what he described as the party’s declining public acceptance. Ologbondiyan alleged that the APC mobilised people from the seven states of the North-west and beyond, with payments reportedly ranging from N50,000 to N100,000 per person. Yet, the stadium, which he put at a capacity of 5,000, remained sparsely occupied. He added that the turnout, which he described as disappointing, was compounded by what he called the unenthusiastic reception given to the speeches and messages of APC leaders. Ologbondiyan further alleged that some attendees expressed dissatisfaction with the ruling party after leaving the stadium, chanting the Hausa phrase “Ba mu yi,” which he interpreted as a rejection of the APC and its policies. The ADC-PCC accused the APC of returning to Kaduna with promises similar to those made during the 2015, 2019 and 2023 election cycles, arguing that the ruling party had failed to account for its years in power adequately. Tinubu’s Kaduna Campaign Flag-off ‘Political Theatre’, Says Makinde On its part, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) said the APC campaign event would not erase what it described as broken promises, worsening hardship and declining public confidence in the ruling party. In a statement issued by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, MDPCO challenged Tinubu to explain what the North had gained from his administration beyond persistent insecurity, economic difficulties and what it called marginalisation. MDPCO alleged that at least 20,000 people had been killed in northern Nigeria since Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while millions had been displaced by insecurity. The statement did not independently verify the figures. The organisation further alleged that the North had been marginalised in appointments to strategic federal positions, accusing the APC of treating the region primarily as a source of electoral support. “No part of the country should be an electoral warehouse to be raided every four years and abandoned after victory,” the group said.

title: NDC Fixes Monday for Third NEC Meeting, Presidential Campaign Council Unveiling
body: •Says 80% of candidates received free nomination forms amid economic hardship Sunday Aborisade in Abuja The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) will unveil its National Campaign Council on Monday as part of preparations for the 2027 general election, while presenting its financial accounts to demonstrate its commitment to transparency and accountability. The party disclosed this in a statement issued yesterday by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, announcing that its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting would be held at 10 a.m. on October 26 at JD Event Centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, Maitama, Abuja. A major highlight of the meeting, according to the party, will be the National Treasurer’s presentation of the party’s statement of account, a move it said is intended to distinguish its financial management practices from those of other political parties. The NDC challenged other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to adopt similar measures to promote transparency in managing party finances. The party also attributed its financial limitations partly to the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, claiming that approximately 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the fees for expression-of-interest forms. It said it had consequently issued the forms to the affected candidates free of charge to enable them to participate in the electoral process. The party blamed the situation on what it described as widespread poverty, hunger and deprivation under the APC-led federal government, criticising its economic policies. Beyond the financial disclosures, the NEC meeting will give the party an opportunity to unveil its National Campaign Council, which it said would coordinate its campaign activities across all levels of government. According to the statement, the council will encompass the presidential, National Assembly, governorship and state Houses of Assembly campaign structures. The party also announced plans to present certificates of return to its candidates contesting the various elective positions. The developments come as political parties intensify preparations for the 2027 general election, with campaign structures, candidate mobilisation and party organisation expected to play important roles in the contest. For the NDC, the planned unveiling of its campaign council and disclosure of its accounts are intended to project organisational readiness and distinguish the party’s approach to internal financial accountability. The NDC expressed confidence in its preparations for the forthcoming elections, saying it was determined to offer Nigerians what it described as altruistic leadership. The statement read, “The leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) wishes to announce that its 3rd National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting will hold on Monday, 26th October 2026, at JD event centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-class park, Maitama, Abuja. The time is 10 am prompt. “A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This reflects our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability. In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in managing their finances. “For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual. “Our finances would have been more robust. However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. The party had to issue forms to such candidates free of charge. “The party will also use the opportunity of the NEC meeting to unveil its National Campaign Council (NCC). “As a party of innovation, our NCC is all-encompassing. It covers the Presidential, National Assembly, Governorship, and State Houses of Assembly Campaign Councils. “Our various candidates will be presented with Certificates of Return for their respective offices. “The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves. A New Nigeria is Possible. We can do it!”

title: How to Run Underdog Saluki 27B: 2-Bit Qwen3.8-27B Tool-Calling Guide
body:
In this tutorial, we work with Underdog Saluki 27B , a 7.9 GB build of Qwen3.8-27B that its makers say keeps tool calling intact at about two bits per weight and even edges out the full 54 GB model on their own 120-task benchmark. Saluki is built on ISTA-DASLab’s GSQ-RCO quantization of the same model, so we put both files side by side in stock llama.cpp. We start with the files themselves: a tensor-by-tensor diff of the two GGUF headers, then a byte-level comparison that shows whether Saluki is a remix of ISTA’s bits or a changed model. We then serve each file on one GPU, read its memory and speed, and score both on the same seeded 120 tasks from the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard, using BFCL’s own checker with strict and lenient parsing.
