title: 2027: North will give Tinubu 100 percent support – Yari
body: The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Abdulaziz Yari, has assured President Bola Tinubu of overwhelming support from northern Nigeria in the 2027 general election. Speaking on Saturday at the APC presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna, Yari said the campaign council was committed to mobilising support across the North through engagements with traditional rulers, Islamic scholars, imams and other influential stakeholders. “Northern Nigeria is 100% yours, insha Allah. This is the promise that we make, and you are going to see it in January 2027,” Yari said. The former Zamfara State governor said the campaign would focus on the administration’s performance in infrastructure, healthcare, education, human capital development and social welfare. Tinubu gave you succour when PDP chased you in 2007, Shettima tackles Atiku Atiku to Tinubu: You can’t light fire of hardship, then blame your neighbours for the smoke According to him, the APC intends to use its campaign to communicate the government’s policies and achievements to Nigerians, particularly in the northern region. Yari said engagements with traditional and religious leaders were part of efforts to explain the administration’s programmes and encourage support for Tinubu’s re-election bid. He also defended the government’s relationship with farmers, dismissing allegations that the administration had neglected the agricultural sector. The APC chieftain claimed that about two million farmers had committed to supporting Tinubu in the 2027 election. “They are lying that the government of Asiwaju Bola Tinubu does not like farmers, that you hate farmers. That is not true,” he said. Yari argued that such claims did not reflect the administration’s position on agriculture, insisting that the government was committed to addressing the concerns of farmers. He also accused critics of deploying artificial intelligence (AI) to circulate false information about the Tinubu administration, urging the campaign to counter such claims by presenting what he described as the government’s achievements. The former governor further cited developments in the foreign exchange market, Nigeria’s foreign reserves and the country’s trade balance as indicators of economic progress under Tinubu. On the exchange rate, Yari said the naira had improved from a level approaching N1,800 to about N1,300 against the dollar. He also claimed that Nigeria’s foreign reserves had increased from $3.9 billion to between $54 billion and $57.7 billion. On trade, Yari said the country’s trade balance had risen from about N44 billion in 2023 to N7.5 trillion. He presented the figures as evidence of progress under the current administration and said they would form part of the APC’s message to voters ahead of the next general election. However, the figures cited by Yari were claims made during the campaign address and would require independent verification against official economic data. Yari also pledged that the APC Presidential Campaign Council would work closely with governors across the country to mobilise voters and strengthen the party’s chances in the 2027 presidential election. He described the governors as key figures in the party’s mobilisation efforts at the state level, adding that the campaign council would complement their activities. “The governors, your commanders in the states, are doing a remarkable job. We are going to complement them, and by God’s grace, the victory is ours,” he said. Yari expressed confidence that coordinated mobilisation and the presentation of the administration’s record would help the APC secure another electoral victory in 2027.

He defeated Salifu Mohammed, who polled 352 votes, and Abdul Halim Wayo Issahaku, who obtained 147 votes. In the race for constituency secretary, Salman Faris Inusah emerged victorious with 598 votes, beating Baba Alhassan, popularly known as Mr Law, who secured 423 votes. title: Are Lebanese Shi'ites abandoning Hezbollah? Poll shows majority favor disarming group - analysis
body: Hezbollah may be facing growing criticism from within Lebanon's Shi'ite community, which has formed the backbone of its support for decades.A recent survey of Shi'ites is getting attention in regional media. As reported by Israel's KAN public broadcaster and the Lebanese Kataeb.org website, the survey, whose results emerged in mid-October, suggests that many Shi'ites are increasingly questioning the terrorist group.The main issue is whether Hezbollah should continue to cling to its arsenal. People are also questioning Hezbollah's conduct in the wars with Israel. However, this does not necessarily mean that Hezbollah is losing its influence over the community.Respondents said decisions regarding war and peace should be left to the Lebanese stateThe survey, conducted by Statistics Lebanon in September among 800 Lebanese Shi'ites, found that 66.4% supported transferring Hezbollah's weapons to the Lebanese state. Another 29.6% preferred that the terrorist organization retain its weapons. The results are significant because Hezbollah has long argued that its arsenal is essential for defending Lebanon against Israel.Roi Kais, head of the Arab world department at Israel's KAN 11, noted, “A new survey has revealed that about 66% of Lebanese Shi'ites support Hezbollah's transfer of weapons to the state, and more than 40% express anger and disappointment with its leadership.Amid growing criticism, the support networks and status the terrorist organization has given the sect still maintain its power, as long as no other entity fills the vacuum.”Of interest is the fact that Kataeb.org, the website of the Phalange Party (Kataeb Party), a political party in Lebanon, published details on it.The Christian Kataeb Party opposes Hezbollah. The website noted that 71.1% of respondents also believed that decisions about war and peace should rest exclusively with the Lebanese state. Only 5.9% believed Hezbollah's leadership should have a greater role in determining Lebanon's future.Only 16.5% of respondents had confidence in Hezbollah's ability to guarantee securityThe survey also revealed considerable confidence in the Lebanese Armed Forces. Some 78.5% expressed trust in the army, while 51.1% identified it as the institution best suited to guarantee long-term security. Only 16.5% selected Hezbollah.These findings have raised questions about Hezbollah's traditional claim to represent the security interests of Lebanon's Shi'ites. They suggest that many within the community may prefer stronger state institutions, even if they continue to identify politically or socially with Hezbollah.The survey also found that 67.4% believed Hezbollah had either failed to achieve its objectives in the war with Israel or had achieved only some of them. Another 42.1% expressed disappointment, anger or concern about Hezbollah's leadership and the consequences of the conflict. Nevertheless, 59.5% continued to express varying degrees of trust in Hezbollah, including 37.1% who reported a great deal of trust.An earlier survey presented a very different picture. In a June 10 analysis published by Israel's Institute for National Security Studies (INSS), researchers Orna Mizrahi and Moran Levanoni cited a May 2026 survey by Lebanon's Information International in which 87.5% of Shi'ite respondents opposed disarming Hezbollah, while only 7.9% supported surrendering its weapons. More than 90% opposed ties with Israel.The contrast with the September findings leads to many questions. How can people have so many different views? Is it possible that some of the surveys are biased in their questions or agendas?Mizrahi and Levanoni said that Hezbollah's influence rests on its social and economic networks, political power, and the historical marginalization of Lebanon's Shi'ites. They also noted that intimidation has discouraged opposition within the Shi'ite community.The researchers suggested that weakening Hezbollah's influence would require a stronger Lebanese army and Western and Gulf financial assistance to enable the state to replace Hezbollah's services.This illustrates the complex relationship between Hezbollah and Lebanon's Shi'ites. Hezbollah is not just a terrorist group. It has built networks of social services, financial institutions, and political influence so that it can hedge and take over the Lebanese state. Now that it is so powerful, it is hard to uproot.Many people in Lebanon have feared opposing Hezbollah over the years. For some Shi'ite families, it remains an important source of employment and assistance, even if they have to sacrifice their security due to the wars that Hezbollah has caused.Lebanese fear Hezbollah-linked facilities could become Israeli targetsKAN highlighted an example from the southern Lebanese city of Tyre, where property owners reportedly opposed opening a branch of Hezbollah-linked financial institution Al-Qard Al-Hassan in their building. They feared the branch could become a target for Israeli strikes. The branches have been targeted in the past.Hezbollah is attempting to regain support through reconstruction assistance. According to KAN, Hezbollah recently announced aid of up to $14,000 for eligible families in Beirut and its southern suburbs whose primary homes were destroyed, and up to $12,000 elsewhere.The broader question is whether dissatisfaction will translate into political change. Hezbollah has suffered significant military and leadership losses since the war began, including the killing of Hassan Nasrallah in September 2024.Yet its influence is rooted in decades of political and social organization. Lebanon did not jump at the opportunity to uproot the group in 2025. In March 2026, a new war broke out, leading to massive destruction of villages in southern Lebanon. Even today, Beirut moves at a snail's pace.The survey's results suggest that support for Hezbollah's terrorist role may be weakening even among its traditional constituency. However, unless the Lebanese state can provide security, reconstruction, and economic opportunities, the criticism won't lead to major change.

title: Ex-NAHCON chair: Over N9trn projects in Kano enough evidence for Tinubu’s re-election
body: Former Chairman of the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria (NAHCON), Professor Abdullahi Saleh Pakistan, has said President Bola Tinubu deserves a second term in office because of projects executed by his administration and what he described as improvements in security. Pakistan, who is also the leader of the Izala group in Kano State, stated this in an interview with DCL Hausa, saying the federal government had executed projects worth over N9 trillion in Kano State. He said many residents were unaware that the projects they could see around them were being executed by the federal government. The cleric said the Kano State Governor had during their meeting told them that several projects were being carried out in the state by the federal government, saying that many people don’t know that they were federal government interventions. Atiku to Tinubu: You can’t light fire of hardship, then blame your neighbours for the smoke 2027: Forget about social media news, Nigerians love Tinubu – Information minister He cited the provision of solar power systems to Northwest University, Kano, which he said cost N6 billion, despite the institution being owned by the state government. He also said the federal government provided a solar power system for Radio Kano at a cost of N2 billion. Pakistan said he would continue to promote Tinubu’s administration because he believed the president had demonstrated the capacity to govern and deserved another term to complete the projects he had started. He cited the Kaduna-Abuja highway, saying travellers had faced serious security challenges in the past but that the situation had improved under Tinubu. The cleric also defended his position on insecurity after a video circulated in which he was alleged to have said kidnapping was not a problem in northern Nigeria. He said the video had been edited, explaining that his argument was that former President Muhammadu Buhari inherited the Boko Haram insurgency, while there was no banditry Katsina, Kaduna, Sokoto and Zamfara at the time. According to him, Tinubu also inherited the kidnapping crisis and remnants of Boko Haram from the Buhari administration. He added that kidnapping became a major problem in Zamfara during Buhari’s tenure, when a former defence minister was also from the state. Pakistan said he believed insecurity had reduced significantly under Tinubu, particularly in the North-East, where he claimed reports of mass killings had become less frequent. On the 2027 presidential election, he said former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar had yet to convince him that he had a better plan than Tinubu for addressing insecurity. He said he had not seen a convincing explanation from Atiku on how he intended to tackle the problem. Pakistan also denied reports that he had threatened Nigeria may fall into violence if Tinubu was not re-elected, saying he had only argued that Tinubu before he became President had made sure that North should be allowed to complete its eight-year presidential tenure under Buhari before power returned to the South. He said Tinubu had supported Buhari’s bid for a second term despite opposition to the former president’s re-election over concerns about his health and other issues. According to him, Tinubu’s support for Buhari demonstrated his willingness to stand by the North, adding that the region should acknowledge the role he played. He recalled that Tinubu had offered Atiku an opportunity to contest under the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN) after the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) denied him its presidential ticket. Pakistan also said he had previously supported the candidacy of Nuhu Ribadu, a northern Muslim, with a southerner as his running mate. He said his support for Tinubu was also informed by his assessment of the president’s record in Lagos, where he claimed projects continued despite delays in the release of funds to the state, alongside the payment of salaries. The cleric, however, said he would not use his religious position to advance his political interests. He said he kept his religious responsibilities separate from politics and did not use the pulpit to persuade his followers to adopt his political views. He added that he did not force his children to share his political choices, stressing that every Nigerian had the right to hold and express an independent political opinion. Pakistan urged Islamic scholars to avoid harsh language when discussing political disagreements, saying people should respect one another’s political choices. He said even though his name was included in a campaign committee for Tinubu and Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, said that his participation would not conflict with his religious teachings. The cleric disclosed that he and about nine other people met Tinubu about two weeks ago for roughly two hours, during which they presented issues affecting the North and requested that the president address them if re-elected. According to him, Tinubu indicated that he was not desperate for power, money or recognition and would be willing to return to private life if Nigerians no longer wanted him in office. Pakistan said he and other supporters had also recently met the Kano State governor and were surprised by the projects presented to them. He maintained that he would not stop promoting Tinubu despite what he described as allegations against him.

title: Dream-1
body:
Give Dream-1 a new bimanual robot with parallel grippers, connect it to our API, and it can start performing tasks out of the box. No fine-tuning, no demonstrations from that robot, and no machine learning expertise required.
This is an important step toward general-purpose robot intelligence.
Today, Dream Labs is also coming out of stealth with $90M in seed funding and making Dream-1 available to people all around the world through a public API.
Dream-1 controls robots it has never seen, on tasks it was never shown, in places it has never been, from $3/hour.
For decades, robotics has been stuck in a chicken-and-egg problem: a robot needs to be useful before people want to buy it, but making it useful requires data from that exact robot, and that data only exists once enough people start using it. Dream-1 is our first step toward breaking that loop.
Self-driving found a way around this cold-start problem. Cars were useful from day one with zero autonomy, so millions of people drove them every day and generated the data needed to train increasingly capable models. Most other robots never had that advantage.
First, robot hardware is getting cheap enough to reach far more people. A capable bimanual arm setup can now cost as little as $2k 1 .
Second, a robot may no longer need a large dataset of its own before it can be useful. If a model can generalize zero-shot to unseen environments, tasks, and even robots, a new robot can start with useful capabilities.
Put those together and the flywheel can finally start. Cheaper hardware puts more robots into the world. Generalizable models make those robots useful earlier. Useful robots generate more data, and that data makes the models better for the next robot.
Robot hardware is getting cheap faster than anyone expected. See the robots above, where 7 semi-humanoid robots cost less than $15k, a price tier that barely existed a year ago. At the far end of the price curve, Hugging Face's $399 Microduck sold more than 10,000 units within 4 days of its launch in late August 2 . We believe the robotics take-off will start with robots like these.
Wheels, two arms, parallel grippers; a tier that barely existed a year ago.
That's because their buyers are consumers, prosumers, and small teams, not enterprises. An enterprise buyer is making a spreadsheet decision. If the robot doesn't beat a person on cost, speed, or reliability, it doesn't get bought; that's a high bar to clear. Consumers are different. 10,000+ people just paid $399 within 4 days for a robot whose main job is to be delightful and cute: it walks, waddles, and roller-skates. Somewhere between that and a fully capable home robot is a sweet spot, a robot affordable enough to be an easy yes and useful enough to earn its place in the home. Once robots hit that point, we think adoption starts to compound, and every robot in a home becomes a source of new training data. Imagine two Microducks folding your laundry, using their beaks as grippers.
In February 2026, our team released DreamZero, the paper that introduced World Action Models 3 . Since then, the community has adopted WAMs as one of the most promising paradigms in robot learning. At that time, the most surprising result for us was when after post-training DreamZero on just 30 minutes of YAM robot data, we saw it generalize zero-shot to tasks it had never seen. That kind of generalization used to take hundreds or even thousands of hours of embodiment-specific data. If 30 minutes of data from a given robot was enough to transfer general-purpose task knowledge to that robot, breaking the chicken-and-egg loop no longer looked impossible. Combined with the hardware wave above, the timing felt right. That's when we decided to start Dream Labs.
After six months of building, we're excited to share a new research breakthrough that was only made possible through world action models: early signs of zero-shot embodiment generalization.
Dream-1 is our first World Action Model available through a public API that can be used all around the world. Out of the box, it can control unseen robots for unseen tasks in unseen environments.

We want generalizable robotics to be accessible to anyone with a robot, not just large labs. So we designed Dream-1 to be as close to plug-and-play as possible. Connect your robot, point it at the API, and run. No machine learning background is needed to get started. Every week, we run internal hackathons to keep time-to-deploy as short as possible. Getting started tutorial
Dream-1 can zero-shot generalize to many bimanual, parallel-gripper robots. Here are some we've tested. It can even control the original PR2, a general-purpose bimanual research robot released 18 years ago. Note that no embodiment-specific data was used to get these rollouts.

Put the fruit that is not the kiwi in the basket
Pick up the mango and place it in the bowl
Pick up all markers one by one and put into black pencil holder using both arms
This is one of the first reported zero-shot generalizations to completely unseen robot embodiments. 4 If you have a bimanual parallel-gripper robot, try prompting Dream-1 and let us know how it goes. Zero-shot performance depends partly on your robot's inverse kinematics (IK) solver, so we've written a guide to help you get the most out of it. IK guide . Performance also varies across robots. Below, we break down zero-shot performance in simulation and on real robots.
Below, we explain how zero-shot embodiment generalization works and where it falls short. We then show how one-shot embodiment learning closes that gap.
Two ways to control a robot: joints or end-effectors. Robot policies commonly output joint angles, which ties them to one specific robot's body. Dream-1 can do the same for the embodiments it supports natively, but it can also predict end-effector (EEF) poses: where each gripper should be and whether it should be open or closed. Every robot with two arms and parallel grippers shares that EEF action space, and its own IK solver turns the poses into joint commands. That shared interface gives Dream-1 a common way to command robots it has never seen, but on its own it isn't enough to make zero-shot transfer work.
Why does this work? Dream-1 sees the world through three cameras: a head view and a wrist view on each arm. Prior work on the Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) showed that policies can transfer zero-shot across robot arms when every arm uses the same gripper and the policy relies only on wrist cameras 5 . From the wrist's point of view, the robots look identical. But that shortcut has a hard limit. It only works when the gripper hardware matches exactly, and it gives up the head camera's view of the whole scene.
World Action Models remove that limit. A WAM learns to predict video and actions together, so controlling a robot and imagining what that robot will do are the same problem. And every robot shows up the same way: as pixels. The head camera sees a UMI gripper, a two-finger gripper or an arm Dream-1 has never met as nothing more than shapes moving through a scene, which makes video the one representation every robot type shares. If Dream-1 can predict what a robot will look like as it completes a task, it can produce the actions that get it there. That’s why it can control robots with grippers that look nothing like UMI’s, and even entirely new bodies seen through the head camera.
Predicting EEF trades some control for generality. Compared with joint-angle prediction with per-embodiment adaptation:
Ahead of launch, Robocurve 6 , a Public Benefit Corporation that measures and reports frontier robotics capabilities to the public, evaluated Dream-1 independently. Their report, above, shows Dream-1 is better, faster and cheaper: a new Pareto frontier for robot control. It scores above the next best models, Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon, at 16x lower cost per task attempt than Gemini 4 Argon and 1.7x faster than the fastest LLM, GPT-6 Astra. While current LLMs excel at planning, robots still require a fast, general System 1 to act, and that is what Dream-1 is built to be.
How much does it cost to run Dream-1 ? We want you to know exactly what to expect before you try it. Running the model costs just $3 per hour for Dream-1 , or $2 per hour for Dream-1-flash. Each call to the model returns 1.6 seconds of actions, so an hour is 2,250 calls: about $0.0013 an action for Dream-1 , and $0.0009 for Dream-1-flash.
Everything above the hourly cost is yours to keep.
Across tasks. We break Dream-1 ’s performance down into eight task categories, from what it handles well to where it still struggles.
Fine-tune for your task with FaaS. If Dream-1 falls short on a task you care about, you don’t have to wait for our next release. Collect some data on your own robot, run it through FaaS, and get a custom model built for that task.
We want anyone with a robot to work like a forward-deployed engineer: find a task someone needs done, collect a bit of data, adapt Dream-1 to it, and deploy. If people will pay for what your robot does, you keep everything above the hourly cost.
It will make mistakes, and it has not been validated for safety-critical use. Please test it in controlled settings, and take extra care whenever a robot is running near people. If you see unsafe behavior, please report it to safety@dreamlabs.ai .
When zero-shot isn't enough, we fine-tune Dream-1 for your robot. We call this Fine-tuning-as-a-Service (FaaS).
Here's what that looks like in practice: timelapses of data collection on two of our partners' robots, 5 minutes each.
After adapting on just those 5 minutes, the difference shows side-by-side with the zero-shot run. Dream-1 now understands a bit better the affordance and kinematics of the robot.
Some embodiments sit much further from what Dream-1 already knows, and closing a gap that large takes more of the robot’s own data. Dexmate with Sharpa dexterous hands grasps with hands in place of grippers, and took 77 minutes of its data. On YAM, we swapped in different end effectors for this task, a compliant gripper and a modified knife gripper, and it took 98 minutes of data.
Dexmate , Sharpa dexterous hands, 77 minutes of data
Pick bread from toaster and place on plate
YAM , compliant gripper and modified knife gripper, 98 minutes of data
Across twelve robots from our FaaS beta partners, fine-tuning lifts the language-following score on ten of them:
One-shot adaptation still outperforms zero-shot, so a gap remains. Closing it is one of our main goals: the better zero-shot gets, the closer any new robot comes to working out of the box.
Dream-1 today is a manipulation policy for bimanual robots with parallel grippers. It’s a starting point. We believe a strong, general robot foundation model can extend to mobile manipulators, dexterous hands, and bodies we haven't imagined yet, opening up many more of the things people actually want robots to do. Robotics won't be solved on day one, and Dream-1 has real limits, which we've tried to show transparently above.
Robotics is still stuck in a difficult loop: every new robot or task demands new data and a custom policy, often with limited generalization. With Dream-1 as a robotics API, we want to break that loop and put robot intelligence into more people's hands, so everyday users, not only researchers, can discover new applications for general-purpose robot intelligence.
If you're building robots or putting them to work on real tasks, we want Dream-1 to be the fastest way to make them useful. Tell us what you're working on.

title: Ellen White Foundation brings free breast cancer screening to Bono East police women
body: In a heartwarming display of commitment to women’s health, the Ellen White Sustainable Foundation, in partnership with the Awat Foundation and the Police Ladies Association, has provided free breast cancer screening to nearly 100 female police officers across the Bono East Region. The screening exercise, held at the Techiman Divisional Police Command, formed part of efforts to promote early detection and awareness of breast cancer among women in uniform. The programme was held under the theme: “Investing in Women’s Health, Investing in Stronger Communities.” Mrs. Ellen White Opoku, founder of the Ellen White Sustainable Foundation and a 2023 Joy Impact Makers Award recipient, said the initiative was born out of the need to reach officers who cannot easily access health facilities due to their busy schedules. “This exercise is to help bring the screening to the doorstep of the police, who are unable to attend to health facilities for the same due to their busy work schedules,” she noted. Police Ladies Association Weighs In ASP Beatrice Okrah, Crime Officer for the Jema District Police Command and a regional executive member of the Police Ladies Association, commended the organizers and encouraged women to prioritize their health. She said the time had come for women to own up and get themselves screened to know their statuses and be treated when diagnosed with the condition. “The time has come for women to own up and get themselves screened to know their statuses and be treated when diagnosed with the condition,” she stated. ASP Okrah added that the awareness talk had been helpful in creating awareness about what the condition is, equipping participants with knowledge to share with colleagues and family members. “The talk has been helpful in creating awareness about what the condition is,” she noted. Service to Support Officers Diagnosed In a reassuring message to personnel, ASP Okrah disclosed that officers found to have the cancer will be taken care of by the Police Service. She explained that the welfare of officers remains a priority, and those diagnosed through the screening will receive the necessary support and care from the Service. A Community Investment The event reflects a growing push to make healthcare accessible to women in security services, who often sacrifice personal wellness for public duty. By investing in the health of these officers, organizers say the ripple effect will be felt across entire communities. The Ellen White Sustainable Foundation has indicated its commitment to sustaining such initiatives, with plans to reach more districts in the Bono East Region and beyond.

title: GH¢49.72m S.A. evacuation: Asafo-Adjei says government’s figures do not add up
body: The Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Nana Asafo-Adjei Ayeh, has raised concerns over the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa, insisting that the figures presented by the government do not add up. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, the opposition lawmaker questioned the credibility of the expenditure, arguing that the inability to satisfactorily establish the number of beneficiaries raises serious concerns about the entire evacuation exercise. “I am at this point confident in everything in me that the figures don’t add up. If you cannot even establish the 1,964, then there is a problem with everything you did,” he stated. Mr Asafo-Adjei maintained that the documents presented to justify the expenditure must be subjected to thorough scrutiny, stressing that the details should support the government’s public explanations. According to him, the Minority’s concerns are based on the contents of the available documentation rather than political disagreements or unrelated issues. “The content of the document is what matters. The devil is always in the details, and that is what we are looking at, and it doesn’t support your communication,” he said. The Deputy Ranking Member emphasised that his focus remains on establishing the facts surrounding the expenditure and ensuring that the government provides satisfactory explanations for the amount spent and the reported number of evacuees. He rejected suggestions that the Minority was diverting attention from the substantive issues, insisting that his interventions have consistently centred on accountability and transparency. “If you listen to the Minority, particularly me, I have never majored in any tangential. I am focused on this matter, and I want to get to the logical conclusion of this matter,” he stressed. His comments come amid scrutiny of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs over the reported GH¢49.72 million expenditure on the evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa.

title: Ghana’s U-15 Boys thrash Uzbekistan 4-1 as Abdul Aziz Issah and Jerry Owusu hit brace each
body: The National U-15 Boys team made a flying start to the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Uzbekistan in their opening Group W match on Saturday. Abdul Aziz Issah and Jerry Owusu were the heroes for Ghana, scoring a brace each to secure all three points in Azerbaijan. Ghana dominated proceedings from the blast of the whistle, showing flair, composure and attacking intent against their Asian opponents. Aziz Issah opened the scoring before doubling Ghana’s advantage, while Jerry Owusu added two more goals to put the game beyond the reach of Uzbekistan, who managed a consolation strike late in the game. The win gives Ghana a strong start in Group W, which also includes Myanmar, Guam, Bahamas and Kazakhstan. Ghana will next face Myanmar and Guam on Sunday, before wrapping up the group phase against Bahamas and Kazakhstan on Monday. The FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival, part of FIFA’s Talent Development Scheme, is aimed at giving every talent a chance to showcase their skills on the world stage.

title: Russia, Ukraine fulfil their commitments toward Alyoshki ceasefire — Russian ombudswoman
body:
MOSCOW, October 24. /TASS/. Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said both Russia and Ukraine honor their commitments toward a humanitarian mission in Alyoshki in the Kherson Region.
"[I and Ukrainian ombudsman Dmitry Lubinets] discussed earlier coordinated details [toward a humanitarian mission in Alyoshki], everything is proceeding in accordance with the arrangements that have been agreed. Both sides are fulfilling their commitments," she wrote on Max channel.
Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov on September 21 described the humanitarian situation in Alyoshki as critical. Food and medicines cannot be delivered to the city amid Ukrainian shelling and drone attacks. More than 1,200 artillery and drone strikes had been delivered by Ukrainian troops on Alyoshki over the week, the district’s head Ruslan Khomenko said on October 19.
On Friday, the White House broke the news about a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in Alyoshki. The localized ceasefire will come into effect on October 29. The sides agreed to cease hostilities in Alyoshki to "allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway," the White House said. An independent US media organization will assist and document the actions of both Russia and Ukraine during the process.
Chief of the General Staff of the Russian Army Valery Gerasimov, in turn, announced that Russian forces will enforce a localized ceasefire in the Kherson direction at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time (1:00 a.m. GMT) on October 27 to allow for a humanitarian operation near Alyoshki.

title: Russian airstrikes on Sloviansk injure two people and damage buildings
body:
According to Ukrinform, Vadym Liakh, head of the Sloviansk City Military Administration, reported this on Facebook .
“Today, October 24, at around 5:00 p.m., the enemy carried out airstrikes on Sloviansk using FAB-250 and FAB-500 bombs. Currently, two people are known to have been wounded. Both have received medical attention. High-rise buildings in various parts of the city, two educational institutions, an administrative building, an infrastructure facility, a café, and cars have been damaged or destroyed,” Liakh wrote.
As reported by Ukrinform, the mandatory evacuation of children has been extended to the entire territory of the Kramatorsk and Sloviansk communities.

title: Houthis launch attacks on Aramco facilities, airports in Saudi Arabia
body:
DOHA, October 24. /TASS/. Yemen’s Ansar Allah rebel group (Houthis) has delivered attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities, an oil pipeline, several airports and a military base in Saudi Arabia, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on Saturday.
"[Houthi] armed forces <...> have carried out seven military operations using ballistic missiles and drones," Saree wrote on his Telegram channel. According to him, Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu, an oil refinery in Rabigh, crude pumping stations and the East-West oil pipeline came under attack. In addition, the Houthi spokesman claimed, Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Najran Airport, an air base near Khamis Mushait were targeted. The attack on the airport in Dammam caused a halt to air traffic, Saree said.
The actions were in response to attacks by the Saudi-led coalition, Saree explained. Over the past 24 hours, the alliance "delivered 100 airstrikes" on Yemen, including the capital Sanaa, he added.

title: One killed, four others injured in Ukrainian attacks on Russia’s Bryansk Region
body:
BRYANSK, October 24. /TASS/. One was killed and four others were injured in the Bryansk Region as a result of Ukrainian attacks on Saturday, Yegor Kovalchuk, governor of the bordering Russian region, wrote on Max channel.
"A 65-year-old man died from the injuries sustained in an enemy UAV drone attack on a lake near the village of Rubezhnoye in the Klimovo District," he wrote.
Also, a Ukrainian UAV hit the Pozitiv shopping mall in the urban locality of Klimovo, injuring a 21-year-old young man and a 40-year-old female employee of a drugstore. A 53-year-old resident of the Klimovo District was injured as a result of a kamikaze drone attack on a passenger car. And a 39-year-old local was injured as a residential building in Klintsy was attacked, the governor said.

title: 2026 U17 WWC: Black Maidens book knockout spot with win over Canada
body: Ghana produced a great second half performance to advance into the knockout stages of the ongoing U-17 Women’s World Cup. The Black Maidens defeated Canada 2-0 in their final group game of the tournament to finish second in Group C after a troubling start to the tournament. Nana Joe Adarkwa’s side came into the final group game knowing only a win was enough to get them into the next phase of the competition. Despite a strong start to the game, the Maidens always rushed their final third decision making, leaving them with no goals after 45 minutes despite 13 attempts. After the recess, Ghana continued to create chances in the game with Gloria Ameaa and Jessica Appiah posing dangers to the Canadian defence but both players were unable to find the back of the net. Adarkwa called on his bench halfway through the second half, bringing on Linda Achiaa and Christiana Ashiaku. Those changes yielded results as Achiaa scored with her first touch after the ball deflected off the crossbar, opening the scoring in the game. In the closing stages of the encounter, Ashiaku doubled the lead for the Black Maidens with a brilliant strike, lobbing it over the goalkeeper to wrap up the victory. The win sees Ghana finish their group campaign in second place with four points, behind Brazil who claimed seven points from three games. Ghana also advance into the round of 16 on their return to the global stage at the U-17 level following their comeback from a two-edition ban.

title: Drone debris found in Latvia
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Latvian National Armed Forces reported this on social media platform X .
“On October 24, a foreign unmanned aerial vehicle was discovered in the Liepne Parish of the Aluksne District; it likely entered Latvian airspace on October 18,” the post states.
After receiving a report of a sound resembling an explosion, the National Armed Forces, in cooperation with the State Police, began searching for the UAV’s probable crash site. Two days later, the search operations were suspended because the information available at that time was insufficient to confirm the actual circumstances of the incident.
The circumstances of the incident are currently under investigation; an internal review has also been ordered to assess the course of the incident and related circumstances.
As a result of the incident, no civilians were injured, no civilian infrastructure was damaged, and no further threats were identified.
As reported by Ukrinform, the Latvian State Land Service, in collaboration with the State Fire and Rescue Service, has compiled information on shelters throughout Latvia in a single location and created a map for the publi c.

title: NDC constituency election records impressive turnout at Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro.
body: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) constituency executive elections have recorded an impressive turnout at the Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro constituency in the Greater Accra Region. The elections, which started in the early hours of today, are approaching their final stage, with delegates arriving in large numbers to cast their votes. Voting is taking place at the Astroturf in Tuba, a suburb of Ngleshie Amanfro, where a large crowd of delegates, party supporters, and observers has gathered. The exercise is being conducted by officials of the Electoral Commission (EC), while members of the party’s election committee are coordinating and monitoring the process to ensure a smooth and transparent election. A number of aspirants are contesting various constituency executive positions, including Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Treasurer, Organiser, Deputy Organiser, Communications Officer, Women’s Organiser, Deputy Women’s Organiser, Youth Organiser, Deputy Youth Organiser and Zongo Caucus Coordinator, in line with the party’s structure. The atmosphere at the venue has been generally calm and orderly, with security personnel present to maintain law and order. Some delegates who spoke to reporters expressed satisfaction with the conduct of the polls so far, describing the process as peaceful and transparent. They said the high turnout reflects the enthusiasm of members to elect competent leaders who will strengthen the party at the grassroots level ahead of the 2028 general elections. Party officials in the constituency said they expect the elections to end peacefully and called on all aspirants and their supporters to accept the outcome in good faith and work together to advance the interest of the NDC in Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro. Counting of ballots is expected to begin immediately after voting ends, with winners to be declared by the Electoral Commission officials.

title: American embassies tighten security as Iran threat warnings intensify ahead of U.S. midterm elections
body:
U.S. embassy officials were on heightened alert around the Middle East as new reports said Iran is in the "advanced stages" of planning attacks against Americans Friday.
A memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said agencies received intelligence that Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel" in the region, according to a New York Times report , and that the threats applied to "certain other countries" as well.
The warnings come after the U.S. ordered non-emergency government employees to leave Saudi Arabia this week, as attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis have worsened and the broader war between the U.S. and Tehran nears its eighth month.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired by the group, aimed towards Taif and Yanbu.
Despite rising tensions, an Iranian official told The Associated Press on Saturday that Tehran remains open to talks with the U.S. under the former Pakistan-brokered deal that was agreed to in June.
Reza Amiri Moghadam, Iran's ambassador to Islamabad, said Iranian officials are prepared to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the Trump administration lifts its naval blockade, AP reported, but he said Washington has rebuffed the proposal. Later in the day, Iranian state media denied the report.
The Trump administration has vowed to put off military strikes on Iran after the midterm elections on Nov. 3, as the fallout from the war in Iran has caused a major disruption in the U.S. economy — with inflation and affordability the top concerns for voters who will decide control of Congress early next month.
Rising Middle East tensions sent oil prices soaring this week. Benchmark Brent crude futures topped $116 a barrel, a six-month high . U.S. West Texas Intermediate rose 3.8% to settle over $103 a barrel.

title: GH¢49.72m S.A. evacuation cost: Flight charter price comparisons alone can’t prove overpricing – IMANI Associate
body: An Associate of IMANI Centre for Policy and Education (CPE), Kay Cudjoe, has cautioned against drawing conclusions of overpricing based solely on comparisons between the reported cost of chartering aircraft for the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa and alternative charter prices. His comments follow public discussions surrounding the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa, including a reported aircraft charter cost of GH¢27,180,700. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, 2026, Mr Cudjoe stressed the need for a careful assessment of the circumstances surrounding the charter arrangements before determining whether the expenditure was excessive. According to him, although comparisons with alternative charter prices may raise legitimate questions about the expenditure, they are insufficient on their own to establish overpricing. “It is important to establish a very important part of the conversation…the area where we should be most careful is where the reported charter cost of 27,180,700. “I think public comparisons with alternative charter prices cannot prove overpricing unless we look at the issues concerning aircraft charter,” he stated.

title: GH¢49.72m S.A. evacuation: Nobody slept in a bus; it cannot be true – Benjamin Quashie
body: Ghana’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Benjamin Quashie, has rejected claims that some Ghanaians evacuated from the country slept in buses before boarding their chartered flights, insisting that accommodation was arranged for them in hotels. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, against the backdrop of the GH¢49.72 million spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa, Mr Quashie said the mission ensured that evacuees travelling from distant provinces were accommodated before their flights. “Let me move to a few of the issues that have been raised because it bothers on the individual evacuees in South Africa. The first one is to state that not a single individual slept in a bus; it was impossible,” he said. He explained that evacuees were brought from areas including the Western Cape and Eastern Cape, as well as East London, and that the buses used to transport them to Pretoria were paid for by the mission. According to him, the evacuees were taken to hotels before their flights, with arrangements made to ensure they had time to rest and refresh themselves. “When you look at the first three flights, the chartered flights, we brought them in from the provinces. Before they got here, we had gotten hotels,” he said. Mr Quashie added that the arrangements were designed to reduce costs while ensuring that passengers arrived in Pretoria ahead of their scheduled departures. “So because we wanted to save costs, if you are supposed to travel on Wednesday, we get you on a bus on Tuesday. So that when you get to Pretoria, all we want you to do is that you spend one day in the hotel, get yourself refreshed, we supply food and other things for you,” he explained. He said the evacuees were subsequently transported from their hotels to the airport for their flights. Mr Quashie challenged anyone claiming to have slept in a bus during the evacuation to come forward, while acknowledging that some journeys to Pretoria could take several hours. “I am daring anyone who comes out and says that they slept in a bus,” he said. He, however, clarified that passengers travelling from places such as the Northern Cape and Cape Town could have slept during the long bus journeys to Pretoria. “The only way they would have slept in a bus is if you are coming from Northern Cape and Northern Cape is 12 hours or 13 hours or Cape Town, and you are coming and it is about 10 hours. Of course, you will sleep in the bus before you get to Pretoria. If that is what they mean by sleeping in the bus,” he said. The evacuation of the 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa has come under scrutiny following reports on the GH¢49.72 million spent on the exercise.

title: Google Quietly Updates Privacy Policy to Let Gmail and Photos Data Feed Ads
body:
Google has carved out an exception to its long-standing promise not to use Gmail, Drive, and Google Photos content for advertising, quietly revising its privacy policy so that data from those apps can help personalize ads when users connect it to the company’s AI features.
The change, which took effect Oct. 16 and was first spotted by Android Authority , adds a conditional clause to a pledge Google has made for years.
The updated policy now reads that Google doesn’t show personalized ads based on content from Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos “unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads.”
The catch hinges on Personal Intelligence, Google’s push to make its AI tools more useful by letting features like AI Mode in Search and Gemini draw on a user’s own data.
Connecting Gmail, Drive or Photos to those tools delivers more tailored answers, such as surfacing a hotel reservation buried in an inbox. But under the revised wording, that same connected data can now also inform which ads a person sees.
Google stressed the limits. Content from the three services still isn’t used for ad targeting by default, advertisers don’t get access to the contents of anyone’s Gmail, Drive or Photos, and the company says it won’t share personally identifying details without permission.
In practice, that means Google isn’t scanning private emails and photos wholesale to sell ads, but users who opt into its AI conveniences may be trading some ad privacy for them.
Users can opt out by disconnecting the apps under Connected Content apps in their Google Account’s Data & privacy settings, or by turning off personalized recommendations, though Android Authority noted that previously collected data may linger in a user’s Search history even after disconnecting.
The quiet rollout echoes recent Google privacy posturing around its AI ambitions. As Decrypt reported in May, Google’s Chrome browser began silently installing a multi-gigabyte on-device AI model on users’ computers, and separately removed a privacy claim tied to its Gemini Nano model , both moves that drew scrutiny over how the company handles user data as it races to embed AI across its products.

title: Can Undersea Volcanoes Power Cities? A Seattle Startup Just Took the First Step
body: A geothermal startup aiming to source energy directly from undersea volcanoes just hit a major milestone that could bring round-the-clock clean energy to cities on the northwest coast of the United States and serve as a critical proof of concept for other regions, with particular relevance for the other 14 countries situated along the Pacific Ring of Fire.  Seattle-based energy startup Endurance Energy just announced that it successfully created net-positive energy from its underwater geothermal plant in a world first. The company successfully demonstrated a full operations cycle from drilling to electricity generation in a major breakthrough for next-gen clean energy tech. Although the demonstration created less than 10 seconds of positive energy production, the implications of those ten seconds are hard to overstate.  "On Sept. 27, we put a power plant on an active underwater volcano and made power," said Andrew Redd, founder and CEO of Endurance Energy. "This historic milestone is also our first end-to-end test. We now know, firsthand, what works at depth, what needs to be improved, and how to build the next system for sustained commercial generation."  Not only does the brief achievement serve as a critical proof of concept for the technology, the project also "showed that operators in Seattle could control the system from an offshore location, remotely starting and stopping the equipment, monitoring temperatures and pressures, and collecting data without being underwater," according to a recent report from Interesting Engineering.  Putting a geothermal plant on the seafloor presents some key benefits as compared to traditional models, but also yields critical trade-offs. The cool water of the seafloor acts as a natural cooling system, and the pressure of the water acts as a natural pressurizer that allows for the plants to be designed compactly, according to Redd. The company's next milestone, building a larger 2-megawatt commercial generator in the Pacific island nation of Tonga, will be a test of these more productive, but still compact, generator systems.  "The 2 MW commercial generators will be about the size of a shipping container, and we are deploying up to six of these generators [to] offshore Tonga," Redd told Ars Technica. "The physical footprint of this project will be relatively small."  However, building a geothermal plant underwater presents extra challenges that could incur prohibitively high upfront costs as compared to on-land models. "It's probably technically feasible, but it would undoubtedly be more expensive than to do it on land," Roland Horne, professor of energy science & engineering at Stanford University, recently told Ars Technica.  Underwater geothermal is just one of many next-gen geothermal technologies being developed and tested today, as the urgency of shoring up new, clean, and indigenous forms of energy production becomes an ever-more urgent imperative against the backdrop of the artificial intelligence boom. Big Tech companies are bullish about investing in enhanced geothermal energy as part of their clean energy portfolios, while the Trump administration has also thrown its weight behind the sector's development.  Indeed, one of the biggest benefits of geothermal energy is that it is one of the vanishingly few clean energy technologies that enjoy broad bipartisan support. By borrowing drilling techniques from the oil and gas industry, the United States could position itself as a global leader in advanced geothermal energy in coming years, a goal which aligns itself with the decarbonization priorities of the left and the energy dominance aims of the right.  "The U.S. has a number of different superpowers, and putting holes in the ground and taking things out of those holes is one of them  and doing so more economically and more efficiently than basically any other place on Earth," Drew Nelson, vice president of Project InnerSpace, was quoted by Cipher News.  Accordingly, the Department of Energy has high hopes for the emerging technology, estimating that enhanced geothermal projects could provide an impressive 90 gigawatts of clean energy in the United States by 2050, or about enough to power at least 65 million homes.  By Haley Zaremba for Oilprice.com

title: The Polyglot's Dilemma: Conformance Testing a Dozen Specs in as Many Languages
body:
MongoDB engineers juggling many implementations of many specs.
At MongoDB, we develop a dozen client libraries (“drivers”) in a dozen programming languages. A few wrap shared cores written in C or Java, but mostly they’re rewrites in their target languages: the JavaScript Driver is pure JavaScript, the Rust Driver is pure Rust, and so on. Building the drivers this way is a big commitment. Lots of database companies just write their client in C and make thin wrappers in various languages. Our way is harder but, in my opinion, better. Our drivers are easier to install, their APIs are more idiomatic in each language, and they participate normally in each language’s runtime: its threading model or async loop, its garbage collection, etc. This is only possible because we keep developing native drivers in each language.
But then, how do we ensure all our drivers’ behaviors and APIs are consistent? Or, that they’re appropriately consistent or inconsistent, according to the conventions of their target languages? Obviously, Python methods are snake_cased and Java methods are camelCased, but MongoDB drivers should have the same basic API in all languages, spelling aside. Node concurrency is async and C concurrency uses threads, but the meaning of causal consistency should be the same in all drivers.
I joined MongoDB as a Python driver engineer in November 2011. Looking back through my emails, I see that we were intensely debating how to standardize our drivers from the moment I arrived. Some engineers were writing Java Driver tests in Cucumber, a “behavior-driven development” syntax, like this:
My very first task at MongoDB was researching whether we could write test-runners for these Cucumber tests in Python, Ruby, and our other languages. I instantly learned that my second task was dealing with my colleagues’ revulsion to Cucumber’s syntax. One engineer wrote that if we replaced his handwritten tests with Cucumber, he’d “have no part in doing it or supporting the resulting disaster.” (I clarified that we weren’t going to replace tests, only complement them.) Our founder Eliot Horowitz encouraged us to make a shared test suite, but he thought Cucumber specifically was “hilarious.”
We gave up on Cucumber. A few years later, I was involved in a new feature, specifying how drivers measure and respond to network latency . I observed that the English spec of the feature could be misunderstood, and some drivers implemented it differently. Once again, Eliot proposed a shared test suite. This time, we avoided Cucumber. We started to develop a custom test language on top of YAML instead. For details, see my conference talk or blog post about YAML tests , with Samantha Ritter.
Testing drivers with YAML is one of the most successful projects I’ve ever been part of. In the 11 years (nearly 12 now) since we started writing YAML tests, the MongoDB drivers have all converged to a shared API and shared set of behaviors. They’re as similar as they should be, with consciously-chosen variations to fit each language’s idioms and conventions. I left the Drivers team a while ago , but the specification and YAML testing process is going stronger than ever. They now have a Unified Test Format, built on YAML, that can test drivers’ conformance to a dozen different specs. The specs cover how drivers read and write documents, how they retry failed commands, how they start and end transactions, how they encrypt private fields client-side, and lots of other intricate behaviors. Nearly 1,500 YAML files ensure that all these independent code bases implement the same protocols.
Here’s an example of a modern Unified Test Format file. It tests that a driver auto-retries the update command after a network error:
For each of our drivers, we implement a test runner which can interpret this syntax and call APIs on the driver being tested. The test runner creates two MongoClient objects: the MongoClient under test, and an “internal” MongoClient for sending side-channel commands to the server (see the failPoint below).
schemaVersion tells the test runner which features the file uses, so an old runner can skip a file it wouldn’t understand instead of failing it. We use JSON Schema to check each YAML test has the proper syntax for its version of the Unified Test Format.
runOnRequirements tells the test runner to skip the file unless the MongoDB server deployment matches—here, a replica set running MongoDB 4.4 or later.
createEntities builds an entity map : a client, a database, and a collection, named with YAML anchors ( &client ) so later operations can refer to them by alias ( *client ). This not only avoids repetition, it means YAML test runners can store and retrieve objects in the entity map, like assigning objects to variables in a real programming language.
initialData puts one document in the collection before the test starts. Then the operations run in order:
This example shows lots of exciting features! The Unified Test Format lets all the drivers share a test suite. We can prove they all act the same by publishing tests they must all pass. We can update a spec, and force all the drivers to comply with the change, by publishing changes to the shared tests and watching all outdated drivers fail.
Additionally, this test is checking hidden behaviors that ordinary integration tests couldn’t observe. We use failPoint to make the server close the connection, so we can exercise the driver’s auto-retry logic. From the API surface, retries are invisible—that’s the point. But this YAML test triggers a retry and tests three hidden behaviors: the driver retries exactly once, it marks the server type Unknown , and it clears its connection pool. We could assert the entire contents of the two update commands the driver sends on the wire, if we wanted to.
The Unified Test Format has saved us tens of thousands of lines of code over the years, and it’s probably saved us from scores of awful bugs. It enforces spec conformance so when you use MongoDB from several programming languages, you get a consistent API and predictable behavior.
Here are some numbers, starting with code savings. When we created the unified format in 2020, we generalized the YAML test format used by lots of different specs into one format to rule them all. Seven drivers replaced their per-spec test runners with a single Unified Test Format runner, and every one of these came out smaller. We cut 22,000 lines total. The Java Driver alone deleted 6,000 lines of test-runner code.
Meanwhile, we added more and more conformance tests. The Unified Test Format corpus went from about a thousand lines in 2021 to 124,000 today. The biggest jumps are when we mechanically ported tests from per-spec YAML formats into the unified format.
Do the tests actually prevent bugs? We identified a natural experiment: Five drivers implemented the CRUD spec years before they adopted its YAML tests, which gives us a before and after to compare. We used Claude to classify every resolved ticket in those drivers—6,836 of them—and counted the ones that were genuine violations of the CRUD Spec. Four of the five drivers had a lower bug rate after adopting YAML tests.
Node.js is the embarrassing one: its bug rate went up . Years after it adopted the YAML tests we discovered that its BulkWriteResult and BulkWriteError classes were inconsistent with the specs and the other drivers. Its test runner hadn’t asserted their contents rigorously enough. The Driver Team filed a bunch of bugs and changed the field names over two major releases.
The IEEE International Symposium on Software Reliability Engineering (ISSRE) just accepted my paper about YAML testing, “The Polyglot’s Dilemma: Conformance Testing a Dozen Specs in as Many Languages.” Driver engineers Jeremy Mikola and Jeff Yemin are my coauthors. The paper has more detail about the history of our YAML tests, and it has plenty of stats and lessons. Check it out, it’s only 6 pages .

title: Africa must take control of its resources and security future – Mahama
body: President John Dramani Mahama has warned that foreign powers are seeking strategic influence and access to Africa’s natural resources, urging African leaders to unite to protect the continent’s sovereignty and security. He cautioned that without a coordinated response, Africa risks surrendering control of its political and security future to external interests. Speaking at the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, on Saturday, October 24, Mr Mahama said competition over natural resources, weak governance and foreign interference were contributing to conflicts across the continent. He cited conflicts in Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where fighting is linked to competition over valuable resources, including gold, coltan and cobalt. “External powers, from the East, the West, and the Gulf, are actively seeking leverage, access, and client states on our soil,” he said. “Let me be clear: Africa is not an empty chessboard for foreign powers to play their games. We are not spectators. But unless we consciously decide to take up the pen and write our own script, someone else will write it for us, and we will not like how the story ends.” Mr Mahama said the continent’s security challenges were also being worsened by governance failures in Somalia, the marginalisation of young people in Mozambique’s gas-rich Cabo Delgado region, and divisions between the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the Alliance of Sahel States. He warned that such divisions weakened regional cooperation and undermined collective efforts to address threats to peace and stability. The President also drew attention to the growing use of commercial drones by armed groups, warning that the relatively cheap and accessible technology was making conflicts increasingly deadly. “Armed groups and non-state actors have mastered the commercial drone—cheap, accessible, and deadly. In Sudan alone, these low-cost flying weapons accounted for the vast majority of civilian casualties early this year,” he added. Mr Mahama called on African leaders to strengthen cooperation, improve governance and take greater control of the continent’s natural resources and security priorities. He warned that failure to pursue a united approach would leave African countries increasingly vulnerable to external influence and prevent them from determining their own future.

title: 2026 Ruby on Rails Community Survey Results
body:
A Markdown version of this page is available at https://railsdeveloper.com/survey/2026.md .
Nearly 1,800 developers from the Ruby on Rails community across 80 countries shared their thoughts on the tools, frameworks, and workflows that shape their daily development lives.
This year, we also asked about something that's on everyone's mind: AI. How teams are using it, how they feel about it, and whether it's actually changing the way they work.
This is the ninth edition of our survey since 2009. For nearly two decades, it has been one of the key ways our team at Planet Argon keeps a pulse on how this community has evolved.
Some of these questions date back to our very first survey, allowing us to track trends over time. Others are new additions, designed to reflect what's changed in our ecosystem since we last asked.
Now it’s time to dig in. We hope you find something useful, surprising, or at least validating here.
How to read the charts: Responses were collected from April to early July 2026. Percentages are based on the people who answered each question. Many questions let people pick more than one answer, so those totals add up to more than 100%. Write-in answers were grouped by hand.
In 2026 : CS degree 44% Self-taught 41% Bootcamp 8% On the job 7%
What stands out to me most is that only 7% of respondents are new to Rails. I don't necessarily read that as a lack of growth, but as a reminder that people who are newest to Rails may also be the least likely to know about a Rails community survey in the first place. Do they even realize they're part of the community yet?
If an agent increasingly influences which framework someone first encounters, the challenge is no longer just helping people discover Rails, it's helping them discover the Rails community, too. How do we make sure those newcomers find the wealth of resources, support, history, and opportunities available to them?
The doors to Rails are open wider than ever before, but we still need folks at the door welcoming people in. That's one of the biggest new opportunities agentic programming creates for the community.

Ever since, I wanted to build a polyglot version manager that solved all of the problems I saw with dev environment setup. It's incredible to see my ideas having such an impact in the Ruby/Rails community. I also recently GA'ed precompiled Ruby binaries for mise and am happy to see that folks really seem to love them.

Two years ago, in the Rails 2024 survey, before AI coding tools were part of daily work for most of us, the top reasons teams gave for not upgrading Rails or Ruby were basically the same as this year: "not enough time," "not enough budget," and "not a priority." That tells us something important. If AI tooling had ever been the missing piece, that list would have shifted by now. It hasn't, because this was never a tooling problem, it's an engineering culture problem.
At FastRuby, we've seen firsthand AI noticeably speed up the mechanical parts of an upgrade: untangling old dependencies, addressing deprecation warnings, and triaging a flaky test suite. But the customers who come to us still running Rails 6 or Ruby 2.x weren't stuck because the tools didn't exist. They're carrying years of technical debt in dependencies nobody made time to address, and no amount of AI assistance fixes a roadmap that never made room for the upgrade. "Not enough time" and "no budget" are just more polite ways of saying "not a priority." Until that changes, neither will the survey results.
We hear both of those every week. In our experience the hard part is rarely the upgrade itself. It’s not knowing how big it’s going to be. Tell us which Rails version you’re on and we’ll send back a quick upgrade complexity snapshot .
Rather keep it in-house? A Rails Upgrade Kickoff gives your team a roadmap and a way to fold upgrades into normal work, so the next one isn’t a project.

In the last couple of years, all big features have been contributed to or heavily requested by the community: single process mode, dynamic recurring tasks, fibers, batches... we're close to version 2.0 now, and I hope it continues maturing and improving, and becoming a boring, reliable piece that people don't need to think about because it just works.

What a difference two years makes. The last community survey feels like another lifetime! Almost overnight, agents have become one of the first resources developers reach for when researching, learning, and building, so they've become an important audience for the Rails Foundation, too. We now need to make discovering, learning, and embracing Rails as seamless for agents as it is for humans.
For the Rails Foundation, the mission remains the same- we still want to make sure someone learns about Rails (wherever they ask the question) and gets quickly from idea to building a working MVP. But it requires a shift in strategy and how we think about documentation, education, and marketing for both humans and agents.
We have a lot of work to do in this new agentic world, but the opportunity for Rails is huge, so we're excited about what the future holds.

It's amazing to see the Ruby/Rails community more connected and active than ever in recent years! Unlike the last decade, when events were mostly local, it feels like borders have simply disappeared. We've truly become a global community of Ruby Friends!
As an attendee, it's exciting to arrive at an event knowing that, beyond the talks, the conversations I'll have in the hallways will be just as enriching, thanks to the diversity of people and perspectives we have today.
And especially as an organizer of larger events like Tropical on Rails 24, and local and consistent ones like Rails Girls São Paulo a project that brings and encourages women to code, seeing Brazil grow in the community's top of mind is incredibly exciting. The numbers around people's intention to visit Brazil make this even more special. I also think this representation comes from all the people who have been organizing and nurturing local events here since Rails was launched. That work over the years has helped build a very strong and welcoming community in Brazil.
The Brazilian vibe, at home or abroad, has been winning people over in recent years, and I believe we'll see more and more people visiting Brazil, joining our events, and speaking at them!
I hope to see our welcome DNA become an increasingly strong part of our wonderfully diverse community!
Débora is a software engineer and has been working with Rails since 2012. She is one of the Rails Girls São Paulo organizers, and has spent years helping grow the local Ruby community through events, mentoring, and teaching programming.
Honestly, I asked our team on multiple occasions to double- and triple-check this data. I knew this was a write-in question, so seeing both Maintainable and On Rails show up so prominently seemed a little suspicious.
It’s an honor to host two podcasts with their own particular flavors. Maintainable lets me talk with people about the messy, long-term realities of building and maintaining software. On Rails is where guests share how Ruby on Rails is part of the secret sauce behind real-world applications. At the time of this survey, On Rails had only been on the air for a little over a year.
It’s a delight to know these conversations are connecting with people, and a privilege to see both shows mentioned alongside so many other talented podcasts in the Ruby and Rails community.
Thanks to everyone who listens, to our real and occasionally not-so-real sponsors, and most importantly, to the guests who keep showing up to talk shop with us.

Ruby was the first programming language I fell in love with. Its relentless focus on beauty, aesthetics, taste, and the joy of programming made me feel seen. People cared about how code felt to read and write. I missed that.
When I returned at the end of 2024 to build Chat with Work, I couldn't believe how familiar Rails still felt. Fifteen years later, Active Record still looked like Active Record. I could come back and build things. I wanted that same feeling from my AI code, and RubyLLM grew out of that desire.
Finding RubyLLM among the five most-loved gems is an incredible welcome home. What started as something I needed for my own application has grown through people building things I hadn't imagined, sharing ideas, and contributing. To everyone who wrote it in: thank you.
