title: Ukrainian forces reportedly strike Russian targets 2,500 kilometers from border
body:
Ukraine struck several targets, including a petrochemical plant and a warehouse in Siberia around 2,500 kilometers away from the border on Oct. 24, monitoring channels reported.
A fire first broke out at the Omsky Kauchuk petrochemical plant in the Russian city of Omsk, according to Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova Plus.
The facility is one of Russia's largest petrochemical plants, and the company behind Omsky Kauchuk says the site is a leading producer of synthetic rubber, organic synthesis products, and methyl tert-butyl ether, an additive used to refine gasoline.
The plant is part of Russia's supply chain for rocket fuel, including for the Iskander ballistic missile used in fatal attacks against Ukraine, Exilenova Plus said.
Russian ballistic missiles targeted Kyiv in a fatal attack on the night of Oct. 13-14, killing five people and injuring another 25. At least one person was killed, and 24 were injured in another Russian ballistic missile attack overnight on Oct. 22.
Later, a warehouse belonging to major Russian online retailer Ozon was also hit in the Ukrainian drone attack, Exilenova Plus reported .
Omsk Oblast Governor Vitaliy Khotsenko confirmed that the region was targeted by Ukrainian drones, saying that a logistics hub in the city of Omsk was hit.
"A logistics hub in Omsk was attacked by a drone. Personnel were promptly evacuated. Emergency services are working at the scene," he claimed.
Reports could not be immediately verified by the Kyiv Independent.
Ozon and its competitor Wildberries have been targeted by Ukrainian forces in recent months. The two are a major part of Russia's economy, with their broader ecosystems accounting for about 8.5% of Russia's GDP.
Ukraine has targeted facilities that often serve as storage sites for dual-use goods used in weapons production and other military purposes.
Ukraine regularly strikes military targets deep within Russia and occupied territories in an effort to diminish Moscow's ability to continue waging its war.
Omsk Oblast was also under fire in an attack on Oct. 8. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed that its forces struck the Omsk oil refinery .
"The destruction of such facilities is the exercise by Ukraine of its inalienable right to self-defense in accordance with Article 51 of the UN Charter and is aimed at reducing the military-economic potential of the Russian Federation," Ukraine's General Staff said .
More recently, on Oct. 24, the General Staff said that Ukrainian forces struck the Tolyattikauchuk petrochemical plant in the Russian city of Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, as well as an aircraft at the Yeysk airfield in Krasnodar Krai.
The synthetic rubbers are used to make solid rocket fuel for tactical and ballistic missiles, according to the General Staff.
"Damage to such objects affects the supply chain of raw materials for the Russian missile program," Ukraine's General Staff wrote.

title: Ghana successfully ends type 2 poliovirus outbreak, maintains over 95% immunisation coverage – GHS
body: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) has announced the successful closure of Ghana’s type 2 poliovirus outbreak in August 2026, marking a significant milestone in the country’s efforts to eliminate the disease. In a statement issued on Saturday, October 24, to commemorate World Polio Day 2026, the Service said the achievement followed sustained immunisation campaigns, strengthened disease surveillance and coordinated outbreak response measures. According to the GHS, the outbreak was successfully closed in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO), UNICEF, Gavi, Rotary International and the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The milestone, confirmed through rigorous Outbreak Response Assessments (OBRA), places Ghana alongside Burundi, Guinea-Bissau, the Republic of Congo and Uganda, which also successfully closed their type 2 poliovirus outbreaks in August 2026. “This milestone, confirmed through rigorous Outbreak Response Assessments (OBRA), demonstrates Ghana’s strong surveillance, immunisation, and rapid response systems,” the statement noted. The Service attributed the progress to years of investment in routine immunisation, supplementary vaccination campaigns and community mobilisation, which have helped prevent endemic polio transmission. It disclosed that since introducing the Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) in 2018 and adding a second dose in 2024, Ghana has consistently maintained immunisation coverage above 95 per cent. Despite the achievement, the GHS cautioned against complacency, stressing that continued surveillance and vaccination remain essential to preventing new outbreaks. “A polio case anywhere is a polio case everywhere,” the statement emphasised, underscoring the importance of sustained collaboration with international health partners. This year’s World Polio Day is being observed under the theme “One Day, One Focus: Ending Polio for Good”, highlighting the importance of community participation and ensuring that every eligible child receives the necessary vaccines. The Service reminded the public that polio can cause lifelong paralysis but is preventable through vaccination, urging parents and caregivers to ensure their children are fully immunised. “Together, we can protect our children and secure a polio-free future for Ghana,” it stated. The GHS, under the leadership of its Director-General, Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining Ghana’s polio-free status and strengthening measures to protect children against future outbreaks.

title: GoldBod rejects claims Sammy Gyamfi endorsed illegal mining, announces new support programme for miners
body: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has dismissed claims that its Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, endorsed illegal mining, describing a viral video circulating on social media as selectively edited and misleading. In a statement issued on Saturday, October 24, GoldBod explained that the video was taken from Mr Gyamfi’s engagement with artisanal and small-scale miners in March 2026, during which he outlined the government’s policy to transition eligible informal miners into a lawful and environmentally responsible mining system. According to the Board, the edited footage removes the context of the CEO’s remarks, creating the false impression that he had approved illegal mining activities. “Government’s policy is not to legitimise illegal mining. It is to end illegality by transitioning eligible operators into a formal system where they can be licensed, regulated, monitored and held accountable for their environmental and operational conduct,” the statement clarified. GoldBod emphasised that providing a legal pathway for eligible informal miners to regularise their operations should not be confused with endorsing illegal mining. The Board recalled that at the 2026 Mining in Motion Summit, Mr Gyamfi advocated firm but inclusive mining regulations, stressing the need to combine enforcement with formalisation, capacity-building and economic opportunities. As part of this approach, GoldBod announced that consultations had commenced on its proposed Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (ASM) Formalisation and Financing Support Programme (FFSP), scheduled for rollout in 2027. The initiative is being developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, the University of Mines and Technology and the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF), with technical support from Rand Refinery SA. It seeks to provide financing and technical support to eligible miners, increase mineral production and revenues, create jobs, reduce operational costs and address environmental degradation. GoldBod disclosed that it had begun engaging government agencies, small-scale miners’ associations, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to ensure the programme is inclusive, sustainable and responsive to industry needs. The Board further announced a partnership with the Ghana Geological Survey Authority (GGSA) to undertake geological investigations at Funsi in the Upper West Region and Benesere in the Ashanti Region. The studies are intended to identify mineralised areas, support responsible mining expansion and reduce environmentally destructive practices associated with speculative or ‘lottery mining’. On environmental restoration, GoldBod said it was supporting the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and investing in responsible gold sourcing, traceability, land reclamation and water remediation. It disclosed that it was funding the reclamation of 50 hectares of degraded land in the Tano Nimiri Forest Reserve, supporting the rehabilitation of water treatment plants affected by illegal mining and procuring a track-and-trace system to strengthen accountability in gold sourcing. “These are not the actions or policies of an institution that endorses illegal mining,” the Board maintained. GoldBod reiterated its opposition to mining activities that destroy water bodies and forest reserves, insisting that environmental protection and effective regulation remain central to its mandate. It further explained that its formalisation initiatives align with Section 3(1)(f) of the Ghana Gold Board Act, 2025 (Act 1140), which mandates the institution to promote the formalisation of small-scale mining through supply chain sustainability. The Board reaffirmed its commitment to ending illegal mining while creating opportunities for eligible operators to transition into a regulated industry that contributes to Ghana’s economic development and environmental sustainability.

title: Babcock opens skills centre on Devonport waterfront
body: Babcock has opened a Skills Centre at Devonport Dockyard able to support fifteen hundred technical staff and apprentices a year, and has broken ground on an Integrated Logistics Hub at Sherford that will pull together more than thirty separate logistics sites, according to the company. Luke Pollard, the Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry and the member for Plymouth Sutton and Devonport, formally opened the Skills Centre, which brings practical training onto the waterfront alongside the work it supports. The logistics hub at Sherford falls within the Plymouth and South Devon Freeport, on an eighteen point eight acre site with room for a thirty thousand square metre facility. Babcock said it will increase operational capacity and resilience for submarine sustainment and deep maintenance at Devonport, supporting the dual-streaming of Astute class submarines and the transition to Dreadnought. Pollard said: “Plymouth has always been at the heart of our national defence, and investments like this show how working with industry partners like Babcock can deliver both the skills our Armed Forces need, and the opportunities and growth this community deserves. “The new Skills Centre will support those already in defence to learn new skills and grow their career and create new pathways for those entering defence for the first time, giving local people the chance to build a career they can be proud of.” Neal Misell, chief executive of Babcock Nuclear, said: “Today demonstrates our long-term commitment to Plymouth and the wider region, developing the skills, capability and infrastructure needed to bolster the UK’s national defence resilience, while creating opportunities for economic growth and prosperity for future generations. Concluding the day at the new Babcock Capability Centre here in Plymouth city centre was a great chance to share our upcoming plans for the facility with regional partners which will see us relocate around 2000 colleagues into the heart of the city, bringing economic benefits and opportunities as we support the retention and creation of high value jobs into the future.” Richard May, chief executive of the Plymouth and South Devon Freeport, said: “This is the Freeport doing what it does best – unlocking opportunities and turning plans into real investment. We’re delighted to be working with Babcock to bring this exciting project forward and build on the momentum we’ve created together. It’s a proud moment for everyone involved – and a great example of the defence dividend delivering real benefits for Plymouth and South Devon.” Councillor Dan Thomas, leader of South Hams District Council, said: “This investment is part of the bigger picture for the South Hams. We promised to support a thriving local economy, create opportunities for good-quality jobs and build strong, resilient communities. By investing carefully and working with our partners, we are turning those promises into practical action that will benefit residents and businesses now and in the future.” The post Babcock opens skills centre on Devonport waterfront first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Instacart reportedly discussed selling itself with DoorDash and Uber
body:
Instacart might sell itself to a larger competitor, according to multiple news reports.
The Information reported Friday that the grocery delivery company has hired an investment bank to help it evaluate its options and that it’s held acquisition talks with DoorDash. And Bloomberg reported that the company has also talked to Uber — although Uber reportedly walked away from those discussions.
Instacart currently has a market cap of more than $13 billion, and its stock price is up 25% for the year to date. The company could see this as a good time to sell at a desirable price, before the grocery delivery market gets more competitive — but Bloomberg noted that these are early discussions that might not result in a sale.
An Instacart spokesperson declined to comment. The reports of a potential sale caused the company’s share price to spike more than 9.2% on Friday, while Uber and DoorDash stock declined.

title: Mahama urges Africa to finance its own peace operations, curb illicit financial flows
body: President John Mahama has called on African countries to take greater responsibility for financing their own peace operations, curbing illicit financial flows and building technological resilience, insisting that the continent must take charge of its own security and development. Addressing the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Peace in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, President Mahama said Africa must reduce its dependence on external funding and strengthen its capacity to respond to security threats. “From financing our own peace operations through the AU Peace Fund to curbing illicit financial flows and building homegrown technological resilience, we must author and fund our destiny ourselves,” he said. President Mahama said Africa’s reliance on external funding for peace operations left the continent vulnerable to decisions taken by foreign governments. He cited the transition from the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (ATMIS) to the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), which he said required about 190 million dollars annually, while the AU Peace Fund could barely muster 20 million dollars. He warned that when funding decisions are taken outside Africa, African countries have limited influence over decisions affecting their own security. “That is not an African solution to African problems. That is external dependency disguised in an African beret. We must fund our own peace,” he said. He also challenged African leaders to move beyond signing agreements and frameworks that are not fully implemented. He cited Agenda 2063, the African Peace and Security Architecture and the “Silencing the Guns” initiative as examples of continental frameworks whose objectives require stronger implementation. “Our problem is not the ink on the paper; it is the courage of our execution,” he said. President Mahama called on the African Union and regional bodies to assess political commitment honestly, identify failures to comply with agreements and hold member states accountable for their pledges. He also urged governments to implement signed protocols, ratify agreements on the free movement of people, fund their peace budgets and strengthen governance beyond national capitals. Presenting the 2026 State of Peace and Security in Africa Report, covering January 2025 to June 2026, President Mahama argued that the continent’s security challenges cannot be resolved by focusing solely on weapons, military capacity and armed groups. “The real disease is mostly in the arena of political economy,” he said, urging African leaders to examine who controls the continent’s natural resources, who benefits from their extraction and whose interests are served by continued instability. He cited conflicts in Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo, the activities of Al-Shabaab in Somalia and tensions in Mozambique’s Cabo Delgado region as examples of how resource exploitation, weak governance and the marginalisation of local communities can contribute to insecurity. In Sudan, he said, the conflict is linked not only to battles over Khartoum but also to gold extraction sites. In eastern DRC, he linked the resurgence of the M23 group to coltan, cobalt and the global competition for minerals needed for the green energy transition. “These are not separate, random brushfires. They are symptoms of a single, continent-wide firestorm,” President Mahama said. He warned that competition for African resources was being intensified by a polarised global environment in which external powers were seeking influence and access across the continent. “Africa is not an empty chessboard for foreign powers to play their games. We are not spectators,” he said, calling for African countries to exercise greater control over their strategic assets and negotiate fairer terms for their exploitation. “Real sovereignty means having the administrative, legal, and economic power to govern your strategic assets, negotiate fair terms, and ensure the wealth beneath our people’s feet actually puts food on their tables,” he added.

title: Arsenal go level at top of Premier League with Man City after easing to win over Everton
body: Arsenal moved to level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League after a comfortable 2-0 win over Everton in the pouring North London rain on Saturday. After table-toppers City fell to their first league defeat of the season earlier in the day, when Enzo Maresca's side lost 2-1 at Aston Villa , reigning champions Arsenal made no mistake a few hours later at the Emirates Stadium. A goal in each half from Ezri Konsa and then Gabriel earned the Gunners all three points against a tepid Everton attacking performance and Arsenal move alongside City – but behind on goal difference – on 21 points from eight games. Victory came on the back of Arsenal's draining Uefa Champions League draw at Bayern Munich on Tuesday when a late goal from Declan Rice had earned Mikel Arteta's team a battling point in Germany, but saw Bukayo Saka limp off with a thigh injury that could rule him out for six to eight weeks. “It is a great feeling to get the three points, it always is. A clean sheet and a goal; it is a fantastic day overall,” said Konsa. Ezri Konsa opens his account for @Arsenal , putting the home side ahead from a corner! ⚽️ #ARSEVE pic.twitter.com/LPdTyxVRyq — beIN SPORTS (@beINSPORTS_EN) October 24, 2026 “I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he said he had been waiting for it as well. It was only right I got it today. A goal from a set-piece has felt like it has been coming and today was the day. “I’m pleased for Gabriel. He is a top player and a top human. He has made my life easy since I joined the club and it is a pleasure to play along side him. “I've come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It's not surprising to me. We are champions and to be champions you've got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.” The opening goal came after an almighty scramble in the Everton's box following Martin Odegaard's in-swinging corner which was eventually bundled home virtually on the goalline by Konsa. It was the England defender's first goal for the club following his summer switch from Aston Villa and, surprisingly, Arsenal's first from a set-piece this season. The second did not arrive until the 68th minute and this time it was Konsa's defensive partner Gabriel – in his 200th Premier League game – who scored it. A nice Arsenal move saw an interchange of short passes ending with substitute Bruno Guimaraes slotting a ball down the flank to Ben White, who was played onside by the away defence, and his cross into the box was headed home at the far post by his Brazilian teammate. Another goal for @Arsenal ! ⚽️ Ben White puts it on a plate for Gabriel to extend the home side's lead! #ARSEVE pic.twitter.com/BcQKksq2DN — beIN SPORTS (@beINSPORTS_EN) October 24, 2026 Next up for Arsenal will an away day at fourth-tier Fleetwood Town in the League Cup last-16 on Tuesday, followed by a trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool next weekend. Everton have now won just once in seven league matches but remain in the top half of the table, although that could change if results go against them on Sunday. They now face a double-header against Newcastle United, starting with Thursday's League Cup tie on Merseyside, followed b “Ultimately two set-pieces have cost us,” said Everton captain James Tarkowski. “I thought we did all right. We created a few chances ourselves but it feels disappointing – the second one especially was a suckerpunch. “The minimum is leaving everything out there. That is what the fans and the club expect of us. There was quality at times and we could have scored one. I’ve had much tougher games here but the three points doesn’t go our way.”

title: Qatar supports Senegal’s preparations for Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games
body: Qatar has provided a total of 15 buses and a consignment of security equipment to the Republic of Senegal to support preparations for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, which run from 31 October to 13 November and mark the first time anOlympic event has been held on African soil. The initiative reflects Qatar’s wider commitment to helping host nations deliver sporting events and enhance international cooperation by sharing expertise and resources gained through hosting the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 and other major tournaments. H.E. Youssef Shaban Ibrahim Al Sada, Ambassador of the State of Qatar to the Republic of Senegal, said: “Qatar and Senegal have a strong and long-standing relationship, and we are pleased to support Senegal’s preparations for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, a historic moment for sports in Africa. Sharing the expertise we have gained from hosting major sporting events is among the most valuable contributions we can make, andreflects our belief in the role of sport in strengthening cooperation between nations.” Qatar has supported the preparations of several host nations in recent years, drawing on its own legacy of staging major tournaments to strengthen cooperation in sport and relations between nations.

title: Sweden's Government Offices Block ChatGPT and Claude, Keep Microsoft Copilot
body:
Sweden's Government Offices—the administrative body supporting the prime minister and cabinet—will block ChatGPT and Claude on staff computers from Monday, directing civil servants to Microsoft's Copilot as the only approved AI tool, according to Sweden’s national, publicly funded radio broadcaster Sveriges Radio .
The reasoning comes from Mikael Wettercrantz, the Government Offices' director of digitalisation, who posted on the staff intranet that using AI services without a formal contract can have "consequences for our information security."
“We have seen several examples of problematic use of open AI services. The examples concern both the sensitivity of the information that has been entered and how the AI-generated responses have been handled,” he said.
Consumer AI tools without formal agreements send user queries to external company servers—and U.S. law allows authorities to compel those companies to hand over data on request.
A formal security agreement, at minimum, defines what the provider can and cannot do with government employees' inputs, which is why the distinction between a vetted enterprise contract and an open consumer tool matters here.
Copilot passes because the Government Offices reviewed it and raised its security settings after the review—something it did not do for ChatGPT or Claude. Some employees can still access both blocked tools through an AI platform the Government Offices built internally, though the press office hasn't said how many people that covers or what restrictions apply.
Sweden's Tax Agency and the National Board of Institutional Care have already imposed similar bans on consumer AI tools. The Enforcement Authority—the agency responsible for debt collection and enforcing court orders—is preparing a decision of its own. An internal audit at the Transport Administration separately found roughly 10 AI services being used there in a "widespread and risky way."
The European Parliament went further in February, disabling AI features across all its work devices—ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot included—after concluding it could not guarantee the security of data those tools processed.
European government concerns about AI data security have been building since Italy's ChatGPT ban in 2023. Sweden is now drawing a narrower line than Brussels, sanctioning one U.S. tech company's product while shutting out two others.
Microsoft incorporated Claude models into Copilot in early 2026. In the EU—where Sweden sits—Anthropic's models default to off and require administrators to deliberately enable them.
Sweden's Government Offices has not confirmed whether its Copilot instance has Claude switched on, which means the distinction between the "banned" AI and the "approved" one is not as clean as the announcement implies.

title: Protector drone flight over Channel was not for Home Office
body: An RAF Protector RG-1 that flew over the English Channel on 14 October was operating in support of defence aims and not in support of the Home Office, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, had asked for what reason the aircraft was tasked to support the Home Office in the Channel on that date. Louise Sandher-Jones, the Minister for the Armed Forces, said: “The Ministry of Defence regularly and routinely monitors our waters to protect UK interests, contribute to domestic maritime security, and act as a deterrent against potentially malign activities. “The deployment the hon. Member refers to was conducted in support of Defence aims, not in support of the Home Office.” Protector RG-1 is the RAF’s version of the General Atomics MQ-9B SkyGuardian, and the United Kingdom has ordered sixteen of them to replace the MQ-9A Reaper fleet that was retired after two decades of operations over Afghanistan, Iraq and Syria. The aircraft has a wingspan of around twenty four metres, an endurance of more than thirty hours and a maximum altitude above forty thousand feet, and carries Brimstone 3 missiles and Paveway IV bombs alongside its electro-optical and infrared sensors and a maritime search radar. The aircraft is built to a NATO airworthiness standard and fitted with a detect and avoid system, lightning protection and de-icing, and that certification allows it to fly in unsegregated British airspace alongside civil traffic without a reserved block of sky being set aside for it. The Reaper it replaced could not, and needed segregated airspace or a danger area for every domestic sortie. The fleet is based at RAF Waddington in Lincolnshire with 31 Squadron, and operations are flown from ground control stations on the station. Surveillance of small boat crossings in the Channel has been contracted out by the Home Office to a commercial operator. The Portuguese company Tekever has operated its AR5 maritime surveillance aircraft over the Channel since 2020 under Home Office contracts, a framework worth up to £1 billion and renewed repeatedly since. The AR5 is a twin-engine fixed-wing aircraft that flies for more than twelve hours and carries maritime and synthetic aperture radars, day and night cameras and receivers for vessel identification and distress beacons. Paul Webb, managing director of Tekever UK, has said of the work that “drones can identify humans in distress in a much faster way and help rescue teams.” The company has since sold the same system to the Portuguese government and has expanded into supplying uncrewed aircraft to Ukraine. The post Protector drone flight over Channel was not for Home Office first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Block’s new voice model sounds eerily human
body:
Jack Dorsey’s Block released a new voice model out of the company’s research lab that runs locally and sounds strangely human with its expressions like laughs, pauses, and cries. The company said the model, called Dessa, is trained fully on human speech and a single Nvidia GPU rack.
Dessa is a full-duplex model, which means it can talk and listen at the same time, just like the GPT-Live model OpenAI released earlier this year . Typically, speech models are paired with a large language model for knowledge retrieval. Block said that Dessa’s knowledge stems from the conversational data it has.
We believe voice is the most natural way to interact with intelligence, so we created Dessa, the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built. Talking with it feels like talking with a person…full of emotion, nuance, pauses, and a natural cadence. https://t.co/r0qFLdvd6c
Block said that the current models can sound unnatural and annoying because they have text in the pipeline that drives speech generation. A lot of models like ElevenLabs v4 or Fish Audio Drama 3 use voice tags to drive emotion in speech generation. Dorsey’s company claims that emotion is built into its model. It’s not clear if that emotion is being steered by some kind of tags.
“Interacting with current voice AI can just plain suck. It turns your voice into text and throws away an incredible amount of information text alone can’t carry. The most powerful AIs in the world can’t hear how you feel. We think that’s ridiculous, leads to a worse experience, and is potentially dangerous,” the company said in a blog post .
The company’s researchers posted multiple examples of conversations with Dessa where the agent had different voices, cadences, and emotions. For instance, in the conversation, the bot said it was tired from work, and at that point it sounded tired.

The company said that the model can run locally on a consumer-grade computer such as a MacBook M4 Max or better. However, there is no public access to Dessa at the moment, and Block has put out a call for safety researchers to test the model. This is likely to test out cases where a voice agent could trick people on the other end.
Block is in the business of finance and selling its solutions to small businesses. Square already uses voice AI to handle ordering . But with its own voice model that can run on-device, it can power a lot more business and consumer experiences at a lower cost.
